result.scope: Deep structural analysis of the KP14 (Kogan–Papanikolaou 2014) model exactly as implemented in /Users/sjpruitt/GitHub/bop-run-upload: full reading of utils_kp14/panel_functions_kp14.py, utils_kp14/sdf_compute_kp14.py, utils_kp14/kp14_fd.py, utils_kp14/integ_kp14.py, utils_kp14/loadings_compute_kp14.py, the KP14 block of config.py, plus the shipped solution files utils_kp14/KP14_solfiles/{G_func.csv, integ_results.npz}. All quantitative claims were produced by re-running the actual simulation code (N=250 firms, T=250 months, seed 7) and by a dense re-implementation of sdf_compute_kp14.sdf_loop that reproduces the shipped max_sr/sdf_ret exactly, evaluated at t=200..248. Also re-solved the G Feynman–Kac ODE and the CIR conditional-expectation integrals independently to test the shipped solfiles.

findings.claim: The shipped solution files are STALE: G_func.csv was solved under the PRE-Jun-18 parameters (GAMMA_X=1.38, SIGMA_EPS=0.2) and is wrong by a factor of ~49 under the current config.py parameters. This is the single largest defect in the KP14 truth.
findings.evidence: I re-solved the same upwind FD system as kp14_fd.py, (rho - L)G1 = C*A(eps,1)^{1/(1-alpha)}, on the identical 1000-point grid. Recover G1 from the file as G1 = a*G_up + (1-a)*G_down with a = mu_L/(mu_L+mu_H) = 0.6809 (the weighting kp14_fd.py itself uses at lines 100-101). At eps = 1.009: G1(file) = 1409.5; G1 re-solved with CURRENT config params (rho = 0.015753, A_0 = 4.3535, sigma_eps = 0.02) = 69,013; G1 re-solved with OLD params (gamma_x = 1.38 -> CONST = 0.3194, A_0 = 3.1309, rho = 0.105453, sigma_eps = 0.2) = 1431.1. Ratio file/NEW = 0.0204; ratio file/OLD = 0.9849. Same verdict for G2 (file 359.3, new 4372.3, old 425.2). kp14_fd.py line 7 imports `from parameters_kp14 import *`, a module that does not exist anywhere in the repo, so the solfiles cannot be regenerated from this repo and were in fact never regenerated after commit 77c5ffc.

findings.claim: integ_results.npz is CORRUPT: scipy.integrate.quad silently failed on ~68% of the eps grid, returning exact zeros. Critically, it returns ZERO over the entire eps interval where the simulated panel actually lives, so Et_A_mod, Et_G_up, Et_G_down and every squared/cross integral are ~0 for essentially every firm-month.
findings.evidence: Counting nonzeros in the shipped file: A_mod_lst 322/1000 nonzero, G_up_lst 317/1000, G_down_lst 311/1000, A_mod2_lst 364/1000, etc. The nonzero indices are isolated islands (30, 106-108, 208-221, 283-295, ...). The simulated eps distribution is eps ~ 1.0003 with sd 0.0237, range [0.930, 1.066] -> grid indices 184-211; ALL of 184..207 are zero. Direct comparison against a correct 4001-point trapezoid quadrature over the noncentral-chi2 CIR transition density: E_t[G_up] at eps=0.95: shipped 3.0e-121 vs correct 1548.3; at eps=1.00: shipped 8.8e-48 vs correct 1622.5; at eps=1.05 (inside a working island): shipped 1703.1 = correct 1703.1. E_t[A_mod] at eps=1.05: shipped 2348.7 vs correct 20614 (9x too small, because the stale file used A_0 = 3.13 not 4.35). Root cause is integ_kp14.py:43: `quad(integrand, 0, 10, epsabs=1e-10, epsrel=1e-10, limit=500)` on a density whose sd is ~0.006 for sigma_eps=0.02 (and ~0.057 even for sigma_eps=0.2) — Gauss-Kronrod on [0,10] never samples the spike, the error estimate is ~0, and quad returns 0 with no warning.

findings.claim: Because Et_G is ~0, the model's TRUE conditional risk premium rp is a pure numerical artifact equal to minus the PVGO share of firm value. It has the wrong sign, the wrong level, and a cross-sectional dispersion 173x the economically correct value.
findings.evidence: erets (panel_functions_kp14.py:199) = (term1 + term2 + term3 + term4)/price - 1 where term2 = Et_z_alph*Et_x*Et_G is the PVGO continuation value. Measured at t=240 over 238 non-degenerate firms: term1/P = 0.90685, term2/P = 0.00115, term3/P = 0.01744, term4/P = 7.8e-06, while PVGO/P = 0.0863. So term2 delivers 1.3% of the PVGO it should. Consequence: shipped rp mean = -0.03206/mo (-38.5%/yr), sd = 0.03616/mo (43.4%/yr); corr(shipped rp, -PVGOshare) = +0.9505, R^2(rp on PVGOshare) = 0.9034 with slope -0.9491. Replacing only Et_G_up/Et_G_down/Et_A_mod with correct quadrature gives repaired rp mean = +0.01102/mo, sd = 0.00356/mo. The continuous-time theory value is rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*share_i, which gives mean +0.00724/mo (8.69%/yr, matching gamma_x*sigma_x + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*E[share] = 0.0869) and sd 0.000210/mo (0.25%/yr). Shipped sd / theory sd = 173x.

findings.claim: Q1 CONFIRMED with a sharp qualification: the code implements KP14's economics correctly in sign (assets-in-place load on x at 8.97%/yr, growth options carry a NEGATIVE IST premium of -6.94%/yr), but EVERY firm has an exposure to the x shock of EXACTLY 1. There is zero cross-sectional dispersion in the loading on the dominant priced shock.
findings.evidence: gamma_x*sigma_x = 0.69*0.13 = 0.0897/yr; alph = alpha/(1-alpha) = 5.6667; alph*gamma_z*sigma_z = 5.6667*(-0.35)*0.035 = -0.06942/yr. Both enter only through discount rates: KP14_CONST = r + gamma_x*sigma_x + delta - mu_x (config.py:264, giving A_0 = 1/CONST) and KP14_RHO which contains +alph*gamma_z*sigma_z (config.py:270-272). So E[R^AIP]-r = 8.97%/yr, E[R^PVGO]-r = 8.97 - 6.94 = 2.03%/yr, and firm i's premium = gamma_x*sigma_x + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*share_i. Value-premium spread AIP vs PVGO = 6.94%/yr. But price = VAP + PVGO with VAP = x*sum K^alpha A(eps,u) (line 165) and PVGO = z^alph * x * lambda_f * G(eps) (line 173) — x factors out of BOTH exactly, so P_t = x_t * Q_t with Q free of x, and P_{t+1}/P_t has unit x-elasticity for every firm. sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 makes this explicit: Et_x2[t] multiplies the whole (term1+term2+term3) block with no firm index. Numerically: the leading eigenvector of the systematic covariance has loading mean 0.03581 with cross-sectional sd 0.00133 (CV = 3.7%), and sigma_x*sqrt(dt) = 0.03753. So beta_x = 1 for all firms to within 4%.

findings.claim: The TRUE conditional covariance matrix has systematic rank EXACTLY 2, and the second (IST/z) factor accounts for 0.034% of the systematic variance. The entire economic mechanism of KP14 is numerically invisible in this calibration.
findings.evidence: Algebraically: term1+term2+term3 in sdf_compute_kp14.py:138-146 is (1-d*dt)^2 s1 s1' + Ez(part1 part2' + part2 part1') + Ez2 part1 part1' with part2 = (1-d*dt)*s1, so it is rank <= 2 spanned by {s1, part1}; term4 adds only {cf/P, 1+eret}, and 1+eret is itself in span{s1/P, part1/P, cf/P}. Numerically at t=240 on the 238 kept firms, eigenvalues of the off-diagonal-formula (systematic) block are [3.03e-15, 3.10e-15, 3.25e-15, 1.0268e-04, 3.0556e-01]; np.linalg.matrix_rank = 2. Second/first eigenvalue = 3.4e-4. Second-factor loading sd = 0.000657 vs the prediction alph*sigma_z*sqrt(dt)*sd(share) = 0.002073. PVGO/P on kept firms: mean 0.0403, sd 0.0363, p10 0.0146, p90 0.0836 — so the p10-p90 value-premium spread is only 0.0694*(0.0836-0.0146) = 0.48%/yr. Avg pairwise conditional return correlation = 0.3907, exactly (sigma_x*sqrt(dt)/total sd)^2 = (0.03753/0.05987)^2 = 0.392, i.e. ALL of the common variation is the uniform-loading x factor.

findings.claim: Q3: after the 10x cut, the CIR shocks (eps, uj) contribute only 2.2% of idiosyncratic return variance (was 69.2%). 97.8% of firm-specific risk now comes from Poisson project death and arrival. Idiosyncratic variance FELL 3.18x and the systematic share ROSE from 14% to 34%. Conditioning of cond_var worsened 4.1x but is not catastrophic once zero-capital firms are excluded.
findings.evidence: Recomputing diag(cond_var) at t=240 with sigma multipliers applied to Et_epsm1_sq/Et_um1_sq: total var 3.765e-03 (current) vs 9.172e-03 (10x sigmas, i.e. pre-Jun-18) vs 3.711e-03 (sigmas set to 0). Systematic part 1.284e-03 is unaffected by the sigmas. Idio residual: current 2.481e-03, pre-Jun-18 7.887e-03 (ratio 3.179), zero-sigma 2.427e-03. So CIR-driven share of idio var = 1 - 2.427/2.481 = 2.2% now, vs 1 - 2.427/7.887 = 69.2% before. Idio share of TOTAL variance: 0.659 now vs 0.860 before. Per-project Var_t(A(eps,u)) at eps=u=1 = 0.003475 = 0.0183% of A_0^2 = 18.953. Condition number of cond_var on kept firms: 680.4 now vs 165.1 with 10x sigmas (max eig 0.30798, min eig 4.526e-04). Cross-sectional dispersion sd(log diag) = 0.405 now vs 0.499 before; sd(log idio var) = 0.664.

findings.claim: Q4 CONFIRMED, and the mechanism is more specific than 'inverse-idio-variance': idio variance scales as 1/(number of live projects) because project death is a Poisson thinning, and project count IS size. corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971 with slope -0.866; regressed on log(mve) the slope is -0.704 with R^2 = 0.743.
findings.evidence: With CIR shocks contributing only 2.2%, firm-level idiosyncratic variance is driven by independent Bernoulli(delta*dt) deaths across the firm's live projects: the diagonal picks up weight (1-delta*dt) per project whereas the off-diagonal formula uses (1-delta*dt)^2, leaving excess delta*dt*(1-delta*dt)*sum_j (K_j^a A_j)^2, i.e. a 1/n_projects diversification term after dividing by P^2 (sdf_compute_kp14.py:171 vs :138). Measured: corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.9713, OLS slope -0.8658; log(total diag) on log(mve) slope -0.4143 R^2 0.6917; log(idio var) on log(mve) slope -0.7039 R^2 0.7432. Resulting MVE tilts: corr(w*, log size) = +0.601, corr(w*, 1/d) = +0.326, corr(w*, bm) = +0.612, corr(w*, PVGO share) = -0.784, corr(w*, rp) = +0.814. Note rp itself already correlates +0.716 with log size (big firms = many projects = low PVGO share = less negative artifact rp), so BOTH channels push w* toward +size, exactly the anti-size-premium artifact recorded in the memory note.

findings.claim: Q4 split of max_sr: 99.3% of the squared maximum Sharpe comes from cross-sectional alpha-harvesting against idiosyncratic variance, and only 0.7% from bearing priced aggregate risk.
findings.evidence: At t=240 (238 kept firms): mu' Sigma^-1 mu = 109.911 -> SR 10.484/mo = 36.3/yr. mu' D^-1 mu (no factor hedging) = 124.755, so hedging the 2 factors removes only 12%. SR^2 of the pure equal-weighted market bet = 0.795 (0.72% of total); value-weighted market = 0.293 (0.27%). Market-neutral cross-sectional part S2 - S1^2/S0 = 71.987 (65.5%). SR of the pure inverse-variance portfolio 1/d (ignoring rp) = -0.737 and equal-weight = -0.892, i.e. essentially just the (wrong-signed) market — so the MVE is NOT a min-variance portfolio; it is (rp - rp_bar)/d, dispersion-in-rp weighted by 1/d. Averaged over 13 months t=200..248 the shipped max_sr is 10.006/mo = 34.66/yr, whereas the model's economically correct upper bound is sqrt(gamma_x^2 + gamma_z^2) = 0.774/yr — a factor of 45.

findings.claim: Q5 HEADROOM: FF/FM's linear-in-characteristics span already captures 70% of the true maximum Sharpe. The missing 30% is exactly the 1/d ratio — and enriching the basis in RANK space (which is what DKKM does) makes things WORSE, not better.
findings.evidence: Population-optimal weights restricted to w = X a for various bases, evaluated with the TRUE rp and cond_var (no estimation error), n=238, full-MVE SR = 10.484: X = [1, 5 raw chars] (the FM span) -> SR 7.352 = 70.1%; X = [1, 5 rank-standardized chars] -> SR 6.729 = 64.2%; X = [1, ranks, all 15 quadratic rank interactions] -> SR 7.190 = 68.6%, i.e. BELOW the raw-linear basis; X = [1, ranks, 1/d, rp/d] -> SR 10.294 = 98.2%. So the entire remaining headroom is two ratio terms, and a nonlinear expansion in bounded rank features does not recover them. Even a single-regressor basis [1, log size] gets SR 6.735 = 64%.

findings.claim: Q2 characteristic recoverability: {size, bm, agr, roe, mom} recover the project COUNT and the idio-variance almost fully, the arrival intensity and regime partially, and the CIR states essentially not at all. Adding quadratic terms buys little for the objects that matter.
findings.evidence: Cross-sectional R^2 at t=240 (n=238), columns = [5 raw chars linear | 5 rank chars linear | ranks + all quadratic interactions]: nlive 0.817/0.800/0.882; log d (idio+sys variance) 0.880/0.793/0.847; PVGO share 0.717/0.464/0.677; lambda_f 0.387/0.347/0.515; mean project-level u 0.239/0.352/0.522; high regime dummy 0.212/0.220/0.315; eps (firm CIR) 0.056/0.027/0.150; true rp 0.644/0.415/0.597; true MVE weight w* 0.471/0.369/0.433. So: RECOVERABLE = capital/project stock and idio variance (~80-88%); PARTIALLY = lambda_f (39-52%) and the H/L regime (21-32%); NOT RECOVERABLE = eps (6-15%) and, weakly, project-level u. Information loss for the truth: ~36% of the variance of rp and ~53-63% of the variance of w* is not a function of the 5 chars. This is consistent with the reported corr_fitted_vs_truth = 0.568 for 'true' in correlations.csv (R^2 = 0.32).

findings.claim: Q6 BUG: mu_H and mu_L are swapped between the simulated regime chain and the LAMBDA_L normalization. The unconditional project-arrival multiplier is 1.717 instead of the intended 1.0, and the G ODE's flow coefficient is correspondingly wrong.
findings.evidence: panel_functions_kp14.py:98 sets switch_prob = mu_H*dt from the HIGH state and mu_L*dt from LOW, so stationary P(high) = mu_L/(mu_H+mu_L) = 0.6809 (simulated 0.650 over t>=100, consistent given regime persistence 1/0.00625 = 160 months). config.py:257 defines LAMBDA_L = (1 - w*LAMBDA_H)/(1-w) with w = mu_H/(mu_H+mu_L) = 0.3191, giving LAMBDA_L = 0.36719 and 0.3191*2.35 + 0.6809*0.36719 = 1.000. But under the SIMULATED chain the unconditional multiplier is 0.6809*2.35 + 0.3191*0.36719 = 1.7172. Separately, kp14_fd.py:100-101 weights G2 by mu_L/(mu_L+mu_H) = 0.6809, which is the SIM convention, yet solves rho*G1 = util + L*G1 with a unit flow coefficient (rhs1 at line 79) — correct only if the stationary-weighted lambda equals 1, which it does not. Note also config.KP14_PROB_H = 0.6809 is used at line 95 only to initialize the chain and is consistent with the sim, so the inconsistency is entirely on the LAMBDA_L / kp14_fd side.

findings.claim: Q6: the intra-month cash flow is deterministic conditional on t, which removes an entire natural source of idiosyncratic return risk and makes the cross-section easier.
findings.evidence: panel_functions_kp14.py:154 sets cashflow[:,1:,:] = eps[:-1]*x[:-1]*uj[:-1]*K[:-1]^alpha*dt, i.e. the payout received AT t+1 uses eps_t, x_t, u_t, K_t — all known at t. sdf_compute_kp14.py:163-165 correctly treats it as known (term4 = outer(cf/P, 1+eret) + transpose - outer(cf/P, cf/P), a construction that contributes exactly zero conditional variance). So the only conditional randomness in R_{t+1} is x_{t+1}, z_{t+1}, eps_{t+1}, u_{t+1}, deaths, arrivals — no dividend surprise at all.

findings.claim: Q6 degeneracy: ~5% of firms per month have zero live projects (book = 0, PVGO/P = 1, rp = -1.0). They are excluded from the SDF solve but their pathological rp = -1.004 still enters the saved rp vector and the saved cond_var, and evaluate_sdfs.py subsets by firm_ids rather than by book>0.
findings.evidence: At t=240, 12/250 firms (4.8%) have nlive = 0; PVGO/P = 1.0 for them and eret = -1.0 exactly (eret min = -1.00000 in the simulation). sdf_compute_kp14.py:269-270 masks them out of the ER solve (keep = book[t,:] > 0), but lines 291 and 299 return the FULL cond_var and rp including the degenerate rows. utils/evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 then subsets rp and cond_var by firm_ids taken from the estimator's panel. The panel drops them via the book==0 -> ret=NaN rule (panel_functions_kp14.py:271) and the roe/agr NaN screen, so in practice they are excluded — but this is an implicit coupling, not a guarantee.

findings.claim: H5 CONFIRMED for KP14: HJD has a hard floor of 0.269 set by the true HJ-portfolio return alone, and the HJ portfolio carries gross leverage of 9x to 44x.
findings.evidence: Over 13 months t=200,204,...,248: sdf_ret mean -0.1788, sd 0.2091, RMS 0.2689; individual values range from -0.5130 to +0.1493. Gross leverage sum|port[1:]| ranges 9.18 to 44.40. Since HJD = sqrt(mean_t (xret_method,t - sdf_ret_t)^2) and the DKKM/FF ridge targets y = 1 (dkkm_functions.mve_data line 292, fama mve uses sklearn Ridge alpha=0 on 6-7 factors), the method portfolio return is bounded by SR^2/(1+SR^2) in mean and SR/(1+SR^2) in sd, both <= 0.5, and is essentially uncorrelated with sdf_ret (corr_actual_vs_truth ~ -0.007 in correlations.csv). Hence HJD ~ sqrt(0.0723 + var_method) for every method, and method differences are second-order.

verdict_on_hypotheses.hypothesis: H1 SPAN — with only 1-2 priced aggregate shocks and 5-6 characteristics near-deterministic in 2-3 latent states, the true conditional MVE is already (over-)spanned by 6 linear characteristic portfolios; complexity has nothing to buy.
verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: The premise is confirmed far more strongly than stated. The systematic conditional covariance has rank EXACTLY 2 (eigenvalues 0.3056, 1.027e-04, then 3e-15), the first factor has an identical loading of 1 for every firm (loading CV = 3.7%; loading mean 0.03581 vs sigma_x*sqrt(dt) = 0.03753), and the second (IST) factor is 0.034% of the first. So there is effectively ZERO cross-sectional dispersion in priced-risk exposure. BUT the conclusion 'FF over-spans the tangency' is false: population-optimal weights linear in the 5 raw chars attain SR 7.35 out of 10.48 = 70.1%, not 100%. FF/FM leave 30% on the table. The reason DKKM does not collect that 30% is H2/H3, not H1. The correct statement is: the priced-risk dimension is 1 (not 2), and the remaining tangency headroom is not a risk-exposure dimension at all but a variance-weighting ratio.

verdict_on_hypotheses.hypothesis: H2 RATIO NONLINEARITY — w* = D^-1 B c is a ratio b(x)/d(x); FF/FM cannot form it; currently d_i may be too homogeneous or too weakly char-linked.
verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: CONFIRMED as the identity of the headroom: adding {1/d, rp/d} to the linear rank-char basis raises the attainable SR from 6.73 to 10.29 = 98.2% of the full MVE, so the entire missing 30% IS the ratio. The MVE weight is w* ~ (rp - rp_bar)/d and corr(w*, 1/d) = +0.326, corr(w*, rp) = +0.814. REFUTED, however, is the diagnosis that d is too homogeneous or weakly char-linked: sd(log idio var) = 0.664 (ample dispersion) and log d is 88% explained by a linear regression on the 5 raw chars (R^2 = 0.880), because idio var ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/size (slope -0.866 on log nlive, corr -0.971). The obstacle is representational, not economic: 1/d is a heavy-tailed, scale-carrying function that the rank-standardized RFF basis cannot express.

verdict_on_hypotheses.hypothesis: H3 RFF BANDWIDTH MIS-SCALING — with L=5 rank-standardized chars, sd(w'x) <= 0.65 so sin is essentially linear; the basis is barely richer than FM.
verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: Arithmetic confirmed: rank_standardize gives per-char variance 1/12, W = gamma*N(0,1) with gamma <= 1.0, so sd(W x) <= sqrt(5/12) = 0.645, where sin is linear to within 3% and cos is a pure quadratic. Directly tested on the true moments: the best weights in span{1, 5 rank chars} give SR 6.729 (64.2% of full) and adding ALL 15 quadratic rank interactions gives only 7.190 (68.6%) — still BELOW the raw-linear-char basis at 7.352 (70.1%). So the entire sin/cos expansion at this bandwidth is worth less than not rank-transforming at all. A further compounding defect: dkkm_functions.rff line 110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a SECOND time, capping every feature in [-0.5, 0.5] and destroying the scale information needed to represent 1/d, whose cross-sectional log-sd is 0.66. Rescaling gamma by sqrt(130/5) = 5.1 would make the features genuinely nonlinear but would still not fix the second rank-standardization.

verdict_on_hypotheses.hypothesis: H4 CHARACTERISTIC POVERTY — real DKKM uses ~130 weak, partly independent chars; here 5-6 mutually redundant noiseless ones; the truth must be dense and high-dimensional for complexity to pay.
verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: CONFIRMED that the truth is low-dimensional and mostly char-spanned: 5 raw chars linearly explain R^2 = 0.880 of log d, 0.817 of nlive, 0.717 of the PVGO share and 0.644 of the true rp, and a quadratic expansion adds nothing (0.847, 0.882, 0.677, 0.597 respectively — several go DOWN). A small model is the right model. However the chars are NOT noiseless proxies for everything: the firm-level CIR state eps is essentially unrecoverable (R^2 = 0.056 linear, 0.150 with quadratics) and the project-level u average only 0.24-0.52, leaving ~36% of var(rp) and ~53% of var(w*) outside the char span. That residual is pure unlearnable noise for every estimator, which is why all three methods have near-zero corr_actual_vs_truth — it does not differentially favor DKKM.

verdict_on_hypotheses.hypothesis: H5 HJD SCALE MISMATCH — if sd(sdf_ret) >> sd(xret_method) then HJD ~ sd(sdf_ret) for every method and the metric cannot separate them.
verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: Measured over 13 evaluation months: sdf_ret mean -0.1788, sd 0.2091, RMS 0.2689, range [-0.513, +0.149]; the HJ portfolio's gross leverage is 9.2x to 44.4x. HJD therefore has a floor of 0.269 attained by a method that holds nothing. The DKKM/FF/FM MVE portfolios are normalized by regressing factor returns on y = 1, so their return has mean SR^2/(1+SR^2) and sd SR/(1+SR^2), both bounded by 0.5 and in practice much smaller; with correlation to sdf_ret near zero (corr_actual_vs_truth ~ 0.007 in correlations.csv), HJD = sqrt(0.0723 + var_method - 2cov) is dominated by the constant 0.0723 for every method. The metric is structurally incapable of separating them in KP14.

verdict_on_hypotheses.hypothesis: H6 EVALUATION HORIZON / SNR — if the panel has far higher cross-sectional predictability than real data (~0.5%/month), estimation is easy, OLS on 6 factors is efficient, and ridge-on-many-features never wins.
verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: Three independent measurements, all ~50-170x too easy. (i) Cross-sectional predictive R^2 = var(rp)/(var(rp)+mean idio var) = 0.345 (34.5%) versus ~0.005 in real US data — 70x. (ii) Maximum conditional Sharpe = 10.006/month = 34.66 annualized (mean over 13 months, range 5.18 to 17.71), versus the model's own economically correct upper bound sqrt(gamma_x^2 + gamma_z^2) = 0.774/yr — 45x. (iii) Cross-sectional sd of true conditional excess returns = 3.62%/month = 43.4%/yr versus the correct alph*|gamma_z*sigma_z|*sd(share) = 0.021%/month = 0.25%/yr — 173x. At this SNR a 6-parameter OLS on 360 monthly observations is already near-efficient and shrinkage across 3600 features has nothing to add. Note the SNR excess is not a calibration choice — it is entirely produced by the corrupt integ_results.npz.

quantitative_claims: alph = alpha/(1-alpha) = 5.6667; assets-in-place expected excess return = gamma_x*sigma_x = 0.69*0.13 = 8.97%/yr; growth-option premium = 8.97 - alph*|gamma_z*sigma_z| = 8.97 - 5.6667*0.35*0.035*100 = 2.03%/yr; AIP-minus-PVGO spread = 6.94%/yr
Firm i's true conditional excess return should be rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*(PVGO_i/P_i); beta_x = 1 for EVERY firm exactly, beta_z = alph*(PVGO_i/P_i)
PVGO/P on kept firms at t=240: mean 0.0403, sd 0.0363, p10 0.0146, p90 0.0836 -> p10-p90 value-premium spread only 0.48%/yr

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: GS21 has exactly one aggregate shock (x), and the implemented conditional covariance matrix is EXACTLY rank-1-systematic plus diagonal. z is purely idiosyncratic and the code integrates z_i' and z_j' independently.
findings.evidence: panel_functions_gs21.simulate_ar1 draws a single scalar path x[0..T] and an (T+1,N) matrix z; only x is shared. In sdf_compute_gs21.integ_zi_zj_x, `weighted` (lines 135-136) integrates out z' firm-by-firm leaving an (N, n_x) matrix of E_{z'}[payoff_i | x'], and line 141 forms the cross-product ONLY over the shared x' nodes: ERR[i,j] = sum_{x'} w_x f_i(x') f_j(x'). The diagonal is overwritten (line 188) with the exact double integral including z' variance. So Sigma = (x-driven common part) + diag. Numerically at N=200, t=251 the eigenvalues of cond_var are [3.047, 5.2053e-4, 5.2029e-4, 5.1994e-4, ...]: ONE systematic eigenvalue carrying 97.34% of total variance, and the remaining 199 eigenvalues lie exactly in the idiosyncratic-variance bulk [2.39e-4, 5.2e-4] = idio sd in [1.54%, 2.27%]/month. Even though the x'-exposure is nonlinear in principle (10 GH nodes could support rank 9), the firms' f_i(x') functions are near-proportional so the systematic block is numerically rank 1. Mean pairwise conditional correlation = 0.944-0.975 (realized panel correlation 0.975).

findings.claim: Because Sigma = beta beta' + D exactly, the true MVE weight is exactly the idiosyncratic-variance-tilted alpha portfolio w* = D^{-1}(mu - beta*lambda), verified to machine precision.

Decomposition of the maximum conditional squared Sharpe: market/beta leg SR = 0.1074 / 0.0626 / 0.0350 and alpha-leg appraisal ratio = 0.3036 / 0.2169 / 0.2129, total max_sr = 0.3206 / 0.2249 / 0.2149. So 89% / 92% / 97% of the maximum squared Sharpe comes from the ALPHA leg, i.e. from diversifying away sd(alpha)=3.5-4.3 bp/month of cross-sectional mispricing across N nearly identical firms with 2.0-2.4%/month idio vol. Per-firm monthly information ratio = 4.33e-4/0.0203 = 0.0213; times sqrt(200) = 0.302.

findings.claim: DEFAULT NEVER HAPPENS. Zero defaults in 2,163,000 post-burnin firm-months at the production configuration (N=1000, T=920, 3 seeds). The default region is not merely rare, it is unreachable by a factor of ~30 in price. The 'genuine nonlinearity' GS21 was supposed to contribute is absent.
findings.evidence: Direct simulation of the state recursion with the repo's own P_up/P_down/i_cut/b_refin interpolators: defaults = 0/2,163,000; minimum post-burnin equity price P = 30.4, 40.8, 49.6 across seeds (default triggers at P <= 0). Stronger: the MATLAB solution files themselves contain no default region over the ENTIRE solved grid -- min(P_down.csv) = 4.728 and min(P_up.csv) = 10.064 over all 200x20x20 = 80,000 grid points, including z at -2.72 sd, x at -2.69 sd, and b = 1.0 (100% debt per unit capital). Consistently, z_cut_down.csv is pinned at the zgrid floor (-0.146826) at EVERY (x,b) point, i.e. the solver found the default threshold to lie below the state grid everywhere. Realized market leverage b/P: median 0.0019, 95th pct 0.0040, max over 2.16M firm-months = 0.0104. GS21's firms are effectively all-equity (max 1% market leverage) and infinitely far from the default boundary. Note the task premise that default frequency follows from GS21_ZETA is incorrect: zeta = 0.03/3 = 0.01 is the monthly REFINANCING (eta=1) probability, not a default hazard.

findings.claim: The cross-sectional price function is essentially EXACTLY log-linear in (z, b). There is no kink, no convexity, and no size x value x leverage interaction anywhere in the visited state space.
findings.evidence: Cross-sectional OLS of log(P_ex) on (z, b) at t = 251/281/311 (N=200): R^2 = 0.9951 / 0.9890 / 0.9508, with d log P / d z = 0.359 / 0.290 / 0.292 and d log P / d b = -1.248 / -1.247 / -1.246. The leverage elasticity is constant to three decimals across dates and price levels -- the debt effect is a pure constant-elasticity level shift, not a kinked or convex one. On the raw solution grid, P_down at (z=0, x=mid) falls monotonically and near-geometrically from 287.9 at b=0 to 70.8 at b=1 -- smooth, no curvature break. R^2 of the true conditional beta on 6 linear rank-std chars = 0.914 / 0.835 / 0.879, rising only to 0.947 / 0.908 / 0.922 with all 21 quadratic terms. The nonlinearity that exists is generic smooth curvature, not a default kink.

findings.claim: A 40:1 elasticity asymmetry -- firm value responds to the aggregate discount-rate shock x forty times more strongly than to its own productivity z -- is the root cause of the 0.97 pairwise correlation and the collapsed cross-section.
findings.evidence: From P_down.csv at z=0, b=0: P rises from 19.1 (x = -0.1537) to 865.4 (x = +0.1537), i.e. d log P / d x = log(865.4/19.1)/0.3074 = 12.4. Both x and z enter cash flow symmetrically as exp(x+z) with similar persistence (rho_x = 0.983, rho_z = 0.965), so the extra factor of ~40 is purely the aggregate discount-rate/risk-premium channel.

findings.evidence: From create_panel: mve = book*P_ex with book = k, so bm = book/mve = 1/P_ex EXACTLY (verified np.allclose(bm * P_ex, 1) = True); mkt_lev = book_lev*bm = b/P_ex; size = log k + log P_ex; roe_t = op_cashflow_{t-1}/book_{t-1} = (1-tau)exp(x_{t-1}+z_{t-1}) - delta, which since x is cross-sectionally constant is a strictly monotone transform of z_{t-1}, so rank-standardized roe IS the rank of lagged z. findings.claim: No zero/negative-book singularity exists in GS21 (unlike BGN/KP14): book = k is always strictly positive and P_ex is floored strictly positive, so ER is numerically healthy. The GS21 analogue of that pathology is instead the arbitrary P_ex floor, which only bites in higher-sigma_z calibrations.
findings.evidence: book = k, initialized to 1, multiplied by g=1.14 on investment, and on default reset to alpha*mean(k) = 0.2*mean(k) > 0 -- it can never reach 0. bm = 1/P_ex is bounded in [0.0033, 0.021] over 24,000 firm-months. Numerically at N=200, t=251: ER has min eigenvalue 2.391e-4, ZERO negative eigenvalues, cond(ER) = 8.86e5; cond_var is exactly symmetric with min eigenvalue 2.391e-4 and cond = 1.27e4. Conditioning scales roughly linearly in N, so at the production N=1000 cond(ER) ~ 4e6 -- still ~10 orders of magnitude inside float64. The `assume_a='pos'` Cholesky path in sdf_loop is safe here. The residual risk is panel_functions_gs21.py line 131, `P_ex = np.maximum(0.05/k, P_ex)`: an arbitrary clamp that floors market equity at 0.05. It never binds in the current calibration (min k*P_ex = 30.4), but at the original sigma_z it produces firms with E[R] and Var[R] of order 1e3-1e6, which is the most plausible mechanism behind the 'true SDF weights up to 1e9 in GS21' noted in the MLP README (a near-singular cond_var passed to np.linalg.solve, which raises no error and silently returns garbage -- exactly the KP14 pathology already documented in memory).

findings.claim: Metric artifact in HJD: the method return and sdf_ret are on uncontrolled and different scales, and the HJD-minimizing ridge alpha partly just selects a scale rather than accuracy.
findings.evidence: Over 114 eval months at N=200: sdf_ret has mean 0.0818 and sd 0.3184 (its own Sharpe 0.257, close to mean max_sr 0.294) -- this is the unit-COST HJ portfolio (port normalized so port.sum()==1). Method weights come from regressing y=1 on factor returns with no intercept (fama_functions.mve_data lines 264-269; dkkm ridge_regr), giving pi = E[RR']^{-1}E[R], whose scale is mean = SR^2/(1+SR^2) and sd = SR/(1+SR^2): 0.099 at span SR=0.10, 0.275 at SR=0.30, 0.369 at SR=0.44. So the scales are the same order of magnitude (H5 is not a degenerate failure) but differ by up to ~30% and nothing enforces a match. Critically, driving DKKM's ridge alpha up shrinks pi toward 0, giving HJD -> sqrt(0.0818^2 + 0.3184^2) = 0.329 regardless of economics; create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model(..., 'hjd') selects argmin HJD over the alpha grid, so it can reward shrinkage-to-zero over a correctly-directed but mis-scaled portfolio.

findings.claim: With zero defaults the firm-size distribution is non-stationary: log capital is a pure Bernoulli random walk, so cross-sectional size dispersion grows as sqrt(t) and never reaches a stationary cross-section.
findings.evidence: k[t+1] = (1 + invest*(g-1))*k[t] with P(invest) = 1.21%/month and no reset (defaults = 0). Predicted sd(log k) at T months = sqrt(T*p*(1-p))*log(1.14) = sqrt(920*0.0121*0.9879)*0.1310 = 0.437; measured 0.401/0.440/0.411 across 3 seeds at T=920, and 0.246 at T=320. Total sd(log mve) = 0.285 at T=320. For comparison, real CRSP sd(log market cap) is roughly 2.0 and sd(log book-to-market) roughly 0.8, versus GS21's 0.29 and 0.101. The cross-section is 7-8x too compressed, and what dispersion exists is an artifact of the burn-in length rather than an economic steady state.

findings.claim: Minor code-hygiene issues that are currently harmless: scipy.linalg is used without being imported, and i_cut_* is floored at 0 but never capped at imax.
findings.evidence: sdf_compute_gs21.py line 207 calls scipy.linalg.solve, but the module imports only `from scipy import interpolate`, `import scipy.special`, `from scipy.sparse import ...` and `from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator`. It resolves only because a transitively-imported submodule binds scipy.linalg as an attribute of the scipy package -- fragile across scipy versions. Separately, pos_interp clamps i_cut below at 0 but nothing clamps it above at GS21_IMAX = 2000, so prob_i = (cutoff-imin)/(imax-imin) could exceed 1 and give a negative no-invest weight; measured cutoff maxes at 43.4, so there is a 46x safety margin today.

verdict_on_hypotheses.reasoning: Confirmed as strongly as the data can confirm anything, and this is THE binding constraint for GS21. One aggregate shock, a numerically exact rank-1-plus-diagonal conditional covariance, and 6 characteristics that algebraically recover the full (k,b,z) state. Population span calculation (N=500, 30 months, zero estimation error): the span of 6 linear rank-standardized characteristic portfolios captures 87.1% of the maximum squared Sharpe; the actual Fama-MacBeth portfolios capture 93.2%; RFF with 180 features captures 95.0% and with 360 features 98.8%. In Sharpe units that is FM 0.965 vs DKKM-ceiling 0.975 (RFF180) to 0.994 (RFF360) of the maximum. BLUNT ANSWER TO Q1: the largest DKKM-over-FM out-of-sample Sharpe advantage GS21 can ever produce, even with a perfect estimator, is about +3%, and the realistic figure is +1%. Real-data DKKM-over-FF gaps are 2-5x. GS21 as specified is off by two orders of magnitude in what it can deliver, and no amount of tuning nfeatures, alpha, or the RFF bandwidth changes that -- the model simply does not contain a nonlinear cross-sectional payoff to find. The only genuinely large gap on the table is DKKM over FF (0.994 vs 0.857 of max Sharpe, +16%), but that is FF's tercile-sorting inefficiency, not complexity: FM, a linear method, already closes almost all of it.

The mechanism is exactly right and I verified it to machine precision: w* = D^{-1}(mu - beta*lambda), with corr(w*, alpha/idio_var) = -1.000 (sign = SDF convention) at all three test dates, and 89-97% of the max squared Sharpe coming from that alpha/d leg rather than the market leg. So GS21's true MVE IS the ratio object H2 describes. But the ratio is nearly linear in the characteristics because both numerator and denominator are: R^2 of the true weight on 6 linear chars = 0.79-0.90, rising only to 0.88-0.94 with all 21 quadratic terms; R^2 of diag(Sigma) on linear chars = 0.68-0.84 -> 0.82-0.95 quadratic. And the dispersion in d_i is far too small to make the ratio bite: idio sd ranges only 1.54%-2.67%/month, a 3:1 spread. Cashing out: the entire quadratic nonlinearity is worth 87.1% -> 90.9% of max SR^2, i.e. +2.2% in Sharpe. To make H2 pay you would need idiosyncratic variance to be strongly and NONLINEARLY char-linked with order-of-magnitude dispersion -- GS21 has neither.

The diagnosis of the bandwidth is arithmetically right but the prescription is backwards for GS21. With L=6 rank-standardized chars, sd(W'x) = gamma*sqrt(6/12) which is in [0.354, 0.707] over GAMMA_GRID, so sin() is ~92% linear and cos() ~pure quadratic: the RFF basis is effectively {linear, quadratic}, exactly as H3 says (RFF36 attains 0.879 of max SR^2, essentially the same as the explicit quadratic basis at 0.909). But I tested the proposed fix directly. Multiplying gamma by 2 changes the population span by at most +0.01-0.02 at 90 features; multiplying by sqrt(130/6) = 4.65 makes it WORSE (36 feats: 0.879 -> 0.799 mean; 90 feats: 0.947 -> 0.950, flat); multiplying by 10 is catastrophic (36 feats: 0.879 -> 0.376). The reason is that GS21's truth is nearly linear, so a narrow-bandwidth (near-linear) kernel is close to the right kernel and widening it wastes the feature budget on high-frequency noise. Bandwidth rescaling is not the GS21 fix.

Confirmed, but with the sign of the problem inverted from the usual reading: GS21's characteristics are not too WEAK, they are too STRONG and too few. bm = 1/P_ex exactly (verified), mkt_lev = b/P_ex, size = log k + log P_ex, and rank-standardized roe is exactly the cross-sectional rank of lagged z. Four chars invert the entire 3-dimensional firm state (k, b, z) with zero measurement error, which is why an MLP on chars explains 98.3% of the true SDF weight. Two of the six are near-degenerate: agr takes literally two values and is 0 in 98.8% of firm-months (investment probability 1.21%/month), and book_lev takes ~101 values concentrated on {0, 0.21, 0.26, 0.32}. The virtue-of-complexity theory needs the truth to be dense and high-dimensional in feature space with a low per-signal SNR; GS21 supplies a 3-dimensional, noiselessly observed, near-log-linear truth. Under those conditions a small model is the correct model and ridge on 3600 features has nothing to buy. This is H1's cause, not a separate channel.

Not structurally degenerate, but the metric is contaminated. Measured over 114 eval months at N=200: sdf_ret has sd 0.3184 and mean 0.0818. Method returns are w'xret with w = E[RR']^{-1}E[R] (unnormalized, from regressing y=1 on factors with no intercept), whose sd is SR/(1+SR^2) = 0.099 at span Sharpe 0.10, 0.275 at 0.30, 0.369 at 0.44. Same order of magnitude, so HJD is not a constant across methods and can in principle discriminate -- H5's strong form fails. However two real problems remain: (i) nothing enforces scale agreement between the unit-cost HJ portfolio and the unnormalized regression weights, so a 30% scale error contributes as much to HJD as a substantial direction error; (ii) driving the ridge alpha up shrinks the DKKM weights toward zero, giving HJD -> sqrt(0.0818^2 + 0.3184^2) = 0.329 mechanically, and create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model(..., 'hjd') picks argmin over the alpha grid, so it can select shrinkage-to-nothing over a correctly-directed portfolio. Recommend normalizing both legs to unit cost or unit variance before differencing.

The premise that GS21 has 'far higher cross-sectional predictability than real data' is false, and estimation noise is nevertheless NOT the binding constraint -- so H6 fails in both directions. On predictability: the cross-sectional sd of true conditional expected excess returns is 3.9-5.6 basis points per month against a cross-sectional mean of 35-133 bp; real US data has a cross-sectional sd of expected returns on the order of 50-100 bp. GS21's cross-section is FLATTER than reality by roughly an order of magnitude. On estimation noise: because idiosyncratic vol is only 2.0-2.4%/month (vs ~13% in real data), the per-firm monthly information ratio is 4.33e-4/0.0203 = 0.0213 and the aggregate max Sharpe is a huge 0.44/month at N=500 (~0.62 at N=1000). Estimating 7 factor weights from 360 months at a span Sharpe of 0.42 loses only ~9% of Sharpe (plug-in efficiency SR/sqrt(1 + K/(T*SR^2))). My population span computation removes estimation error entirely and STILL finds FM at 96.5% of the maximum Sharpe and the DKKM ceiling at 99.4%. The gap is a span gap, not a noise gap. Lengthening the sample or the eval window will not create a DKKM advantage.

blockers: ONE PRICED SHOCK, RANK-1 COVARIANCE. GS21 has a single aggregate state x; z is idiosyncratic and the moment code integrates z_i' and z_j' independently, producing a conditional covariance that is numerically exactly rank-1 systematic plus diagonal (top eigenvalue = 97.3% of total variance, remaining spectrum = the idio bulk). With one factor, the true conditional MVE is one factor-mimicking portfolio plus a D^{-1} tilt. There is no multi-factor rotation, no state-dependent factor structure, and therefore no nonlinear object for a rich basis to approximate. This alone caps the DKKM-over-FM Sharpe gain at +3%.

THE PRICE FUNCTION IS LOG-LINEAR IN THE CROSS-SECTION. Cross-sectional log(P_ex) regresses on (z, b) with R^2 = 0.95-0.995 and a leverage elasticity of -1.247 that is constant to three decimals across dates and price levels. Conditional beta is 83-91% linear in the 6 chars and only 91-95% after adding all 21 quadratic terms. GS21's advertised nonlinearity does not exist in the region of the state space the simulation visits.

DEFAULT IS UNREACHABLE, SO THE KINK IS NOT MEASURE-ZERO -- IT IS EMPTY. Zero defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months; minimum realized equity price 30.4 against a default boundary of 0; the solved value function's global minimum over the entire grid including b=1 and z,x at -2.7sd is P_down = 4.73; z_cut_down is pinned at the grid floor everywhere. Maximum market leverage ever observed is 1.04%. There is no default region, no size x value x leverage interaction, and nothing for a nonlinear basis to earn. This is the single most fixable blocker: GS21 must be recalibrated (higher sigma_z, higher tau/lower delta, or a bgrid extended past the equity-value scale) until default is a live event, and the value function re-solved.

IDIOSYNCRATIC RISK WAS CUT 10x AND THE CROSS-SECTION COLLAPSED WITH IT. GS21_SIGMA_Z was reduced from the paper's 0.16-based value to 0.1x that on 2026-06-09. Result: average pairwise return correlation 0.95-0.975 (real data ~0.17), idio/systematic vol ratio 0.17 (real ~2.2), and only 2% of cross-sectional price dispersion coming from own productivity (98% from a quasi-discrete debt variable that itself only moves value by 10%). Restoring sigma_z is the obvious lever, but it re-opens the default region AND the P_ex-floor pathology that produced the 1e9 SDF weights in the original-vol run -- both must be fixed together, not separately.

THE CHARACTERISTICS ARE THE STATE VECTOR, EXACTLY. bm = 1/P_ex identically, mkt_lev = b/P_ex, size = log k + log P_ex, and rank-standardized roe is the exact rank of lagged z. Four chars invert the whole 3-dimensional firm state with zero measurement error, which is why an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight. Virtue-of-complexity requires many weak, partly-independent, noisily-measured signals over a dense high-dimensional truth. Here the truth is 3-dimensional and observed perfectly, so a 6-regressor linear model is the correctly specified model and 3600 ridge features cannot beat it. Adding measurement noise to chars and adding chars that are genuinely non-redundant would be a minimal, defensible fix -- but it will not help while the underlying state stays 3-dimensional.

TWO OF THE SIX CHARACTERISTICS ARE NEARLY DEGENERATE. Investment occurs 1.21% of firm-months, so agr takes literally two values (0 and 0.14) and is 0 in 98.8% of observations; book_lev takes ~101 values concentrated on {0, 0.21, 0.26, 0.32}. After rank-standardization agr is essentially a constant with a 1.2% tail. Effective characteristic dimension for the RFF input is ~4, not 6, which further shrinks the feature space DKKM can exploit.

THE MODEL'S MAXIMUM SHARPE IS ITSELF AN ARTIFACT OF THE COLLAPSED CROSS-SECTION. Max conditional Sharpe is 0.44/month at N=500 (roughly 0.62 at N=1000, i.e. ~2.1 annualized), and 89-97% of the squared Sharpe comes from diversifying 3.5-4.3 basis points of per-firm alpha across N nearly identical firms with 2% idio vol. That is a near-arbitrage that scales as sqrt(N) and has no real-data counterpart. Any Sharpe comparison against this benchmark is measuring how well a method diversifies a synthetic near-arbitrage, not how well it prices risk.

SECONDARY / METRIC-LEVEL: HJD differences an unnormalized regression MVE return (sd 0.10-0.37 depending on attained Sharpe) against a unit-cost HJ portfolio return (sd 0.318). Shrinking DKKM's weights to zero mechanically yields HJD = 0.329, and the reported alpha is chosen by argmin HJD, so the metric can reward shrinkage over accuracy. Normalize both legs to unit cost or unit variance before differencing.

SECONDARY / CODE: loadings_compute_gs21.py lines 29-32 compute P_down_diff from itself rather than from P_down_mat, leaving it identically zero (dormant -- callers are commented out, but it would silently zero 99% of the Taylor loading). panel_functions_gs21.py lines 81-89 redraw the aggregate xt in the all-firms-default branch without writing it back into x[t], and the enclosing while-loop has no iteration cap. panel_functions_gs21.py line 131 floors P_ex at 0.05/k, an arbitrary clamp that is inert now but is the most plausible source of the 1e9 true SDF weights in the original-vol run (near-singular cond_var passed to np.linalg.solve, which raises no error). i_cut_* is clamped below at 0 but never above at imax. scipy.linalg is used at sdf_compute_gs21.py:207 without being imported.
