So the reported number is the true maximum Sharpe times a cosine, and without max_sr in the table nobody can tell whether FF at 0.2423 is 10% or 90% of the ceiling -- which is exactly the difference between 'the estimator is failing' and 'the model has nothing to estimate'. max_sr is ALREADY computed in every sdf_loop and stored by calculate_moments.py, but evaluate_sdfs.py never reads it. (c) THE TIMING CHANNEL IS DELETED. mean_t(w'rp_t/sqrt(w'Sigma_t w)) is homogeneous of degree zero in w each month, so a method that correctly levers up when the conditional max Sharpe is high gets exactly zero credit -- and conditional scaling is one of the two channels through which complexity pays in the DKKM/KMZ theory. (d) THE TEST ASSETS HAVE NO POWER: 25 portfolios sorted on mve and bm only, which are two of the five characteristics every method already spans linearly.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Not applicable -- this proposal changes no economics. It is included because without (b) the diagnosis of every other proposal is unfalsifiable, and because (a) is a genuine defect that will be caught in refereeing regardless.
proposals.exact_change: (a) bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py lines 51-56 (and the parallel block at analyze.py lines 158 and 219): replace `sq_error = (xret - sdf_ret)**2` and its sqrt-of-mean with `rho_unc = (xret*sdf_ret).mean()/sqrt((xret**2).mean()*(sdf_ret**2).mean()); hjd_scaled = sqrt(max(0, 1 - rho_unc**2))`. Keep the old column alongside for one draft. (b) utils/evaluate_sdfs.py line 172, where sdf_ret = m['sdf_ret'] is read: add max_sr = m['max_sr'] and carry it into the all_returns dict at lines 175-179; then in create_slides_tables.py report sharpe/mean(max_sr) as the headline 'Sigma-cosine' column. (c) create_slides_tables.py lines 34-42: alongside the mean-of-ratios, compute the unconditional Sharpe mean_t(mean)/sqrt(mean_t(stdev^2) + var_t(mean)) from the per-month 'mean' and 'stdev' columns already in fama_results/dkkm_results, and also report the MEDIAN of the monthly ratio (the mean is dominated by months where the interpolating solution produces a near-hedged w_t with a tiny denominator). (d) utils/generate_25_portfolios.py lines 112-119: keep the mve x bm 5x5 and ADD two more sets -- 5x5 on (mve, diag(cond_var)) and 10 deciles of the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp), both available directly from the moments pickle. compute_pricing_errors.py then has assets that load on the part of the truth only a rich basis reaches.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: No free parameters. The scale-free form is derived: least squares through the origin gives min_c E[(c y - z)^2] = E[z^2](1 - (E[yz])^2/(E[y^2]E[z^2])), so dividing by E[z^2] yields exactly 1 - rho_unc^2. The immediate diagnostic the team can run today, before any code change: create_slides_tables.py lines 60-68 already report 'SDF Sharpe' = mean(sdf_ret)/sd(sdf_ret), and by the algebra above that quantity EQUALS SR* exactly. If it exceeds about 1.5 per month, the current HJD is structurally incapable of separating methods at the two decimals printed in the tables, and every HJD number in all_results.pdf should be discarded.
proposals.predicted_effect: Reported HJDs will change substantially and non-uniformly: GS21's FF value of 2.3465 collapses to something in [0,1] and stops being an outlier; the c=1 double-descent HJD explosions (BGN 18.52, GS21 23.57 at P=360, alpha=0) become bounded; the alpha selected by argmin-HJD will move away from the heaviest shrinkage. The new Sigma-cosine column will, on the CURRENT results, show FF at roughly 0.81 of the ceiling in BGN (0.2423/0.2985) and DKKM at 0.85 -- which by itself demonstrates that the estimators are near the ceiling and the DGP is the problem, and is the single most persuasive diagnostic in the paper. The unconditional Sharpe will differ from the conditional one by however much timing matters, which is currently unknown and worth knowing. Sharpe levels and max_sr are unchanged by construction.
risks: A referee will ask why the pricing-error metric changed between drafts. Report both columns and justify the new one from the algebra, not from the results.

Note the asymmetry the current metric has in DKKM's FAVOUR that the fix removes: DKKM gets 6 alphas whose optimum is chosen post hoc on the evaluation metric itself, i.e. six chances at the right leverage, while FF/FM have only alpha = 0 and no way to rescale. A scale-free metric neutralizes this, which will make DKKM look slightly WORSE on pricing error -- disclose that this is the correct direction.

compute_pricing_errors.py's alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha statistic on 25 portfolios is already the statistically correct object and arguably should carry the argument instead of any HJD variant; consider demoting HJD to a robustness table.

Minor universe mismatch to fix while in the file: evaluate_sdfs.py lines 170-171 subset rp and cond_var to firm_ids (the prepare_panel survivors) but sdf_ret comes from moments over the book>0 universe, so the HJ benchmark and the method returns are not defined over the same assets.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero cost on sdf_compute. About 20 lines in the analyze repo plus 3 lines in evaluate_sdfs.py plus ~40 lines in generate_25_portfolios.py. No re-run of the simulation is needed for (a), (b) or (c) if the moments pickles are retained -- max_sr is already in them.

proposals.name: P6. Reporting lags with heterogeneous fiscal year-ends, plus HETEROSKEDASTIC (not classical) measurement error in the accounting characteristics
proposals.one_line: Give each firm a fiscal month so accounting chars update once a year and go stale in between, add a 'months since update' observable, and add measurement noise whose VARIANCE depends on firm size -- and do NOT add classical homoskedastic errors-in-variables, because it provably shrinks the DKKM advantage.
proposals.economic_story: Real accounting characteristics are not observed continuously or cleanly. Firms report on staggered fiscal year-ends, the standard convention lags accounting data by 6 months, and reporting quality varies systematically with firm size, age and analyst coverage. In the current panels every characteristic is a noiseless, contemporaneous, invertible function of the latent state -- in GS21 bm = 1/P_ex EXACTLY (verified to machine precision), mkt_lev = b/P_ex, size = log k + log P_ex, and rank-standardized roe is literally the cross-sectional rank of lagged z, so four chars invert the entire 3-dimensional state and an MLP on chars explains 98.3% of the true SDF weight. A correctly specified small model is then the right model by construction.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: The task asks explicitly whether errors-in-variables helps or hurts a nonlinear estimator, and the derivation gives a clean answer with opposite signs for the two cases. CLASSICAL (homoskedastic) EIV HURTS DKKM MORE THAN FM, so it should NOT be added. Proof sketch: if the target is g(x*) and the econometrician sees x = x* + e with e ~ N(0, sigma_e^2 I), the best predictor is the Gaussian convolution E[g(x*)|x] = (g * phi_{sigma_e})(x), whose Fourier transform is ghat(omega) exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2). The LINEAR component (omega -> 0) is attenuated only by the classical factor lambda = tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2), while every nonlinear component is attenuated EXPONENTIALLY in its frequency. Since the RFF basis is exactly a frequency decomposition at frequencies gamma*|w|, the DKKM span advantage decays like exp(-gamma^2 sigma_e^2/2) while FM's decays like lambda. Classical EIV therefore strictly compresses the DKKM-over-FM gap -- realistic, but working against the goal. HETEROSKEDASTIC EIV HELPS. If sigma_e,i^2 = s(z_i) for an observable reliability proxy z_i (firm size, age, months since last report), the optimal predictor becomes lambda_i * g_smoothed(x_i) with lambda_i = tau^2/(tau^2 + s(z_i)) a firm-specific shrinkage factor. The optimal weight therefore contains a MULTIPLICATIVE interaction between the reliability variable and every signal -- a product that is nonlinear in the chars even when g is linear. STALENESS is the same mechanism with a cleaner economic label: if firm i last reported h_i months ago, the accounting char's informativeness decays in h_i, so the efficient weight is lambda(h_i) * bm_i, and because fiscal year-ends are staggered, h_i varies cross-sectionally within every month, which makes this a live cross-sectional interaction rather than a date-level effect.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM applies ONE coefficient per characteristic to every firm in the cross-section, so it cannot apply a firm-specific attenuation lambda_i to a signal; the best it can do is add h_i as a separate additive regressor, which is not the same object -- the truth is lambda(h_i)*bm_i, a product, not lambda*h_i + b*bm_i. FF is the interesting partial exception and must be conceded: FF's 2x3 design contains exactly one interaction, size x char, so if reliability depended on size alone FF would get a two-bin approximation of the attenuation. That is why the reliability proxy should be STALENESS (months since last report), which is orthogonal to size by construction under staggered fiscal year-ends and is NOT one of FF's sort variables -- and why one would have to add a third sort dimension (2 x 3 x 3 = 18 portfolios per characteristic) to give FF a chance, which is exactly the dimensionality blow-up that motivates a flexible estimator. A Fourier basis represents lambda(h)*bm(x) as a smooth bivariate function at no extra cost.
proposals.exact_change: MEASUREMENT ONLY -- nothing in any sdf_compute and no re-solve. NEW helper in utils_factors/char_library.py (the same file as P3): (1) assign each firm a fixed fiscal month fm_i ~ Uniform{0..11} at generation; (2) after each model's create_panel, for every ACCOUNTING characteristic (book, op_cash_flow, and everything derived from them -- bm, roe, agr, book_lev), replace the contemporaneous value with the value from the firm's most recent fiscal month, lagged an additional 6 months (utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py lines 240-260 is where these are built; the KP14 and GS21 equivalents are the corresponding blocks in their create_panel); market-based chars (mve, size, mom) stay contemporaneous, which is the standard convention and creates a real timing wedge between the two families; (3) add the observable char stale_i,t = months since the firm's last fiscal update, in 0..11; (4) add multiplicative noise to the accounting chars only: bm_obs = bm * exp(sigma_e,i * u), u ~ iid N(0,1), with sigma_e,i = sigma_e0 * (mve_i/median)^{-xi}. Wire the new columns into config.py CHARS lists and CHAR_TO_FACTOR.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: STALENESS: 12-month fiscal cycle plus the conventional 6-month reporting lag means the accounting information age h_i,t runs 6 to 17 months with a uniform cross-sectional distribution -- no free parameter, this is the Fama-French convention. Its bite is set by how fast the underlying state moves: in BGN book = I*num changes only when a project is created or dies, so a 12-month stale bm is nearly as good as a fresh one and the effect will be small; in GS21 z has monthly persistence rho_z = 0.9655, so a 12-month lag attenuates the roe signal by rho_z^12 = 0.657 and the cross-sectional variation in h (6 to 17 months) generates attenuation factors from rho^6 = 0.810 to rho^17 = 0.552, a 1.47x spread -- enough for the interaction to matter. HETEROSKEDASTIC NOISE: calibrate the reliability spread to the accounting-quality literature via the ratio of signal-to-total variance, targeting lambda = 0.90 at the 90th size percentile and lambda = 0.50 at the 10th. lambda = tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2) gives sigma_e/tau = sqrt((1-lambda)/lambda) = 0.333 at the top and 1.000 at the bottom, i.e. a 3.0x spread in noise sd across the size distribution. With sd(log mve) = S in a given model, xi = log(3.0)/(2.563*S) and sigma_e0 = the geometric mean 0.577*tau. In BGN with S ~ 0.6, xi = 1.099/1.538 = 0.71. DO NOT add a homoskedastic component: by the Fourier argument above, a common sigma_e attenuates the DKKM-reachable nonlinear content by exp(-gamma^2 sigma_e^2/2), which at the P2-rescaled gamma of 5.1 and sigma_e/tau = 0.58 in rank units (tau^2 = 1/12) is exp(-5.1^2*0.58^2/12/2) = exp(-0.36) = 0.70 -- a 30% haircut on exactly the components the proposal exists to create. State this trade-off explicitly in the paper; it is a genuine and interesting theoretical point in its own right.
proposals.predicted_effect: Small on its own -- expect the DKKM/FM Sharpe ratio to move by perhaps 5-15%, and possibly DOWN in BGN where the accounting state is nearly static so staleness costs information without creating a usable interaction. Its main value is as an inexpensive realism layer that (i) breaks the GS21 identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly, which is currently the single most indefensible feature of that panel, (ii) supplies a reliability variable that turns every other characteristic's coefficient into a firm-specific function, multiplying the effect of P1 and P3, and (iii) lets the paper make a real theoretical contribution about when errors-in-variables helps versus hurts high-dimensional estimators. max_sr is unchanged (this is measurement, not DGP), and FF/FM Sharpes fall slightly from the attenuation, so the gap widens partly by lowering the benchmark -- which must be disclosed.
risks: The gap can widen partly because FF/FM get WORSE rather than because DKKM gets better. Report the population span ceiling (SR_rff/SR_lin computed on the true moments with the observed chars) so the two are distinguishable.

In BGN the accounting state (book = I*num, a small integer averaging 5.95) barely moves month to month, so staleness may be nearly free and the whole mechanism inert there. Check sd(bm_stale - bm_fresh)/sd(bm) before committing.

Adding multiplicative noise to bm and roe worsens the existing tie/degeneracy problems (agr is 91% zeros in BGN and 98.8% zeros in GS21) in one direction -- it breaks the ties, which is good -- but it also makes the FF tercile sorts on those chars pure noise sorts, which will look like sabotage of FF unless the tie problem is fixed properly at fama_functions.py lines 86-88 in the same commit.

The heteroskedastic-noise story requires the reliability proxy to be observable. Using months-since-report is clean; using size is not, because FF's 2x3 design already contains size interactions and the referee will say FF was given a fair chance and used it.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero on sdf_compute -- the true conditional moments are computed from the model's latent states and are entirely unaffected by what the econometrician is shown. No re-solve of kp14_fd.py and no new GS21 solfiles. About 60 lines in char_library.py plus config edits. One caveat: the fiscal-month assignment must be generated with the panel (it needs a per-firm draw stored alongside firmid), so panels must be regenerated -- but the expensive step, calculate_moments, does NOT need to be re-run if the underlying model parameters are unchanged.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1. Limits-to-arbitrage price wedge (moderate_restructuring)
verdicts.critique:
The economics are the right economics — this is the only proposal that attacks the binding constraint (no unspanned premium) — but the proposal as written is calibrated to the answer, and says so in plain text. Two sentences in the parameter derivation are fatal on their own: 'kappa_med, pinned by the TARGET maximum Sharpe rather than by the misvaluation literature,' and 'run s_k in {0.8, 1.3, 1.9} and report SR* for each; pick the largest s_k for which SR* stays below ~2.5 annualized.' The target itself is reverse-engineered from DKKM's published 2.6-3.4x, i.e. the paper picks the free parameter so that the model reproduces the number the paper claims to explain. A JF referee does not need to be clever to find this; it is in the calibration section. The proposal even flags that 3.3% is conservative relative to Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan's sd~0.40 — which concedes the parameter is not disciplined by the misvaluation literature in either direction, only by the reported Sharpe.

Second problem, deeper: DKKM's AIPT is *defined* as the environment in which expected returns contain a component not spanned by the dominant covariance loadings, and DKKM *prove* complexity is harmful under APT. P1 assumes AIPT. The resulting paper's claim reduces to 'when we assume DKKM's sufficient condition, DKKM's result obtains.' That is a numerical illustration, not a finding. The paper's title claim — that VoC arises in *simple structural models* — becomes false as stated: it arises in simple structural models plus an exogenous non-risk pricing wedge, which is precisely what a structural model is supposed to not need.

Third, internal consistency: the wedge moves the observed price but the firm's investment problem is untouched ('a pricing/holding-cost layer, not a change to the firm's problem'). In BGN and GS21 the investment cutoff is a function of the price/value; in KP14 project arrival is not price-responsive but equity value is the object being mispriced. A referee at JF reads a persistent 3-40% equity misvaluation to which no manager and no firm responds — no market timing, no SEO, no investment distortion — and asks why the segmented-investor story stops exactly at the boundary where responding would be costly to the authors. The two-agent framing is available but is not yet written, and it needs the manager's objective to be fundamental value with a stated reason.

Fourth, the N-scaling. SR_alpha ~ sqrt(N) * (1-rho) * sqrt(E[kappa^2/d]) by the proposal's own derivation. The headline SR* = 0.64/month is an artifact of N=1000. At N=250 it is 0.32; at N=4000 it is 1.28. The reported DKKM/FF ratio will move with N, and the referee will demand the N-robustness table.

Fifth, the two nonlinearity mechanisms are in tension and the proposal admits it: the hump in kappa needs s_k~1.9, but E[kappa^2/d] is right-tail dominated so s_k=1.9 blows up SR*. So the paper can have either the non-monotonicity (the thing FF's monotone terciles provably cannot represent) or a defensible Sharpe, not both. That trade-off is currently resolved by picking whichever s_k gives a printable number.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly — and less than claimed, for a reason the proposal itself creates. The proposal makes the wedge discoverable *through the characteristics*: 'log bm^obs = log bm_fund + q, size^obs = size_fund - q, and mom picks up the q innovations.' So the alpha is alpha_i = (1-rho)*kappa_i*v_it, and v_it is essentially readable off the contaminated bm. FM re-fits monthly on bm (and on size and mom) and therefore captures the *entire* linear-in-bm component of the alpha every month. The span2.py cell that governs this case is 'linear alpha, homogeneous d,' where the measured RFF/linear ceiling ratio is 1.00 — FM loses nothing. The gap depends entirely on (i) the dispersion of kappa across firms, which converts a linear signal into kappa(x)*v(x), and (ii) the 1/(d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2) denominator, which requires P4's idio-variance dispersion to bite. At the recommended s_k=0.8-1.0 the kappa modulation is a ~3-13x p10-p90 spread in a *smooth monotone* function of size and idio-vol — and FF's 2x3 size-by-char sorts contain exactly the size interaction, at coarse resolution. So FF gets a two-bin approximation of the dominant modulation for free. My honest read: at s_k=1.0 with homogeneous d, the gap is closer to span2.py's 1.5-1.9 cell than its 6.4 cell, and the realized (estimation-noise) gap will be smaller still. The 3-5x target is reachable only in the s_k~1.9 + strong-heteroskedastic-d corner, which is exactly the corner where SR* becomes indefensible. There is also a real possibility the gap comes out *negative* for FF specifically: FF's value-weighted sorts weight by mve, and the wedge contaminates mve, so FF's weights become mechanically anti-correlated with the wedge — a KP14-style sign artifact rather than a complexity result.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge; discipline it entirely on moments that are NOT the reported Sharpe or the reported DKKM/FF ratio, and report those two as outputs. Specifically: (i) pin (1-rho) from the anomaly-decay half-life literature (already done, keep); (ii) pin kappa_med by matching the *cross-sectional predictive R^2 of monthly returns on characteristics* to ~0.5%/month, the real-data number the diagnosis already established BGN misses by 10x (0.043%) — this is an external moment, it is the standard target in the return-predictability literature, and it has nothing to do with the Sharpe; (iii) pin s_k by matching the *ratio of the estimated SDF Sharpe in mega/large caps to all caps* to DKKM's measured 1.6/3.7 = 0.43, again an external moment about the size-concentration of the effect rather than its level; (iv) pin phi and psi by matching realized p10-p90 dispersion in an observable arbitrage-cost proxy (Amihud illiquidity or idiosyncratic-vol decile spread) rather than by the self-calibrating rule. Then SR*, the DKKM/FF ratio and the shape of the complexity curve are all predictions, and the paper can state them before running. Additionally: (a) write the two-agent economy explicitly, with the manager maximizing fundamental value under a stated segmentation, so the no-response-to-mispricing is an assumption with a name rather than an omission; (b) report the full N in {250, 500, 1000, 2000} table for SR* and the ratio; (c) report the s_k in {0.8, 1.3, 1.9} table in full, in the paper, including the cells where SR* is uncomfortable, rather than selecting one; (d) add the placebo — the identical pipeline on the identical model with kappa_i set to a constant (no cross-sectional arbitrage-cost variation), which should show DKKM/FF ~ 1.0 and is the control that proves the result is the nonlinearity and not the wedge's mere existence.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair: bandwidth, second rank-standardization, NMAT, alpha grid, c = P/T (reparametrization_only)
verdicts.critique:
Split this into two things that have opposite referee valence, because as bundled it is the single most dangerous item in the packet.

MANDATORY AND UNCONTROVERSIAL — items (c), (d), (f), and the diagnosis behind (b). NMAT=5 -> 1 restores the root convention (config.py:177 comment says nmat=1); the alpha reparameterization to a scale-free fraction of trace(X'X)/P removes the existing GS21 hand-tuned /100 at config.py:193, which is itself an undisclosed per-model tuning that a referee would flag; and item (f) is not a nicety, it is the difference between an acceptable and a rejectable paper. I verified it: create_slides_tables.py:82-97 selects DKKM's alpha by argmax of the reported Sharpe (or argmin HJD) across iterations, and :135-136 then reports that alpha's values, while FF/FM run at ALPHA_LST_FAMA=[0] (config.py:187) through fama_functions.mve_data:270 with no grid at all. DKKM gets six shots at the evaluation metric; FF/FM get one and cannot rescale. Separately, dkkm_functions.rff:92-96 gives BGN's DKKM the interest rate that FF/FM never see. As the pipeline stands today, *any* reported DKKM advantage in BGN is confounded by an information asymmetry and an oracle-selection asymmetry. This must be fixed before any of the other proposals is evaluated, and the fixed version must be the headline specification, not a robustness appendix.

DANGEROUS — item (a), the sqrt(130/L) bandwidth rescale. The justification is 'match DKKM's real-data kernel exponent,' but the paper is not replicating DKKM's real-data implementation; it is asking whether a structural model generates the phenomenon. Rescaling the estimator's bandwidth to a value imported from the setting whose result you are trying to reproduce is exactly the move a referee reads as tuning. It is worse than that here, because the proposal *concedes in its own risk section* that the GS21 agent measured the rescale to HURT (36 features: 0.879 -> 0.799 at x4.65; 0.879 -> 0.376 at x10) and then says 'do not apply it before P1/P3' — i.e., the hyperparameter is to be chosen conditional on which DGP is in force. That is a forking path with a written-down decision rule for taking it. Do not do this. P2's own text supplies the escape: at L=35 (P3), sd(Wx) = 1.708*gamma with the ORIGINAL grid, which delivers genuine nonlinearity with zero hyperparameters touched. Take that route and drop (a).

ITEM (b) needs care. Replacing the second rank-standardization with per-column z-scoring is defensible on the stated grounds (it restores gamma-dependence while keeping the 3.1x sin/cos amplitude equalization that plain deletion would destroy), but note that the file header at dkkm_functions.py:1-17 says this is 'a near-exact copy of the root codebase' and the proposal admits it could not verify whether DKKM's published code rank-standardizes the features. Changing an estimator step away from the reference implementation, in the direction that enriches your favored estimator, without being able to say what the reference implementation does, is a disclosure liability. Either obtain DKKM's code and match it, or report both variants.

ITEM (e), P=36000: fine, and the c-range extension is a genuine improvement, but note it multiplies the number of DKKM cells to ~55 per model against FF/FM's 1, which makes item (f) even more urgent.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal says so: 'on the CURRENT three models the impact of this bundle is approximately zero.' That honesty is correct and is the reason this cannot be a source of result. But there is a sharper adversarial point the proposal misses. Because P2 is pure plumbing, *any* portion of a post-P1 gap attributable to P2 is attributable to nothing economic at all — and P2's bandwidth item in particular can manufacture a gap on its own once the DGP has *any* high-frequency content, whether or not that content is economically meaningful. A referee will ask for the 2x2 the proposal itself suggests ({old, rescaled} gamma x {old, new} DGP) and will read a large gamma main-effect as evidence that the result is a kernel-bandwidth choice. My prior: with P1's wedge in place, the gamma rescale contributes a substantial fraction of the measured DKKM/FM ratio, because the wedge's kappa modulation is smooth and the extra reachable dimensions will mostly be fitting the alpha's spikiness rather than any structural nonlinearity. That is the outcome that kills the paper, and P2(a) is what causes it.
verdicts.salvage: Ship items (c), (d), (f) and the z-scoring in (b) as a separate, clearly-labelled 'estimator correctness' commit *before* any DGP change, and report the before/after on the current models — where the visible effects are pure bug fixes (the c=1 double-descent HJD explosions of 18.52 in BGN and 23.57 in GS21 at P=360, alpha=0 disappear; the alpha=0 column stops realizing 1.4-13% of max Sharpe). That commit establishes that the estimator was fixed with no result attached, which is exactly the provenance a referee wants. Drop item (a) entirely and let P3's L=35 deliver the bandwidth as a by-product. On item (f), go further than the proposal: the right answer is not to give FF/FM the same post-hoc selection, it is to give NEITHER method post-hoc selection. Choose alpha and nfeatures by nested cross-validation *within the 360-month training window only*, for every method, and report the resulting single number per method. Post-hoc selection on the evaluation metric with 6-11 alphas x 4-5 nfeatures is a garden of forking paths that no amount of symmetry repairs. Finally, add the information-audit table to the paper: one row per method, columns for characteristics seen, macro conditioning seen, regularization grid, and number of tuning decisions. If the rf_stand column is kept for DKKM it must be given to FF/FM as a char-by-macro interaction; the audit table makes hiding it impossible.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
This proposal is more honest about its own weakness than any other in the packet, and the honesty is disqualifying: 'P3 is an enabling and realism change, not by itself a source of a 3-5x gap,' and 'this alone would produce a spurious-looking DKKM/FM ratio of maybe 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency, not span, and should be labelled as such.' A referee reading that will ask why the paper contains a change whose only standalone effect is to handicap the benchmark.

The handicap is real and quantified by the proposal: FM at K=37, T=360 loses ~20.6% of squared Sharpe, ~11% of Sharpe. FF is worse — 35 collinear tercile-sorted long-shorts with an unregularized OLS tangency at T=360. So the DGP is unchanged, the truth is unchanged, and the benchmark's score falls by construction. That is the textbook shape of a rigged comparison.

The technical objection that will actually kill this item: 35 characteristics built from 4-5 quantities in a 2-3 dimensional latent state are not 35 characteristics, they are 35 measurements of three numbers. The EffRank(L) ladder cited (L=5 -> 16.5, L=35 -> ~250) was measured on the RFF map; I could not find evidence it was measured with *collinear* inputs of the kind P3 actually builds. Multi-horizon momentum at (1,2-6,7-12,13-36,37-60), four horizons of log book change, five roe transforms, and 6/12-month lags of size and bm are, in a model whose state is (num_i, sum_j exp(-beta_j)) for BGN or (k,b,z) for GS21, near-degenerate. The characteristic matrix itself will have effective rank ~4-6. The RFF EffRank is driven by the geometry of the *realized* input cloud, not by the nominal column count, so the true post-P3 EffRank is very likely far below 250 — possibly barely above the current 16.5. The whole dimensional argument for P3 may simply not survive measurement.

Separately, the proposal's own risk list flags that several new chars will be degenerate the way agr already is (91% ties in BGN, 98.8% in GS21), and that rank_standardize's argsort tie-breaking (dkkm_functions.py:57-62, verified) converts a tied column into a persistent pseudo-random characteristic that enters all 3600 features multiplicatively. Building 35 chars on top of a state that changes only when a discrete project arrives or dies will produce many such columns. The 20%-tie screen proposed is a good idea but will delete a large fraction of the 35.

One item in P3 is genuinely valuable and should be extracted: the fairness repairs. Deleting rf_stand from the BGN RFF, and turning on the FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156 (which I verified is commented out, so FM currently regresses log-size of order 5 against bm of order 1 through pinvh with default rcond) are both required regardless of whether L changes.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The dimension-counting channel almost certainly fails, for the collinearity reason above. The estimation-efficiency channel will produce a gap of the size the proposal predicts (1.2-1.3x), and that gap is not a complexity result — it is the observation that unregularized OLS on 37 collinear factors is a bad estimator, which nobody disputes and which the proposal's own mitigation (ridge-regularized FM at the same z-grid) will erase. So the honest expected outcome is: ridged FM on 35 chars matches or beats DKKM, and the paper is left with nothing from this proposal. There is also a scenario where it produces a gap in the *wrong* direction for the paper's story: FF with 35 tercile sorts, several of them on tie-degenerate columns, may collapse badly enough that the DKKM/FF ratio looks large purely because FF became a broken estimator — which a referee will correctly call sabotage of the benchmark rather than a virtue of complexity.
verdicts.salvage: Three things survive and should be pulled out. (1) The fairness repairs — delete rf_stand from dkkm_functions.rff:95-96, enable the FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156, and fix the tie-aware tercile split at fama_functions.fama_french:86-88 (currently q30=q70=0 for agr gives a 92/0/8 split with an empty medium bucket). These are bug fixes and belong in the P2 correctness commit. (2) A *measured* rather than extrapolated dimension argument: before committing to L=35, build the 35 chars on an actual simulated panel and report EffRank of the resulting RFF map and the effective rank of the char matrix itself. If EffRank does not clear ~150 the proposal is dead and you have learned that cheaply. (3) If you keep the expansion, the headline benchmark must be ridge-regularized FM on the same 35 chars with the same nested-CV-selected penalty, reported in the main table, not in an appendix — and the paper must report the population span ceiling (mean_t SR_rff/SR_lin on the true rp and cond_var, both computable from the moments pickles) alongside the realized Sharpes, so that the span channel and the estimation-efficiency channel are separated in the same table. Absent that separation, a referee cannot distinguish this from benchmark sabotage and will assume the worst.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block in all three models (reparametrization_only)
verdicts.critique:
This is the most defensible proposal in the packet and the one a referee is least able to attack, for a structural reason the other proposals lack: every parameter moves toward an externally observable moment (average pairwise monthly correlation 0.15-0.20, idiosyncratic vol ~10%/month, sd(log idio variance) ~1.0-1.3), and two of the three edits literally undo commits the authors themselves made. BGN's line is self-incriminating in the source — utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py:54 carries the comment '# added a factor of 0.1' — and the current calibration forces mean corr_zj = 0.958, i.e. firm cash flows are 96% systematic, which is indefensible against any real-data moment. GS21's average pairwise conditional correlation of 0.95 against a real-data 0.15-0.20 is not a calibration choice, it is a broken calibration. A referee will read these as corrections, not as tuning, provided they are disclosed as corrections with the commit history shown.

The honest weakness is that the proposal concedes it does nothing on its own: max_sr falls in all three models, all Sharpes fall roughly proportionally, and the ratio moves a few percent. So it is a multiplier, not a source. That is fine for a referee — a change that makes the model more realistic and does *not* by itself produce the result is precisely the kind of change that establishes good faith.

The real risks are execution risks and they are severe. GS21 needs a MATLAB re-solve: the solfiles' zgrid spans exactly +/-2.7247 stationary sd of the 0.1x sigma_z, so at 0.5x it covers +/-0.54 sd and every interpolation extrapolates. Worse, raising sigma_z makes default a live event for the first time (currently 0 defaults in 2.16M firm-months, z_cut_down pinned at the grid floor everywhere) — which is *desirable*, it is the only genuine nonlinearity GS21 has, but it changes the equilibrium and requires re-examining bgrid. And the arbitrary floor at utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py:131, which I verified reads P_ex = np.maximum(0.05/k, P_ex), is inert today but is the most plausible source of the 1e9 SDF weights recorded in the original-vol run; it must go in the same commit with an eigenvalue guard on cond_var.

KP14 cannot be recalibrated at all yet. I verified both blockers: utils_kp14/integ_kp14.py:43 calls quad on [0, eps_max] with epsabs=epsrel=1e-10 against a CIR transition density whose sd is ~0.006, and utils_kp14/kp14_fd.py:7 does 'from parameters_kp14 import *' with no such module anywhere in utils_kp14/. So the solution files cannot be regenerated from this repository and the shipped ones are stale by ~49x. Every KP14 number currently in all_results.pdf is a quadrature artifact.

One choice needs justifying in the text: GS21 at 0.5x rather than the paper's 1.0x. The stated reason (1.0x overshoots the ~10%/month idio-vol target to ~21%) is a moment-matching reason and is acceptable, but it must be written as such, with the implied moment reported, or it reads as splitting the difference to avoid a re-solve.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, standalone, and the proposal correctly says so. The adversarial question is whether it is even a useful multiplier. The span2.py evidence cited (RFF/linear ceiling 1.00 -> 1.91 when heteroskedastic d is added to a linear alpha) is the load-bearing claim, and it is fragile in one specific way: it requires d to be dispersed *and* char-linked in a way that is not a monotone function of a single characteristic. The proposal concedes this — 'if d is a MONOTONE function of a single characteristic, FF's tercile sorts on that characteristic get a crude approximation of the tilt.' In BGN, d is proportional to bm/mve; in KP14 post-fix, d is driven by the CIR shocks but the project-count channel remains; in GS21 the dispersion is small. So in at least two of three models the restored d dispersion will be close to a monotone function of size and/or bm, and FF's existing 2x3 size-by-value sorts capture much of it. The proposal's answer — ride on P1's wedge so that d = d_fund + kappa^2 sigma_v^2 is a sum of two power laws in two chars — is correct but makes P4's value entirely contingent on P1 surviving. Note also the direction risk: KP14's negative Sharpes are currently caused by idio var ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/size making w* proportional to +size; restoring SIGMA_EPS/SIGMA_U breaks that identity and should flip KP14's sign, which is good, but it is a large uncontrolled change to a model whose truth is currently corrupt, so nobody can predict the outcome.
verdicts.salvage: Endorsed essentially as written, with four required additions. (1) Make the KP14 repair a hard gate: fix integ_kp14.py:43 (fixed grid over [mean-8sd, mean+8sd] of the noncentral chi-square, or scipy.stats.ncx2 moments directly), restore parameters_kp14.py, re-solve G_func.csv under current config, and *validate* by checking that the recomputed rp reproduces the closed-form rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*share_i to within a stated tolerance. Until that passes, KP14 must be dropped from the paper entirely rather than reported with a caveat — a referee who discovers a reported column is a quadrature artifact rejects the whole paper, not the column. (2) Report the target-moment table in the paper: for each model, before and after, the average pairwise conditional correlation, idio vol, sd(log idio variance), and the p10-p90 idio-vol ratio, against the real-data values. That table is what converts this from tuning into calibration, and it is cheap. (3) Do the GS21 re-solve properly — extend zgrid and bgrid, report the realized default frequency (which should become nonzero for the first time) and the realized market leverage distribution, and remove the P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 with an explicit eigenvalue guard on cond_var replacing it. (4) Report this as its own row in the results decomposition, so a reader can see that P4 alone moves the ratio by ~0 and moves max_sr toward realism. That row is the paper's strongest defense against 'you changed the model until you got the answer.'

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair: scale-free pricing error, report Sharpe/max_sr, unconditional Sharpe, test assets with power (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
Items (a), (b) and (c) are correct and required. Item (b) in particular is the highest-value line of code in the entire packet: max_sr is already computed (verified at utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py:326-328) and stored by calculate_moments, but utils/evaluate_sdfs.py:174-179 carries only sdf_ret and mkt_rf into all_returns, so it never reaches a table. Without it, no reader can tell whether FF at 0.2423 is 10% or 90% of the ceiling — which is the entire difference between 'the estimator is failing' and 'the model has nothing to estimate.' Given the identity SR_t(w) = SR*_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*_t), reporting Sharpe/max_sr turns every table cell into an interpretable cosine. Three lines.

Item (a) is a genuine repair and the derivation is right: min_c E[(cy-z)^2]/E[z^2] = 1 - rho_unc^2. The current HJD is not a Hansen-Jagannathan distance, it is an RMSE between an unnormalized regression return and a unit-cost portfolio return, and I verified the argmin-HJD selection at create_slides_tables.py:82-97 can and does reward shrinkage toward zero (the HJD floor equals sqrt(E[sdf_ret^2]), which is 0.2860 in BGN). The proposal deserves credit for stating that the fix will make DKKM look *worse* — that disclosure is what makes the metric change defensible when the referee asks why it moved between drafts.

Item (d) is where this goes wrong, and it goes wrong badly. Adding test assets sorted on 'the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp)' is not a pricing test. It is sorting the test assets on the answer. The alpha of a method's MVE return against portfolios sorted on w* is, up to a monotone transform, a restatement of the Sigma-cosine that the Sharpe column already reports — and a referee will say so in one sentence. It also has the perverse property that any method whose weights happen to be *anti*-correlated with w* (KP14, where all three methods are negatively correlated with the truth) will produce a spectacular-looking alpha on assets that were constructed from w*. Delete this. The 5x5 sort on (mve, diag(cond_var)) is fine and is a real improvement, because idiosyncratic volatility is an observable-in-principle sort variable that the linear char span does not price by construction.

Item (c)'s unconditional Sharpe is correct and important — the current mean-of-ratios is homogeneous of degree zero in w each month, so the conditional-timing channel, one of the two channels through which complexity pays in DKKM/KMZ, is deleted by construction. Adding it is not optional if the paper wants to claim it tested the DKKM mechanism.

One omission: the proposal's own risk list mentions the universe mismatch at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 (rp and cond_var subset to firm_ids, sdf_ret computed over the book>0 universe) but files it as 'minor.' In BGN and KP14, where zero-book firms are ~5% of the cross-section and carry eret = -1.0 exactly, this is not minor; it means the HJ benchmark and the method returns are defined over different assets in every month. Promote it.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It cannot and must not, and that is the point — but there is one adversarial angle worth stating. Because item (a) removes DKKM's existing leverage advantage (six alphas selected post hoc on a scale-sensitive metric = six chances at the right scale), the *measured* DKKM/FF pricing-error gap will shrink when this lands. If the authors ship P1 and P5 in the same commit, the referee cannot tell how much of the post-change gap is the wedge and how much is the metric. Ship P5 first, alone, on the current models, and publish the revised current-model table. The revised table will show FF at ~0.81 of the ceiling in BGN and DKKM at ~0.85, which is itself the paper's most persuasive single diagnostic: it demonstrates that the estimators are near the ceiling and the DGP is the problem, before any DGP is touched.
verdicts.salvage: Endorse (a), (b), (c) and the (mve, idio-var) sort in (d); delete the w*-decile test assets. Add three things the proposal misses. (1) Paired standard errors: every number in all_results.pdf is a mean over simulation iterations with no dispersion reported, and the current DKKM-over-FF differences are 2.5-15%. Report the paired across-seed standard error of the DKKM minus FF difference in every table. If the current 'DKKM ties FF/FM' null is within one standard error, that is worth knowing before anyone changes a model. (2) Report the shape of the complexity curve (Sharpe vs nfeatures at fixed, CV-selected penalty) as a primary exhibit rather than the level. A monotonically rising curve over c from 0.017 to 100 is DKKM's actual identifying prediction and is far harder to produce by tuning than a level difference; a flat curve with a level gap is exactly what a plumbing artifact looks like. (3) Promote the universe mismatch at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 to a fix, and state in the paper which universe each metric is computed over.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with heterogeneous fiscal year-ends + heteroskedastic measurement error (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
The Fourier argument is correct and genuinely interesting — classical homoskedastic errors-in-variables attenuates a nonlinear component by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) while attenuating the linear component only by tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2), so it compresses the DKKM-over-FM gap; heteroskedastic error with an observable reliability proxy generates lambda_i * g(x_i), a firm-specific attenuation that FM's single coefficient per characteristic cannot express. As a theoretical point it is publishable on its own.

As a proposal for this paper it is the item most likely to end the referee report in one line, because the proposal states its own selection rule in the headline: 'do NOT add classical homoskedastic errors-in-variables, because it provably shrinks the DKKM advantage.' The authors have written down, in the design document, that they will include the form of measurement error that helps their result and exclude the form that hurts it. Real accounting data has both. There is no reading of that decision that survives refereeing.

The second selection is worse because it is subtler and the proposal is equally explicit about it: staleness is chosen as the reliability proxy 'because it is orthogonal to size by construction under staggered fiscal year-ends and is NOT one of FF's sort variables — and why one would have to add a third sort dimension (2 x 3 x 3 = 18 portfolios per characteristic) to give FF a chance.' That is choosing the interacting variable specifically so that the benchmark's functional form cannot reach it. It is designing the DGP around the competitor's estimator. A referee who reads that sentence stops reading.

Third, the proposal concedes the mechanism may be inert where it is most needed: in BGN, book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95 that changes only on project birth or death, so a 12-month-stale bm is nearly as informative as a fresh one. So the one model where the diagnosis found the *largest* structural blocker gets the *smallest* benefit from this fix.

Fourth, the direction of the gap. The proposal admits 'FF/FM Sharpes fall slightly from the attenuation, so the gap widens partly by lowering the benchmark — which must be disclosed.' Combined with the sabotage-shaped selection of the proxy, this is a change whose primary measured effect is to degrade the benchmark.

Fifth, an interaction the proposal misses: adding multiplicative noise to bm and roe breaks the existing tie masses (91% zeros in BGN's agr, 98.8% in GS21's), which the proposal counts as a benefit — but it turns the FF tercile sorts on those characteristics into sorts on pure noise. Combined with the unfixed degenerate split at fama_functions.fama_french:86-88 (verified: q30 = q70 = 0 for agr, giving a 92/0/8 split with an empty medium bucket), the net effect on FF is unpredictable and probably negative for reasons that have nothing to do with complexity.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The proposal's own estimate is 5-15% on the DKKM/FM ratio, 'and possibly DOWN in BGN.' That is small relative to the 3-5x target and small relative to the plumbing effects in P2 and P3, so even taking the estimate at face value this cannot carry a result. And the estimate is optimistic in one respect the proposal does not flag: the staleness interaction lambda(h_i)*bm_i is a *bivariate smooth function of two observed variables*, and FM can approximate it well by simply adding the interaction column h_i * bm_i to its regressor set — which costs FM one parameter, not a dimensionality blow-up. The proposal's claim that 'the best FM can do is add h_i as a separate additive regressor' is wrong: FM's design matrix is whatever the econometrician chooses to put in it, and a competent implementation of the linear benchmark facing a known reporting-lag structure would include the interaction. The claimed asymmetry exists only if the paper withholds the interaction column from FM, which is a fifth selection on top of the four already named.
verdicts.salvage: There is a real paper in the Fourier attenuation result, but it is not this paper's mechanism, and it must be presented symmetrically. If any of P6 is kept: (i) include BOTH homoskedastic and heteroskedastic measurement error, calibrated jointly to the accounting-quality literature, and report the decomposition — showing that classical EIV shrinks the gap and heteroskedastic EIV widens it is a *more* interesting result than showing only the second, and it inoculates against the selection charge completely; (ii) give FM the h_i * char interaction columns and FF the third sort dimension, and show DKKM still wins — if it does not, the mechanism was never about complexity; (iii) drop the reporting-lag layer for BGN specifically after running the proposal's own pre-check, sd(bm_stale - bm_fresh)/sd(bm), and report that number rather than assuming; (iv) fix the tie-aware tercile split at fama_functions.py:86-88 in the *same* commit, before adding any noise that interacts with it. What survives unconditionally and should be kept regardless of the rest: staggered fiscal year-ends with the conventional 6-month lag is the standard Fama-French convention, has no free parameters, and breaks the GS21 identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly — which is currently the single most indefensible feature of that panel and would be flagged by any referee who reads the code. Keep that piece and label it a realism correction, not a mechanism.

missed_ideas: THE NEGATIVE-RESULT PAPER, WHICH NOBODY PROPOSED AND WHICH IS THE MOST LIKELY TO BE ACCEPTED. Every proposal assumes the goal is to manufacture a DKKM advantage. But the diagnosis already contains a clean, general, publishable theorem: under exact K-factor pricing (mu = B lambda, Sigma = B Omega B' + D) with K small and N large, the maximum conditional Sharpe is attained to within O(1/N) by ANY well-diversified portfolio with the right factor exposure — measured at SR* = 0.0999 vs equal-weight 0.0998 vs linear-char span 0.0999 vs RFF 0.0994 at N=1000, with the shortfall 1/(2 sigma_f^2 beta'D^{-1}beta) = 1.81% at N=100, 0.186% at N=1000, 0.019% at N=10000. Therefore no frictionless rational-expectations production economy with a low-dimensional priced-risk space can generate the virtue of complexity, for any estimator, any bandwidth, any feature count. That is a sharp impossibility result, it explains DKKM's own APT/AIPT dichotomy structurally rather than by calibration, it is immune to every 'you tuned it' objection because there is no tuned parameter, and it converts the empirical VoC finding into evidence ABOUT the world (markets are not APT economies) rather than a target to be reproduced. The three structural models then become the illustration, not the result. A JF referee would take this paper. The paper the proposals are building — 'we added a mispricing wedge calibrated to hit the published number, and hit it' — is a much harder sell.

RAISE THE NUMBER OF PRICED AGGREGATE SHOCKS. This is blocker #2 in two of three model-level diagnoses and the theory agent ranked it second overall, yet no proposal implements it. It is the one change that produces an unspanned-in-FF/FM premium WITHOUT any AIPT/mispricing assumption: replace the single TFP shock with J >= 20 priced shocks (sectoral, vintage, intangible-capital, financial-constraint) with characteristic-dependent loadings. That raises EffRank(E[FF']) from ~2 toward the hundreds inside a fully rational frictionless economy, which is exactly DKKM's stated criterion (their Theorem 3), and it is defensible with a straight face at a seminar in a way that a demand wedge is not. It is more work than P1 — GS21 and KP14 would need re-solving with a multi-dimensional aggregate state — but for BGN it is nearly free, since the SDF is already log M = -r - 0.5 sigma_z^2 - sigma_z nu and nu could be replaced by a J-vector with firm-specific beta_j vectors drawn from a char-linked distribution. Given the choice between 'we assumed mispricing' and 'we assumed a richer priced-risk space,' every referee prefers the second.

THE DGP PLACEBO, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THAT ANSWERS 'YOU TUNED IT.' The GS21 agent ran a placebo on the BASIS (150 random Gaussian directions attain 0.74-0.82 of max SR^2 with zero characteristic information — a devastating number that says much of the RFF-360 result is dimension counting). Nobody proposed the corresponding placebo on the DGP: run the identical, final, fully-fixed pipeline on a DGP where the truth is exactly linear in the characteristics, and show DKKM does NOT beat FF/FM. Without that control, a reader cannot distinguish 'complexity pays when the truth is complex' from 'this estimator configuration wins everywhere.' Paired with the placebo you also want the reverse: a synthetic DGP with a known nonlinear w*(x) and known unspanned alpha, where the theoretical DKKM/FM ratio is computable in closed form, to validate that the pipeline recovers the right ratio. These two controls should be the paper's Figure 1, before any structural model appears.

SELECTION-ADJUSTED INFERENCE, NOT SYMMETRIC POST-HOC SELECTION. P2(f) proposes giving FF/FM the same post-hoc alpha selection that DKKM currently enjoys. That is the wrong fix. The reported DKKM number is currently a maximum over 6 alphas at fixed nfeatures=3600 (create_slides_tables.py:107-108, :135-136), and if P2(e) lands it becomes a maximum over up to 11 alphas x 5 nfeatures = 55 cells, all selected on the evaluation metric itself. Symmetrizing the abuse does not remove it. The correct design is nested selection inside the 360-month training window only — choose alpha and nfeatures by cross-validation on months m-360..m-1 and apply the choice at month m, for every method — and then report a single number per method with no grid visible in the main table. This is also what DKKM themselves would have to defend. As a secondary matter, no proposal reports how many simulation iterations underlie the tables or any standard error; with the current DKKM-over-FF gaps at 2.5-15% and no dispersion reported anywhere in all_results.pdf, the existing null may not even be estimated precisely enough to be a null.

THE SPAN-VERSUS-REGULARIZATION 2x2, WHICH DECOMPOSES THE RESULT AND WHICH A REFEREE WILL DEMAND. Run ridge (same CV-selected penalty) on the 7 FF/FM factors, and run unregularized OLS on the RFF factor set, alongside the two existing cells. That 2x2 separates 'DKKM wins because its basis spans more' from 'DKKM wins because it is shrunk and FF/FM are not,' which is precisely the ambiguity that P3 creates and that P2 half-addresses. It costs nothing — both estimators already exist in the repo — and it is the first table a referee will ask for. Note the current pipeline makes the second cell impossible to interpret without it: FF/FM run at ALPHA_LST_FAMA=[0] through fama_functions.mve_data:270, so every reported comparison is confounded ridge-vs-OLS as well as rich-vs-sparse.

AN EXPLICIT INFORMATION-AND-TUNING AUDIT TABLE IN THE PAPER. No proposal asks for the disclosure artifact that would actually settle the fairness question. One table, one row per method: characteristics seen; macro/date-level conditioning seen; regularization grid; how alpha was chosen; how nfeatures was chosen; number of free tuning decisions. Filling it in for the current pipeline immediately exposes that BGN's DKKM sees rf_stand (dkkm_functions.rff:95-96) while FF/FM do not (fama_functions._compute_monthly_fama passes only data[chars]), that DKKM has 6-55 tuned cells and FF/FM have 1, and that GS21's DKKM alpha grid is hand-divided by 100 (config.py:193) with no such adjustment for FF/FM. Any of these three, discovered by a referee rather than disclosed by the authors, is fatal; disclosed up front and repaired, they are a strength.

KP14 SHOULD BE DROPPED FROM THE PAPER UNTIL IT IS REPAIRED, AND NO PROPOSAL MAKES THIS A GATE. P4's risk list mentions the two blockers in passing. They are not risks, they are a correctness gate: utils_kp14/integ_kp14.py:43 runs quad on [0, eps_max] with epsabs=epsrel=1e-10 against a CIR transition density of sd ~0.006, silently returning exact zeros over the eps interval where 98% of firm-months live; and utils_kp14/kp14_fd.py:7 imports parameters_kp14, a module absent from the repository, so the stale G_func.csv (solved under pre-Jun-18 parameters, ~49x off) cannot be regenerated. The consequence is that KP14's reported max_sr of 10/month (34.7 annualized against the model's own bound of 0.774) and its negative Sharpes for all three methods are quadrature artifacts. A referee who finds one artifactual column does not delete the column, they reject the paper and distrust the other two models. The paper should either fix and validate KP14 (validation criterion: recomputed rp matches the closed form gamma_x sigma_x dt + alph gamma_z sigma_z dt share_i to a stated tolerance) or state plainly that KP14 is excluded pending a numerical repair.

REPORT THE CEILING DECOMPOSITION AS THE PAPER'S CENTRAL EXHIBIT. P5(b) proposes propagating max_sr, which is right but under-ambitious. The full exhibit is three numbers per model per month, all computable from the existing moments pickles with no re-simulation: SR* (the ceiling), SR_lin (the best attainable inside the linear characteristic span, sqrt(mu' X (X' Sigma X)^{-1} X' mu)), and SR_rff (the same with the configured RFF basis). The ratio SR_rff/SR_lin is the maximum DKKM advantage the DGP can ever deliver, and the ratio of realized Sharpe to each is the estimation efficiency. Publishing that decomposition for the CURRENT models — where it will read roughly SR_rff/SR_lin = 1.00 in BGN and 1.03 in GS21 — is a complete, self-contained, unfalsifiable-by-tuning demonstration that the models cannot produce the phenomenon, and it should appear before any proposed change. Publishing it again after the changes is then the only credible evidence that the change created span rather than benchmark degradation. No proposal makes this the organizing exhibit; P5 files it as a metric fix and the theory agent lists it as diagnostic D2.

RANKING BY ECONOMICS-VERSUS-PLUMBING, WHICH THE PROPOSALS DO NOT SUPPLY AND WHICH DETERMINES WHETHER THE PAPER IS READ AS A RESULT. My ordering, most economics to most plumbing: P4 (~90% economics — moves three parameters toward externally observed moments and undoes the authors' own commits; the only proposal a referee will wave through); the unproposed multi-priced-shock change (~90% economics, and strictly better than P1 on defensibility); P1 (~60% economics, 40% target-tuning as currently calibrated, recoverable to ~85% if kappa is disciplined on external moments and SR* becomes an output); P6 (~40% economics, and contaminated by two explicit selections against the benchmark); P3 (~30% economics — its admitted standalone effect is a 1.2-1.3x ratio from estimation efficiency, i.e. benchmark handicap); P2 (~0% economics, and its bandwidth item is the single most likely source of a plumbing-driven result); P5 (~0% economics but 100% correctness, with no result attributable to it, which is the right kind of zero). The paper must present its result decomposed along this ordering, one row per change, so a reader can see how much of the final DKKM/FF ratio survives when only P4 and P5 are applied, then P4+P5+P1, then the estimator changes. If the ratio is small until the estimator row is added, there is no paper.

THE SINGLE SENTENCE THAT WOULD KILL THE PAPER, STATED SO THE AUTHORS CAN PRE-EMPT IT. As the packet currently stands it is: 'The authors calibrate the mispricing wedge by choosing the parameter that reproduces the published Sharpe ratio they set out to explain (P1: kappa_med is pinned by the target maximum Sharpe, and s_k is chosen as the largest value for which the resulting Sharpe stays printable), while simultaneously rescaling the estimator bandwidth toward the value used in the empirical study whose result they are reproducing, excluding the form of measurement error that they state would shrink their effect, and awarding the favored estimator six post-hoc tuning choices on the evaluation metric that the benchmarks do not receive.' Every clause of that sentence is currently true of the packet or of the shipped code, and every clause is independently fixable. Fix all four and the sentence cannot be written.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1. Limits-to-arbitrage price wedge (moderate_restructuring)
verdicts.critique:
This is the only proposal that can move the number, and as written it is rigging. Three structural failures.

(1) NO AGENT SUPPORTS THE OBSERVED PRICES. The proposal invokes Shleifer-Vishny / DSSW and asserts 'the arbitrageur faces a position limit', but no constraint is ever modeled. v_it is drawn iid across 1000 firms, so noise-trader risk is diversified away by the LLN: an arbitrageur with any finite risk aversion and any positive capital takes an unbounded position and eliminates the wedge. The manufactured SR_alpha grows as sqrt(N) BY DESIGN (the proposal's own kappa_med formula divides by sqrt(N)) -- i.e. the wedge is a near-arbitrage that is inconsistent with the existence of the very arbitrageur whose frontier evaluate_sdfs.py scores against. After the change, `port = ER^{-1}1` (sdf_compute_bgn.py:305-311, sdf_compute_gs21.py:196-206) is no longer the projection of any agent's marginal rate of substitution onto the return span; it is the projection of nothing. The models stop being equilibrium models.

(2) THE FREE PARAMETER IS CALIBRATED TO THE ANSWER. The proposal says outright: 'kappa_med, pinned by the TARGET maximum Sharpe rather than by the misvaluation literature', and then reverse-engineers 3.3% from a total SR* of 2.20 annual chosen to 'reproduce that ratio exactly'. That is the definition of manufacturing the result. Every referee will find this paragraph.

(3) MISSING MANAGERIAL FEEDBACK, and it is not innocuous. In BGN investment triggers on exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r)>1 (panel_functions_bgn.py:79), a fundamental-value NPV rule, so the wedge is harmless there. In KP14 arrivals are exogenous Poisson (panel_functions_kp14.py sim_arrivals). But in GS21 the investment cutoff and the refinancing debt choice are value-function policies (panel_functions_gs21.py:93-106) computed from P_up/P_down, i.e. from fundamental value; a manager facing a persistent 3-40% equity misvaluation would time issuance (Stein 1996, Baker-Wurgler 2002). Silently assuming managers maximize fundamental value must be stated as an assumption, not omitted.

MECHANICS ARE CORRECT, credit where due: ER_obs = diag(a) ER diag(a) with a = exp(q_t - kappa rho v_t + 0.5 kappa^2 sigma_v^2) and a diagonal bump exp(kappa^2 sigma_v^2) is exactly right given independence across firms, and the call sites named (after ER[1:,1:] /= np.outer(P,P) at sdf_compute_bgn.py:285) are the right ones. And it is true that no solfile needs re-solving.

Also: the proposal implicitly requires P4 (it assumes sigma_idio = 10%/month; at BGN's current 3.9% the same kappa_med delivers SR_alpha = 1.0/month = 3.5 annual, an absurdity) and requires P3 (with only mom(2,13) and bm in the char set, a rho=0.96 latent wedge is barely detectable -- you need long-horizon reversal columns). Neither dependency is flagged as blocking.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Much less than claimed, and the claim rests on the wrong span2.py cell. The proposal's headline 2-11x comes from the 'nonlinear alpha' rows, where g was a hand-planted arbitrary nonlinear function of the chars. What P1 actually delivers is alpha_i = (1-rho)*kappa(size_i, d_i)*v_it: a SMOOTH, MONOTONE two-variable modulation of a single latent signal. FM already spans anything linear in the chars; if the char set contains long-horizon reversal (which it must, or nothing is detectable at all), the signal itself is linear and FM captures the level. FF's 2x3 design contains exactly the size x signal interaction, i.e. a coarse two-bin version of the dominant kappa modulation -- the proposal concedes this and then waves it away. What is genuinely outside both spans is only (a) the division by d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2 and (b) the hump. But (b) requires s_k ~ 1.9, i.e. a p10-p90 kappa ratio of ~90x, and the proposal itself notes SR* then blows up past 2.5 annual and must be capped -- so the hump is available only at parameters the proposal rules out. Strip the planted nonlinearity and I would guess a realized DKKM/FM ratio of 1.3-1.8x, not 3-5x. Getting to 3-5x requires making kappa a deliberately non-monotone function of several characteristics, at which point the nonlinearity IS planted and the paper is circular.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge, but make it an equilibrium object and stop calibrating it to the target. Concretely: (i) replace the exogenous v_it with a modeled arbitrageur who has finite capital W_t and mean-variance preferences, so the surviving wedge is the FOC residual and its amplitude is pinned by (risk aversion x capital / holding cost), not chosen; or adopt Merton (1987) segmented participation, where alpha_i = delta_i*sigma_i^2/q_i falls out of an equilibrium with an investor base q_i that has direct empirical counterparts (breadth of ownership). (ii) Give the demand shock a small COMMON component so that noise-trader risk is not diversifiable at N=1000 -- this is what makes limited arbitrage survive in the first place. (iii) Report SR* as an OUTPUT of independently-disciplined parameters (Pontiff 2006 arbitrage costs, RKRV misvaluation dispersion, anomaly half-lives) and accept whatever DKKM/FF ratio comes out. (iv) State the manager's objective explicitly. (v) Run it in BGN only for the first draft -- BGN is the one model where nothing else has to be fixed first.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (reparametrization_only)
verdicts.critique:
Outside my lens in the sense that it touches no economics -- and that is also its problem: it is presented as a precondition when most of it is a hyperparameter choice dressed in derivation language.

The honest items: NMAT 5->1 restores the root convention (config.py:177-178 literally says 'ROOT: main_revised.py line 12: nmat = 1'), the scale-free ridge reparameterization is unambiguously right and removes the existing GS21 /100 hand-tuning (config.py:193), and giving FF/FM the same ridge grid and the same post-hoc alpha selection (currently ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], config.py:187) is a fairness repair that must happen regardless. Endorse all three.

The dishonest item is the bandwidth. 'Hold gamma^2*L/12 fixed at DKKM's real-data value' is a CHOICE of invariance, not a derivation. DKKM ran gamma in [0.5,1.0] at L=130; there is no theorem saying the kernel exponent is the object to hold fixed rather than gamma itself, and the GS21 agent measured directly that widening HURTS when the truth is near-linear (0.879 -> 0.799 at 4.65x, -> 0.376 at 10x). A referee reading 'we multiplied the bandwidth by 5.1 and then DKKM won' will not be persuaded by a footnote about kernel exponents. P3's route -- raise L so sd(Wx) rises with the ORIGINAL grid -- is the referee-proof version and the proposal admits it.

P=36000 is close to pointless at N=1000: the stock-weight map factors through R^N (w_t = S_t*lambda), and the monthly factor returns S_t'R_t live in a space of rank <= N, so beyond a few thousand features you are duplicating directions, not adding them. DKKM's c=1000 comes with a far larger cross-section. Cap at 3600-10800 and spend the compute on replications instead.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal says so: 'on the CURRENT three models the impact of this bundle is approximately zero'. Worse, the fairness repairs it proposes (same ridge grid for FF/FM, same oracle alpha selection) will move the measured DKKM/FF ratio DOWN, since FF/FM currently run unshrunk at alpha=0 while DKKM gets six post-hoc chances at the evaluation metric. Net expected effect on the headline number: negative. That is the correct direction and should be embraced, not hidden.
verdicts.salvage: Split it. Commit now, unconditionally: NMAT=1, the scale-free ridge parameterization, the alpha grid with points at df in (63,360), and identical ridge + identical alpha-selection for FF/FM. Defer the bandwidth rescale entirely -- do not ship it as a fix; report it as one axis of a 2x2 robustness table {old, rescaled gamma} x {old, new DGP}, and let P3's larger L do the work in the headline specification. Drop P=36000.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set to ~35 (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
Contains a factual error about the models and a category error about the theory.

FACTUAL: 'industry = a fixed random partition into 10 groups correlated with the model's own permanent firm type (beta_j in BGN, lambda_f in KP14, initial k in GS21)'. In BGN there IS no permanent firm type: panel_functions_bgn.py:44 draws `beta = -expon.rvs(size=(T, N), ...)`, a fresh iid draw for every (date, firm-slot); sigmaj likewise (line 49). Firms are ex ante identical and differ only through the realized history of project arrivals and deaths. In GS21 every firm starts at k=1, b=0 (panel_functions_gs21.py:56-57) and heterogeneity is again pure z-history. Only KP14 has a permanent type (lambda_f, panel_functions_kp14.py:112). So in two of the three models the proposed 'industry' variable would be a random label with literally zero information -- and rank_standardize's argsort tie-breaking would turn it into exactly the persistent pseudo-random column the proposal elsewhere warns about.

CATEGORY ERROR: the proposal's whole quantitative case is EffRank(feature matrix) 16.5 -> ~250. But DKKM Theorem 3 is a joint condition on the eigenvalue spectrum AND on the alignment of risk premia with that spectrum -- their own D5 diagnostic. Thirty-five multi-horizon, lagged and peer-demeaned transforms of a 2-3 dimensional latent state are linearly redundant BY CONSTRUCTION: they raise the rank of the design matrix while leaving the premia concentrated in the same top one or two eigenvectors. That is DKKM's APT calibration with more columns, which is exactly the configuration in which they PROVE complexity is harmful. Padding the design matrix does not create a flat premium spectrum.

SECONDARY: 35 tercile sorts in fama_french will produce mostly degenerate splits in these models (agr is 91% zeros in BGN, 98.8% in GS21; book_lev has ~101 values concentrated on four points; GS21's agr takes literally two values). Handing FF 35 near-degenerate sorts and then reporting that DKKM beats it is not a complexity result.

The fairness repairs bundled in -- delete the BGN-only rf_stand input (dkkm_functions.rff:95-96; FF/FM never see rf, fama_functions:200) and turn on the commented-out FM standardization (fama_functions.py:152-156) -- are correct and should be committed independently of everything else here.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal's own predicted effect concedes it: 'a spurious-looking DKKM/FM ratio of maybe 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency, not span'. FM with 35 chars spans every linear combination of them; the only DKKM edge is that FM pays 2K/T ~ 21% of squared Sharpe in plug-in noise while ridge does not. A ridge-regularized FM on the same 35 chars -- which P2 mandates anyway -- erases essentially all of it. So P3's standalone contribution is a handicap applied to the benchmark, and the two proposals as bundled cancel each other.
verdicts.salvage: Keep only the parts with independent justification: (i) long-horizon reversal / multi-horizon momentum columns, because without them P1's persistent latent wedge is undetectable by anyone and P1 dies; (ii) the two fairness repairs (kill rf_stand, standardize FM's regressors); (iii) a tie-aware tercile split in fama_functions.py:86-88, which is a bug fix. Drop the peer/industry columns until the models actually have permanent firm types (see missed idea on permanent heterogeneity), drop the EffRank argument entirely, and never report an EffRank gain as evidence of a complexity gain without the premium-alignment diagnostic alongside.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block in all three models (reparametrization_only)
verdicts.critique:
Three very different changes bundled under one label; they deserve three different verdicts.

BGN: CORRECT AND FREE, and I verified it. sigmaj appears nowhere in vasicek.py -- D(r), Jstar, and the fitted (beta_star, scale) depend only on r, Cbar, pi and the beta distribution (vasicek.py:22-77). Valuation is A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values (panel_functions_bgn.py:157) and the risk-neutral cash flow is Chat*exp(-beta_j), which is invariant to sigmaj because C = exp(Cbar - 0.5*sigmaj^2 + eps*sigmaj) has E[C] = exp(Cbar) by construction. So removing the 0.1 changes the conditional COVARIANCE only: prices, expected returns, the investment rule and the growth-option solution are all untouched, and no solfile is re-solved. Endorse. But two honest qualifications the proposal skips: (a) sigmaj has no BGN calibration target at all -- it is pinned only by |corr_zj| <= 1 -- so 'restoring the calibration' oversells what is a nuisance-parameter knob; (b) the arithmetic is wrong. Idiosyncratic LOG variance is sigmaj^2 - (beta/sigma_z)^2 = 2bu + u^2 with b = |beta|/sigma_z ~ 1.59; going from u ~ U[0,0.111] to u ~ U[0,1.11] raises it from ~0.18 to ~2.08, a factor of 12, not 6. And the conditional second moment enters through exp(sigmaj^2) (sdf_compute_bgn.py:246-252): exp(4.84) = 126 versus exp(2.72) = 15. Expect a large overshoot, extremely fat-tailed firm returns, and possible conditioning trouble in ER. Titrate the multiplier to an idio-vol target rather than setting it to 1.0.

KP14: cannot be executed. sigma_eps and sigma_u enter the Feynman-Kac solve for G and the CIR conditional-expectation integrals, so both solfiles must be regenerated -- and kp14_fd.py:7 imports `parameters_kp14`, a module absent from the repo. The proposal flags this; I am only confirming it is a hard blocker, not a caveat.

GS21: the diagnosis is right and the prescription is incomplete in a way that matters for the model's identity. Restoring sigma_z requires new MATLAB solfiles (the zgrid spans exactly +/-2.72 stationary sd of the CURRENT sigma_z), which the proposal says. What it misses is that sigma_z is not the only thing broken. config.py:284 sets GS21_KAPPA_E = 0 -- there is NO equity issuance cost -- and realized market leverage never exceeds 1.04% with zero defaults in 2.16M firm-months. GS21's economics is the interaction of leverage, default and costly external finance; the shipped object has none of the three. Separately the AGGREGATE side is miscalibrated in the opposite direction: d log P / d x = 12.4 with sigma_x = 0.0105 gives systematic vol ~13%/month ~ 45%/year, roughly 2.5x the data. Raising sigma_z to 0.5x leaves total return vol around 45-46%/year, i.e. you fix the idio/systematic RATIO by making an already-too-volatile market slightly less dominant. A genuine GS21 recalibration must jointly target aggregate equity vol (~18%/yr), average leverage (~30% book), a default rate of ~1%/yr and a credit spread, with kappa_e > 0 and a b-grid that reaches those leverages.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: On its own, provably almost nothing, by the proposal's own span2.py evidence: under exact factor pricing the D^{-1} tilt is worth 1.81% of SR* at N=100, 0.186% at N=1000 and 0.019% at N=10000, and it stays worth nothing even with a 20x spread in d. Idiosyncratic risk is diversifiable; making it more dispersed only buys back the undiversified residual, which is O(1/N). And where d IS strongly char-linked and monotone (KP14: log d on log nlive, slope -0.87, corr -0.97), FF's tercile sorts on size get a crude version of the tilt for free. It is a multiplier on P1, nothing more -- and it will LOWER max_sr in all three models, which is a good and honest outcome but will look like a regression in the tables.
verdicts.salvage: Do BGN now, alone, with the multiplier titrated to a ~10%/month idio-vol target rather than set to 1.0, and report it as a covariance-only change that provably leaves prices and premia identical -- that framing is airtight and I verified it. Hold KP14 until the quadrature and G_func are repaired and parameters_kp14 is restored. Treat GS21 not as a one-line sigma_z edit but as a full re-calibration with kappa_e > 0, an extended b-grid, and joint targets on aggregate vol, leverage, default rate and credit spread -- otherwise the paper is calling something 'GS21' that has neither default nor costly external finance.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
Three of the four items are unambiguous repairs and should ship today. Propagating max_sr into results.pkl is the single highest-value line in the entire proposal set -- it is already computed at sdf_compute_bgn.py:326-328 and sdf_compute_gs21.py:222-224 and stored by calculate_moments.py, and without it nobody can distinguish 'the estimator is failing' from 'the DGP has nothing to estimate'. Reporting the unconditional Sharpe alongside the mean-of-ratios is correct because the conditional metric is homogeneous of degree zero in w and therefore assigns exactly zero credit to the timing channel, which is half of the DKKM/KMZ mechanism. Adding test assets sorted on something other than the two chars every method already spans linearly is obviously right.

My objection is to the HJD replacement. sqrt(1 - rho_unc^2) is scale-free precisely because it optimally rescales the method's return -- but an SDF that gets the direction right and the LEVEL wrong genuinely misprices, and the Hansen-Jagannathan distance is supposed to punish that. Making the metric blind to leverage is not obviously an improvement; it is a different metric that answers a different question. More importantly the proposal solves the wrong problem: the reason sdf_ret is pathological is not the metric, it is that sdf_ret is the min-second-moment portfolio of 1000 simulated returns in economies whose max Sharpe is a sqrt(N) diversification artifact (KP14 10/month, GS21 0.44/month with 89-97% coming from diversifying 4bp of per-firm alpha across nearly identical firms). All three models have a CLOSED-FORM SDF -- BGN's is written down explicitly at panel_functions_bgn.py:34-36 as log M = -r - 0.5*sigma_z^2 - sigma_z*nu; KP14 and GS21 are exponential-affine in the aggregate states. Benchmark against that and the artifact disappears at the source.

Minor but real: the universe mismatch the proposal notes (evaluate_sdfs.py subsets rp/cond_var to prepare_panel survivors while sdf_ret comes from the book>0 universe) is a correctness bug, not a metric preference, and should be fixed in the same commit.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No -- and it should shrink the currently-reported gap. As the proposal itself discloses, the current HJD gives DKKM six post-hoc chances at the right leverage (create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model takes an argmin over alphas on the evaluation metric) while FF/FM have only alpha=0.
