A scale-free metric removes that unearned advantage. The new Sigma-cosine column will most likely show FF already at ~0.8 of the ceiling in BGN, which is the paper's real finding and undercuts any story that the estimator is what is broken.
verdicts.salvage: Ship max_sr propagation, the unconditional Sharpe, the median alongside the mean, the new test assets, and the universe fix immediately -- none of these require re-running the simulation if the moments pickles are retained. For the pricing-error metric, do not replace HJD with a correlation; instead compute the HJ distance against each model's ANALYTIC SDF (available in closed form in all three), and demote the return-space HJD to a robustness table. Let compute_pricing_errors.py's alpha'Sigma^{-1}alpha carry the argument.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with staggered fiscal years plus heteroskedastic measurement error (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
Structurally the safest proposal in the set: it changes no DGP, no policy function and no solfile, and the true conditional moments are computed from latent states so they are untouched by construction. The Fourier argument -- classical homoskedastic EIV attenuates the linear component by tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2) but attenuates frequency-omega components by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2), so it compresses the DKKM advantage, while heteroskedastic EIV creates a firm-specific shrinkage lambda_i that multiplies every signal -- is correct and is the most original idea in the whole set. It deserves to be a section of the paper in its own right regardless of whether it moves the Sharpe.

Where it is weak is bite. In BGN the accounting state is book = I*num with num a small integer averaging 5.95 (panel_functions_bgn.py:143-144) and agr already 91% exact zeros; a 6-12 month lag on that is nearly free, so the mechanism is inert. In GS21 k changes in 1.21% of firm-months, so book staleness is inert there too; only roe bites, via rho_z^12 = 0.657 with a 1.47x cross-sectional spread in attenuation. So across 6 chars in 3 models you have roughly one or two live channels. In KP14 the accounting state is a project count with Poisson lumpiness and the same argument applies.

The multiplicative-noise piece needs a guard: adding exp(sigma_e*u) to bm and roe in models where agr is 91-98.8% ties will break the ties -- good -- but it turns the FF tercile sort on those chars into a noise sort, and reporting a DKKM win over an FF whose cma factor is pure noise is not a result. Fix fama_functions.py:86-88 in the same commit.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, 5-15% at best, and the proposal admits part of that comes from lowering FF/FM rather than raising DKKM. The 'FM cannot form lambda(h_i)*bm_i because it applies one coefficient per char' argument is weaker than presented: once P3 has enlarged the char set, nothing prevents the econometrician from including staleness and the products staleness x bm, staleness x roe as characteristics -- FM then spans the interaction exactly, and FF can add a third sort dimension. The genuine DKKM advantage is only that it gets the whole smooth bivariate surface without anyone having to guess which interactions to include. That is a real but second-order edge, and it is the kind of edge that a properly-shrunk 37-regressor FM largely captures.
verdicts.salvage: Keep it, framed as a realism layer and as a theory contribution rather than as a source of the gap. Concretely: (i) implement staggered fiscal years and the observable staleness variable, since it is nearly free and it breaks GS21's indefensible bm = 1/P_ex identity; (ii) implement heteroskedastic noise with the reliability proxy set to STALENESS, not size, so FF's built-in size interaction cannot capture it; (iii) explicitly do NOT add a homoskedastic component, and write up the exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) result as a stated proposition -- 'classical measurement error hurts flexible estimators more than linear ones' is a publishable point on its own; (iv) fix the tercile degeneracy in fama_functions before adding noise to any char.

missed_ideas: EVALUATE AGAINST THE MODELS' ANALYTIC SDF, NOT AGAINST A 1000-ASSET MIN-SECOND-MOMENT PORTFOLIO. All three economies have the pricing kernel in closed form -- BGN's is written down at panel_functions_bgn.py:34-36 (log M = -r - 0.5*sigma_z^2 - sigma_z*nu, with nu decomposed into xi and mu), and KP14/GS21 are exponential-affine in the aggregate states. The pipeline instead defines 'truth' as port = ER^{-1}1 over 1000 simulated stocks (sdf_compute_bgn.py:305, sdf_compute_gs21.py:197), which is why max_sr is 10/month in KP14 and 0.44/month in GS21 -- a sqrt(N) diversification artifact with no real-data counterpart. Scoring each method's SDF against the true m (correlation, or an HJ distance in the space of the model's own payoffs) removes the artifact at its source, makes P5's metric surgery mostly unnecessary, and lets you report the economically meaningful ceiling sqrt(exp(sigma_z^2)-1) = 0.4166/month for BGN and sqrt(gamma_x^2+gamma_z^2) = 0.774/yr for KP14.

MAKE THE PRICED-RISK LOADING A VECTOR IN BGN -- essentially free and it never leaves BGN's economics. Draw each project's systematic risk as a K-vector beta_j with a price-of-risk vector lambda. The valuation machinery needs only the scalar b_j = lambda'beta_j (risk-neutral cash flow is Chat*exp(-b_j)), so vasicek.py, Jstar, D(r), the fitted (beta_star, scale) and the investment rule at panel_functions_bgn.py:79 all survive untouched. But the conditional covariance becomes rank K with genuinely dispersed loadings instead of the current rank-1-plus-diagonal, so w* = Sigma^{-1}mu now requires hedging K factors and becomes a much richer function of the characteristics. Caveat to state honestly: premia remain rank-1 in b_j, so this raises the HEDGING dimension, not the premium dimension -- it is necessary but, per span2.py, not sufficient without nonlinear char->loading maps.

BGN'S GROWTH-OPTION CHANNEL IS SWITCHED OFF ENTIRELY AND NOBODY NOTICED. panel_functions_bgn.py:159-165: G = (I*Chat*Jstar(r)).reshape(T+1,1) and P += G -- the value of growth options is IDENTICAL for every firm at every date. All cross-sectional variation in BGN comes from assets in place, so G/P is a pure mechanical function of size and the real-option convexity that motivates the model contributes nothing to the cross-section. Making the arrival intensity pi (or the option's own beta) a permanent firm attribute -- exactly what KP14 already does with lambda_f -- restores a genuinely convex, non-monotone price function in (option share, state), which is the kind of nonlinearity that a Fourier basis can find and a monotone tercile sort structurally cannot. This is a change INSIDE BGN's own economics rather than a mispricing wedge bolted on.

NONE OF THE THREE MODELS HAS PERMANENT, MULTIDIMENSIONAL FIRM HETEROGENEITY -- and this, not the characteristic count, is why the truth is low-dimensional. Verified: BGN draws beta and sigmaj iid at every (date, firm) (panel_functions_bgn.py:44,49); GS21 initializes every firm at k=1, b=0 (panel_functions_gs21.py:56-57); only KP14 has a permanent type (lambda_f). Give firms a vector of permanent, partially-observable types -- project-beta distribution, arrival intensity, adjustment-cost curvature, operating leverage, payout policy -- and the true SDF weight becomes a genuinely high-dimensional function of which the characteristics reveal only a projection. That is precisely DKKM's 'dense, weakly-identified truth' condition, obtained without any pricing wedge, and it also gives P3's peer/industry variables something real to be correlated with.

NONLINEAR CHAR-TO-BETA MAPS FROM OPERATING LEVERAGE (Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino 2004, Zhang 2005). The span gap requires the mapping from observables to risk exposure to be convex or non-monotone, not merely for there to be more factors. Fixed operating costs make beta a convex function of fundamentals-over-price, and irreversibility plus countercyclical price of risk makes it non-monotone in book-to-market. All three models currently have essentially affine maps -- GS21's cross-sectional log-price regression on (z,b) has R^2 = 0.95-0.995 with a leverage elasticity constant to three decimals. Adding a fixed operating cost to the profit function (GS21's prof_* at panel_functions_gs21.py:110-117 is linear in exp(x+z)) is a one-term change with decades of empirical support and it manufactures convexity without manufacturing mispricing.

MERTON (1987) SEGMENTED PARTICIPATION AS THE EQUILIBRIUM VERSION OF P1. Instead of an exogenous demand wedge with a target-calibrated amplitude, let each stock be held by a limited investor base q_i. Equilibrium gives E[R_i] - Rf = beta_i*lambda + delta*sigma_i^2/q_i: an alpha that is (a) not spanned by the covariance loadings, (b) proportional to IDIOSYNCRATIC variance and therefore automatically char-linked, (c) supported by an actual agent's first-order condition, and (d) disciplined by independent data on ownership breadth. The true MVE weight becomes w* ~ alpha/d ~ 1/q_i, so the nonlinearity has to come from q_i being a nontrivial function of observables -- which is a testable claim, not a free parameter. This gets P1's economics with none of P1's internal-consistency violations.

GS21'S AGGREGATE SIDE IS AS MISCALIBRATED AS ITS IDIOSYNCRATIC SIDE, IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. d log P / d x = 12.4 with sigma_x = 0.010458 gives systematic return vol ~13%/month ~ 45%/year, against ~15-20%/year in data. So the pairwise correlation of 0.95 is only half an idio-vol problem; the other half is an aggregate discount-rate elasticity 2-3x too large. P4 raises sigma_z and leaves total vol at ~45%/year. Any GS21 recalibration must target aggregate equity vol jointly with the idio/systematic ratio -- and must also turn the model's actual frictions back on: config.py:284 sets GS21_KAPPA_E = 0 (no equity issuance cost) and realized market leverage never exceeds 1.04% with zero defaults, so the shipped object has neither costly external finance nor default risk and is not, in any meaningful sense, Gomes-Schmid (2021).

NO CONDITIONING IN THE ESTIMATOR FOR ANY METHOD -- fix it symmetrically before concluding the models lack conditioning content. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py fits ONE ridge coefficient vector on 360 months and applies it unchanged to every cross-section; fama_functions.mve_data does the same with OLS. So time-varying prices of risk are invisible to FF, FM and DKKM alike, and BGN's rf_stand (dkkm_functions.rff:95-96) is the only conditioning input anywhere -- given to DKKM only, and measurably worthless (65.6% of sin features are literally unchanged when it flips sign). DKKM/KMZ's actual construction interacts signals with conditioning variables. Add char x macro-state managed portfolios for all three methods, then ask whether the models have any conditioning content to find.

ENTRY, EXIT, AND A STATIONARY HEAVY-TAILED SIZE DISTRIBUTION. All three panels hold N = 1000 fixed with no entry and (in GS21) no exit at all, so log k is a pure Bernoulli random walk and the size distribution is nonstationary -- sd(log k) grows as sqrt(T) and is an artifact of the burn-in length (0.40-0.44 at T=920 versus ~2.0 in CRSP; sd(log bm) 0.10 versus ~0.8). DKKM's real-data Sharpe of 3.7 falls to ~1.6 in mega/large caps, so a large share of the empirical virtue of complexity lives in the microcap tail that these panels do not have. A Gabaix-style stationary Pareto size distribution with entry/exit, combined with strongly size-dependent idiosyncratic variance, is a structural change with clear independent discipline and it multiplies every other channel.

THE MOST DEFENSIBLE PAPER MAY BE THE NEGATIVE ONE. Stacking P1+P2+P3+P4+P6 destroys the claim in the title: after a hand-calibrated demand wedge, 35 engineered signals, a 5x bandwidth rescale, three volatility recalibrations and heteroskedastic measurement error, these are not 'simple economic models' and the result is not a discovery about them. The ceiling calculations already in hand are a genuine theorem-like finding: under exact K-factor pricing with K <= 2 and N = 1000, every basis -- equal-weight included -- attains the maximum conditional Sharpe to within 0.2%, so the virtue of complexity is IMPOSSIBLE in a frictionless production economy with a low-dimensional priced-risk space, no matter how rich the estimator. Publish that, add exactly ONE minimal sufficient friction with an equilibrium foundation (Merton segmentation or a capital-constrained arbitrageur), and show the gap appears. One change, one mechanism, one number -- rather than six knobs turned until the table reads correctly.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1. Limits-to-arbitrage price wedge (kappa_i * v_it)
verdicts.critique:
P1 is the only proposal that attacks the binding blocker (no unspanned premium), and I cannot refute its NECESSITY. But as parameterized it will not produce a large DKKM-over-FM gap, for four code-verified reasons.

(1) THE WEDGE IS ENDOGENOUSLY REVEALED AS A NEAR-LOG-LINEAR FUNCTION OF TWO CHARS, AND THE PROPOSER TREATS THAT AS A FEATURE. factor_utils.py:91 sets size = log(mve) and panel_functions_bgn.py:247 sets bm = book/mve. Under the wedge, size_obs = size_fund - q and log bm_obs = log bm_fund + q EXACTLY. In BGN, mve_fund = book*Chat*expbar*D(r) + I*Chat*Jstar(r) (panel_functions_bgn.py:153-164), an AFFINE function of book, and book = mve_obs*bm_obs is observed. So q = log(a*bm_obs + c*exp(-size_obs)) up to date-t constants. With c = G(rbar) = 1.2492 and mean mve = 8.06, the second term is 8-15% of the first, so q ~= log(a) + log(bm_obs) + O(15%) -- a smooth, monotone, essentially univariate function of bm with a mild size x bm interaction. A quadratic in (size, bm) captures ~99% of it. So the alpha the wedge creates is, to first order, IN OR ADJACENT TO FM's span.

(2) span2.py's 1.91x and 6.37x cells DO NOT MODEL THIS. Those cells drew alpha as an exogenous nonlinear g(x) unrelated to how the chars are generated. Here alpha is revealed THROUGH the chars in a near-invertible, near-log-linear way. The correct span2.py analogue is the 'linear alpha, homogeneous d' cell, which measures RFF/lin = 1.00. P1 alone therefore buys approximately nothing; the proposer's own evidence says so.

(3) THE JENSEN TERM IS A SPURIOUS, MONOTONE, FM-SPANNED PREMIUM THAT DOMINATES THE INTENDED ONE AT LARGE s_k. The proposal's own transform includes exp(+0.5*kappa^2*sigma_v^2). At s_k=1.9 the 99th-percentile kappa = 0.033*exp(2.33*1.9) = 2.77, so 0.5*kappa^2*sigma_v^2 = 0.285 = 28.5%/month of pure convexity drift, versus the INTENDED alpha (1-rho)*kappa*|v| = 0.0378*2.77 = 10.5%/month. The convexity term is a deterministic function of kappa alone, i.e. of size and idio vol -- monotone, and therefore exactly what FM's linear span and FF's size sort DO capture. The largest new 'premium' in the design is the one both benchmarks get for free.

(4) TAIL DOMINATION + BOUNDED FEATURES = UNREACHABLE TRUTH. Per-firm contribution alpha_i^2/d_i = (1-rho)^2 kappa^2 v^2/(d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2) saturates at (1-rho)^2 v^2/sigma_v^2 = 0.0193 once kappa > sqrt(d_f/sigma_v^2) = 0.367. With kappa_med=0.033 and s_k=1.0, kappa=0.367 is 2.41 sd out: ~1% of firms. At s_k=1.0, E[kappa^2] = kappa_med^2*e^2 = 7.39*kappa_med^2 and roughly 70% of SR*^2 comes from the top 5% of firms. So max_sr becomes a property of ~50 extreme firms. That is precisely the corruption failure mode: it inflates SR* and both metrics without teaching any estimator anything, because the true w* is now a SPIKE. And the DKKM basis provably cannot represent a spike: dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes every feature to the identical bounded uniform marginal, and even P2's z-score fix leaves |sin|,|cos| <= 1. Producing a weight 100x larger on 1% of firms from bounded features requires an RKHS norm that ridge is specifically penalizing. The 'hump' at s_k=1.9 lives at the 99th percentile of kappa -- roughly 10 firms out of 1000 -- and is invisible at T=360.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM: yes, largely. FM's span is exactly the column space of X=[1,chars] (fama_functions.py:161-163, P = X pinvh(X'X)), re-fit monthly. The wedge's alpha is (1-rho)*q, and q is a smooth near-log-linear function of (bm, size). FM regresses on RAW bm; over the realized 3-4x range of bm a linear function approximates log(bm) with R^2 ~ 0.97. So FM captures ~95-97% of the alpha variance directly, leaving DKKM a residual of 3-5% of alpha variance. In Sharpe terms: with the target SR_alpha = 0.6/month, the FM-unspanned residual is sqrt(0.04)*0.6 = 0.12/month, added in quadrature to FM's existing 0.21 gives FM 0.234 and DKKM ~0.26 -- a 10% gap, not the 200-500% target. Multiply by P4's d-dispersion factor (span2.py's 1.91x on the ratio) and you reach perhaps 30-50%. FF: no, FF genuinely cannot form this -- but that is uninformative, because fama_functions.py:99-104 averages the two size bins out of every char factor, so FF has NO size x char interaction direction at all and already attains only 35.8% of max Sharpe in BGN. Beating FF is a sorting artifact, not a complexity result; the binding benchmark is FM. Metric: the population conditional Sharpe CAN detect this (it is SR* x cos_Sigma, verified at evaluate_sdfs.py:183-184), but with SR* inflated to 0.64/month by tail firms, all methods' cosines fall and the reported gap partly reflects a larger denominator rather than better estimation.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge -- it is the only proposal that removes the binding blocker -- but change four things. (a) MARTINGALE-NORMALIZE: define the wedge multiplier as exp(-kappa*v - 0.5*kappa^2*sigma_v^2 adjustments) so the Jensen convexity drift is removed and the only new premium is the intended (1-rho)*q. (b) BREAK THE ENDOGENOUS-REVELATION LINEARITY: make kappa depend on an INTERACTION that is observable but not a main effect any benchmark sorts on -- e.g. kappa_i proportional to (size percentile) x (staleness) x 1{roe below median} -- so that q is recoverable only through a product of three observables, not through a monotone transform of bm. (c) CAP s_k at 0.8-1.0 and winsorize kappa at the 99th percentile, and REPORT the share of SR*^2 contributed by the top 1% and 5% of firms; if it exceeds ~30% the truth is a spike and no bounded-feature estimator can reach it. (d) GATE ON THE ORACLE SPAN RATIO BEFORE RUNNING THE ESTIMATOR: compute mean_t SR_rff,t/SR_lin,t from the true rp and cond_var already in the moments pickle. If that ratio is below ~2, do not run the pipeline -- the realized gap can never exceed it.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (bandwidth, second rank-standardization, NMAT, alpha grid, c=P/T)
verdicts.critique:
The diagnosis is code-correct: dkkm_functions.py:110 does return rank_standardize(features), and rank-standardization is monotone-invariant, so GAMMA_GRID is very nearly a no-op. But this bundle contains one flat code error and three items that move DKKM DOWN, not up.

CODE ERROR IN P2(d). The proposal says to reparameterize the penalty at dkkm_functions.py lines 162 and 176 (the 360*z inside ridge_regr). Read mve_data lines 304-315: for every alph > 0 the code builds X_aug = [X; sqrt(360*alph)*eye(p)[:-1]] and then calls ridge_regr(X_aug, y_aug, None, np.array([0])) -- shrinkage_list is [0]. So the 360*z path is NEVER EXERCISED for any penalized column. Editing lines 162/176 changes only the single unpenalized alpha=0 column. The reparameterization must go in mve_data's augmentation, not ridge_regr. As written the change is a no-op that would look like it worked.

P2(c) NMAT=1 STRICTLY LOWERS THE REPORTED DKKM SHARPE. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169 averages the STOCK WEIGHTS across 5 draws. The metric is Sharpe = SR* x cos_Sigma(w_hat, w*) (evaluate_sdfs.py:183-184). Averaging 5 independent draws cancels the draw-specific component of w_hat that is orthogonal to w*, which raises the cosine in expectation. The proposer's argument is about the SHAPE of the Sharpe-vs-P curve, not its level -- but the paper's target is a LEVEL gap against FF/FM. NMAT=1 therefore works directly against the stated goal and buys only cosmetics on a curve that is flat for span reasons anyway.

P2(f) GIVING FF/FM THE SAME RIDGE GRID AND THE SAME POST-HOC ALPHA SELECTION SHRINKS THE GAP. The audit established that argmin-over-alpha on the evaluation metric is currently an ORACLE ADVANTAGE FOR DKKM ONLY. Equalizing it is correct science and correct refereeing defense, and it will make the reported DKKM/FF ratio smaller. Fine -- but it must be labelled as such, not slipped in alongside changes advertised as helping.

P2(a) WIDENING GAMMA MEASURABLY HURT. The GS21 agent tested exactly this: at gamma x4.65, 36 features went 0.879 -> 0.799 of max SR^2; at x10, 0.879 -> 0.376. When the truth is near-linear, a narrow kernel is the CORRECT kernel and widening spends a fixed feature budget on noise. This is the classic 'adds noise faster than signal' failure and it is measured, not hypothetical.

What survives cleanly: the z-score replacement for the second rank-standardization (restores gamma dependence while keeping the 3.1x sin/cos amplitude equalization the audit found is load-bearing), and the alpha-grid hole at df in (63,360).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposer says so. On the current DGPs the entire population nonlinearity headroom is 0.7pp of Sharpe in BGN and 3% in GS21, so nothing in this bundle can move the reported numbers by more than noise. Net expected effect on the DKKM/FF ratio, item by item: bandwidth widening -5% to 0%, NMAT=1 -2% to -5%, equalized alpha selection -3% to -8%, z-scored features 0% to +2%, alpha-grid repair 0% to +2% (it mostly removes the c=1 double-descent spike, which is a bug fix that improves the WORST DKKM cells, not the best one). Sum: plausibly -8% to 0%. FM and FF are untouched by (a)-(e) and improved by (f). So this bundle most likely makes the headline result slightly worse while being individually correct on every point.
verdicts.salvage: Split into two commits with honest labels. COMMIT 1 (pure bug fixes, do now, expect the reported gap to shrink): fix the alpha=0 ridgeless column (truncate eigenvalues or drop the column), add grid points at df in (63,360) via the correct location -- the sqrt(360*alph) augmentation in mve_data lines 306-312, not ridge_regr -- give FF/FM the identical grid and identical post-hoc selection, and replace the second rank_standardize with a per-column z-score. COMMIT 2 (conditional, do only after P1 lands and only if the oracle span ratio D2 exceeds ~2): widen GAMMA_GRID and raise N_DKKM_FEATURES_LIST. Report the 2x2 of {old, rescaled} gamma x {old, new} DGP. Drop NMAT=1 entirely -- report the 5 draws as a spread AROUND the averaged estimator rather than replacing it.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 model-generated signals
verdicts.critique:
This manufactures a DKKM/FM gap by degrading FM and FF, and the proposer half-concedes it. Three specific problems.

(1) THE 35 CHARS ADD NO DIMENSIONS TO THE TRUTH. Every proposed transform (multi-horizon momentum, multi-horizon agr, roe moments, valuation anchors, realized vols, lags, peer-relative) is a deterministic function of the SAME 2-3 latent states already exhausted by the existing chars. In BGN the date-t cross-section is bijective in (num_i, sum_j exp(-beta_j)); in GS21 the state is (k, b, z) and bm = 1/P_ex EXACTLY. A 35-column deterministic re-encoding of a 3-dimensional state is a 3-dimensional object with 32 redundant coordinates. The true w* gains no new nonlinear content whatsoever; the population span ceiling is IDENTICAL before and after.

(2) THE PROPOSAL CONFLATES TWO DIFFERENT EFFECTIVE RANKS. DKKM Theorem 3's criterion is on EffRank(E[F F']) of the FACTOR RETURN second moment TOGETHER WITH the alignment of the risk premia across that spectrum. P3 raises the EffRank of the cross-sectional FEATURE second moment (16.5 -> ~250). Those are different objects. If the premia remain concentrated in 1-2 eigen-directions -- which they must, because the priced-risk space is still 1-2 dimensional -- then a flat feature spectrum with concentrated premia is precisely DKKM's misaligned case, in which complexity is neutral or harmful. P3 satisfies the first clause of condition (C3) and leaves the second clause untouched.

(3) FM IS SILENTLY SABOTAGED BY A NUMERICAL PATH THE PROPOSAL DOES NOT MENTION. fama_functions.py:161-163 computes P = X @ linalg.pinvh(X.T @ X) on RAW, UNSTANDARDIZED chars. With 35 highly collinear derived columns (cumret(2,6) vs cumret(7,12) vs mom; 1m/12m/36m/60m book growth) X'X becomes severely ill-conditioned and pinvh's DEFAULT rcond will truncate real directions with no warning. FM's span then collapses below its own linear ceiling and DKKM 'wins' for a floating-point reason. The proposal flags the missing standardization (lines 152-156) but not the rcond truncation, which is the larger hazard at L=35.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It produces a gap of roughly the size the proposer predicts (DKKM/FM 1.2-1.3x) and essentially ALL of it is benchmark degradation. Arithmetic: FM with K=37 factors at T=360 loses ~2K/T = 20.6% of squared Sharpe, i.e. ~11% of Sharpe, taking BGN's FM from 0.211 to ~0.188. DKKM's ridge loses less. That alone is a 1.12x ratio before any pinvh truncation, and pinvh truncation could take FM lower still. FF is worse: 35 collinear tercile long-shorts, several of them (agr and its variants) with >30% ties so the tercile split degenerates -- fama_functions.py:86-88 computes quantile(0.3) and quantile(0.7), which are EQUAL when a char is 91% zeros, producing an empty medium bucket and a 92/8 split. So FF's degradation is worse than FM's. Meanwhile the true w* is unchanged, so DKKM's cos_Sigma cannot rise. A referee who computes the population span ceiling before and after will find it identical and will correctly read the result as 'the authors added 30 noise regressors to the benchmarks.'
verdicts.salvage: Two pieces are worth keeping. (a) The FF tie-aware split guard at fama_functions.py:86-88 is a genuine bug fix independent of everything else -- agr is 91% zeros in BGN and 98.8% zeros in GS21, which currently degenerates the cma sort to a 92/8 two-bin split with an empty medium bucket. Fix it and screen every char for tie fraction, dropping anything above ~20% (rank_standardize's argsort tie-breaking at dkkm_functions.py:57 turns a 91%-tied column into a persistent pseudo-random characteristic entering all 3600 features multiplicatively). (b) The FAIRNESS repairs are mandatory regardless: delete the BGN-only rf_stand input at dkkm_functions.py:95-96, and turn on the FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156. But do NOT expand L as a route to a Sharpe gap. If you want the bandwidth effect that P3 delivers as a by-product, get it honestly through P2(a) and label it as a hyperparameter choice. The only version of P3 that would change the truth rather than the measurement is characteristics that are genuinely NON-INVERTIBLE encodings of the state -- e.g. report ONLY ratios and never levels, so the state is recoverable only from products -- and that is a different proposal (see missed ideas).

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block (raise level, dispersion, and char-nonlinearity)
verdicts.critique:
Directionally right, standalone worthless, and the BGN arithmetic is wrong -- though by luck the target is roughly hit anyway.

WHAT I VERIFIED AND CONCEDE: BGN's edit is genuinely free. panel_functions_bgn.py:151-164 sets A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values and P = G + A, with beta_avg = mean(exp(-beta)). Prices depend on beta, NEVER on sigmaj. sigmaj is drawn conditionally on beta with lower bound |beta|/sigma_z (line 52), which is exactly what enforces |corr_zj| <= 1. Widening the upper bound therefore changes idiosyncratic cash-flow risk and NOTHING else -- no re-solve, no change to the value premium, no change to the calibrated beta_star/scale. This is the cleanest edit in the whole proposal set.

THE ARITHMETIC IS WRONG. The proposal says idio vol goes 3.90% -> 3.90*sqrt(6) = 9.6%/month because mean(1-corr_zj^2) rises ~6x. I simulated the actual draw (2M samples, exact code path from lines 49-61): mean(1-c^2) goes 0.0711 -> 0.4195 (5.9x, matching), but the relevant object is the idiosyncratic LOG-variance (1-c^2)*sigmaj^2, which goes 0.181 -> 2.177 (12x), and the return-relevant object is the lognormal coefficient of variation sqrt(exp(v)-1), which goes 0.42 -> 3.63, i.e. 8.6x -- NOT sqrt(6) = 2.45x. Applying sqrt() to a variance ratio is the wrong operation on a lognormal. The saving grace: only ~0.8%/month of BGN's current 3.90% idio return vol is cash-flow risk (the shock enters returns only through free_cash_flow/P at line 166, a ~1.8% dividend yield); the other ~3.4% is project-count lumpiness from chi. So the total goes to sqrt(3.4^2 + (3.63*1.84)^2) = 7.5%/month, close to the 10% target by accident. But the resulting idiosyncratic return distribution is lognormal with log-sd ~1.48 -- extremely right-skewed and fat-tailed -- which will destabilize the 360-month rolling ridge and inflate realized-return-based metrics (HJD) far more than the population conditional Sharpe.

STANDALONE VALUE IS ZERO, AS THE PROPOSER CONCEDES. The proposal's own span2.py number: the D^{-1} tilt is worth 1.81% of SR* at N=100, 0.186% at N=1000, 0.019% at N=10000 -- and it stays worth ~nothing EVEN WITH a 20x spread in d, because idiosyncratic risk is diversifiable and the tilt only recovers the O(1/N) undiversified residual. At the production N=1000 this is 19 basis points of a 0.30/month Sharpe: 0.0006/month. Undetectable.

THE 'MAKE d NONLINEAR' RIDER IS CIRCULAR. The proposal's mechanism for nonlinear char-linkage of d is 'ride on P1's wedge, which contributes kappa^2*sigma_v^2 to d.' That is not an independent change; it is P1. Absent P1, d in all three models is a MONOTONE function of size (BGN corr(log d, log(bm/mve)) = 0.910; KP14 corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971), and a monotone function of a single sort variable is exactly what FF's tercile sorts and FM's linear span partially capture.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, not alone, and the sign is against you in the short run. Raising idio vol lowers SR* in all three models -- BGN from 0.2985 toward 0.15-0.20/month, GS21 from 0.44 toward 0.2 -- and since every method's score is SR* x cos_Sigma, every reported Sharpe falls roughly proportionally while the RATIO barely moves. FM captures the D^{-1} tilt to first order whenever log d is linear in the chars, which it is: BGN R^2(log d | deg-3 poly) = 0.984, KP14 R^2(log d | 5 raw chars linear) = 0.880. FF captures it partially via the size sort, since d ~ 1/size in KP14 and d ~ bm/mve in BGN. And the ratio alpha/d is only nonlinear to the extent that the DENOMINATOR's dispersion is large relative to its mean -- with sd(log d) rising from 0.263 to maybe 0.8, the ratio's departure from a linear function of the chars is a second-order effect worth, by span2.py's own 'linear alpha, homogeneous d' vs 'linear alpha, het d' comparison, a factor of 1.91 ON THE RATIO ONLY WHEN AN UNSPANNED ALPHA IS ALREADY PRESENT. Absent P1: 1.00.
verdicts.salvage: Do the BGN edit (panel_functions_bgn.py:54, drop the 0.1) -- it is free, price-preserving, and fixes an indefensible 96%-systematic-cash-flow calibration. But recalibrate the multiplier properly: target the CV of the idiosyncratic cash-flow multiplier, not mean(1-corr_zj^2), and consider an intermediate factor (0.3-0.5 rather than 1.0) to land idio return vol near 10%/month without a log-sd of 1.48. HOLD the KP14 and GS21 edits: KP14 cannot be recalibrated at all until integ_kp14.py:43's quadrature and the stale G_func.csv are fixed (the KP14 truth is currently a numerical artifact, and its SIGMA_EPS/SIGMA_U restoration is being sold on the grounds that it breaks idio var ~ 1/nlive -- which is right, but unverifiable while the moments are garbage); GS21 requires a MATLAB re-solve whose zgrid currently spans exactly +/-2.72 sd of the 0.1x sigma_z, so at 0.5x every interpolation extrapolates. Sequence P4 strictly AFTER P1, and report it as a multiplier with an explicit before/after on the oracle span ratio, never as a standalone result.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (scale-free pricing error, report max_sr, unconditional Sharpe, better test assets)
verdicts.critique:
This is the most valuable proposal in the set and the only one that can FALSIFY the others, but P5(a) as written has a sign bug that would be catastrophic in KP14.

P5(b) IS VERIFIED AND SHOULD SHIP TODAY. calculate_moments.py:79-86 stores max_sr in every moments dict. evaluate_sdfs.py:160-179 reads m['rp'], m['cond_var'], m['sdf_ret'] and NEVER m['max_sr']. So the single most informative number in the project -- the ceiling against which 0.2423 is either 81% or 8% -- is computed, pickled, and thrown away. Three lines. No re-run of anything.

P5(a) HAS A SIGN BUG. The proposed statistic is sqrt(1 - rho_unc^2) where rho_unc is the uncentered correlation between the method return and sdf_ret. This is derived from min over c of E[(c*y-z)^2], with c UNRESTRICTED -- so c is allowed to be NEGATIVE. A method whose portfolio is perfectly ANTI-correlated with the true HJ portfolio scores rho_unc = -1 and hence a pricing error of ZERO, i.e. 'perfect.' In KP14 every method is negatively correlated with the truth (correlations.csv: fm -0.0080, ff -0.0053, dkkm -0.0069, and MLP-fitted -0.148/-0.117/-0.122). The proposed metric would report KP14's three catastrophically wrong estimators as excellent. Fix: constrain c >= 0, or report the SIGNED rho_unc alongside, or use 1 - rho_unc*|rho_unc|. Without this, P5(a) is worse than the metric it replaces.

P5(c) IS UNDERSOLD. The Sharpe metric mean_t(w'rp_t/sqrt(w'Sigma_t w)) is homogeneous of degree ZERO in w each month (evaluate_sdfs.py:183-184 computes stdev and mean separately, and create_slides_tables forms the ratio per month before averaging). Conditional scaling is one of the TWO channels through which complexity pays in DKKM/KMZ, and this metric deletes it by construction. That is not a robustness nicety -- it means the experiment as designed is structurally incapable of observing half the theory. This should be the headline item of P5, not the third bullet.

P5(d) IS RIGHT AND CHEAP. generate_25_portfolios.py sorts on mve and bm only, which every method already spans linearly. Deciles of the TRUE w* = solve(cond_var, rp) are the right test assets and are one line from data already in the moments pickle.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, by design -- and it will most likely make DKKM look WORSE, which is the correct direction. The audit established that the current argmin-over-6-alphas on the evaluation metric is an oracle advantage available only to DKKM (ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] at config.py:187), i.e. six chances at the right leverage versus FF/FM's one. A scale-free pricing error neutralizes exactly that. Separately, reporting Sharpe/max_sr will very likely show FF at ~0.81 of the BGN ceiling (0.2423/0.2985) and DKKM at ~0.85 -- which is itself the single most persuasive result the project can produce, because it proves the estimators are near the ceiling and the DGP is the problem. That is a paper-saving diagnostic even though it is not a gap.
verdicts.salvage: Ship P5(b) and P5(d) immediately -- they require no re-simulation and P5(b) is three lines in evaluate_sdfs.py. Ship P5(c) but promote it to first place and add BOTH the unconditional Sharpe mean_t(w'rp)/sqrt(mean_t(w'Sigma w) + var_t(w'rp)) AND the median of the monthly ratio (the mean is dominated by months where the ridgeless interpolator produces a near-hedged w_t with a tiny denominator -- exactly the mechanism behind the BGN HJD of 18.52 and GS21's 23.57 at P=T=360). Fix the sign bug in P5(a) before it is used on KP14. Add one item the proposal omits: a hard GO/NO-GO gate. Before running the full pipeline on any candidate DGP change, compute mean_t SR_rff,t/SR_lin,t from the true rp and cond_var alone. That ratio is the mathematical CEILING on any DKKM-over-FM advantage; if it is below ~2, no estimator can deliver the target and the run should not be spent. Also fix the universe mismatch: evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 subsets rp and cond_var by firm_ids (prepare_panel survivors) while sdf_ret comes from moments computed over the book>0 universe -- the benchmark and the method returns are not defined over the same assets.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with heterogeneous fiscal year-ends plus heteroskedastic measurement error
verdicts.critique:
The theory in P6 is the best-argued in the set and the classical-vs-heteroskedastic EIV asymmetry is a genuine and publishable point. But the specific mechanism dies to a one-line counterargument the proposal does not address.

THE PROPOSED NONLINEARITY IS A SINGLE PRODUCT OF TWO OBSERVABLES. P6's own statement of the optimal weight is lambda(h_i) * bm_i, i.e. attenuation-times-signal. That is one bilinear term. Any econometrician handed a staleness variable h would add h and h*bm as regressors. FM's span is the column space of X = [1, chars] (fama_functions.py:161-163) and is re-fit monthly -- add h*bm as a 36th CHARACTERISTIC COLUMN and FM spans the truth EXACTLY. So P6 does not demonstrate that a rich function class is needed; it demonstrates that a specific interaction term was omitted from the benchmark. A referee will say so in one sentence, and the fix costs the benchmark one column. That is a missing-regressor result masquerading as a complexity result.

THE PROPOSAL'S OWN FF ARGUMENT IS BASED ON A CAPABILITY FF DOES NOT HAVE. P6 concedes 'FF's 2x3 design contains exactly one interaction, size x char.' It does not. fama_functions.py:99-104 computes factor = 0.5*(high_big + high_small - low_big - low_small): the two size bins are AVERAGED, so the size x char interaction is netted out and FF emits ONE size-neutralized long-short per characteristic. FF has no interaction direction at all. This cuts both ways -- it strengthens the claim that FF cannot capture lambda(h)*bm, but it also means the proposal's whole justification for choosing staleness over size as the reliability proxy (that FF would otherwise 'have been given a fair chance and used it') is based on a misreading. Choosing staleness costs FF information for no analytical reason.

MAGNITUDE IS SMALL AND MODEL-DEPENDENT. In BGN the accounting state is book = I*num, a small integer averaging 5.95 that changes only when a project is created or dies -- a 12-month-stale bm is nearly as informative as a fresh one, so the mechanism is close to inert there, as the proposal admits. In GS21 rho_z = 0.9655 gives attenuation factors from rho^6 = 0.810 to rho^17 = 0.552, a 1.47x spread. A 1.47x spread in a single multiplicative coefficient, applied to one characteristic, is worth a few percent of Sharpe at best.

SELF-DEFEATING CLASSICAL COMPONENT. The proposal's own Fourier argument -- nonlinear components attenuate as exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) while linear components attenuate only as tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2) -- means the multiplicative noise term added in step (4) directly shrinks the DKKM-reachable content. At P2's rescaled gamma of 5.1 the proposal computes its own 30% haircut. So the proposal adds a mechanism whose helpful part is one bilinear term and whose harmful part is an exponential haircut on everything DKKM uniquely reaches.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM: yes, completely, the moment h*bm (and h*roe, h*agr) are added to the char list -- which they must be, because P6 itself requires h to be an observable and it would be indefensible to give the reliability variable to DKKM's feature map but withhold its interactions from FM. There are only 4 accounting chars, so 4 interaction columns fully span the mechanism; FM goes from K=7 to K=12, a 2K/T cost of 6.7% of squared Sharpe -- trivial. FF: no, FF genuinely cannot form it (the size bins are averaged out per fama_functions.py:99-104), but as with P1 this only widens the DKKM-over-FF gap, which is a sorting artifact. Magnitude: the proposal's own estimate of 5-15% on the DKKM/FM ratio is if anything optimistic, and it explicitly notes the gap widens partly because FF/FM get WORSE from attenuation. Metric: the population conditional Sharpe measures cos_Sigma against the TRUE w*, which is unchanged by measurement (max_sr is a DGP property) -- so any observed gap here is purely a change in how well each estimator uses degraded information, i.e. an information-set result, not an economics result.
verdicts.salvage: Two things survive and both are worth doing for reasons other than the Sharpe gap. (1) BREAKING GS21's bm = 1/P_ex IDENTITY is independently mandatory. That identity holds to machine precision and is the single most indefensible feature of that panel -- four chars invert the entire 3-dimensional state, which is why the MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight and why a 6-regressor linear model is the CORRECTLY SPECIFIED model by construction. Staleness plus multiplicative noise breaks it at essentially zero cost and with zero effect on sdf_compute. Do it, and justify it as realism, not as a source of complexity gain. (2) THE EIV ASYMMETRY IS A REAL THEORETICAL CONTRIBUTION and should be written up as a proposition with the Fourier derivation, independent of whether it moves any number in the tables -- 'classical measurement error compresses the complexity advantage exponentially in frequency while compressing the linear benchmark only by the classical attenuation factor' is a clean, checkable, novel statement about when high-dimensional estimators are worth deploying. What should NOT be done is presenting lambda(h)*bm as evidence that complexity is required; add the interaction to FM's char list yourself and show whatever gap survives.

missed_ideas: RAISE THE NUMBER OF PRICED AGGREGATE SHOCKS -- the diagnosis names this as blocker #2 in every model and NOT ONE PROPOSAL IMPLEMENTS IT. Every model has 1 (GS21) or 2 (BGN, KP14) priced shocks and, in KP14, beta_x = 1 for EVERY firm exactly (price = VAP + PVGO is homogeneous of degree 1 in x, panel_functions_kp14.py:165,173, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 factors Et_x2 out of the whole cross-firm block). This is the ONLY change that satisfies both clauses of DKKM's condition C3 -- it raises EffRank(E[FF']) AND spreads the risk premia across the spectrum, which is what P3's char expansion conspicuously fails to do. Concretely and cheaply: in GS21 replace the scalar x with J=20-50 sector shocks, assign each firm a sparse loading vector drawn at birth, and price all J. Firms then differ in WHICH risks they bear, not just how much, and the true MVE is a J-dimensional rotation that no 7-factor OLS can find. Cost: the GS21 solve is per-(z,x,b) so a J-dimensional x is expensive -- but a two-block version (J=2 orthogonal aggregate shocks with heterogeneous loadings) is nearly free and would already double the systematic rank, which is currently exactly 1 (top eigenvalue 97.3% of total variance).

MAKE THE FACTOR LOADING NON-MONOTONE IN A CHARACTERISTIC. Every proposal adds nonlinearity as a RATIO or a PRODUCT, both of which linear regression approximates well over the realized range. The one functional form that FM and FF provably cannot represent is NON-MONOTONICITY: FM applies one signed coefficient per char, and a tercile long-short is by construction monotone in the sort variable -- it will SHORT exactly the firms whose alpha is largest if the relationship humps. Structural sources are standard and defensible: financial-constraint models generate risk exposure that is hump-shaped in leverage (unconstrained firms and hopeless firms both have low exposure, marginal firms have high); real-options models generate exposure hump-shaped in moneyness. In GS21 this is nearly free -- the default boundary is supposed to supply exactly this kink and currently supplies nothing (ZERO defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months, min realized P = 30.4, z_cut_down pinned at the grid floor everywhere). Making default a live event is the single most economically defensible way to get a non-monotone loading, and it is a recalibration of a model that already has the machinery.

MAKE THE STATE-TO-CHARACTERISTIC MAP NON-INVERTIBLE SO RECOVERY REQUIRES A PRODUCT. Far cheaper than P3's 35 columns and it changes the truth rather than the measurement. If the econometrician sees only RATIOS (bm, roe, agr) and never levels, then a state variable that enters multiplicatively can be recovered only from a product of two chars. Currently the opposite holds: GS21's four chars invert (k,b,z) exactly, and BGN's (size, bm) recover (book, mve) to machine precision. Deleting or coarsening ONE char so the state becomes recoverable only through interactions is a one-line change to MODEL_CHARS at config.py:318-320 that raises the required function class without touching any DGP, any solve, or any benchmark's fairness.

CHARACTERISTIC x MACRO-STATE INTERACTION COLUMNS. The diagnosis names time-varying prices of risk as blocker #6 and notes that KP14 and GS21 have NO time-varying input to the feature map at all (the ridge coefficient is one vector estimated on 360 months and applied unchanged to every cross-section). No proposal fixes this. A date-level macro state is invisible to every cross-sectional weight -- it must enter as char x macro columns available to ALL THREE methods. This multiplies the effective dimension of the truth without adding a single latent state, and it directly activates the conditional-timing channel that P5(c) points out is currently deleted by the metric. Note also that BGN's rf_stand (dkkm_functions.py:95-96) is a broken attempt at exactly this: it is appended raw, acts as a per-feature phase shift of sd ~0.19 rad, and is annihilated by the second rank-standardization for 65.6% of sin features -- it is simultaneously unfair (FF/FM never see it) and worthless (span 89.9% with vs 90.1% without).

A HEAVIER-TAILED SIZE DISTRIBUTION AND FIRM ENTRY/EXIT. DKKM's own decomposition says the real-data SDF Sharpe falls from 3.7 full-sample to ~1.6 in mega/large caps -- most of the virtue of complexity lives in microcaps. GS21 has sd(log mve) = 0.285 against ~2.0 in CRSP, and log capital is a pure Bernoulli random walk with zero defaults, so the size cross-section is non-stationary and grows as sqrt(t) rather than reaching a steady state. N is fixed at 1000 with no entry or exit in all three models. A fat-tailed, stationary size distribution widens the range over which every char-dependent function must be approximated, which is exactly where a linear model fails and a flexible one does not -- and it is a calibration target, not a modelling innovation. No proposal touches the size distribution; P4 changes idiosyncratic volatility, which is a different object.

REPRODUCE THE PUBLISHED REAL-DATA RESULT WITH THIS CODEBASE BEFORE CHANGING ANY MODEL. DKKM report FF6 = 0.74 -> complex 1.93-2.50 using exactly the five characteristics this project uses, the same gamma grid, the same [-0.5,0.5] rank-standardization, and T=360. If this repo's dkkm_functions.py cannot reproduce that on real CRSP/Compustat data, the problem is the estimator (double rank-standardization, NMAT=5, the alpha grid hole, c capped at 10) and no amount of model surgery will help. If it CAN, then every subsequent null result is attributable to the DGP and the paper's argument is airtight. This is the cheapest decisive experiment available and nobody proposed it.

VARY T. DKKM's condition (C5) requires T to be small relative to the true model dimension -- otherwise the correctly-specified small model, precisely estimated, simply wins. DKKM themselves report that T=120 still gives complex 1.9 vs best simple 1.1. T is a free knob (the 360-month rolling window at dkkm_functions.py:287 and fama_functions.py:265) that directly tests the limits-to-learning channel with zero economics and zero re-simulation. Currently FF/FM at K=7, T=360 lose only 2K/T = 3.9% of squared Sharpe, i.e. they sit at their population optimum with nothing for shrinkage to buy back. Shortening the window is the one-line way to make estimation genuinely hard.

UNBOUNDED / HEAVY-TAILED FEATURES, OR A DIFFERENT ACTIVATION. Every proposal that relies on the true w* being large on a subset of firms (P1's hump, P4's 1/d tilt, KP14's 1/d ~ nlive^0.87) collides with the fact that sin and cos are BOUNDED and dkkm_functions.py:110 forces every column to the identical bounded uniform marginal. P2's z-score fix does not help: |sin| <= 1 regardless. Producing a weight 100x larger on 1% of firms from bounded features requires an RKHS norm that ridge is explicitly penalizing, so the estimator is structurally barred from the shape several proposals are trying to create. Fixes nobody proposed: include the raw chars and their pairwise products UNPENALIZED alongside the RFF block; add a ReLU or tanh block (DKKM report 3.0-3.5 with those activations); or add explicit 1/d-type unbounded columns. This is a real internal contradiction in the proposal set and it should be resolved before P1 or P4 is run.

MAKE FIXING KP14's CORRUPT TRUTH A FIRST-CLASS DELIVERABLE, NOT A RISK BULLET. integ_kp14.py:43 calls quad(integrand, 0, 10, ...) against a CIR transition density with sd ~0.006 and returns EXACT ZEROS over the entire eps interval where 98% of firm-months live; G_func.csv was solved under the pre-Jun-18 parameters and is 49x off; and kp14_fd.py:7 does 'from parameters_kp14 import *', a module absent from the repo, so the solfiles cannot be regenerated. One third of the paper's evidence is therefore uninterpretable -- KP14's rp is literally minus the PVGO share (R^2 = 0.90, slope -0.95), its max_sr is 34.7 annualized against the model's own correct bound of 0.774, and its negative Sharpes for all three methods are an artifact. Every proposal mentions this in passing and none owns it. It should be a prerequisite with a named owner and an acceptance test (rp mean within 10% of gamma_x*sigma_x + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*E[share] = 8.69%/yr), because until it is fixed, no KP14 verdict on any proposal means anything.

REPORT THE ORACLE COMPLEXITY CURVE, NOT JUST THE ORACLE SPAN RATIO. Compute the population ceiling max_a SR(S_t a) at P = 36, 360, 3600, 36000 using the true rp and cond_var. If that ORACLE curve is flat in P, the estimated curve will be flat no matter what is done to the ridge, the bandwidth, or NMAT -- and the project can stop tuning the estimator immediately. This costs one script against data already in the moments pickles and it distinguishes 'the basis cannot reach the truth' (P2's story) from 'there is no truth to reach' (H1's story), which is the single unresolved question separating the proposals.

proposals.name: Repair the KP14 'truth': regenerate integ_results.npz and G_func.csv, and fix the H/L regime convention
proposals.one_line: The shipped quadrature file returns exactly 0 for E_t[G] over the entire eps region the panel occupies, so every reported KP14 number (rp, cond_var, max_sr, sdf_ret, the 'true SDF weights') is a numerical artifact — nothing can be evaluated until this is fixed.
proposals.economic_story: This is not an economic change, it is a precondition. KP14's economics are that assets in place earn gamma_x*sigma_x = 8.97%/yr and growth options earn 8.97 - alph*|gamma_z*sigma_z| = 2.03%/yr, so the true cross-section is rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*(PVGO_i/P_i) with a 6.94%/yr AIP-vs-growth-option spread. Right now the code delivers rp_i = -PVGO_i/P_i (R^2=0.90 on the PVGO share, slope -0.95), mean -38.5%/yr with the WRONG SIGN and a cross-sectional sd 173x the correct value, because term2 (the PVGO continuation value, panel_functions_kp14.py:193) is multiplied by E_t[G] ~ 1e-53. That, and not any economic feature, is what produces the negative Sharpes (-2.64 FF, -5.35 FM) and max_sr = 34.66/yr against the model's own HJ bound of 0.774/yr. A referee reading the current KP14 table is reading noise.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: No direct DKKM gain — this proposal buys correctness, not headroom, and I say so explicitly. Its indirect mechanisms: (i) it restores PVGO/P from 0.040 to ~0.55 (see arithmetic), which restores beta_z = alph*share to a real second factor with p10-p90 premium spread ~2.7%/yr instead of 0.48%/yr; (ii) it flips rp positive so that the Sharpe metric SR = SR* x cos_Sigma(w, w*) stops being dominated by a sign flip and the DKKM/FF/FM ordering becomes interpretable; (iii) every other proposal below is scored against these true moments, so all of them are uninterpretable without it.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Not applicable — this is a bug fix, not a source of DKKM advantage. Stated honestly: on its own this proposal will NOT create a DKKM-over-FF/FM gap. After the fix, PVGO share is still (to first order) an exact affine function of book-to-market — I verified VAP_i/book_i = (1/alpha) x [K-weighted mean of z_t*A(eps_t,u_j)/(z_{t_j}*A(eps_{t_j},1))] with cross-sectional sd of only 3.2% of its mean (measured: mean 1.2489, sd 0.0401 at N=200, t=210, vs 1/alpha = 1.1765). So share_i = 1 - v_i*bm_i with v_i almost constant, beta_z is affine in bm, and FM spans it exactly. Expect FF ~ FM ~ DKKM after this fix, all with SHARPE ~0.15-0.22/month and the right sign.
proposals.exact_change:
(a) utils_kp14/integ_kp14.py:43 — replace `quad(lambda ep: integrand(fun, ep), 0, eps_max, epsabs=1e-10, epsrel=1e-10, limit=500)[0]` with a quantile-anchored quadrature that cannot miss the CIR transition spike: build nodes `eps_nodes = c * ncx2.ppf(np.linspace(1e-9, 1-1e-9, 20001), d, lam)` and integrate f against the uniform weights (i.e. E[f] = mean(f(eps_nodes))); add `assert abs(np.trapz(ncx2.pdf(eps_nodes/c,d,lam)/c, eps_nodes) - 1) < 1e-8`. Root cause verified: with sigma_eps=0.02 and dt=1/12 the transition density has sd ~0.006 on [0,10], so Gauss-Kronrod on [0,10] never samples the spike and returns 0 with a ~0 error estimate. I confirmed this directly: at eps=1.00 the file's E_t[G_up] is 6.6e-53 while G_up(1.00) itself is 1621; the file only becomes correct for eps >= 1.049 (file 1701 vs G_up 1704), and the simulated panel lives at eps = 1.000 +/- 0.024.
(b) utils_kp14/kp14_fd.py:7 and utils_kp14/integ_kp14.py:6 — `from parameters_kp14 import *` refers to a module that does not exist in this repo, which is why the solfiles were never regenerated after commit 77c5ffc cut SIGMA_EPS/SIGMA_U 10x and halved GAMMA_X. Add utils_kp14/parameters_kp14.py as a 15-line shim re-exporting the KP14_* names from config.py under the short names (dt, mu_x, sigma_eps, theta_eps, rho, alpha, C, A, A_0..A_3, mu_H, mu_L, lambda_H, lambda_L). Then re-run kp14_fd.py, then integ_kp14.py, and overwrite utils_kp14/KP14_solfiles/{G_func.csv, integ_results.npz}.
(c) utils_kp14/panel_functions_kp14.py:98 — change `switch_prob = np.where(curr == 1, mu_H*dt, mu_L*dt)` to `np.where(curr == 1, mu_L*dt, mu_H*dt)`. config.py:257 defines LAMBDA_L = (1 - w*LAMBDA_H)/(1-w) with w = MU_H/(MU_H+MU_L) = 0.3191, and kp14_fd.py:100-101 weights G2 consistently with P(high)=0.3191; only the simulation is inverted. Verified: with w=0.6809 the normalization gives LAMBDA_L = (1-0.6809*2.35)/0.3191 = -1.880, i.e. negative, which is impossible — so 0.3191 is the intended convention and the sim is the error.
(d) config.py:263 — `KP14_PROB_H = KP14_MU_H / (KP14_MU_H + KP14_MU_L)` (0.3191), to match (c).
(e) utils_kp14/sdf_compute_kp14.py:291,299 return the FULL cond_var and rp including the ~5% of firms with zero live projects (rp = -1.0 exactly). Mask those rows/cols to NaN so evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 cannot silently include them via a firm_ids mismatch.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: No new parameters. Consequences, derived: the current unconditional arrival multiplier is 0.6809*2.35 + 0.3191*0.36719 = 1.7172 instead of the intended 1.000, so fix (c)/(d) shrinks lambda by 42%. Fixing (a)/(b) raises G by ~49x. Net PVGO scaling = 49*0.582 = 28.5x. Current PVGO/P = 0.0403 on kept firms, so VAP/P = 0.9597 and share_new = 28.5*0.0403/(0.9597 + 28.5*0.0403) = 1.149/2.108 = 0.545. Value premium spread at that share: alph*|gamma_z*sigma_z| * (p90-p10 of share) = 0.0694 * 0.384 = 2.67%/yr if sd(share)=0.15. Correct max Sharpe = sqrt(gamma_x^2 + gamma_z^2)/sqrt(12) = 0.774/3.464 = 0.223/month.
proposals.predicted_effect: DKKM Sharpe: from -0.60 to about +0.15/month. FF: from -2.64 to about +0.15/month. FM: from -5.35 to about +0.16/month. max_sr: from 10.0/month to 0.223/month. HJD: from ~0.38-0.61 (all clustered at the sdf_ret RMS floor of 0.269) to a floor of Rf*SR*/sqrt(1+SR*^2) = 1.006*0.223/1.024 = 0.219, with a genuine ~27% dynamic range between zero-skill and perfect. DKKM-vs-FF/FM gap: essentially unchanged at ~1.0x. This proposal makes the table honest, not favourable.
risks: Regenerating G_func.csv under the CURRENT parameters raises G by ~49x (I verified the file matches a pre-Jun-18 solve with gamma_x=1.38, sigma_eps=0.2, rho=0.10545 to within 1.5%). PVGO/P will jump to ~0.5, which changes every characteristic's distribution and every downstream table. Every previously-run KP14 result becomes non-comparable.

With rho = 0.015753 at the current alpha=0.85 the growth-option Feynman-Kac operator is only 1.6%/yr away from the transversality boundary rho=0 (which sits at gamma_z = -0.4294, see Proposal 2's arithmetic). The FD solve at 1000 grid points may be badly conditioned; check that kp14_fd.py's fixed-point iteration converges to <1e-8 and that G is monotone and positive on [0.01,5].

integ_kp14.py loops 11 functions x 1000 grid points; with a 20001-node quantile grid that is 2.2e8 evaluations of interpolated splines. Vectorize over nodes (one interp1d call per function per grid point) or it will take hours.
Fix (c) changes which regime is the majority state, which changes the firm-size distribution and the lambda_f-to-size mapping; the burn-in of 200 months may need lengthening.
proposals.implementation_cost: Zero cost to sdf_compute's O(N^2)/month inner loop — the analytic second-moment structure (sdf_compute_kp14.py:138-229) is untouched; only the values in the eleven interpolants at lines 61-71 change. One-off re-solve: kp14_fd.py is a 1000-point sparse fixed point (seconds); integ_kp14.py is embarrassingly parallel over the eps grid (minutes if vectorized).

proposals.name: Investment-specific technology SPACE: replace the scalar IST shock z by K priced technology-domain shocks over an observable 2-D technology map
proposals.one_line: Make z a K-dimensional, spatially-correlated field over an observable technology coordinate theta_i, with domain-specific prices of risk gamma_k — turning KP14's single priced growth-option factor into ~100 priced factors whose loadings are share_i x bump_k(theta_i), a product no linear-in-characteristics rule can form.
proposals.economic_story: KP14's z is investment-specific technological change, identified empirically from the relative price of equipment. It is a stylized fact — not a stretch — that IST progress is domain-specific: semiconductors, communications equipment, industrial machinery, biotech instrumentation and structures have wildly different equipment-price trends and different exposures to the same innovations (Papanikolaou 2011; Kogan-Papanikolaou-Stoffman; Greenwood-Hercowitz-Krusell's equipment-price series is a weighted average of exactly such components). Firms hold growth options in a technology neighbourhood, and technologically proximate firms' options move together (Hoberg-Phillips TNIC, Bloom-Schankerman-Van Reenen technology space, Lee-Sun-Wang-Zhang technology links). Whether an IST innovation in a domain is good or bad news for the incumbents holding options there — cost reduction vs. creative destruction — differs by domain, so the price of risk gamma_k differs by domain. The scalar-z KP14 is the K=1 special case. This is the single most defensible way to raise the number of priced aggregate shocks from 2 to ~100 while leaving KP14's identity (growth options load on IST, assets in place load on neutral productivity) completely intact.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: With K priced IST factors the true conditional MVE weight is w*_i = [gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*share_i*sigma_z*(p(theta_i) . c_t)] / d_i, where p(theta_i) in R^K is the firm's technology loading vector and c_t is a month-specific K-vector determined by the realized cross-section. So the priced part of w* is share_i x g_t(theta_i) / d_i with g_t(.) = p(.) . c_t an arbitrary smooth function on the technology torus with ~K degrees of freedom. The attainable Sharpe of any estimator whose stock-weight function lies in a function class F is SR^2 = gamma_x^2 + sum_k gamma_k^2 x (fraction of R^K reachable), and the reachable fraction is (number of independent modes of g that F can express)/K. Formally: the map a -> exposure vector e_k = sum_i w_a(x_i) alph share_i sigma_z p_ik has rank equal to dim(F restricted to functions of theta, times share). FM has rank ~3 ({1, theta1, theta2} — it can multiply by bm, which is affine in share, but cannot multiply by a nonlinear function of theta). DKKM's RFF spans smooth functions of all 7 characteristics jointly, so it reaches all quadratic (6) modes at the coded bandwidth and ~45 modes with the bandwidth rescaled. This is a first-order (not O(1/N)) loss for FM: it is a loss of factor Sharpe, not of diversification.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's investable set each month is exactly {X_t a : a in R^{L+1}} with X_t = [1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom, theta1, theta2] (fama_functions.py:158-160 builds P = X pinvh(X'X) on raw chars), i.e. its stock-weight FUNCTION is a fixed LINEAR functional of the characteristics, identical in every month. It therefore cannot produce share_i x g(theta_i) for any nonconstant g, and cannot produce any nonlinear function of theta at all. The image of its exposure map in R^K is a subspace of dimension at most L+1 = 8; with K=100 it can harvest at most 8/100 of sum_k gamma_k^2 outside the common direction. FF is strictly worse: fama_functions.py:82-104 builds, per characteristic, a value-weighted 2x3 tercile double sort with size, so its weight function is mve_i x (piecewise-constant on a 2x3 grid of (size-tercile-of-median-split, char-tercile)). It contains size x char interactions and nothing else — no theta1 x theta2 interaction, no share x theta interaction, and only tercile resolution in theta (2 modes). Its exposure-map rank is 7. Neither can express a product of two non-size characteristics, which is the minimum requirement here.

proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation:
BUMP NORMALIZATION. With Gaussian bumps phi_k(theta)=exp(-||theta-c_k||_torus^2/(2h^2)) on a 2-D torus with K=1/h^2 centers, sum_k phi_k -> (1/h^2)(2 pi h^2) = 2 pi and sum_k phi_k^2 -> (1/h^2)(pi h^2) = pi, so with L2-normalized loadings p = phi/||phi||_2 the quantity q = sum_k p_k = 2*pi/sqrt(pi) = 2*sqrt(pi) = 3.5449, independent of K and h. I verified numerically: K=100,h=0.10 gives q = 3.54490 +/- 0.00019 across 20,000 random theta; K=64,h=0.125 gives 3.54452. L2 normalization is what preserves each firm's own z process EXACTLY as in the current model (drift mu_z, vol sigma_z), which is what keeps A_0..A_3, C and the eps machinery untouched.
FIRM-LEVEL PRICE OF IST RISK. Firm i's effective price is g_i = p(theta_i).gamma, with mean q*GAMMA_Z_BAR and sd SIGMA_GAMMA_Z (since ||p||_2 = 1). Set the mean to -0.175, i.e. HALF of KP14's -0.35, which preserves the sign and the economics of the value premium while buying transversality headroom. Hence GAMMA_Z_BAR = -0.175/3.5449 = -0.049366. Set SIGMA_GAMMA_Z = 0.30, i.e. the cross-domain dispersion of IST risk prices is 1.7x their mean level, so ~28% of technology domains carry a positive IST premium (creative-destruction domains). 
TRANSVERSALITY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND IS WHY ALPHA MUST FALL. rho_i = r + gamma_x sigma_x - mu_x - alph(mu_z - g_i sigma_z - 0.5 sigma_z^2) - 0.5 alph^2 sigma_z^2 (config.py:270-272), which I evaluate as rho(g) = base + alph*sigma_z*g. At alpha=0.85 (alph=5.667): rho = 0.085169 + 0.198333 g, so rho = 0 at g = -0.4294 — only 0.079 below the current gamma_z = -0.35. ANY meaningful cross-domain dispersion blows up the growth-option value. At alpha=0.80 (alph=4): rho = 0.10235 + 0.14 g, zero at g = -0.7311. At alpha=0.75 (alph=3): rho = 0.111025 + 0.105 g, zero at g = -1.0574. With mean -0.175 and sd 0.30 truncated at 2.5 sd, the worst firm has g = -0.925 and rho = 0.0139 > 0. SAFE. alpha=0.75 is well inside the empirical range for returns to scale (Basu-Fernald, Cooper-Haltiwanger report 0.7-0.9); alph = alpha/(1-alpha) falls from 5.667 to 3.000 and KP14_C = alpha^{1/(1-alpha)}(1/alpha - 1) from 0.05972 to 0.10547.
RESULTING SHARPE ACCOUNTING (annualized, K=100). Total: SR*^2 = gamma_x^2 + K(GAMMA_Z_BAR^2 + SIGMA_GAMMA_Z^2) = 0.4761 + 100(0.002437 + 0.09) = 9.720, SR* = 3.118/yr = 0.900/month. This lands exactly on DKKM's real-data attainable Sharpe of 3.7. The 'common' IST direction K*GAMMA_Z_BAR^2 = 0.244 is spanned by everyone; the unspanned budget is K*SIGMA_GAMMA_Z^2 = 9.00. FM (m=3 theta-modes): SR = sqrt(0.4761+0.244+0.03*9.00) = 0.995/yr = 0.319 of SR* — right on top of FF6's real-data 0.74-1.2. DKKM at the CODED bandwidth (effective dictionary rank ~16, giving ~6 quadratic theta-modes): SR = 1.122/yr = 0.360 of SR*. DKKM with GAMMA_GRID rescaled by sqrt(130/7)=4.31 (effective rank ~78, ~45 theta-modes): SR = 2.184/yr = 0.701 of SR*.
WHY K MUST BE LARGE. I checked the small-K version: K=6 with a 1-D theta gives SR* = 1.03/yr, FM 0.841, DKKM-coded 0.942 — a 1.12x gap. The gap scales as sqrt(m_DKKM/m_FM) and needs K >> L to open up. K=100 on 1000 firms leaves ~10 firms per cell but ~30-50 within one bandwidth, so each domain's mimicking portfolio diversifies idio risk from 5%/mo to ~0.9%/mo against a factor exposure of alph*share*sigma_z/sqrt(12) = 3*0.5*0.035/3.464 = 1.5%/mo — 74% systematic, so the factors are genuinely spannable. K=64 (h=0.125) is the safer choice if N is ever reduced.
proposals.predicted_effect: DKKM Sharpe 0.32/month (coded bandwidth) or 0.63/month (bandwidth rescaled); FF/FM 0.29/month; max_sr 0.90/month. DKKM/FM ratio: 1.13x at the coded bandwidth, 2.19x with GAMMA_GRID rescaled by 4.31. The model change creates the headroom; the estimator change realizes it. Both are required. proposals.name: Historical-cost book value plus the characteristics KP14 already generates (capital vintage/age, project count, cash-flow volatility, investment intensity)
proposals.one_line: Stop marking book equity to current replacement cost — record it at the historical prices actually paid — and add the vintage, count and volatility characteristics the state already contains, so that PVGO share becomes bm x g(age) rather than an exact affine function of bm.
proposals.economic_story: panel_functions_kp14.py:144 sets book = (x_t/z_t) * sum_j K_j, i.e. it revalues every project's capital at TODAY'S investment price. Real book equity is historical cost: the firm records what it paid, which is exactly the cash outflow the model already writes down at line 157, -K_j * x_{t_j}/z_{t_j}. The gap between the two is the source of a large fraction of the real value premium's information content (Fama-French have always argued B/M works partly because book is a stale, historical-cost anchor; the whole 'q vs. B/M' literature is about this wedge). Making book historical-cost simultaneously (i) makes bm a mixture of value and capital vintage rather than a pure valuation ratio, and (ii) makes capital age a genuinely informative, separately observable characteristic — which is exactly what it is in real data (accumulated depreciation / gross PP&E is a standard char). The other three additions are quantities the model already simulates: number of live projects (segment/establishment count), trailing investment intensity (R&D + capex over assets, the observable proxy for lambda_f and the H/L arrival regime), and trailing cash-flow volatility (the observable proxy for d_i).
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: I verified the current identity numerically: VAP_i/book_i = (1/alpha) x [K-weighted mean over projects of z_t A(eps_t,u_j)/(z_{t_j} A(eps_{t_j},1))], measured mean 1.2489 with cross-sectional sd 0.0401 — only 3.2% dispersion. Hence share_i = 1 - v_i * bm_i with v_i almost constant, so beta_z = alph*share is an AFFINE function of bm and FM spans the entire z-channel exactly. Under historical-cost book, v_i acquires the extra factor (x_t/z_t)/(K-weighted mean of x_{t_j}/z_{t_j}), whose log has cross-firm sd approximately sd(log(x/z) increment) x sqrt(E[age]) / sqrt(n_eff) = 0.1346 x sqrt(10) / sqrt(6) = 0.174 — a 5.4x increase in the multiplicative wedge, and one whose cross-firm variation is driven by capital AGE, which is now an observable characteristic. So beta_z,i = alph*(1 - bm_i * exp(c0 + c1*age_i + eta_i)): a product of bm with a nonlinear function of age. The true MVE weight inherits it. Separately, cfvol makes 1/d_i learnable directly rather than only through size, which is what the D^{-1} tilt needs to be a multiplier on the unspanned premium in Proposals 2 and 6.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: The required object is bm_i x exp(c1 * age_i), a product of two NON-SIZE characteristics. FM produces only a0 + a1*bm + a2*age + ...; the bilinear term bm*age is orthogonal to its span by construction (its span is literally the column space of [1, chars], fama_functions.py:158-160). FF's 2x3 sorts (fama_functions.py:80-104) form exactly one interaction — size x char — because `big`/`small` come from the size median split at line 70 and are crossed with each char's terciles one at a time; there is no age x bm portfolio anywhere in the seven columns, and adding age as a seventh char produces an age-vs-size sort, not an age-vs-value sort. DKKM's RFF, even at the coded bandwidth where sd(Wx) = 0.53 and the dictionary is ~86% quadratic in the chars, contains every pairwise product including bm x age. This is the one nonlinearity that the CURRENT estimator configuration can already reach, which is why this proposal has the best impact-per-line of any economic change here.

proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: No new economic parameters at all. The magnitude follows from the existing calibration. Project age is Exponential with rate delta = 0.1, so E[age] = 10 years and the log investment-price ratio log(x_t/z_t) - log(x_{t_j}/z_{t_j}) has vol sqrt(sigma_x^2 + sigma_z^2) = sqrt(0.13^2 + 0.035^2) = 0.1346/yr, giving a per-project sd of 0.1346*sqrt(10) = 0.426 in logs. Averaging over n_eff ~ 6 live projects (measured mean nlive 6.14, sd 4.32 at N=200) gives firm-level sd 0.426/sqrt(6) = 0.174. Non-affine-in-bm component of beta_z = alph x bm_bar x v_bar x 0.174 = 3.0 x 0.4 x 1.25 x 0.174 = 0.26 (at alpha=0.75, post-Proposal-1), translating into an expected-return dispersion of 0.26 x |gamma_z sigma_z| = 0.26 x 0.006125 = 0.16%/yr from the pure vintage channel alone. To actually amplify it you must raise the age DISPERSION across firms rather than the mean, which is done by raising sigma_lambda (arrival-rate heterogeneity) so that some firms are dominated by one old vintage and others by many young ones. HJD and max_sr are essentially unchanged because nothing about the true moments changes — this proposal only alters what the ESTIMATORS see. That is also its strongest defence: it cannot corrupt the truth.

That is a modest and favourable side effect but it changes every DKKM number, so it must not be confounded with the economic change — run the L=5 and L=9 char sets as separate arms.

proposals.name: Firm-level, non-diversifying productivity risk: recalibrate theta_eps/sigma_eps and the project count so idiosyncratic variance stops being 1/size
proposals.one_line: Make the firm-level eps process persistent and volatile enough to dominate Poisson project-count lumpiness, so that d_i is no longer mechanically proportional to 1/n_live ~ 1/size and the true MVE weight stops being a value-weighted market portfolio in disguise.
proposals.economic_story: This is the head-on answer to the size artifact. eps is the FIRM-level productivity shock and u is the PROJECT-level shock. After the Jun-18 10x cut, the CIR shocks contribute only 2.2% of idiosyncratic return variance (was 69.2%) and 97.8% comes from independent Bernoulli project deaths and arrivals. Because death is a Poisson thinning over the firm's live projects, that residual variance scales as 1/n_live, and n_live IS size (I measured corr(log nlive, log mve) = 0.9871). So d_i ~ 1/size mechanically, 1/d_i ~ size, and w* = Sigma^{-1}mu collapses onto a size-weighted portfolio that ANTI-correlates with the empirical size premium — with no sign bug anywhere. Economically the current calibration says firm-level productivity is essentially deterministic and all firm risk is 'did a plant close this month', which is indefensible: measured firm TFP is highly persistent (annual AR(1) of 0.90-0.95, i.e. theta = -log(0.92) = 0.083/yr, not the coded 0.35) and its within-industry cross-sectional dispersion is large (Syverson 2011: 90-10 TFP ratios near 2, sd(log TFP) ~ 0.3-0.6). The current theta_eps = 0.35 and sigma_eps = 0.02 give a stationary sd(eps) of 0.0239 — a firm-level productivity dispersion of 2.4%, which is off by more than an order of magnitude.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Two channels, and I am honest that the direct one is weak. (i) DIRECT, WEAK: making d_i dispersed and char-linked makes w*_i = numerator_i/d_i a genuine ratio. But under exact K-factor pricing the D^{-1} tilt is worth only 1/(2 sigma_f^2 beta'D^{-1}beta) = O(1/N) of SR* — the diagnosis-phase span experiment measured 0.19% at N=1000 even with d spanning a 20x range. So this buys almost nothing on its own. (ii) INDIRECT, STRONG: heteroskedastic, char-linked D is a MULTIPLIER on any unspanned premium. In the population span experiment, adding d ~ exp(6 x2) raised the RFF-over-linear ceiling from 1.00 to 1.91 in the presence of a LINEAR unspanned alpha and from 2.88 to 6.37 with a nonlinear one, and cut the linear span's share of SR* from 1.00 to 0.31. The reason is that 1/d = exp(-linear-in-chars) is a convex function that FM cannot form even when log d is perfectly linear in chars, and the curvature bites in proportion to sd(log d). So the value of this proposal is entirely conditional on Proposal 2 or 6 being adopted.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Even in the best case for FM, where log d_i is exactly linear in the characteristics (measured R^2 = 0.880 on the 5 raw chars), the object FM needs is 1/d_i = exp(-b'x_i), and FM's span is {a'x}. The best linear approximation to exp(-b'x) over a distribution with sd(b'x) = s has relative L2 error 1 - (s^2 e^{-s^2}... ) rising steeply in s: at the current sd(log d) = 0.664 the linear approximation loses ~5% of the variance of 1/d; at sd(log d) = 1.0 (the real-data value) it loses ~13%; at 1.3 it loses ~21%. FF is worse still: its weight function is mve_i x (2x3 step function), so it can only produce a step approximation to 1/d and, critically, mve_i multiplies EVERY column — FF's weights are structurally proportional to size, which is the very artifact this proposal is trying to remove. DKKM's RFF spans smooth convex functions of the chars directly.

WHY mu_lambda = sigma_lambda = 8. Steady-state live projects = (unconditional arrival multiplier) x lambda_f / delta. With lambda_f = delta*(mu_lambda - sigma_lambda*log U), E[lambda_f] = delta*(mu_lambda + sigma_lambda) = 0.1*16 = 1.6/yr and (after the Proposal 1 regime fix) the multiplier is 1.0, so E[n] = 1.6/0.1 = 16, up from the measured 6.14. The Poisson component of idiosyncratic variance falls by sqrt(16/6.14) = 1.61x, from 4.69%/month to 2.91%/month.

Make sigma_eps itself heterogeneous across firms: sigma_eps,i drawn from a 7-point grid spanning [0.09, 0.36] (a 4x range in vol, 16x in variance, matching real sd(log idio variance) of ~1.0), assigned independently of lambda_f and hence of size, and reported as the observable char cfvol from Proposal 3. Then the non-diversifying variance component varies 16x across firms ORTHOGONALLY to size, corr(log d, log size) falls to roughly -0.4, and 1/d becomes a genuinely char-linked convex function. Combined with Proposal 2, expect it to add 20-40% on top of Proposal 2's DKKM/FM ratio (2.19x -> 2.6-3.0x), by the heteroskedastic-D multiplier effect measured in the span experiment.
risks: Raising sigma_eps 9x and lowering theta_eps 3.5x pushes eps far from 1, and A(eps,u) = A_0 + (eps-1)A_1 + (u-1)A_2 + (eps-1)(u-1)A_3 is a LINEAR approximation in (eps-1),(u-1). With sd(eps)=0.40 and sd(u)=0.45 and A_1/A_0 = 0.697, A can go NEGATIVE for eps below about 1 - 1/0.697 = -0.43 — safe for eps but check A(eps,u) > 0 over the realized joint support, because K_j = (alpha z A(eps,1))^{1/(1-alpha)} takes a fractional power of it.

The 10x cut was presumably made for a reason (the memory note records that removing the diagonal variance excess made cond_var near-singular). Reversing it changes the conditioning of ER: I would expect it to IMPROVE (the diagnosis measured cond(cond_var) = 680 now vs 165 with the 10x sigmas), but verify the scipy.linalg.solve(..., assume_a='pos') call at sdf_compute_kp14.py:275-277 still succeeds every month.

Larger sigma_eps makes eps a bigger driver of d_i, and eps is only 5.6% linearly / 15% quadratically recoverable from the characteristics. That fraction of the variation in d is pure unlearnable noise for EVERY estimator and dilutes the DKKM advantage. This is why the heterogeneous-sigma_eps,i version (reported as cfvol) matters more than the level change.
