When log d is linear in x, FM's shortfall is only the curvature of exp(-b'x), which at sd(log d) = 1.0 is ~13% of the variance of 1/d — and a referee will simply ask you to add exp of the fitted linear index, or a squared term, to the FM design. Separately: the proposal's headline extension (heterogeneous sigma_eps,i on a 7-point grid, reported as cfvol) is the part that would actually break the size link, and it requires solving G and eleven integrals on a 7-node sigma grid on top of Proposal 2's 20-node rho grid — 140 solves. That is real machinery introduced to move a ratio by 2%.
verdicts.salvage: Split it. (a) Adopt a MINIMAL version framed purely as a bug correction rather than a recalibration: the current calibration makes 98% of firm risk 'did a plant close', which is indefensible on its face, so restore sigma_eps and sigma_u to their pre-Jun-18 values (i.e. delete the two `0.1*` factors at config.py:248 and 250) and STOP. One change, one sentence, no new literature citations, and it demonstrably improves the conditioning of cond_var (680 -> 165). (b) Leave theta_eps, mu_lambda and sigma_lambda alone; there is no defensible story for quadrupling firm size other than that it helps. (c) If you want d_i to stop tracking size, do it the honest way: make sigma_eps,i firm-specific and INDEPENDENT of lambda_f, disclose it as a deliberate device, and report the resulting corr(log d, log size) as a calibration target against the real-data value of roughly -0.35. That is a defensible modelling choice; recalibrating four parameters is not. (d) Before any of this, verify A(eps,u) > 0 and check the implied sd(log K) against real sd(log market cap) ~ 2.0.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 5 — Heterogeneous operating leverage: a firm-specific fixed operating cost per project
verdicts.critique:
The best economics-per-line in the set, and the only proposal attacking the single most embarrassing structural fact about KP14 as implemented, which I verified directly: VAP = x*K^alpha*A(eps,u) (panel_functions_kp14.py:165) and PVGO = z^alph*x*lambda_f*G(eps) (line 173) are both homogeneous of degree one in x, so beta_x = 1 for EVERY firm, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 bakes that in by factoring Et_x2[t] out of the whole cross-firm block. The dominant price of risk (gamma_x = 0.69) therefore generates literally zero cross-sectional dispersion in exposure. Any referee shown that fact will regard the KP14 cross-section as vacuous. Operating leverage is the canonical, heavily-cited fix (Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino, Zhang, Novy-Marx), it is disclosed in one sentence, and nobody will accuse you of inventing it to win an estimator horse race. That is the highest bar any of these proposals clears.

FOUR CONCERNS.
(i) THIS IS THE RISKIEST CODE SURGERY IN THE SET, AND THE PROPOSAL UNDERSTATES IT. sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 is a single line that carries the entire O(N^2) cross-firm block and is valid ONLY under x-homogeneity. Splitting P' into an x-proportional and an x-independent piece requires new closed forms for E[n' Q'] and E[n'^2] and a rewrite of the term4 cash-flow correction at lines 162-165, whose `- np.outer(cf/price, cf/price)` double-counting subtraction is only correct under the current normalization. There are two commented-out single-pair validation blocks in the file (lines 148-159 and 231-254) that must be un-commented and made to pass. If they do not, every number in the KP14 column is silently wrong in a way no assertion will catch — which is precisely how the integ_results.npz failure survived.
(ii) THE LEVEL EFFECT CONTAMINATES THE MARKET PREMIUM. mean beta_x = 1.207 raises the equity premium from 8.97% to 10.8%/yr. The proposal's own fix (rescale gamma_x to 0.572) triggers a re-solve because gamma_x enters KP14_CONST and hence A_0..A_3 and KP14_RHO (config.py:264-272). Do it anyway: leaving the market premium free to move with the operating-leverage calibration lets a referee argue you tuned the aggregate premium.
(iii) NEGATIVE EQUITY. The proposal caps kappa at 0.60 to keep projects NPV-positive, but a high-kappa firm in a bad eps state can still have P <= 0, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:269 filters only on book > 0. Extend the keep mask to price > 0 and report the frequency.
(iv) TWO MORE CHARACTERISTICS, SAME FF PROBLEM. grossmargin and salesprice must be added to config.py:229-236 AND both hardcoded copies of _CHAR_TO_FACTOR (fama_functions.py:61-62 and 170-171) or fama_french KeyErrors at line 104. And note grossmargin = 1 - kappa is a CONSTANT for each firm forever — a fixed firm label, which after rank-standardization is a perfectly persistent characteristic. That is fine economically but it means the DKKM kernel gets a free, noiseless firm fixed effect, which is worth flagging.

ATTRIBUTION: ~85% economics, 15% plumbing. The highest economics share of any proposal here.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Only if the referee lets you keep FM linear, and the referee will not. The mechanism is exactly beta_x,i = 1 + kappa_i*(Rev_i/P_i)/(r+delta) — a single product of two observable characteristics. The proposal is candid that this works at the CODED bandwidth precisely because 86.7% of the RFF feature variance is quadratic in the chars. But anything a quadratic reaches, a quadratic-augmented OLS reaches better: add kappa*salesprice (one column) to fama_macbeth's design at fama_functions.py:158-160 and FM captures the entire mechanism with 8 parameters and T = 360, i.e. at essentially zero estimation cost, while DKKM pays P/T = 10 complexity risk to reach the same function. My prediction is that augmented-FM BEATS DKKM under this proposal, not ties it. There is a second, subtler problem: the two ingredients are not independent. Rev/P is itself close to (1 - PVGO share)/A_0, which is close to affine in bm — so kappa*(Rev/P) is close to kappa*bm, one interaction among two chars, in a 7-char space. That is a 1-dimensional nonlinearity, and one-dimensional nonlinearities are what small models are for. Finally, FF should IMPROVE here (a gross-margin 2x3 sort is a real factor), which narrows the DKKM-over-FF gap that is the paper's headline comparison.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt it, but adopt it as a MODEL CORRECTION rather than as the source of the result, and lead with that framing: 'the implementation had beta_x = 1 for every firm; we add heterogeneous operating leverage so that the dominant priced shock has a nontrivial cross-section.' That sentence is unimpeachable. Then report, in the same table, FM augmented with the interaction, and accept that the DKKM gap is small. Two amplifications worth trying since they cost nothing extra: (a) make kappa_i time-varying and mean-reverting rather than a permanent firm label, so it is a genuine characteristic rather than a fixed effect and so FF's static sort is not artificially handicapped; (b) let the fixed cost be denominated in a factor whose price differs from x (e.g. a wage that co-moves with the aggregate state), which turns beta_x,i into a ratio of two aggregate exposures rather than an affine function of one — that is a genuinely non-quadratic object and is the version augmented-FM cannot absorb. Combine with Proposal 1 (mandatory) and, if you take anything from Proposal 4, only the sigma_eps restoration.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 6 — Persistent mean-reverting demand wedge on price with a fundamental anchor nonlinear in the characteristics
verdicts.critique:
This is the proposal that would kill the paper, and it would kill it in one sentence in my report: THE AUTHORS ASSUME AN EXPECTED-RETURN COMPONENT THAT IS A NONLINEAR FUNCTION OF CHARACTERISTICS AND THEN REPORT, AS A FINDING, THAT A NONLINEAR ESTIMATOR RECOVERS IT BETTER THAN A LINEAR ONE.

The proposal knows this — it lists 'IT CHANGES WHAT TRUE MEANS' as its first risk and calls itself the most contested choice in the set. That self-awareness does not save it, for three reasons.
(1) THE PAPER'S ENTIRE PREMISE IS THAT THESE ARE STRUCTURAL, FRICTIONLESS MODELS AND THE TRUTH IS THE MODEL'S OWN SDF. The title is 'The Virtue of Complexity in Simple ECONOMIC Models.' Bolting an exogenous OU noise process onto the price and declaring the resulting mispricing to be part of the true MVE is not a simple economic model producing the virtue of complexity; it is an assumption producing its own consequence. Reframing it as 'segmented markets' does not change the mathematics: w is an i.i.d.-across-firms exogenous process with no agent, no constraint and no market-clearing condition behind it.
(2) THE MAGNITUDE IS BACKED OUT FROM THE TARGET, EXPLICITLY. The derivation section is titled 'TARGET THE NEAR-ARBITRAGE SHARPE FIRST, THEN BACK OUT THE PARAMETERS' and proceeds from DKKM's real-data 3.7 to sd(alpha) to kappa_w*SD_W. Every parameter in the proposal is the solution to 'what makes the answer come out.' There is no independent moment being matched.
(3) THE RESULT WOULD BE A DIVERSIFICATION ARTIFACT. alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N*E[alpha^2/d] grows with N, so SR* = 1.36/month = 4.7/yr comes from 1000 quasi-independent bets with per-stock information ratio 0.034. That is a near-arbitrage in a model with no limits to arbitrage — the model contains a 4.7 Sharpe and no reason nobody takes it. A referee will ask why the demand wedge is not competed away by the very investor whose portfolio you are computing. The proposal's own N-robustness check (report N = 250/500/1000, show the RATIO is stable) is the right check but it does not answer the economic question, only the statistical one.

SEPARATELY, THE CODE SURGERY IS THE RISKIEST HERE AND THE PROPOSAL SAYS SO: unbundling term4 at sdf_compute_kp14.py:162-165 into a four-way expansion, where the existing `- np.outer(cf/price, cf/price)` is a double-counting correction valid only under the current normalization.

ATTRIBUTION: 0% economics in any sense a structural macro-finance referee would recognize. It is an assumption, and the resulting number measures how well each estimator inverts an assumed function.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes — it is the only proposal here that plausibly reaches 3-5x, which is exactly what makes it damning rather than persuasive. And even taking it on its own terms, the gap is not robust. alpha_i = kappa_w*dt*(log bm_i + h(chars_i)), so DKKM's advantage over FM is entirely 1 - R^2(h | linear chars). The proposal's own diagnostic instruction — 'if the linear R^2 is above 0.85, this proposal will not deliver' — concedes that the result is a free parameter set by how nonlinear you choose to make the fundamental-value map, and that map is itself made nonlinear only by adopting Proposals 3 and 5 first. So the chain is: assume a wedge, assume the anchor is nonlinear, then measure that a nonlinear estimator inverts it better. Moreover, the wedge is orthogonal to everything, which means the alpha is recoverable ONLY through the chars — there is no unlearnable component and no reason FM cannot be augmented. Give FM the same degree-3 polynomial basis in the chars (56 columns, T = 360, still estimable) and it will recover most of h; the remaining DKKM edge is then shrinkage efficiency at c = P/T, i.e. the KMZ estimation-variance channel, which is a statistics result and not an economics result.
verdicts.salvage: Very little, and I would advise against attempting it in this paper. If you must have an unspanned premium, do it with a MICROFOUNDED friction rather than an exogenous price wedge: (a) a participation or short-sale constraint that binds as a function of firm characteristics, so the shadow price is an equilibrium object with a first-order condition behind it; (b) heterogeneous investors with genuinely different SDFs and a market-clearing condition, so the observed price reflects a wealth-weighted average and the 'alpha' relative to any one agent's SDF is an equilibrium outcome rather than an assumption; (c) intermediary capital constraints. Each of those is a real paper's worth of work and none is a KP14 patch. The far better use of this insight is REPORTING it: state in the paper that the diagnosis establishes, with an explicit population-span computation, that under exact K-factor pricing with N = 1000 every basis attains the maximum Sharpe to within 0.2%, and therefore that NO frictionless production model can generate the virtue of complexity. That is a clean, novel, publishable negative result. It is also, in my view, the paper you actually have.

missed_ideas: FIX THE BENCHMARK BEFORE FIXING THE MODEL — this is the omission that matters most, and it is a fairness defect that will kill the paper regardless of which economic change you adopt. I verified it: config.py:187 sets ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], so FF/FM get plain OLS with one specification and zero tuning decisions, while config.py:190 gives DKKM six alphas and config.py:181 four feature counts = 24 cells, and create_slides_tables.py:81-97 (find_best_alpha_for_model) then selects the argmax/argmin cell USING THE REPORTED EVALUATION METRIC ITSELF, pooled across all iterations. GS21 additionally gets a hand-tuned grid (ALPHA_LST_GS = ALPHA_LST/100, config.py:193, 333) — model-specific tuning applied to DKKM only. So the current headline 'DKKM ties FF/FM' is an oracle-tuned DKKM tying an untuned FF/FM, and any post-change 'DKKM beats FF/FM' inherits the same defect. Required: (a) give FF/FM a ridge grid of the same cardinality and select their alpha the same way, or (b) select DKKM's alpha and nfeatures INSIDE the 360-month training window by cross-validation, never on the evaluation metric. Report the full 6x4 grid in an appendix, not the argmax cell. No proposal mentions this.

REPORT max_sr AND THE SIGMA-METRIC COSINE. max_sr is computed at sdf_compute_kp14.py:294-296 and saved into the moments pickle, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it (I grepped — the string does not appear in the file), so it never reaches a table. Because Sharpe_t(w) = SR*_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*_t) is an exact identity, the interpretable quantity is Sharpe/SR*. Without it a referee cannot distinguish 'the estimator is failing' from 'the model has nothing to estimate', which is the entire question the paper is asking. This is a two-line change and it should precede every proposal here.

RUN THE ORACLE SPAN DIAGNOSTIC AS A GATE, NOT AS A POST-MORTEM. For each candidate model change, compute max_a SR(S_t a) with S_t = the configured RFF basis versus S_t = [1, chars], using the TRUE rp and cond_var already sitting in *_moments.pkl and zero estimation error. Report mean(SR_rff)/mean(SR_lin). Real-data DKKM-over-FF6 is 3-5x; below ~2 the model cannot deliver and no estimator tuning will change it. This costs minutes and would have pre-emptively killed Proposals 3, 4 and 5 and correctly identified 2 and 6 as the only candidates. Pre-register the threshold.

THE AUGMENTED-LINEAR BENCHMARK IS THE ROBUSTNESS CHECK THAT DECIDES THIS PAPER, AND NO PROPOSAL PRE-EMPTS IT. Proposals 3 and 5 each turn on exactly one bilinear interaction (bm x age; kappa x salesprice). Add those interactions to fama_macbeth's design (fama_functions.py:158-160) and the mechanism is absorbed at negligible estimation cost. Every proposal should be scored against 'FM on [1, chars, all pairwise products]' — 28 columns at L=7, T=360, still OLS — not against FM on 7 linear columns. A DKKM advantage that survives THAT is a real result; one that does not is a statement about the arbitrariness of the linear benchmark.

KP14'S OWN PROJECT-PORTFOLIO STRUCTURE IS AN UNEXPLOITED, FULLY NATIVE SOURCE OF HIGH-DIMENSIONAL NONLINEARITY. A firm is a portfolio of projects with heterogeneous (K_j, u_j, vintage). Firm value is currently a LINEAR aggregator over that portfolio (VAP = sum_j x*K_j^alpha*A(eps,u_j), panel_functions_kp14.py:165), which is why five low-order moments of the portfolio recover almost everything. Make the aggregator nonlinear using KP14's own machinery — firm-level decreasing returns, a capacity or managerial-attention constraint, or a financing constraint whose shadow price depends on the whole project distribution — and the map from observable portfolio moments to value becomes genuinely nonlinear with many quasi-orthogonal directions, WITHOUT inventing a technology torus (Proposal 2) or a demand wedge (Proposal 6). This is strictly more defensible than either and nobody proposed it.

NMAT=5 MISLABELS THE COMPLEXITY AXIS AND MUST BE SET TO 1. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169 averages stock weights across five independent W draws (config.py:178, with the comment noting the root codebase used nmat = 1). Averaging M random-feature ridge fits converges to KERNEL ridge with the same explicit penalty, cancelling exactly the draw-specific high-frequency components that finite-width random features are supposed to supply. It mechanically flattens the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve — which is the curve the paper is trying to produce. Any proposal whose payoff is 'a rising virtue-of-complexity curve' is fighting this line of code. Set NMAT = 1 and report the five draws as replications.

THE SECOND RANK-STANDARDIZATION MAKES GAMMA_GRID NEARLY A NO-OP, WHICH BREAKS PROPOSALS 2 AND 4's ESTIMATOR FIX. dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time, and rank-standardization is invariant to strictly monotone transformations; since sin is monotone over the realized range of Wx for ~76% of directions at the coded bandwidth, rank_standardize(sin(gamma*w'x)) is numerically the rank of w'x regardless of gamma. Proposals 2 and 4 both rely on rescaling GAMMA_GRID by sqrt(130/L) and neither mentions line 110. The rescale must be paired with replacing the second rank-standardization by unit-variance standardization, or it will be partly absorbed and the predicted 2.19x will not appear.

THE 25 TEST ASSETS HAVE NO POWER AND WILL NOT ACQUIRE ANY UNDER ANY OF THESE PROPOSALS. generate_25_portfolios.py:112-113 sorts on mve and bm quintiles only — two of the characteristics every method already spans linearly — and compute_pricing_errors.py then runs each method's MVE return as a single factor against them. The paper's second headline claim (lower pricing error) is therefore untestable. Add test assets sorted on the specific interaction each proposal creates (bm x age, kappa x salesprice, tech1 x bm) and on deciles of the model's TRUE conditional SDF weight. Only Proposal 2 mentions this in passing.

CHECK PER-FIRM SIGNAL-TO-NOISE, NOT JUST THE AGGREGATE SHARPE. Several proposals target SR* near 3-4 annualized. That number can be hit two ways: a realistic per-firm cross-sectional R^2 of ~0.5%/month diversified across N = 1000, or an implausible per-firm R^2 diversified less. Proposal 6 explicitly takes the first route (per-stock IR = 0.034) and Proposal 2 the aggregate-factor route; neither reports the resulting cross-sectional predictive R^2 against the real-data benchmark. Report var(rp)/(var(rp) + mean idio var) per month for every calibration and target ~0.005. The current repaired KP14 will be far above it.

ADD AN N-SCALING TABLE FOR ANY PROPOSAL WITH A NEAR-ARBITRAGE COMPONENT. If SR* grows as sqrt(N) (true for Proposal 6 by construction and partly for Proposal 2), the DKKM/FM RATIO must be shown stable across N in {250, 500, 1000, 2000}. If the ratio moves with N you have measured diversification, not complexity. Proposal 6 flags this for itself; it applies to Proposal 2 equally.

CONSIDER PUBLISHING THE NEGATIVE RESULT INSTEAD. The diagnosis phase already establishes something clean, general and novel: under exact K-factor pricing with K small and N large, the population maximum Sharpe is attained to within 0.2% by any well-diversified portfolio with the right factor exposure, so the RFF-over-linear span ratio is 1.00 and NO estimator change can create an advantage. Combined with DKKM's own Theorem 3 (complexity pays iff the eigenvalue spectrum of E[FF'] is flat) and the measured effective rank of ~16 for the configured feature map, that is a precise statement of what standard frictionless production-based models lack. 'Three canonical structural models cannot generate the virtue of complexity, and here is exactly the condition they fail' is a publishable JF-quality paper that requires none of these six changes and cannot be accused of tuning. It is also the framing under which Proposals 1, 3 and 5 become straightforward model corrections rather than suspicious interventions.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Repair the KP14 truth (regenerate integ_results.npz + G_func.csv, fix H/L regime convention)
verdicts.critique: I verified the central claim directly and it is worse than described. utils_kp14/KP14_solfiles/integ_results.npz reports 762/1000 'nonzero' entries, but that count is meaningless: reading G_up_lst on the eps grid from G_func.csv over the interval the panel actually occupies (eps in [0.93,1.066], grid indices 185-212) gives 0.0, 1.25e-111, 2.25e-72, 1.39e-41, 6.01e-19, and only at index 212 does it jump to 1.718e3 -- against the underlying G_up values of 1523, 1559, 1597, 1637, 1678, 1721 on the same nodes. So E_t[G] is between 40 and 120 orders of magnitude too small everywhere the simulation lives, and term2 in panel_functions_kp14.py:193 (Et_z_alph*Et_x*Et_G) is identically zero. erets at line 199 is therefore (term1+term3+term4)/price - 1, i.e. minus the PVGO share, which is exactly the reported rp = -PVGO/P artifact. Everything downstream -- rp, cond_var, max_sr, sdf_ret, the correlations.csv 'true' column, the -2.64/-5.35 FF/FM Sharpes -- is a quadrature failure, not economics. Two corrections to the proposal. (i) The regime fix (c)/(d): I confirmed panel_functions_kp14.py:98 gives stationary P(high)=mu_L/(mu_H+mu_L)=0.6809 while config.py:257 normalizes LAMBDA_L assuming w=MU_H/(MU_H+MU_L)=0.3191, and that the alternative repair (renormalize LAMBDA_L at w=0.6809) yields LAMBDA_L=-1.88, impossible. But the proposer did not consider the third option: keep the sim and cap LAMBDA_H at 1.47 (the largest value consistent with LAMBDA_L>=0 under P(high)=0.6809). Flipping the sim instead preserves the 2.35/0.367 H-L spread, which is the right call for cross-sectional dispersion, but it should be stated as a choice, not a forced move. (ii) The predicted max_sr of 0.223/month is the SDF's own bound sqrt(gamma_x^2+gamma_z^2)/sqrt(12), not the attainable stock-cross-section Sharpe. Since beta_x = 1 for every firm (price is homogeneous of degree 1 in x at panel_functions_kp14.py:165,173; sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 factors Et_x2[t] out of the whole cross-firm block) and beta_z = alph*share has tiny dispersion, the attainable number will be ~gamma_x/sqrt(12) = 0.199/month with a sliver from z. Expect all three methods to cluster at 0.19-0.20 against a 0.20 ceiling.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It will not, and the proposer says so. Worse than neutral for the paper's thesis: after the repair the truth becomes rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*share_i, an EXACT affine function of a single scalar (share), and the proposer's own check shows VAP_i/book_i has cross-sectional sd of only 3.2% of its mean, so share_i = 1 - v_i*bm_i with v_i near-constant and FM's raw-bm column spans the entire z-channel to within a few percent. FM's span in fama_functions.py:158-160 is literally the column space of [1, raw chars]; bm is one of those columns. FF's hml 2x3 sort (fama_functions.py:84-104) is a tercile step approximation to the same monotone object, so FF will be a few points behind FM and DKKM will be within noise of FM. The repaired table will show a CLEANER null than today's, because today's -2.64/-5.35 at least look like a difference. The one genuinely favorable side effect: with SR* falling from 10.0/month to ~0.20/month, HJD stops being pinned at its 0.269 floor and acquires real dynamic range (at SR*=0.2 the span between rho=0 and rho=1 is wide), so the metric becomes able to discriminate -- it just will not have anything to discriminate.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt as a hard prerequisite. Two additions the proposer omits. (1) Propagate max_sr from moments into results.pkl -- utils/evaluate_sdfs.py never carries it through, so no table can currently report Sharpe/SR*, which is the only interpretable number and the single cheapest diagnostic for every other proposal. (2) Add a regression test that asserts E_t[G_up](eps) is within a few percent of G_up(eps) at eps=1.0 (the CIR transition sd at sigma_eps=0.02, dt=1/12 is ~0.006, so E_t[G] must be close to G itself); the current file fails that assertion by 50 orders of magnitude and would have been caught instantly.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: K priced technology-domain IST shocks over an observable 2-D technology map
verdicts.critique: The algebra checks out: I verified alph*(3*alpha-1)/(1-alpha) == 2*alph^2 - alph identically, so E_t[z_i'^a z_j'^a] = Et_z_alph_i * Et_z_alph_j * exp(a^2 rho_ij sigma_z^2 dt) reduces exactly to the existing Et_z_alph2 at rho_ij=1, and the sdf_compute change really is a precomputed elementwise multiply on an N x N matrix. This is the only proposal in the set that satisfies condition C3 (many quasi-orthogonal priced directions). But three of its supporting claims are wrong. (1) THE BANDWIDTH PRESCRIPTION IS BACKWARDS. I built the exact rff() code path (rank_standardize chars, W = gamma*N(0,1), [sin;cos], rank_standardize again) on the proposal's own construction (K=100, h=0.10, L=7 rank chars, 360 features, N=1000) and measured cross-sectional R^2 on g(theta) = p(theta).gamma. Coded GAMMA_GRID: 0.730. Rescaled by 4.31 as the proposal demands: 0.720. Rescaled by 22 (what you would actually need to resolve an h=0.10 bump on a unit torus, ~31 rad/unit): 0.373. Widening HURTS, exactly as the GS21 agent found. The proposal's headline 2.19x is derived from a generic 'effective rank rises 16.5 -> 78' argument that says nothing about resolution in the two theta directions specifically -- and an isotropic direction in R^7 puts only sqrt(2/7) of its length in the theta plane. (2) HALF THE MEASURED R^2 IS DIMENSION COUNTING. Placebo: 360 pure-noise columns on 1000 firms attain R^2 = 0.343 on g, and RFF360 built on 5 chars carrying NO theta information attains 0.351. So RFF360's 0.730 is ~0.58 of real signal, against quad7 (35 terms, placebo ~0.035) at 0.458 and linear-7 at 0.242. Honest unspanned-variance shares are FM 0.24 / explicit-quadratic 0.44 / DKKM 0.58, not 0.03 / -- / 0.45. Recomputing the proposal's own Sharpe budget (SR*^2 = 0.476 + 0.244 + 9.00) gives FM 1.70/yr, DKKM 2.44/yr, ratio 1.43x -- not 2.19x, and not the 3-5x target. (3) THE BENCHMARK IS HANDICAPPED BY CONSTRUCTION. The proposal gives FM and FF two continuous scalars theta1, theta2. But the empirical analogue it cites (patent classes, TNIC, industry) is CATEGORICAL with ~100 levels, and the standard practice is dummies. A cross-sectional regression with 100 domain dummies on 1000 firms -- which is what fama_macbeth's X @ pinvh(X'X) at fama_functions.py:158-160 would produce if you handed it the dummies -- spans ALL K modes EXACTLY, and FM beats DKKM. The DKKM advantage here is entirely an artifact of choosing an encoding the benchmark cannot use.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures it if you encode theta the way a real researcher would (domain dummies), which is the natural encoding of the exact empirical objects the proposal cites -- and then FM is not approximating g at all, it is spanning it, and DKKM loses. Even with the continuous-coordinate encoding, an explicit quadratic in 7 chars gets 0.44 of 0.58, so DKKM's marginal contribution over 'FM plus interaction terms' is 32%, i.e. sqrt of that in Sharpe on the unspanned budget only. And the estimation side is hostile: 360 features against T=360 is exactly c=1, the double-descent point where the existing BOP results already show BGN Sharpe collapsing to 0.006 and HJD to 18.5 at alpha=0. Finally the theta coordinates and the gamma_k vector are drawn ONCE and are time-invariant, so g(theta_i) is a static cross-sectional variable -- 360 months of data to learn one fixed smooth 3-D function of (share, theta1, theta2), which is a much easier problem than the real-data one and is exactly the regime where a modestly-flexible small model wins.
verdicts.salvage: The idea survives, but reframe it. (a) Drop the GAMMA_GRID rescale entirely -- I measured that it hurts. (b) Make the technology field UNOBSERVABLE and inferable only through its footprint in the other characteristics (e.g. domain affects the arrival-rate regime, the capital intensity, and the cash-flow seasonality) rather than handing everyone theta1, theta2. That kills the dummy-variable objection and it is more faithful to the real-data situation, where technology exposure is not a column in Compustat. (c) Report the placebo (K random Gaussian directions carrying no economics) in every span table, or the 360-feature number cannot be interpreted. (d) Report the DKKM/FM ratio at N=250, 500, 1000 -- if it moves with N you have measured diversification. (e) Keep alpha=0.75 for transversality; that arithmetic I could not fault.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Historical-cost book value plus vintage/count/investment-intensity/cash-flow-volatility characteristics
verdicts.critique: The mechanism claim is that beta_z,i = alph*(1 - bm_i*exp(c0 + c1*age_i)) is a product of two non-size characteristics that FM cannot form. That is true as a statement about function spaces and false as a statement about Sharpe. Under exact K-factor pricing -- which is what KP14 is after P1, with mu = B*lambda and Sigma = B*S_f*B' + D -- the attainable Sharpe of ANY portfolio w is SR(w)^2 = lambda'... = 1/(sigma_f^2 + w'Dw/(w'beta)^2) in the 1-factor case, and the shortfall of a mis-specified beta is governed by the idiosyncratic term, which is O(1/N). I ran the exact experiment with the proposal's own structures: beta_x bilinear (P5), beta_z = 3*share with share = 1 - bm*exp(-0.2 + 0.03*age) (P3's bm x age), dispersed char-linked idio variance sd(log d) = 0.66 (P4), and a linear span containing only {1, log(1/sd), bm, age, kappa, sales/price, share} with NO products. Result: the best linear-span portfolio attains 96.6% / 99.1% / 99.7% of SR* at N = 250 / 1000 / 4000, and adding all 21 quadratic terms takes it to 99.7% / 99.9% / 100.0%. At the production N=1000 the ENTIRE nonlinearity headroom created by bm x age plus bilinear beta_x plus 20x idio-variance dispersion is 0.9 percentage points of Sharpe, and it vanishes as 1/N. That is the whole proposal.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures it to 99.1% at N=1000 by the measurement above, with no interaction terms at all, because the object is a LOADING and loadings only need to be right up to a diversification residual. FF also gets a free pass here that the proposal ignores: prepare_panel sets size = log(mve) (utils_factors/factor_utils.py, ROOT line 62), and every FF weight in fama_functions.py:70-113 is proportional to mve_i = exp(size_i). FF therefore carries an exponential-in-a-characteristic that neither FM (linear in log mve) nor DKKM (features capped in [-0.5,0.5] by the second rank_standardize at dkkm_functions.py:110) can form. If the target tilt has any size-level component -- and under P4's d ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/mve it is exactly proportional to mve -- FF's mkt_rf column IS the answer. Finally, the historical-cost change makes bm a NOISIER proxy for share; the KP14 diagnosis already measured eps at only 5.6% linearly / 15.0% quadratically recoverable from chars, so the added noise is unlearnable for every estimator and dilutes DKKM's residual edge along with everyone else's.
verdicts.salvage: Two pieces survive, neither for the stated reason. (1) The char additions are the cheapest available route to raising L, which is the one lever that reliably raises RFF effective rank (the theory agent measured 16.5 at L=5, 38.5 at L=10, 98.3 at L=20, 432 at L=50). But go far beyond four columns -- see missed ideas. (2) Before adopting historical-cost book, run the diagnostic the proposal itself specifies (R^2 of true share on linear chars vs. all pairwise products) and abandon the change if the quadratic gain is under 0.10; the KP14 diagnosis already measured 0.717 linear-raw vs 0.677 rank+quadratic, i.e. the gain is NEGATIVE in the space DKKM actually operates in. Drop the bm x age Sharpe claim entirely.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Recalibrate theta_eps/sigma_eps and project count so idiosyncratic variance stops being 1/size
verdicts.critique: The economics is right and the current calibration is indefensible: theta_eps = 0.35 (config.py:247) implies a firm-TFP half-life of 2 years and sigma_eps = 0.1*0.2 = 0.02 gives a stationary sd of 0.024, against Syverson's within-industry sd(log TFP) of 0.3-0.6 and annual persistence of 0.90-0.95. Fixing it is correct on its own terms and it removes the mechanism behind KP14's negative Sharpes. But as a source of DKKM advantage it is dead twice over. First, the D^-1 channel under exact factor pricing is O(1/N): my span experiment above gave FM 99.1% of SR* at N=1000 with sd(log d) = 0.66 already in place. Second -- and this is the part the proposal misses -- the change is actively ANTI-DKKM given the estimator as coded. dkkm_functions.rff line 110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time, so every DKKM regressor is a bounded uniform on [-0.4995, 0.4995] and no feature can be large-amplitude on a small subset of firms. The object DKKM needs is 1/d_i, which is exp(-b'x) -- monotone, heavy-tailed, and amplitude-carrying. rank_standardize is invariant to monotone transformations, so rank_standardize(sin(gamma*w'x)) = rank_standardize(w'x) for the ~76% of directions where sin is monotone over the cross-section; DKKM sees the ORDERING of 1/d and never its SCALE. FM, by contrast, regresses on RAW unstandardized characteristics (fama_functions.py:152-160, the standardization block is commented out), so it retains raw scale. The KP14 diagnosis measured exactly this: [1, 5 raw chars] attains 70.1% of SR* while [1, 5 rank chars] attains only 64.2% and [1, ranks, 15 quadratic rank interactions] 68.6% -- the rank-space nonlinear basis loses to the raw linear basis.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF captures it better than DKKM does. If d_i is char-linked and the tilt is inverse-variance, the optimal weight is w* proportional to beta_i/d_i, and under the current 1/nlive mechanism that is proportional to mve_i -- which is precisely FF's value weighting. Even after this proposal weakens the link (the proposal's own arithmetic takes the non-diversifying share only from 2.2% to 24%, leaving corr(log d, log nlive) around -0.85 versus a real-data target of -0.35), the residual is still dominantly size. And the magnitude is second-order regardless: even at 20x dispersion in d the theory agent measured SR(equal-weight)/SR* = 0.998 at N=1000. In basis points, this proposal is worth roughly 20 bp of monthly Sharpe out of ~200 bp available, i.e. 1%, and it hands most of that to FF.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt the theta_eps/sigma_eps recalibration on CORRECTNESS grounds only -- it is needed to stop 97.8% of firm risk being 'did a plant close', and it is needed to break the size artifact documented in docs/kp14_size_idio_var.md. Drop the DKKM-advantage claim. The one variant worth pursuing is the extension buried at the end: heterogeneous sigma_eps,i drawn INDEPENDENTLY of lambda_f and hence of size, reported as cfvol. That makes d orthogonal to size, which is the actual fix for the negative-Sharpe artifact. But it will only pay in Sharpe if paired with a genuine unspanned premium (P2 or P6), and it will only pay for DKKM if the second rank_standardize at dkkm_functions.py:110 is replaced by an amplitude-preserving standardization -- an estimator change nobody in this set proposes.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Heterogeneous operating leverage (firm-specific fixed cost per project)
verdicts.critique: This is the clearest case of confusing loading dispersion with Sharpe. Yes, beta_x is currently exactly 1 for every firm -- I confirmed the mechanism: price = VAP + PVGO with VAP = x*sum K^alpha*A (panel_functions_kp14.py:165) and PVGO = z^alph * x * lambda_f * G(eps) (line 173), x factors out of both, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 hard-codes the consequence by multiplying the entire cross-firm block by the scalar Et_x2[t]. And yes, adding a fixed cost makes beta_x,i = 1 + kappa_i*(Rev_i/P_i)/(r+delta), a genuine product of two non-size characteristics that FM's [1, chars] span cannot form and FF's size-crossed tercile sorts cannot form. But x is a SINGLE priced factor. With mu = beta*lambda_x and Sigma = beta*beta'*sigma_f^2 + D, the maximum attainable Sharpe is lambda_x/sigma_f * sqrt(beta'D^-1 beta*sigma_f^2/(1+beta'D^-1 beta*sigma_f^2)), which converges to gamma_x as N grows regardless of how dispersed beta is. Numerically with beta ~ 1, d ~ (5%/mo)^2, N = 1000: beta'D^-1 beta = 400,000, so the idiosyncratic correction is 2.5e-6 against sigma_f^2 = 1.4e-3, i.e. 0.18%. A portfolio using a linear approximation beta_hat with cosine 0.9 to the true beta raises that to 3.1e-6, and the Sharpe ratio between the two is sqrt(1 - 4e-4) = 0.9998. FOUR BASIS POINTS of relative Sharpe. The proposal's predicted 1.15-1.30x standalone is off by roughly three orders of magnitude, and it is the only proposal in the set that predicts a large gap at the CODED bandwidth, so this error is load-bearing for the whole set.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Both FF and FM capture it to within a fraction of a basis point, for the same reason: cross-sectional dispersion in the loading on a single priced factor is worth only the diversification residual, which is O(1/N). My span experiment with bilinear beta_x explicitly included and NO product terms in the span gave FM-linear = 99.1% of SR* at N=1000 and 99.7% at N=4000. The equal-weighted market already has beta_x ~ 1.2 and captures gamma_x. Separately, the proposal is the most expensive in the set: it breaks the x-homogeneity that sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 exploits, requiring new closed forms for E[n'Q'] and E[n'^2] on the diagonal and a full re-derivation of the term4 double-counting correction at lines 162-165. That is the highest-risk surgery in the set purchased for four basis points. There is also a live blow-up risk the proposal only half-flags: for a high-kappa firm in a bad eps state, P_i = VAP - n_i*f_i/(r+delta) can go to zero or negative, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:269 filters only on book > 0, not price > 0. A near-zero price makes 1+eret and the whole ER row explode, and scipy.linalg.solve with assume_a='pos' returns garbage without raising -- the exact 1e57 max_sr pathology already documented in the comment block at lines 262-268.
verdicts.salvage: Almost nothing. The only defensible residue: if you want beta_x dispersion for its own sake (so that the CAPM row in the table stops being degenerate and the 25-portfolio GRS test has any factor structure to reject), a fixed cost is the right way to get it, and it costs nothing in the Sharpe metric either way. Do NOT present it as a source of DKKM advantage. If it is adopted, add price > 0 to the keep mask at sdf_compute_kp14.py:269 and assert min(price) is bounded away from zero.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Persistent mean-reverting demand wedge on price
verdicts.critique: This is the only proposal that satisfies condition C2 -- an expected-return component that is NOT minus a covariance and whose contribution alpha'D^-1 alpha grows with N. The parameter derivation is sound (I reproduced sd(alpha) = (1-e^{-0.135/12})*0.15 = 0.00168/month, and the implied 2.25%/month extra idiosyncratic vol is a move toward real-data levels). The lognormal OU moments really are elementary and really do keep sdf_compute at O(N^2) via outer(a,a). But the LEARNABILITY argument, which is the whole mechanism, does not survive contact with the KP14 diagnosis. The proposal's own identity is w_i = -log bm_i - h(chars_i) with h = log(P^fund/book). In KP14, P^fund/book = (VAP + PVGO)/book and the proposal itself measured VAP/book = (1/alpha)*[a factor with cross-sectional sd of 3.2%], so h = const - log(1 - share_i) up to a 3% wobble. That is a UNIVARIATE MONOTONE CONVEX transform of a single scalar, not a rich multi-characteristic map. DKKM's incremental recovery of alpha over FM is bounded by the incremental R^2 of a nonlinear-vs-linear fit of share -- and the KP14 diagnosis already measured that increment: share R^2 = 0.717 on 5 raw chars linear, 0.464 on 5 rank chars linear, 0.677 on rank chars plus all quadratic interactions. The nonlinear rank-space basis is WORSE than the raw linear basis. So the expected DKKM-minus-FM recovery of alpha is approximately zero or negative, and the residual (share is driven by eps, which is 5.6% linearly / 15.0% quadratically recoverable) is unlearnable noise for everyone. A second, quieter problem: the wedge contaminates log bm directly, so log bm alone -- which FM sees via raw bm and DKKM sees via rank(bm), the same ordering -- already correlates strongly with w. If sd(log(V/B)) ~ 0.2 and sd(w) = 0.15, the wedge is ~36% of the variance of log bm, so bm ALONE is a 0.6-correlation signal for alpha, available to FM at zero cost.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures most of it because the wedge is revealed by a single raw characteristic (bm) net of a monotone univariate correction. DKKM's advantage is confined to the curvature of -log(1-share), which is one-dimensional and which rank-standardization partly reproduces for free. Quantifying the proposal's own accounting honestly: if FM recovers 55% of var(alpha) and DKKM 65% (rather than the assumed 40%/70%-90%), SR_DKKM/SR_FM = sqrt((0.65*1.79+0.05)/(0.55*1.79+0.05)) = 1.08x, not 1.33-2.4x. Three further attacks. (a) The near-arbitrage is a pure sqrt(N) artifact -- the proposal flags this but understates it: with alpha independent across firms, SR*^2 = N*E[alpha^2/d] scales linearly in N, so the headline Sharpe of 1.36/month is entirely a statement about N=1000 and would be 0.68 at N=250. (b) The Sharpe metric as coded is scale-invariant month by month (evaluate_sdfs.py:183-199, create_slides_tables.py:34-42 form mean/stdev per month then average), so it gives ZERO credit for the timing channel -- and a mean-reverting wedge is precisely a timing story. (c) The term4 unbundling at sdf_compute_kp14.py:162-165 is a genuine correctness hazard: the existing -outer(cf/P, cf/P) correction is valid only because the two legs share a normalization, and the two commented-out single-pair tests at lines 148-159 and 231-254 must be reactivated before any number is trusted.
verdicts.salvage: The proposal is right about WHAT is missing (an unspanned, N-scaling premium) and wrong about WHAT MAKES IT HARD TO FIND. Two changes make it work. (1) Give the wedge a FACTOR STRUCTURE with characteristic-dependent loadings -- a small number of crowded-trade / flow factors whose exposures are nonlinear functions of several characteristics -- rather than i.i.d. firm-level noise. That satisfies C2 and C3 simultaneously and is at least as defensible empirically (Koijen-Yogo demand system, index and flow effects) as pure noise-trader OU. (2) Make the wedge's AMPLITUDE characteristic-dependent, sigma_w,i = f(chars), so the optimal weight alpha_i/d_i is a genuine ratio with BOTH numerator and denominator char-linked -- that is the configuration in which the theory agent measured the RFF-over-linear ceiling ratio hit 6-21x, versus 1.0 for a linear alpha. Also run the proposal's own pre-flight diagnostic (R^2 of true w on linear chars vs. degree-3) and abort if the linear R^2 exceeds 0.85; on the numbers already in hand it will.

missed_ideas: THE WITHIN-FIRM PROJECT DISTRIBUTION IS A FREE SOURCE OF 30-50 CHARACTERISTICS, AND NOBODY USES IT. KP14 already simulates K[t1,t2,n], chi, uj and Kj per project (panel_functions_kp14.py:126-152). Every firm-month therefore carries a full distribution over 6-24 live projects. Moments of that distribution -- HHI of capital across projects, sd and skewness of project vintages, fraction of capital in the largest project, dispersion of project-level u, age of the oldest and newest project, count of projects created in the last 12/36/60 months, capital-weighted vs equal-weighted mean age -- are dozens of genuinely distinct, weakly-informative, mutually non-redundant characteristics that require ZERO model change and ZERO re-solve. The theory agent measured RFF effective rank going 16.5 (L=5) -> 38.5 (L=10) -> 98.3 (L=20) -> 432 (L=50). Raising L from 5 to ~35 is the single cheapest way to move the estimator from DKKM's APT regime (EffRank ~2.5, complexity harmful) toward their AIPT regime (EffRank ~500), and it is far more defensible than inventing an observable technology coordinate. P3 gestures at this with four columns and stops.

PRICE THE PROJECT-ARRIVAL SHOCK. 97.8% of KP14's idiosyncratic variance is currently Poisson project death and arrival, and every bit of it is UNPRICED. Making a component of the arrival intensity aggregate (a technology-diffusion wave common across firms, with firm-specific exposure through lambda_f and the H/L regime) and giving it a price of risk turns the model's dominant source of return variance into a priced factor whose loading is multiplicative in intensity -- genuinely nonlinear, and orthogonal to both the x and z channels. This is a smaller change than P2's technology map and it repurposes machinery that already exists (sim_arrivals at panel_functions_kp14.py:91-107).

THE DOUBLE RANK-STANDARDIZATION IS A MODEL-INDEPENDENT CEILING AND NO PROPOSAL TOUCHES IT. dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time. Because rank-standardization is invariant to monotone transformations, this makes GAMMA_GRID a near-no-op for the ~76% of directions where sin is monotone over the cross-section, and it forces every one of the 3600 regressors to the identical bounded uniform marginal. No feature can be large-amplitude on a small subset of firms. Any proposal whose target weight is amplitude-carrying -- 1/d (P4), exp(size), a heavy-tailed alpha -- is structurally unreachable no matter what the model does. P2's gamma rescale does not fix this and I measured that it makes span WORSE. The minimal fix (winsorize then standardize to unit variance, preserving the sin/cos amplitude equalization that rank-standardization was accidentally supplying) is orthogonal to all six proposals and is plausibly worth more than any of them.

NMAT=5 WEIGHT AVERAGING SUPPRESSES THE MECHANISM BEING TESTED. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py averages stock weights across 5 independent W draws. Averaging M random-feature ridge fits of the SAME target on the SAME months converges to kernel ridge with the same explicit penalty, cancelling exactly the draw-specific high-frequency directions and mechanically flattening the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve -- which is the curve the paper is trying to measure. config.py notes the root codebase used nmat=1. Setting NMAT=1 and reporting the 5 draws as replications is free and should be done before any economic change is evaluated.

agr IS A DEGENERATE CHARACTERISTIC IN KP14 AND IT ASYMMETRICALLY PENALIZES DKKM. Investment in KP14 is a Poisson event, so book jumps discretely and agr is mostly exactly zero (the same pathology the BGN agent quantified at 87-92% ties). rank_standardize breaks those ties with np.argsort (dkkm_functions.py:57-62), producing a persistent pseudo-random column that enters all 3600 RFF features MULTIPLICATIVELY while polluting only one of FM's six additive regressors, and it degenerates FF's cma tercile sort to q30 == q70. Measure the tie fraction in the KP14 panel and either drop agr or replace it with a smoothed multi-year investment rate before attributing any DKKM shortfall to economics.

NO PROPOSAL CREATES A CHARACTERISTIC x MACRO-STATE INTERACTION, WHICH IS THE ONLY CONDITIONING CHANNEL THE ESTIMATOR CAN SEE. The DKKM ridge coefficient is a single vector estimated over 360 months and applied unchanged to every cross-section, and KP14's feature map has no time-varying input at all (dkkm_functions.rff appends rf only for model == 'bgn', line 95). Time-varying prices of risk are one of the two channels through which complexity pays in the DKKM/KMZ theory, and in KP14 they are invisible by construction. Any conditioning story must be built so that the premium of a characteristic moves with a state that is itself readable from the cross-section (e.g. cross-sectional dispersion of PVGO share as a proxy for the IST cycle).

MEASUREMENT ERROR AND REPORTING LAGS ARE THE CHEAPEST DEFENSIBLE WAY TO MAKE THE SMALL MODEL MIS-SPECIFIED. Every characteristic in these panels is observed exactly, with no missing values, no accounting lag, and no reporting discretion, and N is fixed at 1000 with no entry or exit. In that environment the 6-regressor model is correctly specified and ridge over 3600 features can only add variance. Reporting each characteristic as a noisy, lagged, partially-missing proxy -- and supplying several redundant-but-imperfect proxies for the same latent state, which is what real characteristic datasets look like -- is a minimal change that makes shrinkage-over-a-rich-basis the statistically right answer. This is the mechanism that lets DKKM's five-characteristic real-data model reach 1.93-2.50 while these models' five characteristics reach nothing.

A FAT-TAILED SIZE DISTRIBUTION WITH ENTRY AND EXIT. DKKM's real-data Sharpe falls from 3.7 to ~1.6 when restricted to mega/large caps, so a large share of the empirical virtue of complexity is a microcap phenomenon: small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility, high-alpha names. KP14 already produces zero-project firms (~5% per month, currently a nuisance masked out at sdf_compute_kp14.py:269). Turning that into genuine entry and exit with a Pareto size distribution and a size-dependent alpha and idio vol would reproduce the tail where the real gap lives.

THE TEST ASSETS HAVE NO POWER AND NO PROPOSAL FIXES THEM. utils/generate_25_portfolios.py sorts only on mve and bm -- two of the five characteristics every method already spans linearly -- and compute_pricing_errors.py runs each method's MVE return as a single factor against them. Any proposal that creates nonlinear or interactive mispricing will be invisible to the GRS test. Add portfolios sorted on deciles of the model's OWN true conditional SDF weight, and on characteristic interactions.

REPORT SHARPE/SR* AND THE SPAN-CEILING DIAGNOSTIC BEFORE RUNNING ANY ESTIMATOR. max_sr is computed in every sdf_loop and stored in the moments pickles but never propagated by utils/evaluate_sdfs.py into results.pkl. Every one of these six proposals can be pre-screened in minutes without touching the estimator: per month compute sqrt(mu' X (X' Sigma X)^-1 X' mu) for X = [1, chars] and for X = the configured RFF, take the ratio, and report it alongside a PLACEBO basis of the same width carrying no characteristic information. My placebo here (360 pure-noise columns attaining R^2 = 0.343 on 1000 firms) shows that roughly half of any 360-feature span number is dimension counting; without that control the span tables are uninterpretable.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Restore/overshoot the idiosyncratic cash-flow band (sigmaj) + ivol characteristic
verdicts.critique:
The INVARIANCE claims are correct and I verified them by reading the code, not by trusting the proposer. sigma_j enters create_arrays only at panel_functions_bgn.py:51-55 (the draw), :61 (corr_zj = beta/(sigma_z*sigmaj)) and :121 (C = exp(Cbar - 0.5*sigmaj^2 + eps*sigmaj)). Because corr_zj is DEFINED as beta/(sigma_z*sigmaj), cov(log M, log C_j) = -sigma_z*sigmaj*corr_zj = -beta_j identically, so E[C]=Chat and the risk-neutral value Chat*exp(-beta) are invariant. Nothing in the investment rule (:82), beta_avg (:148-149), A (:153), G (:157), P (:161-164) or any of the four eret terms (:172-186) touches sigmaj. In sdf_compute_bgn.py the OFF-DIAGONAL cash-flow term is result4 = exp(kron(col2,col2)) with col2 = chi*sigmaj*corr_zj, whose entries are sigma_i*c_i*sigma_j*c_j = beta_i*beta_j/sigma_z^2 -- literally invariant to the band. Only the i=j diagonal correction diag4_add, which carries exp(sigmaj^2) (:246-256), moves. So the change is exactly and only 'inflate the diagonal of Sigma'. Jstar.csv, D(r), beta_star, scale, prob_in_money are all untouched. That is a genuinely clean, minimal, non-rigging intervention and I endorse the direction.

Five objections. (1) THE 'RESTORATION' FRAMING IS FALSE AND THE PROPOSER'S OWN SCAN PROVES IT. git show 2cce11f (2026-06-18) shows the original was `+ 0.3*np.abs(Cbar)`, i.e. m=1.0, cut 10x that day. The proposer's scan reports m=1.0 gives sd(log d)=0.309 and pairwise corr 0.421 -- essentially no improvement over the status quo. The entire gain lives at m=1.75, a 75% OVERSHOOT of anything BGN or this codebase ever used. Do not sell m=1.75 as 'returning toward BGN's own un-multiplied band'; it is a new free parameter, and it should be defended as such.

(2) sigma_j HAS NO ECONOMIC CONTENT WHATSOEVER, so the new d-dispersion is exogenous noise, not a characteristic-linked object. It is an i.i.d. U[|beta|/sigma_z, |beta|/sigma_z + band] nuisance draw per project (:51-55) that affects NOTHING except the diagonal of Sigma. At m=1.75 sigma_j spans roughly [1.59, 3.53] so exp(sigma_j^2) spans 12.6 to 2.7e5 -- d_i is then determined almost entirely by the single highest-sigma live project among ~6, a max-statistic of pure luck that is orthogonal to size, bm, roe, agr and mom by construction. H2 requires d to be char-LINKED; this makes it maximally char-UNLINKED.

(3) THE SPAN NUMBERS ARE AN ORACLE. '{1, log mve, bm, log ivol} = 72.04%' and 'full quadratic = 93.53%' must be computed with the TRUE log d as the ivol column. The econometrician gets a 60-month realized return sd. For per-project cash flows that are lognormal with sigma ~= 2.6, the relative standard error of a 60-observation variance estimate scales like exp(2*sigma^2)/sqrt(60) ~ 10^5: realized volatility is a nearly information-free estimator of d, and d itself jumps by orders of magnitude the month the max-sigma project dies. The 93.5%-vs-72.0% gap is not reachable.

(4) YOU ARE ABOUT TO IMPORT THE KP14 PATHOLOGY, AND THE PROPOSAL NEVER MENTIONS IT despite it being documented in this project's own memory (docs/kp14_size_idio_var.md). d_i ~ sum_j chi_j*exp(sigma_j^2)/P_i^2 ~ num_i/P_i^2 ~ 1/(size*bm-ish), so D^{-1} ~ size and w* = D^{-1}(rp - Bc) tilts toward LARGE firms while every empirically estimated tangency portfolio loads on the size PREMIUM (small). That is precisely the mechanism that produced KP14's negative Sharpes for all three methods with no sign bug anywhere. At d_max/d_min = 4715 the 1/d leg dominates w* completely. There is a live risk that m=1.75 turns BGN into KP14: all Sharpes collapse or go negative and the DKKM-vs-FF comparison becomes uninterpretable rather than favourable.

(5) THE CALIBRATION MATCH IS ONE MOMENT OF A PATHOLOGICAL DISTRIBUTION. At sigma_j ~ 2.6, median project cash flow is exp(Cbar - 0.5*sigma^2) = e^{-7.1} against mean e^{-3.7}: essentially all cash flow arrives as a rare lottery payoff. Matching sd(return)=12.3%/mo, pairwise corr 0.22 and idio share 0.75 simultaneously is real, but skewness and kurtosis are astronomical, roe (op_cash_flow/book) becomes a lottery-outcome char, and the FF 2x3 sort on roe becomes a sort on which firm got lucky last month. That degrades FF/FM -- which flatters the headline ratio for the wrong reason.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, but the honest ceiling is well below 1.30x and FM gets more of it than claimed. Once you hand the econometrician an ivol characteristic, log d is (by the proposer's own construction) close to linear in log ivol, so FM regressing on [size, bm, log ivol] recovers the numerator AND the log-denominator linearly; the only thing it misses is the RATIO curvature. The proposer measures that residual as 72.0% -> 93.5%, but that is with oracle log d. With a 60-month realized vol of a sigma~2.6 lognormal the ivol column is mostly noise, which pushes DKKM's attainable share DOWN toward FM's 69-72% rather than up to 93.5% -- DKKM has strictly more parameters to burn on a noisy regressor. Worse, FF is not obviously handicapped: a size x ivol 2x3 double sort is a coarse but genuinely nonlinear b/d approximation, and the real-data low-vol/betting-against-beta literature shows exactly such sorts capture most of the inverse-variance tilt. And there is a scenario where the gap goes NEGATIVE: if w* becomes 1/d-dominated and 1/d is unlearnable luck, all three methods degrade toward noise and the ranking is a coin flip, exactly as in KP14. Finally, the DKKM feature map cannot represent a 4700x-range reciprocal anyway: dkkm_functions.rff rank-standardizes the chars and then rank-standardizes the sin/cos features again, so every regressor is capped in [-0.5,0.5] and rank(1/d) = -rank(d) identically -- the basis is monotone-invariant and therefore cannot distinguish d from 1/d at all. The proposal's own mechanism is annihilated by the estimator it is meant to help unless the second rank-standardization is replaced, which Proposal 3 only 'considers'.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the lever, change what drives it. (a) Cap m at 1.0-1.25 (the historical value and mildly above) so cash flows stay economically recognisable, and get the dispersion instead from making idiosyncratic volatility a DETERMINISTIC, persistent, economically motivated function of firm/project observables -- e.g. sigma_j increasing in the project's beta (riskier technologies are also more firm-specific), or a per-FIRM (not per-project) volatility type drawn once and persistent, so d_i is stable, char-measurable, and estimable from a 60-month window. That preserves H2's ratio nonlinearity (b/d is still nonlinear even when both legs are linear) while making 1/d learnable, which is the whole point. (b) Before running anything, compute at a single month: corr(true log d, log of the 60-month realized vol the estimator will actually see) and corr(w*, size). If the first is below ~0.6 or the second is above ~0.7, stop -- you have built KP14. (c) Ship only together with a fix to dkkm_functions.py:110 (replace the second rank_standardize with per-column unit-variance scaling), otherwise the basis is monotone-invariant and cannot express the reciprocal by construction.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: Project-scale / intangible-capital wedge kappa breaking the rp = a + b/mve + Chat*pi*bm identity
verdicts.critique:
The premise is correct and it is the single most important structural fact in this file. I re-derived it from the code rather than trusting the proposer: P = G + A (panel_functions_bgn.py:161-164), term2 = pi*A*E[D']/D (:176) so term2/P = pi*e_t*(1 - G_t/P), term4 = Chat*pi*book (:181) so term4/P = Chat*pi*bm, and term1, term3 are date-level scalars (:172, :179). Hence eret_i = [pi*e_t - 1] + [(term1+term3) - pi*e_t*G_t]/P_i + (Chat*pi)*bm_i, exactly affine in (1/mve, bm) with a bm coefficient of Chat*pi = 0.024476 at every date. The cross-section of expected returns in BGN as coded is EXACTLY two-dimensional. Any proposal that does not break this identity cannot raise the dimensionality of the premium, which immediately downgrades P1, P4 and (in premium terms) P6. Breaking it via term4 is the right surgical target.

Now the objections. (1) THIS IS A MEASUREMENT-ERROR PROPOSAL WEARING A STRUCTURAL COSTUME. If kappa_j scales cost AND cash flow proportionally, a kappa=2 project is economically identical to two kappa=1 projects; the exercise rule exp(Cbar-beta)D(r) > 1 is scale-free and J* is unchanged because E[kappa]=1. So kappa introduces NO new economic force whatever. One hundred percent of the mechanism lives in the accounting assumption at :144 that book = I*num rather than I*sum(kappa). The paper must say that plainly.

(2) THE INTANGIBLE FRAMING IS INCOHERENT FOR HALF THE FIRMS. Peters-Taylor / Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou intangibles make book UNDERSTATE economic capital -- the wedge is one-sided. A mean-one lognormal kappa gives book OVERSTATING capital for ~half of projects, which corresponds to no accounting mechanism at all. Use kappa >= 1 (e.g. 1 + expensed intangible) and re-normalise I, or drop the intangible citation.

(3) THE MOMENT ALGEBRA IN THE PROPOSAL IS ALREADY WRONG IN AT LEAST ONE PLACE, AND THIS IS THE KP14 SILENT-CORRUPTION CLASS. term5 = kron(col1, col3*integ_Dexpy) (sdf_compute_bgn.py:180-181) is the assets-in-place leg of i crossed with the cash-flow leg of j; at i=j, s=s' both legs refer to the SAME project and each carries kappa_s once, so diag5_sub (:259-265) needs kappa_s^2 -- exactly what it inherits from col1 and col3. The proposal's instruction (step 8) to 'remove one factor' from diag5_sub is an error that would silently bias the diagonal of cond_var with no exception raised, precisely the failure mode already burned into this project's memory for KP14. If a proposal cannot get one of eight terms right in prose, it will not get eight right in code.

(4) LOOK-AHEAD BUG IN THE PROPOSED CHARACTERISTIC. Step 10 defines payout = op_cash_flow/mve with no shift. Trace the indexing: op_cash_flow[t,:] is the date-t+2 cash flow (:124-126 and the comment at :123); create_panel stacks concatenate((zeros(1,N), op_cash_flow)) so panel row month=t carries op_cash_flow[t-1] = the cash flow paid at date t+1 -- i.e. the cash-flow component of xret_t. That is exactly why roe is defined with a .shift() at :237-243. An unshifted payout hands every method next month's dividend. It would produce a spectacular DKKM result and it would be fraudulent.

(5) IT DOES BREAK 'THE BGN MODEL'. BGN (1999)'s headline is that size and book-to-market are sufficient statistics for risk BECAUSE book measures the capital whose cash flows carry known beta. Deliberately severing book from capital repeals the paper's namesake theorem. That may be the right thing to do, but the paper must then describe the model as 'BGN with mismeasured book equity', not as BGN.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM can capture much more of this than the proposal admits, and the model already hands it the ingredients. Once you add payout yield as a characteristic, the new premium term pi*Chat*I*(Lambda_i/mve_i) is LINEAR in a supplied char up to attenuation, so FM's single-coefficient projection captures E[Lambda/mve] with the average shrinkage and loses only the cross-sectional variance of (pi_i - pi_bar)*y_i. That is a second-order interaction, not a first-order span gap. Worse, the model ALREADY contains the interaction FM needs in linear form: roe = op_cash_flow_{t}/book_{t-1} (:237-243) and bm = book/mve (:245) are both existing chars, and Lambda/mve is roughly roe*bm/Chat -- a single pairwise product, the easiest possible nonlinearity, and one that FF's 2x3 double sorts (which are literally designed to capture pairwise interactions) approximate reasonably well. So the honest prediction is DKKM/FM of 1.05-1.15x from this channel, not 1.2-1.35x. The genuinely unspanned part -- the firm-specific optimal shrinkage weight pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + noise_i^2/(num_i*H)) -- is real but small, and it requires num_i and ivol_i as chars, of which num_i is an exact function of chars you already have (see P3) and ivol_i is the unreliable object criticised under P1. Also note that raising cross-sectional predictive R^2 from 0.043% to 0.5% makes estimation HARDER for everyone in absolute terms but does not by itself favour the high-dimensional estimator; the diagnosis's own est3.py result is that with a LINEAR alpha and homogeneous d, OLS-on-6 (0.267) BEATS ridge-RFF-3600 (0.254). Lambda/mve enters linearly. Without P1's heteroskedastic d as a multiplier, this proposal alone plausibly WIDENS FM's lead.
verdicts.salvage: Keep it, but (i) make kappa one-sided and call it 'expensed intangible investment', citing Peters-Taylor, and re-normalise I so E[cost] is unchanged; (ii) do NOT hand the econometrician a clean payout yield -- the whole point is that Lambda is revealed only noisily, so supply properly LAGGED payout at 12/36/60-month horizons and let the estimator do the filtering; (iii) validate cond_var by brute-force Monte Carlo before believing anything: simulate R_{t+1} many times at a fixed t with N=30 and check E[R R'] elementwise against sdf_loop's ER, term by term. Do not accept the analytic edits on inspection; (iv) run the D2 span diagnostic (max Sharpe attainable in the RFF span divided by max Sharpe attainable in the linear-char span, at the true rp and cond_var) BEFORE writing the sdf_compute edits. If that ratio is below ~1.5 the eight-term algebra is not worth the risk. This is the only proposal here that attacks the verified binding constraint (the exact two-dimensional premium), so it deserves the effort -- but only with the Monte Carlo gate.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Repair agr, add age/nproj/payout/ivol chars, rescale GAMMA_GRID
verdicts.critique:
Correct in spirit, and the agr and bandwidth diagnoses are real. But three of the proposed characteristics are defective, and one of them is a look-ahead bug.

(1) 'age' IS CROSS-SECTIONALLY CONSTANT. There is no firm entry or exit in BGN as coded: create_arrays gives every one of the N firms the identical opportunity stream from t=0 (chi[range(T),range(T),:] = invest, panel_functions_bgn.py:96-97), no firm is ever born or delisted, and every firm faces the same arrival process. `df.groupby('firmid').cumcount()` therefore returns the MONTH INDEX for every firm -- an exactly constant column within each cross-section. rank_standardize (dkkm_functions.py:57) would resolve it entirely by np.argsort tie-breaking, i.e. it would inject a SECOND pseudo-random persistent column into all 3600 features, reproducing precisely the agr pathology this proposal exists to remove. This is the same defect class as rf_stand. Delete 'age'.

(2) 'nproj' IS AN EXACT ALGEBRAIC FUNCTION OF TWO EXISTING CHARACTERISTICS. book = I*num (:144), bm = book/mve (:245), size = log(mve) (factor_utils.py:72). Hence nproj = num = bm*exp(size)/I identically. It adds zero information. What it DOES do is hand FM a new LINEAR direction spanning a nonlinear function of (size, bm) that FM previously could not form -- an own-goal that strictly narrows the DKKM-over-FM gap. Delete it, or if you want num in the information set, recognise that you are helping the linear benchmark.

(3) 'payout = op_cash_flow/mve' IS A ONE-MONTH LOOK-AHEAD. As traced under P2: panel row month=t carries op_cash_flow[t-1], which is the date-t+1 cash flow, i.e. part of xret_t. The existing roe is safe only because it applies .shift() (:237-243). Any new payout char must be shifted identically.

(4) THE agr FIX IS COSMETIC AND MISDIAGNOSES THE CAUSE. The degeneracy is not a pandas issue; it is that book = I*num with num a small integer (mean ~6) and P(invest) ~ 5%/month, so book literally cannot change smoothly. Over 12 months a firm with 6 projects expects ~0.7 deaths and ~0.6 arrivals, so P(num_t = num_{t-12}) is on the order of 30-40%, not the claimed sub-20%, and the values remain a coarse lattice of small-integer ratios. The economically honest fix is to make investment less lumpy -- many smaller projects per firm, or a higher arrival intensity -- which simultaneously repairs agr, repairs FF's degenerate cma sort (q30 = q70 = 0), and makes book growth a continuous variable. That is a model change, not a characteristic change, and it is the one this proposal should have made.

(5) THE BANDWIDTH RESCALE IS THE RIGHT DIAGNOSIS WITH THE WRONG PRESCRIPTION ORDER, and the proposer half-knows it. Rescaling gamma while dkkm_functions.py:110 still rank-standardizes the features a second time recovers only the sin-folding part: rank-standardization is invariant to monotone transformations, so gamma is a near no-op for ~76% of features. Rescaling gamma is worth doing only jointly with replacing that second rank_standardize by per-column unit-variance scaling (deleting it outright raises the linear share from 49% to 86%, so it must be replaced, not removed).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposer concedes this: standalone it is worth perhaps 1.02-1.05x, and my reading says the sign is not even guaranteed. Three of the proposed additions actively help the linear benchmark: nproj hands FM a nonlinear function of (size,bm) for free; a clean 12-month agr repairs one of FF's seven factors (currently a degenerate 92/0/8 split with literally empty middle portfolios) more than it helps DKKM; and every additional characteristic enlarges FM's span exactly as much as it enlarges DKKM's if the truth is linear in it. The bandwidth rescale is the only genuinely DKKM-only knob, and the independent estimation experiment in the diagnosis found an x8 rescale HURT badly (0.157 vs 0.254) when the truth was low-order -- which, absent P2 or P5, BGN's truth demonstrably is (rp exactly affine in two chars, verified). Applying P3's bandwidth rescale to the CURRENT model would most likely make DKKM worse. It is a multiplier, and multipliers on zero are zero.
verdicts.salvage: Keep: the 12-month agr (as a partial improvement), ivol, properly LAGGED payout at 12/36/60m, lagged bm, and multi-horizon past returns. Drop: age (constant), nproj (exactly redundant, and pro-FM). Add instead: the economically correct fix for agr, which is to raise the number of projects per firm / the arrival intensity so book growth is continuous -- this also gives the cross-section a real size distribution (currently sd(log mve) is tiny because all firms are ex-ante identical Poisson draws). Sequence the bandwidth change LAST, after a model change has been verified by the D2 span diagnostic to put genuine high-frequency content in the truth, and make it jointly with replacing dkkm_functions.py:110. Also adopt the NMAT=1 and finer-alpha-grid recommendations -- those are unambiguously right and cost nothing.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Cohort (vintage) common cash-flow factors with age-dependent hedge weights
verdicts.critique:
The stated mechanism does not exist in this model. The proposal's core claim is that 'firm i's exposure to cohort m is phi_m(i) = the value share of its live projects born in window m, which given pi = 0.99 is in expectation a function of firm age: zero for cohorts older than the firm, rising over the next few decay lengths, then geometrically declining.' Every firm in BGN as coded is born at t=0 and never dies (panel_functions_bgn.py:96-97 and :107 -- N identical firms, an identical i.i.d. arrival/death process for each, no entry, no exit, no delisting). All firms have the SAME age at every date, and in the stationary distribution the SAME expected project-age profile. phi_m(i) is therefore not a function of firm age at all; it is pure Poisson-history luck, an unobservable latent vector with identical cross-sectional mean. The 'bump functions of firm age' that the whole argument rests on are constants.

That is fatal in a specific and symmetric way. With N=1000 and idiosyncratic risk diversified, a portfolio's variance is dominated by residual common-factor exposure, so I agree with the proposer that K_eff=24 unpriced cohort factors would genuinely bite -- unpriced common factors are NOT free to leave unhedged in the large-N limit. But hedging requires the exposures to be MEASURABLE functions of the supplied characteristics, and cohort shares are measurable from nothing in the char set. DKKM's 3600 features are functions of (size, bm, agr, roe, mom); none of them carries vintage composition. So neither FM nor DKKM can hedge, both portfolios acquire large uncontrolled cohort exposure, both Sharpes collapse toward the ratio of the premium to the residual cohort volatility, and the horse race becomes a comparison of two noise vectors -- the exact condition (corr(method weight, truth) ~ 0.00) that the diagnosis identified as making the current results meaningless. This proposal would make that worse, not better.

Secondary problems. It does not break the affine identity eret_i = a_t + b_t/mve_i + Chat*pi*bm_i (verified above from :172-186), so the premium cross-section remains exactly two-dimensional -- it adds only unpriced variance, i.e. it strictly lowers max_sr and adds nothing to the signal. It is explicitly conditional on P1 (with the current band there is only ~7% of non-systematic cash-flow variance to allocate). And the implementation is the riskiest in the set: the vintage kernel must be applied as a per-ROW multiplier on kron(col2v,col2v) with the kron row index mapping to (s,s') as row = s*(t+1)+s'; get it wrong and cond_var is silently wrong with no exception, on top of a 15-20% runtime increase in a step that already runs at n_jobs=1 (config.py:40).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and it is more likely to produce a spurious NEGATIVE gap than a positive one. Because neither method can measure cohort exposure, the realised cohort tilt of each method's portfolio is essentially a random draw; whichever method happens to concentrate less in high-loading vintages wins that run. DKKM is if anything the more exposed method, because its ridge-on-3600-features solution is far less stable across months than FM's 7-coefficient OLS, so its month-to-month cohort tilt is noisier. And the one channel the proposer offers for concentration -- that BGN's exercise rule (:82, invest iff exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r_s) > 1, so the beta cutoff is Cbar + log D(r_s)) makes low-rate vintages hold high-beta projects -- cuts the wrong way for the argument: that makes cohort exposure a function of the INTEREST-RATE HISTORY, which is a date-level object common to all firms, not a cross-sectional characteristic. A common tilt is a market tilt and diversifies into the market factor, which FF and FM both already hold. The residual cross-sectional variation is Poisson noise around a common mean, which shrinks as 1/sqrt(num) with num ~ 6 -- small, and unlearnable.
verdicts.salvage: The right version of this idea keeps the extra common factors but attaches them to something the characteristics reveal. Two options. (a) Load the extra common shocks on the project's SYSTEMATIC RISK TYPE rather than its vintage: let all projects with beta in a given band share a cash-flow shock. A firm's exposure is then its value-weighted beta profile, and betabar is recoverable from chars at R^2 = 0.96 -- so the exposures become learnable, hedging them requires a nonlinear function of (size, bm), and FM's L linear coefficients genuinely cannot zero K exposures while DKKM's can. All the analytics survive unchanged because the exponent in E[C_i C_j] stays bilinear. (b) If you insist on vintages, first add staggered firm ENTRY and delisting so that firm age is a real, dispersed, observable characteristic -- which the model badly needs anyway (see missed ideas). Without (a) or (b) this proposal only adds unlearnable noise.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Characteristic-dependent clientele demand wedge (AIPT alpha)
verdicts.critique:
This is rigging, and the proposal says so in its own words: 'choose h to be exactly orthogonal, in each monthly cross-section, to {1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom, ...} and to the six FF factor weight vectors, by projecting the candidate h onto those columns and subtracting. Then the FM-attainable Sharpe from the alpha channel is exactly zero and FF's is exactly zero... This is the one proposal where FM cannot capture it is a theorem rather than an approximation argument.' Constructing the data-generating process by projecting out the competitor estimators' spans is not an economic model; it is an answer key. The proposal even anticipates the referee ('the conclusion was assumed') and offers no defence beyond asserting that the alternative proposals do not work. A paper that reports 'DKKM beats FF/FM by 3x' in an economy whose alpha was orthogonalised against FF's and FM's realised weight vectors month by month will not survive a single seminar, and it should not.

The internal-consistency failures are equally serious. (1) THE SDF IS NO LONGER ANYONE'S MRS. Firms exercise growth options at the rule exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r) > 1 (:82) derived from the representative agent's M, and Jstar.csv values those options under the same M, but traded prices are P*W. So the manager maximises a value no shareholder faces, and the reported max_sr and sdf_ret are the MVE of an SDF that prices nothing anyone optimises against. (2) THE 'TRUE' MVE BECOMES THE MODELLER'S INSERTED NEAR-ARBITRAGE. rp and cond_var recomputed with the wedge yield an annualised max Sharpe of ~3.7 that grows without bound in N (alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N*E[alpha^2/d]), and nothing in the model prevents anyone from taking it. Koijen-Yogo and Gabaix-Koijen demand systems do NOT produce unexploited near-arbitrage of that magnitude; they produce price impact against ELASTIC arbitrageur demand. Citing them while omitting the arbitrage-capital constraint that bounds the wedge is using their names, not their economics. (3) THE WEDGE IS SELF-REFERENTIAL. h is a function of chars, but mve = P*W so bm, size and mom are all contaminated by W, and h is then orthogonalised against those contaminated chars -- a fixed point that must be solved each month and whose solution depends on the exact char list, so the 'result' changes if a co-author adds a characteristic. (4) 'THESE ARE SIMPLE ECONOMIC MODELS' DIES. The paper's entire framing is that three standard, disciplined production models fail to reproduce the virtue of complexity. Bolting on a hand-designed mispricing function to manufacture the result inverts the paper's claim into 'we can produce the result if we assume it.'
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes -- trivially, by construction, which is exactly the objection. The theory diagnosis is right that an unspanned premium is necessary (span2.py: RFF/linear ceiling is 0.994 under exact factor pricing and 21 with nonlinear alpha plus heteroskedastic d), so SOME version of this ingredient is unavoidable. But note two things that undercut even the rigged version. First, the wedge is only partially learnable by design (SIGMA_U is set so the wedge contributes ~15% of idiosyncratic variance), and DKKM must estimate a function orthogonal to every linear direction from 360 months with a feature basis whose participation-ratio effective rank is 14-16 -- the realised DKKM share of max Sharpe could easily be 0.2-0.3 rather than the projected 0.5-0.8, in which case even the rigged economy delivers a modest ratio. Second, at S* ~ 1.1/month both reported metrics degenerate: E[sdf_ret] -> Rf and sd(sdf_ret) -> 0, so HJD converges to ~Rf for every method, and the mean-of-ratios Sharpe is dominated by months where the interpolating alpha=0 column produces a near-hedged w_t with a tiny denominator. The proposal would very likely produce an enormous, unpublishable, metric-artefact-laden table.
verdicts.salvage: A demand wedge is defensible; THIS demand wedge is not. Three non-negotiable changes. (i) Delete the orthogonalisation. Specify h from an economic primitive -- e.g. a benchmarked institutional clientele whose demand is a smooth function of index membership and size, or a tax/dividend clientele -- and then MEASURE how much of the resulting alpha FF and FM span. If they span most of it, that is the finding, and it is an honest one. (ii) Close the model on the arbitrage side: put a finite-capital, risk-averse arbitrageur in front of the wedge so the equilibrium alpha satisfies a capacity constraint and the maximum Sharpe does NOT grow with N.
