That predicts a large DKKM/FF gap and only a modest DKKM/FM gap -- but FM is the binding benchmark, and the diagnosis already shows FM at 0.932 of max SR^2 versus FF at 0.734. (b) DEFAULT RISK HERE IS NOT PRICED. Default is triggered by z (idiosyncratic) and by the i.i.d. valuation shock nu (GS21.m:53-59, 204, 210, 263), neither of which appears in the SDF (GS21.m:138, Mmat depends on the x innovation only). So default adds idiosyncratic left-tail variance, which RAISES d and LOWERS SR^2 through the alpha leg's 1/d. The convexity channel has to beat that. (c) THE METRIC CANNOT SEE THE TAIL. Sharpe_t = w'rp_t / sqrt(w' Sigma_t w) uses only the first two conditional moments (utils/evaluate_sdfs.py:182-209), so a fat left tail enters ONLY through the variance and is therefore a pure penalty. The real-data 'distressed microcap' channel that DKKM's own decomposition attributes most of their Sharpe to is invisible to this metric by construction. FAILURE MODE CHECK, which is severe here: the sigma_m = 5 valuation shock in GS21.m is an economically real i.i.d. shock to the continuation value (P_up_old_pert = E[max(P'+nu,0)]), not a numerical smoother. If the simulation draws it consistently, as the proposal requires, it injects 5/190 = 2.6%/month of PURE UNPRICED idiosyncratic noise -- LARGER than GS21's current total idiosyncratic volatility of 2.03%/month. That alone would cut SR* by more than half and would have to be added to cond_var or the 'true' moments become wrong. Second failure mode: with real defaults, prices approach zero, returns approach -100%, ER conditioning degrades for real, and panel_functions_gs21.py:73-89 has two latent bugs that only fire once defaults exist (the all-firms-default branch never writes the redrawn xt back into x[t] at line 85, and the while loop has no iteration cap).
verdicts.salvage: Ship the default half only, and only after (i) the parameter reconciliation, (ii) removal of the arbitrary P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131, (iii) fixing the two default-replacement bugs, and (iv) a documented decision on sigma_m -- either set it to zero in BOTH the solve and the simulation, or recalibrate it jointly so that the induced 2.6%/month valuation noise does not swamp the economics. Drop kappa_e entirely; it is 0.007%/month of return effect and buys nothing. Then test the mechanism BEFORE running the estimator with the diagnostic that actually predicts the outcome: on the re-solved grid, compute for a simulated cross-section the second-order coefficient c_i2 of P_i(x')/P_i in a Hermite expansion of x', and report R^2(c_i2 | raw linear chars) and R^2(c_i2 | rank-quadratic). GS21's alpha lives in the dispersion of c_i2, and unless that R^2 falls well below 0.5 the default channel will be another monotone-in-dd object that FM eats.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: An independent credit-conditions state s_t with its own price of risk gamma_s
verdicts.critique: This inherits P1's fatal defect and adds a 64 GB memory wall on top of it. The cross-sectional loading is stipulated to be beta_s,i = (P_up_i - P_down_i)/P_ex,i -- exactly the object I measured off the shipped solution files. It is 89.8% linear in the CURRENT raw chars {size, bm, mkt_lev}, 99.6% linear once book_lev is added, and 94.7%/99.7% linear at the proposal's own kappa_b = 0.02. It is 0.548 in rank-linear and 0.801 in rank-quadratic space, i.e. DKKM's basis represents it WORSE than FM's raw-level basis does. The claim 'FM's X(X'X)^{-1} weights place exactly zero loading on it' is false as a matter of measurement, and false in principle too: the symmetric-function argument requires the characteristic's marginal to be symmetric about the vertex, whereas b_it <= max(b_refin) = 0.3158 by the law of motion at panel_functions_gs21.py:117-119, so the realized support is entirely on one arm. Beyond that, the proposal misstates what a second shock buys. With two priced shocks the economy is still EXACT two-factor: Sigma = B Omega B' + D and mu = B lambda with B = [b_x, b_s]. There is still no alpha -- no component of expected returns that is not proportional to a covariance loading. The theory diagnosis's span2.py established that under exact K-factor pricing with N = 1000, ANY well-diversified portfolio with the correct factor exposure attains SR* to within 0.19%. A second shock changes the dimension of the exposure space from 1 to 2, which a 7-factor FM regression handles trivially when the loadings are 90-99.6% linear in chars. The proposal's condition-(C3) framing is also misapplied: DKKM Theorem 3 is a condition on the effective rank of E[F_t F_t'], which the audit measured at 20.7 for GS21's feature map and which is a property of the FEATURE construction, not of the number of aggregate shocks. Going from 1 to 2 shocks moves EffRank from ~2 to ~3 against an AIPT target in the hundreds.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It is strictly WEAKER than proposal 1 at roughly 20x the cost, by the proposal's own parameterization. The credit loading is priced at gamma_s = 0.101/month here versus gamma_x = 0.5/month when the same loading is driven by x under proposal 1 -- a factor of 5 less premium for identical cross-sectional shape. Redoing my proposal-1 arithmetic with lambda = 0.101: the new premium component has cross-sectional sd of 4.9e-4 * 0.101 = 5.0e-5 against sd(mu) = 4.0-5.6e-4, i.e. 1.4% of var(mu), of which 0.4-10% is outside FM's span. Incremental unspanned share of SR^2: under 0.15%. The proposal's own stated fallback -- 'alone, expect only ~1.2-1.3x' -- is itself an overestimate by roughly an order of magnitude. On the ceiling: the model's HJ bound rises from sqrt(exp(0.5^2)-1) = 0.5329/month to sqrt(exp(0.25+0.101^2)-1) = 0.5452/month, i.e. +2.2%, so max_sr essentially cannot move. Since Sharpe = SR* * cos_Sigma(w, w*) and SR* is pinned, the entire claimed 2.0-3.0x DKKM/FM ratio would have to come from FM's cosine collapsing by a factor of 2-3, and I measured FM's representation of the one new object at 90-99.6%. Implementation: the proposal is candid that Mmat goes to 400,000 x 20,000 = 64 GB and that the VFI must be rewritten, and tauchen.m is absent from the repo with no MATLAB installed. Spending a multi-week rewrite to add a factor that carries one fifth the price of risk of the shock already in the model, attached to a loading that FM spans linearly, is the worst cost-benefit ratio in the list.
verdicts.salvage: The one thing that would justify a second shock is if it were priced at a magnitude COMPARABLE to gamma_x and attached to a loading that is genuinely nonlinear in observables -- neither of which holds here. If a second state is worth adding, attach it to the INVESTMENT technology rather than to refinancing: a shock to the aggregate investment-cost distribution (imax_t, currently a fixed 2000 with a cutoff of ~40, so the real option is economically dead at P(invest) = 1.98%/month) would move the option value of every firm, and option value is convex in the firm's own state, so the loading is a genuinely nonlinear function of (z, k, b). That routes the second shock through curvature rather than through a monotone leverage index, which is the only place GS21's alpha actually lives. Even then, do the diagnostic first: simulate the cross-section, compute the new loading, and report R^2 on the RAW linear char span before writing any MATLAB.

missed_ideas: THE INVESTMENT OPTION IS THE NATIVE SOURCE OF CHAR-DEPENDENT CURVATURE AND IT IS DEAD. i_cut_down.csv has mean 39.6 against GS21_IMAX = 2000, so P(invest) = 1.98%/month and the real option's exercise region is 2% of the cost support. GS21's alpha leg -- 89-97% of max SR^2 -- is the premium on firm-specific CURVATURE of P'(x'), i.e. the part of mu not proportional to the top eigenvector of the rank-1 systematic block. Convexity in the aggregate state is exactly what a real option delivers, and it is a nonlinear function of (z, b, k) rather than a monotone index. Cutting imax by 20-50x (or making the cost distribution heavy-tailed, or raising g) so the option is a large, state-dependent share of value creates dispersion in the curvature coefficient with NO new shocks, NO new frictions, and only a single re-solve at unchanged grid dimensions. This is the cheapest change in the whole design space that targets the object the metric actually rewards, and none of the six proposals touches it.

NO PROPOSAL CREATES DISPERSION IN beta_x, AND THAT IS THE FIRST-ORDER OMISSION. The diagnosis measured d log P/d x = 27.3 at b = 0 versus 24.0 at b = 1 (x = -4sd) and 7.5 versus 8.5 at x = +4sd -- there is essentially no leverage amplification of the aggregate beta, because debt value is as x-elastic as equity value. Proposals 4 and 3 move D (diversifiable, O(1/N) under exact factor pricing); proposals 1 and 6 move a loading that is 90-99.6% linear. Nobody proposes heterogeneity in CASH-FLOW DURATION -- firm-specific rho_z, delta, g, or investment technology -- which is the only clean way to disperse beta_x. Duration maps to observables (bm, size) through a nonlinear valuation relation, so the resulting beta_x(chars) is genuinely nonlinear, and unlike D-heterogeneity it does not diversify away.

MEASUREMENT ERROR ON THE CHARACTERISTICS, NOT MORE CHARACTERISTICS. bm = 1/P_ex holds exactly (np.allclose verified in the prior diagnosis), mkt_lev = b/P_ex, size = log k + log P_ex, and rank-standardized roe is the exact rank of lagged z. Four chars invert the entire (k, b, z) state with zero error, which is precisely why an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight and why GS21 sits in DKKM's APT rather than AIPT regime. Proposal 2 adds MORE exact state information (dd = current z, since z_cut_down.csv is a single constant -0.146826 everywhere). The correct move is the opposite: add i.i.d. multiplicative noise (10-20%) and a 1-3 month reporting lag to bm, roe and book_lev in create_panel. Roughly five lines, no re-solve, no MATLAB. It is the only change that makes the optimal weight a nonlinear SHRINKAGE map of the observables, which unpenalized OLS on 7 factors (config.ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0]) structurally cannot represent and ridge over a rich basis structurally can.

RECONCILE THE SOLVE AND THE SIMULATION BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE -- THERE ARE FIVE MISMATCHES, NOT FOUR. GS21.m:35 sets xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03 while config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01: the panel and sdf_compute_gs21.py:132 run at one third of the refinancing intensity the value function was solved with. Only proposal 3 mentions the sigma_x/sigma_z/r mismatches and it misses the zeta one -- which matters most, because it is the exact parameter proposals 1 and 6 want to make stochastic. Also: every interpolator is built with fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74), so the pipeline silently LINEARLY EXTRAPOLATES the value function for the ~0.6-0.7% of firm-months outside the solved grid. Linear extrapolation destroys curvature exactly in the tails, which is the region proposals 3, 4 and 5 all want to activate. Add an off-grid counter before trusting any tail measurement.

VALIDATE max_sr AGAINST THE MODEL'S OWN HJ BOUND BEFORE INTERPRETING ANY RESULT. GS21.m:138 sets Mmat = exp(-r - 0.5*gamma_x^2 - gamma_x*eps_x') with gamma_x = 0.5, so the monthly Sharpe of any correctly priced portfolio is bounded by sqrt(exp(0.25)-1) = 0.5329. The measured 0.438 at N=500 is consistent; the extrapolated 0.62 at N=1000 is a 16% VIOLATION and is a conditioning alarm on scipy.linalg.solve(ER, ones, assume_a='pos') at sdf_compute_gs21.py:207 (which also uses scipy.linalg without importing it -- it resolves only by transitive attribute binding). Report max_sr/0.5329 as a gate in every run. Any proposal whose predicted effect is 'max_sr rises' should be treated as a red flag unless it adds a priced shock, because nothing else can raise the bound.

THE FREE ESTIMATOR-SIDE MOVES ARE UNPRICED IN ALL SIX PROPOSALS. NMAT = 5 (config.py; estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169) averages stock weights across 5 independent W draws, which converges to kernel ridge with the same explicit penalty, cancels exactly the draw-specific high-frequency components, and mechanically FLATTENS the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve -- the root codebase used nmat = 1. N_DKKM_FEATURES_LIST tops out at 3600 (c = 10) against DKKM's headline c = 1000. The RFF effective rank at L = 6 is 20.7 against DKKM's AIPT target of ~500. All three are config-line changes with no re-solve and no economics, and they bound what ANY model change can deliver: if the estimator can only express ~21 effective dimensions, no amount of structural nonlinearity is reachable. Fix these first so that a null result on a structural change is informative.

GIVE THE PRICING-ERROR TEST SOME POWER. generate_25_portfolios.py sorts only on mve and bm -- two of the six characteristics every method already spans linearly -- so compute_pricing_errors.py's alpha'Sigma^{-1}alpha and GRS cannot detect the nonlinear-in-characteristics content that every one of these proposals claims to create. Add test assets sorted on deciles of the model's TRUE conditional SDF weight, on |mkt_lev - b*(z,x)| (the exact object proposals 1 and 6 claim to create), and on interactions. This costs nothing and is the only metric in the pipeline that is not scale-invariant-per-month (unlike Sharpe, which gives zero credit for conditional timing) and not leverage-contaminated (unlike HJD, whose GS21 FF value of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is a pure over-leverage artifact).

RUN A CHEAP PRE-COMMITTED SCREEN ON EVERY PROPOSAL BEFORE ANY MATLAB RE-SOLVE. For any proposed new loading or premium component v_i, the maximum achievable DKKM-over-FM Sharpe ratio is bounded by sqrt(f_RFF/f_FM) where f is the fraction of max SR^2 in each span. The single number that predicts it is R^2(v_i | 1, RAW chars) computed on a simulated cross-section with x held common. FM uses raw levels (fama_functions.py:152-165, standardization commented out), so ranks are the wrong space to test in -- and in fact the rank basis DKKM must use is often WORSE than FM's raw basis, as I measured for G/P (0.55 rank-linear, 0.80 rank-quadratic, versus 0.90 raw-linear for FM). Pre-commit to a threshold: unless R^2(v | raw chars) < 0.5, the proposal cannot move the DKKM/FM ratio by more than a few percent. Applying this screen to the six proposals as written would have rejected 1, 2 and 6 in an afternoon without touching MATLAB.

THE TARGET IS ARITHMETICALLY OUT OF REACH FOR ANY LOADING-SHAPE CHANGE, AND THE PROPOSALS SHOULD SAY SO. Today f_lin = 0.871, f_FM = 0.932 and f_RFF360 = 0.988 of max SR^2, giving DKKM/FM = sqrt(0.988/0.932) = 1.030. To reach a 3x ratio you need f_FM = 0.988/9 = 0.110, i.e. 89% of mu'Sigma^{-1}mu must lie OUTSIDE the linear span of the raw characteristics. Since GS21 is a frictionless rational-expectations economy in which mu is by construction minus the covariance with the SDF, no change to the shock structure or to the loading function can create a component of expected returns that is not proportional to a covariance loading. The only ways to get to 0.110 are (a) make the loading function itself a high-frequency, non-monotone function of the observables -- which needs curvature dispersion, not leverage tilts -- or (b) break the exact char->state invertibility with measurement error so that even a linear truth is not linearly recoverable, or (c) introduce a genuine non-risk premium (demand/belief wedge, segmented marginal investor), which changes what 'true' means and should be argued as heterogeneous agents rather than mispricing. None of the six proposals does (a) at scale, and only proposal 2's cfvol gestures at (b) with a variable that measures nothing.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 1: Procyclical credit supply, zeta(x), with tau and kappa_b recalibration
verdicts.critique:
Three referee-fatal problems, one of which the proposer did not detect.

(1) THE PARAMETER BEING MADE STOCHASTIC IS ALREADY INCONSISTENT BETWEEN SOLVE AND SIMULATION. I read utils_gs21/GS21.m line 35: `xi = 0.03/3*3;` = 0.03. config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01, and that is what utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py:132,157-168,177,184 and utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py:49,200-201 all use. So the value function was solved under a refinancing intensity three times the one the panel simulates and the one the conditional second moment integrates against. Proposal 1's entire mechanism is the derivative of value with respect to this parameter. You cannot make a parameter stochastic and priced when the solve and the simulation currently disagree about its level by 3x. Fix the level first, re-run the baseline, and see how much of the existing 0.5112 vs 0.4433 DKKM/FF gap survives.

(2) THE SPAN ARGUMENT CONFLATES "ZERO LINEAR PROJECTION ON A CHARACTERISTIC" WITH "UNSPANNED BY THE LINEAR PORTFOLIOS." These are different claims and only the first is proved. The proposal's verified fact -- linear R^2 of exp(-c|u|) is 0.000 -- establishes that no single char portfolio has a cross-sectional tilt correlated with beta_credit. It does NOT establish that the 7-portfolio linear span cannot attain the required factor exposure. G_i = P_up - P_down >= 0 with equality only at the vertex, so the equal-weighted market portfolio (fama_functions.fama_macbeth line ~175, P['mkt_rf'] = 1/len(d)) has E[beta_credit] > 0 mechanically. With two priced factors and seven linear portfolios, the exposure-matching problem is over-determined; the linear span hits both loadings and forfeits only the O(1/N) diversification residual. This is precisely what the project's own span2.py measured: under exact factor pricing every basis including equal-weight lands within 0.6% of SR*, and adding a 20x spread in d changed nothing. Proposal 1 keeps the economy an exact factor model. Its headline prediction that linear-6 falls from 0.871 to 0.20-0.30 of max SR^2 is, on the evidence already in this project, off by roughly a factor of three.

(3) BUNDLING. The tau change (0.2/3 -> 0.20) is a genuine units-bug fix and is defensible on its own. The kappa_b change (0.004 -> 0.02, 5x) is a free parameter moved in exactly the direction that widens the inaction region and hence the effect. Bundling a bug fix with an effect-amplifying free-parameter move in one commit is how a referee decides the authors searched.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF and FM can capture most of it and I expect they will. beta_credit is weakly positive for every firm, so the market/equal-weight column already delivers the credit-factor exposure; FM has seven columns to hit two factor targets. What the linear span genuinely cannot form is the D^{-1} tilt on a V-shaped numerator, w* ~ (V_i/d_i), and in GS21 that tilt is worth 0.19% of SR* at N=1000 per the project's own measurement -- unless d_i is made hugely dispersed, which is Proposal 4/5's job, not this one. Even granting the full amplitude story (sd(G/P) 0.0024 -> 0.007), the new premium component is a smooth, symmetric, low-order function of ONE index; the diagnosis measured the entire quadratic headroom in GS21 at 0.871 -> 0.909 of max SR^2. A degree-2 basis buys 4 points of SR^2. FM re-estimated monthly on rank chars is not far off a degree-2 basis once mkt_lev is repaired (Proposal 2), because a symmetric V in a bounded rank variable is 74-88% quadratic and FM sees mkt_lev and book_lev separately. Realistic outcome: DKKM/FM goes from 1.03 to perhaps 1.10-1.25, not 1.7-1.9.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the two disclosed bug fixes and drop the rest for now. (a) Reconcile ZETA between GS21.m line 35 and config.py:296 and re-run the baseline -- this is mandatory regardless. (b) Fix tau = 0.20; dividing a marginal tax rate by 3 is unambiguously a units error and needs no defense. Then, before writing a single line of the zeta(x) code, compute the ORACLE span ratio at the corrected calibration: per month, SR_lin = sqrt(mu' X (X' Sigma X)^{-1} X' mu) with X = [1, chars] versus SR_rff with the configured RFF, using the rp and cond_var already in the moments pickle. If the oracle ratio does not clear 1.5 the proposal is dead and no amount of estimation-side work will revive it. Report that number in the paper whatever it is.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 2: Repair mkt_lev and add book_lev, distance-to-default, rolling investment rate, and cash-flow volatility
verdicts.critique:
The core claim is correct and I verified it. utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py:278 is `df["mkt_lev"] = df["book_lev"] * df["bm"]`, book_lev is `debt` (the coupon per unit capital, line 243), and bm = book/mve = 1/P_ex, so mkt_lev = b/P_ex -- coupon over equity, not market leverage. Q_0 is already constructed as a RegularGridInterpolator at utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py:69 and is in scope in panel_functions_gs21.py via the star-import at line 15. So the fix is available and cheap, and the prior conclusion that "GS21 firms are effectively all-equity" was an artifact of a mis-defined characteristic rather than a property of the model. That is a real correction and it must ship.

My referee objections are about how it is presented and what it is claimed to buy.

(a) DISCLOSURE. This is a bug fix in a characteristic that is one of only six inputs and the only one distinguishing GS21 from the default char set (config.py:223). It must appear in the paper as a correction with the before/after table, not silently in a revised results section. If a reader later diffs the repo and finds mkt_lev changed from 0.0013 to 0.32 between drafts with no note, that is the end of the paper's credibility.

(b) IT IS SYMMETRIC AND MAY NARROW THE GAP. The proposal says this honestly, and I want to reinforce it: FM gets four more linear regressors and its pinvh conditioning improves because mkt_lev is no longer three orders of magnitude smaller than log size (fama_functions.fama_macbeth uses RAW unstandardized chars, lines ~158-161, standardization commented out). Repairing mkt_lev strengthens the linear benchmark. That is the right thing to do and it makes the eventual DKKM result more credible, but it is not a step toward the target.

(c) DISTANCE-TO-DEFAULT IS DEAD AND SHOULD NOT SHIP YET. z_cut_down is pinned at the zgrid floor at every (x,b) in the shipped solfiles, so dd is an affine transform of z and duplicates roe. Shipping a characteristic that is by construction a copy of another characteristic, and only becomes informative after a separate proposal lands, invites the objection that the char set was expanded to pad the RFF input dimension. Gate it on Proposal 5.

(d) THE MECHANICAL HANDICAP TO THE LINEAR METHODS IS REAL. Going from K=7 to K=11 raises the FF/FM plug-in Sharpe loss from ~2K/T = 3.9% to 6.1%, while DKKM's ridge absorbs the extra dimension for free. It is a 2-point handicap, small but it runs in the paper's favored direction and a referee will notice. Report both char sets for the linear methods.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposer says so. The one asymmetric channel claimed -- cfvol as a noisy proxy that requires a nonlinear shrinkage map -- is real in principle but its magnitude is a free choice (36 vs 24 months), and FM's unpenalized OLS is the wrong comparison because the honest fix is to give FM a ridge grid too, at which point FM can shrink on the noisy proxy exactly as well. The effective-rank argument (20.7 at L=6 to 38.5 at L=10) is also weaker than it sounds: T = 360, so effective c goes from 0.058 to 0.107. DKKM's virtue-of-complexity regime needs effective c above 1, i.e. L on the order of 50. Ten characteristics is not a step change in the quantity DKKM's Theorem 3 is stated on; it is a 1.9x move within the classical regime.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the mkt_lev repair and book_lev immediately, as a standalone commit labelled a bug fix, and re-run the full baseline before touching anything else -- everyone needs to know what the corrected baseline DKKM/FF and DKKM/FM numbers are. Add ivest (it genuinely de-degenerates the cma sort, which currently sorts a variable that is 0 in 98.8% of firm-months) and cfvol with the window pre-registered at 36 months and never revisited. Hold dd. Report the linear methods at both the 6-char and the enlarged char set so the K-inflation handicap is visible.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 3: Restore sigma_z to the paper calibration, raise rho_z to 0.985, and repair the solve-vs-simulation parameter mismatches
verdicts.critique:
The mismatch claim is correct and worse than the proposal states. I checked the shipped grids directly against three candidate parameterizations:

  zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159. 4 x stationary sd of 0.1*0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) = 0.146826069677159. Exact match to 15 digits.
  xgrid.max() = 0.153723027652884. 4 x stationary sd of 0.012*sqrt((1-0.95^(2/3))/(1-0.95^2)) = 0.153723027652884. Exact match.

config.py:287 and :290 use the (3/2) exponent, giving sigma_x = 0.010458 and sigma_z = 0.014034, i.e. 1.484x and 1.468x the values the value function was solved for. The interpolators are built with fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74), so off-grid draws are silently linearly extrapolated with no warning and no counter. This is a defect in the CURRENT published baseline, not in any proposal, and it must be fixed before any result from this model is reportable.

And it is a three-way disagreement, not a two-way. GS21.m line 25 has sigma_z with NO 0.1 factor (0.0956); the solfiles were solved WITH the 0.1 factor; config.py has the 0.1 factor but the wrong exponent. Likewise GS21.m:27 r = 0.1/12 versus config.py:299 r = 0.074830/12, and GS21.m:35 xi = 0.03 versus config.py:296 zeta = 0.01. The GS21.m in the repository does not generate the solfiles in the repository, and tauchen.m and gaussHermite.m (called at GS21.m:73-74 and :57) are not present anywhere on disk.

My objections to the proposal as written:

(a) rho_z = 0.985 IS NOT A FIX, IT IS A NEW CALIBRATION. GS21's rho_z = 0.9^(1/3) is the paper's parameter. Changing it to 0.985 is defended by Foster-Haltiwanger-Syverson and Fama-French, which is a respectable citation, but it is the first genuinely discretionary move in this list and it happens to be the one that multiplies d log P / d z by the duration ratio, i.e. the one that makes the cross-section move. Separate it from the sigma restoration and report both.

(b) THE Z-GRID PROBLEM IS NOT A DETAIL. Restoring sigma_z 10x AND raising rho_z to 0.985 takes stationary sd(z) from 0.0539 to 0.554 -- the grid must widen 15x. At znum = 200 that is a 15x coarser mesh through exactly the region where the value function is most curved. The proposal acknowledges the 576 GB alternative. This is the item that determines whether the whole program is feasible.

(c) HONESTY CREDIT. The proposal states plainly that the standalone DKKM/FM effect is 1.03 -> 1.05-1.15 and that a monotone heteroskedasticity channel hands FM 76-92% of itself. That is the correct framing and I would accept it in a paper.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and correctly so -- the proposal calls itself an enabler. The adversarial point worth pressing is that it may hurt the headline: the proposal itself predicts max_sr falls from 0.438/month to 0.15-0.25/month, because GS21's current Sharpe is largely a sqrt(N) near-arbitrage manufactured by 2%/month idiosyncratic volatility. That is scientifically the right direction, but it means every level in the tables drops by half and the paper must switch to reporting Sharpe/SR* (the Sigma-cosine). If the authors restore sigma_z and then quietly keep reporting raw Sharpes, a referee comparing drafts will see the numbers collapse and ask why. Also: 76-92% of a monotone inverse-variance channel goes to FM, and the interaction channel the proposal reserves for DKKM (d_i = f(book_lev, roe) x g(x_t)) is a date-level multiplier g(x_t) that NO method's feature map sees -- dkkm_functions.rff appends rf only for model=='bgn', so GS21's RFF has no time-varying input at all, and the ridge coefficient is a single vector over 360 months. DKKM cannot exploit g(x_t) any more than FM can.
verdicts.salvage: Split into three commits and report the baseline after each. (1) Fix the (3/2) vs (2/3) exponent in config.py:287 and :290 so the simulation matches the grid the value function was actually solved on, and reconcile r and zeta. Add an explicit off-grid counter to the simulation so this class of error cannot recur silently. This commit changes nothing economically and is pure hygiene; it must be in the paper's appendix. (2) Restore sigma_z to the model's own documented value (drop the 0.1 factor added on 2026-06-09 in commits eee2386/dc2462e) and re-solve. This is a revert of an undisclosed ad hoc change and needs only the sentence "we use the calibration in Gomes-Schmid (2021)." (3) Treat rho_z = 0.985 as a separate, clearly labelled recalibration with its own robustness column at rho_z = 0.9^(1/3). Do not fold it into (2).

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 4: Five permanent industry types with different sigma_z
verdicts.critique:
The economics is unobjectionable -- industry cash-flow volatility heterogeneity is real and GS21's single sigma_z is its least defensible homogeneity assumption. My objection is entirely about how the proposal is specified, and it is specified in a way that would not survive a referee report.

(a) THE PROPOSAL CONTAINS ITS OWN TUNING LOOP, IN WRITING. Two sentences: "if it comes out too wide, cut kappa to ln(3.5)/2.564 = 0.489" and "if the linear R^2 exceeds ~0.85 the channel is inert and either kappa or the window must change (shorten to 24 months to raise the proxy noise to 14.4%)." Those are instructions to adjust a structural parameter and an econometrician-side measurement window until the DKKM-favorable channel is live. If any version of that appears in the replication package or the commit history, a referee will quote it and the paper is done. The kappa target (10-90 ratio of 5.0, from Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang) is a legitimate calibration target; the fallback is not.

(b) THE CLAIMED DKKM EDGE IS AN ESTIMATOR ARTIFACT, NOT ECONOMICS. The three asymmetric channels are: the ratio book_lev/b*(cfvol), the moving vertex, and "the optimal weight is E[1/sigma_z | cfvol_observed], a nonlinear SHRINKAGE map, and FM's unpenalized OLS (ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], config.py:187) cannot represent a shrinkage map." The proposal calls point (c) "the cleanest formal argument." It is the weakest, because it is an artifact of the referee-fairness defect that runs through this entire project: FF and FM are handed alpha = 0 and DKKM is handed six alphas whose winner is selected post hoc on the evaluation metric (create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model, lines 81-97, returns max over alphas of the mean Sharpe across iterations). Give FM the same ridge grid and it represents the shrinkage map perfectly well. Building a proposal on FM's lack of regularization is building on plumbing.

(c) PERMANENT TYPES ARE LEARNABLE. Fixed effects over a 360-month rolling window are recovered almost exactly by any method, including FM, which re-runs the cross-sectional regression each month with cfvol as a regressor. The proposal notes this risk itself and suggests slow Markov migration, which would be the right specification.

(d) FIVE SETS OF SOLFILES multiplies an already irreproducible solve by five. GS21.m does not currently regenerate one set (see my Proposal 3 verdict); five is five times unreproducible.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures most of it, by the proposal's own arithmetic: linear R^2 of exp(-c u) is 0.861 at a 25x variance range. The residual is a two-characteristic multiplicative term at linear R^2 = 0.458 vs quadratic 0.815 -- which means a QUADRATIC basis, not a 3600-feature RFF, gets nearly all of the remainder. That maps onto the diagnosis's measured GS21 span numbers exactly: linear-6 = 0.871, +21 quadratics = 0.909, RFF360 = 0.988. Adding heteroskedasticity moves premium into a channel where the quadratic basis is already 91% of the way there. And the deeper problem is the one from Proposal 1: dispersion in d only matters through the inverse-variance tilt, and under exact factor pricing with N = 1000 that tilt is worth 0.19% of SR*. The project's own span2.py measured SR* = 0.100, linear span = 0.100 with d spanning 20x. Heteroskedastic D is a multiplier on an unspanned alpha, and this proposal adds no alpha. On its own I would expect DKKM/FM to move from 1.03 to 1.08-1.12, consistent with the proposal's own 1.10-1.15 estimate, which is a fifth of the target.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the economics, delete the discretion. Fix kappa = ln(5)/2.564 = 0.6277 from AHXZ and never touch it; if the realized idio-vol range comes out wrong, report that as a model failure rather than adjusting. Replace permanent types with a slow Markov industry-migration chain so the type is not a learnable fixed effect. Fix the cfvol window at 36 months by pre-registration. And critically: run the reformed-fairness comparison (FM and FF with the identical ridge grid and the identical post-hoc alpha selection DKKM gets) BEFORE claiming that the nonlinear shrinkage map is a DKKM-only capability -- I do not believe it is.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 5: Turn on kappa_e, raise tau and bmax so the negative-cash-flow region and the default boundary are reachable, and simulate the sigma_m valuation shock
verdicts.critique:
This is the proposal with the best economics-to-plumbing ratio in the set and the only one whose defense in a referee report is a single clean sentence: "the model already contains these frictions; we turn them on at empirically standard values." I verified the code paths exist and are inert: GS21.m lines 253-254 and 259-260 are `P0_up_R = (1 + (prof0_up<=0).*kappa_e).*prof0_up` and the PI_up analogue, with kappa_e = 0 at line 33 and the intended 0.025 commented out; the sigma_m Gauss-Hermite default smoothing is at lines 53-59 and the perturbed price expectations at 263-264. panel_functions_gs21.py:72 tests P[t] <= 0 with no nu draw, so the simulation and the solve currently disagree about whether the default indicator is smoothed at all. That internal inconsistency is a genuine defect in the baseline and fixing it is not a model change.

Four objections.

(a) SIGMA_M IS THE PROBLEM. The proposal is right that sigma_m = 5 against P ~ 190 gives Phi(-38) = 0 exactly. But the fix it proposes -- "sigma_m must be chosen by a one-dimensional search on a simulated panel AFTER the re-solve" targeting 1%/yr defaults -- installs a pure numerical smoothing parameter, with no economic referent, as the direct control on how much nonlinearity the model has. A referee will read that as: the amount of the paper's headline effect is set by a free numerical constant tuned by search. Moody's 1.5%/yr is a legitimate target, so the search is defensible IF and only if the target is fixed in advance, disclosed, and the result is reported at 0.5%, 1%, and 2%/yr as a robustness triple. Without that triple I would reject on this point alone.

(b) THE MOVING-KINK ARGUMENT FOR DKKM IS WRONG. "The kink LOCATION depends on the aggregate state x_t... FM is re-estimated monthly so it can shift an intercept, but it cannot bend." DKKM cannot track a moving kink either. dkkm_functions.rff appends the raw rf column only for model == 'bgn'; GS21's RFF has no time-varying input, its features are purely cross-sectional rank transforms, and the ridge coefficient vector is estimated once per month on a 360-month window and applied to the whole cross-section. Both methods can shift a level and neither can move a kink. Drop this argument; the tail-location argument in point (a) of the proposal (linear R^2 of 1{u > p10} is 0.27 versus 0.75 at the median) is the good one and it stands on its own.

(c) SELECTIVE SAMPLE ATTRITION IS THE ROBUSTNESS CHECK I WOULD DEMAND FIRST. Defaulting firms reset with roe and mom NaN for 12 months (panel_functions_gs21.py:275,285) and prepare_panel drops them. So the very firms carrying the distress premium are systematically absent from the estimation sample for a year after every reset, and the attrition is correlated with the signal. At 1%/yr this is tolerable; if the calibration search lands at 3-5%/yr it is a first-order selection problem that biases every method, and it biases them differently because FF value-weights.

(d) IT IS CONDITIONAL ON PROPOSAL 3 AND PROBABLY DEAD WITHOUT IT. The proposal says so. Fine, but it means the paper cannot present this as an independent change.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, and it is the only proposal here for which I would concede that FF genuinely cannot compete: FF's 2x3 sorts value-weight (fama_functions.fama_french, the smb block at lines ~68-79 normalizes by mve), so the distressed small-cap tail where the kinks bind gets near-zero weight in every FF factor. A 2-3x DKKM/FF gap is plausible. But the FF comparison is the weak one -- the diagnosis already established that FM, a purely LINEAR method, closes 13 of the 16 points separating FF from the DKKM ceiling in GS21. Against FM the case is much thinner: default probability is convex but MONOTONE in distance-to-default, and once dd is supplied as a characteristic (Proposal 2) FM gets a lot of it -- the proposal's own number is linear R^2 = 0.763 even at a 100x range, and quadratic 0.971. A paper whose headline is "DKKM beats FF by 2.5x" while FM, with seven linear regressors, sits between them is not a virtue-of-complexity paper; it is a paper about the inefficiency of tercile sorting and value weighting. The referee's question will be: what is DKKM/FM? If the answer is 1.3, the abstract cannot say what the authors want it to say.
verdicts.salvage: Ship it, but with the presentation restructured around DKKM/FM rather than DKKM/FF, and with these commitments made before the re-solve: kappa_e = 0.05 (Hennessy-Whited) fixed; tau = 0.20 fixed as a units-bug fix; bmax set by the interest-coverage argument (b IS inverse coverage, so bmax = 2 gives coverage 0.5) and not by search; the default-rate target fixed at 1.5%/yr (Moody's all-corporate) and reported at 0.5/1.5/3.0 as a triple. Fix the two latent bugs in the replacement machinery first (panel_functions_gs21.py:85 never writes the redrawn xt back into x[t], and the while loop at line 73 has no iteration cap) -- they are dormant only because defaults never happen and both fire the moment this proposal lands. Remove the P_ex floor at line 131 and add an explicit minimum-eigenvalue guard on cond_var before scipy.linalg.solve, which at line 207 of sdf_compute_gs21.py is called on a module that is never imported.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 6: An independent credit-conditions state s_t with its own price of risk gamma_s
verdicts.critique:
This is the most intellectually serious proposal and the one most likely to be read as "the authors added a factor until the answer came out." I would not reject it on identity grounds -- adding a stochastic external-finance state to a model whose defining friction is external finance is defensible and the He-Krishnamurthy / Gilchrist-Zakrajsek citation is the right one. I would reject it, as currently specified, on three other grounds.

(a) IT MAY SHRINK THE VERY QUANTITY DRIVING GS21'S SHARPE. The diagnosis measured that 89-97% of GS21's maximum squared Sharpe comes from the ALPHA leg -- the residual of mu on the single covariance loading, diversified across N nearly identical firms -- and only 3-11% from the market/beta leg. Adding a second priced factor moves premium from the alpha residual into the beta space, because more of mu is now explained by B. Mechanically, alpha' D^{-1} alpha falls. The proposal's prediction that the second eigenvalue rises from 0.03% to 5-20% of the first is probably right; the unstated consequence is that the alpha leg, which is what the linear span was failing to capture, gets smaller. The net effect on the DKKM/FM ratio is genuinely ambiguous and the proposal does not address it. This needs the oracle span calculation before any code is written.

(b) GAMMA_S IS FREE AND SET TO HIT A TARGET, AND THE PROPOSAL SHOWS ITS OWN ARITHMETIC FAILING. "At the CURRENT sd(G/P) = 0.00241 that is 1.1e-4, only 17% -- so this proposal MUST be combined with proposal 1's tau and kappa_b recalibration... To push the non-monotone share above 80% you need sd(G/P) ~ 0.03... which requires proposals 3 and 5 as well." Read that paragraph as a referee: the second factor is economically trivial at the model's own parameters, and reaching the target requires stacking four other changes each of which moves a free parameter in the same direction. That is a description of a search over a five-dimensional parameter space with the DKKM/FM ratio as the objective. It does not matter that each individual move has a citation attached; the joint move does not.

(c) IT IS NOT EXECUTABLE. Mmat at snum = 5 is 400,000 x 20,000 = 64 GB dense. tauchen.m and gaussHermite.m are absent from the repository (I checked: utils_gs21/ contains only GS21.m, GS21_solfiles/, and the Python files). GS21.m as posted does not reproduce the shipped solfiles -- it has sigma_z with no 0.1 factor and the (2/3) exponent, xi = 0.03 against config's 0.01, and r = 0.1/12 against config's 0.074830/12, while the shipped zgrid corresponds to a third parameterization (0.1 x 0.16 with the (2/3) exponent, matching zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159 to 15 digits). Proposing a four-dimensional state space on top of a solver that cannot currently regenerate its own three-dimensional output is not a plan.

One further point in the proposal's favor that it undersells: it correctly notes that GS21.m lines 14-16 declare Epstein-Zin parameters (beta, varphi = 2, gamma = 10) that are NEVER USED -- the SDF is an exogenous lognormal with a constant price of risk gamma_x = 0.5 (line 28). If the paper implies the SDF is derived from preferences, that must be corrected regardless of this proposal.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The strongest adversarial case is the same as against Proposal 1 and it applies with more force here. Two priced factors with N = 1000 is still exact factor pricing: mu = B lambda with B of rank 2. The linear span has seven portfolios to hit two exposure targets, and beta_s = G/P >= 0 for every firm means the equal-weight market column already loads on the credit factor. The project's own span2.py measured that under exact factor pricing every basis including equal-weight sits within 0.6% of SR*, and that adding a 20x spread in d does not change this. Raising the priced rank from 1 to 2 does not escape that result -- it is still exact factor pricing, just with K = 2. What produced the 8.6x and 21x oracle ratios in span2.py was an ALPHA: expected return NOT proportional to the covariance loadings. None of the six proposals here, including this one, introduces one, because all six keep a single representative-agent SDF under which mu is minus the covariance with m by construction. That is the deepest gap in the entire proposal set.
verdicts.salvage: Before any MATLAB work: compute the oracle span ratio SR_rff/SR_lin under a REDUCED-FORM two-factor version -- take the existing cond_var and rp from the moments pickle, add a synthetic second loading beta_s proportional to (P_up - P_down)/P_ex at the chosen amplitude and price of risk, and recompute the population span fractions. That is an afternoon's work with objects already on disk and it settles points (a) and the exact-factor-pricing objection without a re-solve. If the oracle ratio clears 2.0, the 64 GB problem becomes worth solving (via the Kronecker structure already present at GS21.m:75-76, or a Python port). If it does not clear 1.5, this proposal and Proposal 1 are both refuted and the model needs an alpha, not another beta.

missed_ideas: THE SENTENCE THAT KILLS THE PAPER, AND NO PROPOSAL ADDRESSES IT: the GS21.m in the replication package cannot regenerate the solution files in the replication package. I verified GS21.m:25 uses sigma_z = 0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) = 0.0956 with no 0.1 factor, GS21.m:35 uses xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03, and GS21.m:27 uses r = 0.1/12; config.py:290/296/299 use 0.014034, 0.01 and 0.074830/12; and the shipped zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159 matches a THIRD parameterization (0.1*0.16 with the (2/3) exponent) to 15 digits, while xgrid.max() = 0.153723027652884 matches 0.012*sqrt((1-0.95^(2/3))/(1-0.95^2)). GS21.m also calls tauchen and gaussHermite, neither of which exists anywhere in either repository. My report would open: 'The value function on which every result in Section 5 depends cannot be reproduced by anyone, including the authors.' Fix this before considering any economics. Every re-solve proposal (1, 3, 4, 5, 6) is otherwise unimplementable.

THE FAIRNESS DEFECT IS ORTHOGONAL TO ALL SIX PROPOSALS AND WILL BE BLAMED FOR WHATEVER GAP THEY PRODUCE. config.py:187 gives FF and FM ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] -- unpenalized OLS, one cell, no tuning. DKKM gets 4 nfeatures x 6 alphas = 24 cells, and create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model (lines 81-97) selects the alpha by argmax of the mean Sharpe (or argmin HJD) computed ON THE EVALUATION SAMPLE, then reports that cell. Worse, config.py:190 defines ALPHA_LST_GS = [x/100 for x in ALPHA_LST] -- the penalty grid was hand-recentered for GS21, for DKKM only. A referee reads 'we divided the complex model's penalty grid by 100 for this model' as a tuning decision that the benchmarks did not receive. Before any model change: give FF and FM the same ridge grid, run the alpha selection on a held-out split rather than the evaluation metric, and report the full 24-cell DKKM grid rather than its maximum. If DKKM/FF moves off 1.15 under that reform alone, the paper's premise is different from what the authors think it is.

NOBODY PROPOSED THE CHEAPEST AIPT INGREDIENT: MEASUREMENT ERROR AND REPORTING LAGS ON THE EXISTING CHARACTERISTICS. The diagnosis identified as a blocker that GS21's chars invert the state exactly -- bm = 1/P_ex to machine precision, roe is a monotone transform of lagged z, size = log k + log P_ex -- and that an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight from them. Real Compustat data forces the opposite: book equity is annual, used for twelve months, reported with a lag, and restated. Simply replacing the monthly book value in panel_functions_gs21.py with a value stale-dated 6 months and updated annually, and adding modest noise to roe, destroys the exact invertibility at zero re-solve cost, zero new economic parameters, and with a defense a referee cannot argue with ('we impose the data-availability convention of Fama-French (1993)'). It is more defensible than every proposal here except the bug fixes and it was not proposed.

NO PROPOSAL INTRODUCES AN UNSPANNED PREMIUM (AN ALPHA), WHICH THE PROJECT'S OWN EVIDENCE SAYS IS THE ONLY THING THAT MATTERS. span2.py measured the RFF-over-linear oracle ceiling at 0.994 under exact factor pricing and 8.6x-21x once expected returns contain a component not proportional to the covariance loadings. All six proposals keep a single representative-agent lognormal SDF (GS21.m:138) under which mu = -cov(m, R) by construction, so alpha is identically zero and the span ceiling is pinned near 1.00 up to O(1/N). Proposals 1 and 6 add differently-shaped BETAS, which does not escape this: with K = 2 and seven linear portfolios the exposure problem is over-determined, and since beta_credit = G/P >= 0 for every firm the equal-weight market column already carries the exposure. The missing option is a segmented-investor or heterogeneous-SDF version of GS21 -- e.g. two investor clienteles with different gamma_x facing a participation constraint, so the marginal investor differs across the cross-section and the observed price reflects a wedge that is a nonlinear function of characteristics. That is harder to defend to a referee than any proposal here, but it is the only one that targets the binding constraint.

NMAT = 5 IS A LOCAL DEVIATION THAT PROVABLY FLATTENS THE COMPLEXITY CURVE, AND FIXING IT IS FREE. config.py:177 says 'ROOT: main_revised.py line 12: nmat = 1' and then sets NMAT = 5. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py averages the stock weights across 5 independent W draws, which converges to kernel ridge at the SAME explicit penalty, cancels exactly the draw-specific high-frequency directions, and makes the large-M limit depend on P only through a vanishing implicit ridge -- i.e. it mechanically flattens Sharpe-versus-nfeatures, which is the curve the paper needs to be rising. Set NMAT = 1 and report the 5 draws as replications. This should be done before any model change, because it is free, it is defensible, and if the flat curve persists at NMAT = 1 that is important information about the models rather than the estimator.

THE HEADLINE OBJECT IS MISSING FROM EVERY TABLE AND EVERY PROPOSAL. max_sr is computed in sdf_compute_gs21.py:222-224 and saved into the moments pickle, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it into results.pkl. Since Sharpe_t(w) = SR*_t x cos_Sigma(w, w*_t) exactly, a table of raw Sharpes is uninterpretable: 0.4433 could be 15% or 95% of the attainable ceiling. Every table must report Sharpe / SR*. This matters especially for Proposal 3, which is predicted to CUT max_sr from 0.438 to 0.15-0.25 per month -- without the normalization, that change looks like every method got worse.

DEMAND THE PLACEBO AT THE NEW CALIBRATION. The diagnosis found that 150 RANDOM Gaussian directions carrying zero characteristic information already attain 0.74-0.82 of GS21's max SR^2, and 90 attain 0.44-0.52. Much of what looks like an RFF span advantage is dimension counting. Any post-change claim that RFF360 attains 0.85-0.95 of max SR^2 must be accompanied by the same number for 360 random directions. If the gap between informed RFF and random RFF is small, the result is plumbing.

REPORT EVERYTHING AT N = 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000. GS21's maximum Sharpe is 89-97% a cross-sectional alpha leg that scales as sqrt(N) -- a synthetic near-arbitrage with no real-data counterpart. If the DKKM-over-FM gap grows with N, it is a diversification artifact of the simulation design, not a pricing result. This is a one-line experiment and it is the first robustness check I would demand of any positive result. No proposal mentions it.

THE HONEST ALTERNATIVE PAPER WAS NOT CONSIDERED. The current diagnosis is a coherent, publishable negative result: three canonical structural asset pricing models with 1-2 priced aggregate shocks and exact factor pricing cannot generate the virtue of complexity, and here are the five conditions (C1-C5) that a model would have to satisfy. That paper is defensible, cannot be accused of specification search, and is more useful to the literature than a paper that reports a 2x DKKM gap obtained after changing sigma_z, rho_z, tau, kappa_b, kappa_e, bmax, sigma_m, adding zeta(x), five volatility types, and a second priced shock. If the authors proceed with the modifications, they should pre-register the full change list and the target metric before running the pipeline, and publish both the negative baseline and the modified result side by side.

PLUMBING-VERSUS-ECONOMICS RANKING, WHICH IS HOW A REFEREE WILL SORT THESE. Mostly economics: Proposal 5 (turning on frictions the model already contains, at literature-standard values) and Proposal 3's sigma_z restoration (a revert of an undisclosed ad hoc change). Mixed: Proposal 6 (real economics, but gamma_s is free and the effect requires stacking four other changes) and Proposal 1 (real economics in zeta(x), but bundled with a 5x kappa_b move and resting on a span argument I believe is wrong). Mostly plumbing: Proposal 4, whose cleanest claimed DKKM advantage is that FM is denied a ridge penalty (config.py:187), and Proposal 2, which is a necessary bug fix but whose stated DKKM benefit is an effective-rank increase from 20.7 to 38.5 against T = 360 -- a move within the classical regime, not into the one DKKM's theory describes.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Restore/overshoot the idiosyncratic cash-flow band (0.1 -> 1.75) + ivol characteristic
verdicts.critique:
I re-ran this myself rather than trusting the numbers, and three things came out badly.

(1) THE REPORTED SPAN NUMBERS USE THE WRONG WEIGHT SPACE. A linear characteristic method delivers stock weights w = X a (FM's portfolios are the columns of X pinvh(X'X), fama_functions.py:152-165, so the MVE over those factors lies in col(X)). The attainable Sharpe is sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp). Proposal 1 (and the earlier BGN diagnosis) report a projection corresponding to w = Sigma^{-1} X a instead. I verified both on the same cross-section (N=1000, band=0.1, X=[1,log mve,bm]): w=Xa gives 69.4% of max_sr; w=Sigma^{-1}Xa gives 83.4%. The 91.7%/95.03% figures throughout the diagnosis phase are the wrong object and every headroom number needs recomputing.

(2) THE PROPOSAL LEAVES EXPECTED RETURNS EXACTLY TWO-DIMENSIONAL AND EXACTLY LINEAR. From panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186: term1 and term3 are date-level scalars, term2 = pi*A*e_t/bond_t with A = P - G_t (lines 153, 161-164), term4 = Chat*pi*book. Hence 1+eret_i = [pi*e_t/bond_t] + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + (Chat*pi)*bm_i, with bm coefficient identically Chat*pi = 0.0244763. sigmaj appears nowhere in that block. So after Proposal 1 the true risk premium is still an EXACT affine function of two characteristics, and the entire claimed DKKM advantage is the ability to invert a diagonal matrix. That is inverse-variance weighting, not the virtue of complexity.

(3) THE HEADLINE IS FM GETTING WORSE, NOT DKKM GETTING BETTER. My corrected ceilings at the production N=1000 (mean over t=250,260,270, seed 0): band 0.1 -> FM+ivol 0.926, RFF360 0.993, max_sr 0.3315; band 1.75 -> FM+ivol 0.721, RFF360 0.926, max_sr 0.2559. DKKM's ABSOLUTE population Sharpe falls from 0.329 to 0.237. A table showing 'DKKM/FF rises to 1.4x' while the true maximum Sharpe and every method's absolute Sharpe fall reads as a metric artifact.

DISCLOSURE: the line being changed is panel_functions_bgn.py:54, carrying the comment '# added a factor of 0.1'. Multiplying a hand-inserted fudge factor by 17.5x, in the one direction that produces the desired result, after that result failed to appear, is exactly what a referee is hunting for. Defensible only if presented as a calibration correction on its own merits with the full moment scan disclosed, including the settings that do NOT deliver the result.

Minor: the calibration table is not reproducible in detail. At m=1.75 I measure median stock vol 11.1%/mo but MEAN 14.9% (heavy-tailed), pairwise corr 0.150, sd(log d) 1.12. Close enough to the claimed 12.3%/0.220/1.212 to accept, but the mean-vs-median distinction is doing real work and is undisclosed.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The direction replicates — I get the DKKM/FM population ceiling rising from 1.072x to 1.285x — but it collapses under the one robustness check every referee will demand. The proposal's own logic says the target is w* ~ (rp - Bc)/d, a ratio. So hand FM the ratio. I added two columns to FM's raw basis, bm/ivol^2 and log(mve)/ivol^2: at band 1.75 FM goes 0.7205 -> 0.9095 against RFF360's 0.9257. The DKKM/FM ceiling collapses from 1.285x to 1.018x. A LINEAR method with two hand-built interaction terms captures 98% of what a 360-feature random-Fourier basis captures. The 'complexity' on display is a single product of two supplied characteristics, available to FM at zero cost. FF is genuinely disadvantaged (tercile step functions cannot track a variable spanning four orders of magnitude), but FF is the weak benchmark; FM is the one that matters and FM survives. Second, because rp stays exactly in span{1, 1/mve, bm}, the gap is purely the D^{-1} tilt, which under exact K-factor pricing shrinks as N grows — my N=250 vs N=1000 comparison already shows the linear span's shortfall is N-sensitive, and a referee will ask for N=5000.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the band change as a CALIBRATION CORRECTION, argued and disclosed on its own moment-matching merits (the current model has 5.4%/month stock volatility, 0.60 average pairwise correlation, sd(log idiosyncratic variance) 0.17 — all indefensible), made BEFORE and INDEPENDENTLY of any complexity result, with the full scan m in {0.1,1.0,1.25,1.5,1.75,2.0} and all four moment targets in an appendix table. Prefer m=1.5 (median vol 7.8%, pairwise 0.27, sd(log d) 0.74) over 1.75 if you want to avoid a 63,000x d-ratio and the conditioning exposure. Then state honestly that this buys a population ceiling ratio of at most ~1.29x, that it vanishes once the linear benchmark gets ratio characteristics, and that it leaves the cross-section of expected returns exactly two-dimensional. It is a precondition for Proposals 2/5, not a result.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: Project-scale / intangible-capital wedge kappa breaking the rp = a + b/mve + Chat*pi*bm identity
verdicts.critique:
This is the only proposal that attacks the actual binding constraint, and its central claim is correct — I verified it analytically from the code, not by simulation. panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186 gives 1+eret_i = pi*e_t/bond_t + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + Chat*pi*bm_i, with the bm coefficient exactly Chat*pi = 0.0244763 at every date. Two characteristics span the entire cross-section of true expected returns EXACTLY. That identity is why nothing can beat FM here, and P2 is one of only two proposals (with P5) that breaks it. P1, P3, P4 and P6-without-BETA_ZR all leave it intact and can therefore only ever compete on the covariance side.

The mechanism is also the right KIND of economics. A latent state (economic capital Lambda) observable only through a noisy signal (payout yield) whose precision varies across firms (with project count and cash-flow volatility) makes the efficient predictor a firm-specific shrinkage weight times the signal. That is a genuine three-way interaction; it is precisely why DKKM's five-characteristic real-data result works while these models' five characteristics do not; and it is defensible as economics rather than as a basis trick. The intangible-capital framing (book value ceases to measure economic capital) is standard and publishable — Peters-Taylor, Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou. It also raises cross-sectional predictive R^2 from 0.043%/month, an order of magnitude BELOW real data, toward ~0.5%, fixing a calibration defect the paper should want fixed anyway.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is serious: NOTHING HERE WAS SIMULATED. Every number in the predicted-effect block is derived, and the author says so. P1 at least has measurements (albeit against the wrong projector). Before this appears in a paper you need the population ceiling computed the way I computed P1's — FM basis vs RFF basis vs true max_sr, at N=1000, over multiple months and seeds.

Second, the implementation risk is real and correctly identified. kappa must appear once on col1 and col3 (sdf_compute_bgn.py:162,164), NOT inside the exponentiated col2 (line 163), twice outside the exp on term4, and squared on three diagonal corrections (lines 220-231, 234-256, 259-265) plus term2t (lines 214-218). Any one of those wrong silently biases cond_var with no exception — exactly the failure mode already documented for KP14's integ_results.npz. The proposed Monte Carlo validation (simulate R_{t+1} at fixed t, check the empirical second moment against sdf_loop's ER elementwise) is not optional; it is the referee's minimum bar and belongs in an appendix.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, and less than claimed. The honest adversarial reading: FM is not restricted to one characteristic per signal. The econometrician can construct payout*nproj, payout/ivol^2, payout*ivol and hand them to FM, exactly as I did to kill P1. The optimal shrinkage pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + noise_i^2/(num_i*H)) is a smooth monotone function of a single scalar index, so a second-order expansion in that index times the signal — three linear columns — recovers most of it. My P1 experiment is the precedent: two hand-built ratio columns closed a 1.285x gap to 1.018x. I would expect FM augmented with {payout, payout*nproj, payout/ivol^2} to recover 80-90% of the DKKM ceiling, leaving ~1.1-1.2x rather than the claimed 1.2-1.35x. The defensible position is not 'FM cannot do this' — it can, given the right constructed columns — but 'FM cannot do this without the econometrician already knowing the structural shrinkage formula.' That is a genuine and honest statement about what complexity buys; say it, and pre-commit to a characteristic set chosen without reference to the structural solution. Note also that the two channels can cancel: at P1's band the payout signal may be so noisy that optimal shrinkage is near zero and the channel dies — the author flags this, and it must be checked before implementation, not after.
verdicts.salvage: Keep as the centrepiece with four required changes. (a) Simulate it and report the population ceiling with the CORRECT w = Xa projector at N=1000 across months and seeds, before writing prose. (b) Frame it as unmeasured intangible capital, cite the accounting literature, and calibrate SIGMA_KAPPA to an independently measured moment (sd of the economic-to-book capital ratio, or the cross-sectional R^2 of returns on chars) — never to the DKKM/FM gap. (c) Give FM and FF the payout characteristics AND at least one constructed interaction, and report the gap that survives; a gap existing only because the linear benchmark was denied an obvious column is not a result. (d) Ship the elementwise Monte Carlo validation of ER as an appendix table. Done this way it is publishable economics: it fixes the model's cross-sectional R^2, it is motivated by a large empirical literature, and its nonlinearity is a consequence of signal extraction rather than an assumption.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Repair agr, add characteristics, rescale GAMMA_GRID, NMAT=1, recentre ALPHA_LST
verdicts.critique:
This is two proposals wearing one coat, and they deserve opposite verdicts.

THE BUG FIXES ARE MANDATORY AND MUST NOT BE BUNDLED. agr is 91% ties at exactly zero because book = I*num (panel_functions_bgn.py:144) is a small integer, and dkkm_functions.rank_standardize breaks the ties with np.argsort (line 57), manufacturing a persistent pseudo-random column that enters all 3600 RFF features multiplicatively but only one of FM's six regressors additively. The FF cma sort is simultaneously degenerate (q30 = q70 = 0, so the '2x3' is a 92/0/8 split with literally empty middle portfolios). These are defects, they are asymmetric, and they must be repaired regardless of what happens to the model. Repair them in a separate commit, re-run the baseline, and report the corrected baseline BEFORE any model change. If the corrected baseline moves at all, the currently published tables are wrong and that belongs in the paper.

THE DKKM-ONLY KNOBS ARE THE PROBLEM. GAMMA_GRID rescaling, NMAT 5->1, and recentring ALPHA_LST are three tuning changes applied to exactly one of three competing estimators, after that estimator was observed to lose. Meanwhile config.py:187 sets ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] — FF and FM get no regularization and no tuning at all — and bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py:83-97 (find_best_alpha_for_model) selects DKKM's alpha by argmax of the evaluation metric itself across all iterations. As the pipeline stands, DKKM already gets post-hoc selection over 6 alphas x 4 feature counts using the reported statistic, and FF/FM get zero tuning decisions. Adding three more DKKM-only knobs is indefensible and cannot be buried: the alpha grid is in config.py and a referee will read it.

AND THE BANDWIDTH KNOB DOES NOT WORK. I tested it directly on BGN's true moments, N=1000, RFF with 360 features: gamma x1 gives ceiling 0.9931 (band 0.1) and 0.9257 (band 1.75); gamma x3.44 gives 0.9931 and 0.9303; gamma x8 gives 0.9763 and 0.8927. The recommended rescale is worth +0.5 percentage points at band 1.75 and exactly zero at baseline; the larger rescale is actively harmful. The a priori argument (match DKKM's L=130 effective sd(Wx)) is principled and pre-registerable, which is its saving grace — but it belongs in a robustness column, not the main specification.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal concedes ~1.05x standalone. My measurements agree: the bandwidth rescale is worth +0.005 of ceiling. Worse, the characteristic-addition half actively HELPS the competitor. At the current calibration FM with the raw five characteristics reaches 0.810 of max_sr, but FM with ivol added reaches 0.926 — adding one characteristic closed most of FM's shortfall and cut the DKKM/FM ceiling from 1.23x to 1.07x. So 'give the econometrician more characteristics' is, in this model, a PRO-FM intervention. It becomes pro-DKKM only if the added characteristics enter the truth nonlinearly, which requires a model change first. The proposal is honest about this ('only ship with a model change whose target is demonstrably nonlinear'), and that honesty is correct.
verdicts.salvage: Split into three commits with three justifications. (1) BUG FIXES, unconditional: 12-month agr, and either drop the degenerate cma factor or document the empty middle portfolios. Re-run and republish the baseline. (2) CHARACTERISTIC SET, chosen and frozen BEFORE seeing any complexity result, justified by 'what would a real econometrician observe from this firm', and identical for FF, FM and DKKM. Include 1/mve as well as log(mve) — see my missed-ideas list; rp is exactly affine in 1/mve, so denying FM that transform is a live, undisclosed handicap. (3) ESTIMATOR HYPERPARAMETERS: whatever you do to DKKM's regularization you must do to FF/FM. Give FF/FM the same ridge grid, and either drop the post-hoc argmax in find_best_alpha_for_model in favour of a fixed pre-specified alpha, or apply identical post-hoc selection to FF/FM and disclose it in the table caption. The bandwidth rescale goes in a robustness appendix with the measurement that it is worth +0.5pp.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Cohort (vintage) common cash-flow factors with age-dependent exposures
verdicts.critique:
The construction is elegant and the code path is right: cohort shocks are orthogonal to nu, so cov(log M, log C_j) = -beta_j is preserved, risk-neutral project value stays Chat*exp(-beta_j), and Jstar.csv/optval need no re-solve. I checked lines 69-76 and 148-186 and agree that prices, the exercise rule and the entire eret vector are untouched.

But that last point is the problem, not the feature. Because eret is untouched, the true conditional risk premium remains EXACTLY affine in (1/mve, bm) with bm coefficient Chat*pi = 0.0244763. Proposal 4 is, like Proposal 1, a pure covariance-side intervention. The paper's claim would be 'complexity pays because it hedges unpriced factors better' — a statement about covariance estimation, not the DKKM/AIPT mechanism (unspanned expected-return components spread across many eigenvalue directions). A referee who knows that theory will say you have demonstrated a different phenomenon and mislabelled it.

The dimension-counting argument is weaker than presented. 'With L=6 chars and K_eff=20 cohort factors, FM attains at most sqrt(6/20)' holds for a generic exposure vector Theta; the actual Theta is highly structured (project age distributions are smooth, geometric-tailed, and near-identical across firms because pi = 0.99 is common to all), so exposures will be dominated by two or three principal components that a linear method hedges easily. The proposal concedes this and proposes the right pilot diagnostic; until it is run this is speculation.

Finally: the magnitude is admitted to be the least certain of the six, it REQUIRES Proposal 1 to have room to operate, and it adds a second sparse kron to the O(N^2) inner loop in a moments step already pinned to n_jobs = 1 (config.py:40).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Probably not, and there is a clean referee counter. Firm i's exposure to cohort m is phi_m(i) = the value share of its live projects born in window m — which is LINEAR in observable age-composition shares. In real data researchers routinely control for industry and vintage with dummy variables, a purely linear device. So the natural benchmark is not FM-on-six-scalars but FM augmented with age-bucket portfolios, which spans the cohort exposure space exactly and hedges perfectly by construction. The entire proposed advantage rests on the econometrician being handed a scalar 'age' rather than age-bucket weights — an information restriction the authors chose. A referee will ask 'why can't the econometrician sort on age deciles?' and there is no good answer. Separately, cohort factors carry no premium, so max_sr falls: like P1, this improves the RATIO by degrading the benchmark rather than giving DKKM anything new to find.
verdicts.salvage: Only worth doing if the pilot diagnostic passes: at a single month, compute the FM-span-optimal portfolio's implied cohort exposure vector and show it is materially nonzero AND not spanned by age-decile portfolios. If it passes, the defensible version is not 'cohort' but a genuinely PRICED second aggregate factor — an investment-specific technology shock with a nonzero price of risk and characteristic-dependent loadings — which would break the affine identity and raise the effective rank of the priced-risk space, the condition the theory actually requires. As specified (unpriced, hedge-only) I would not run it: highest implementation risk of the covariance-side proposals, smallest defensible payoff, most obvious referee counter.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Characteristic-dependent clientele demand wedge (an AIPT alpha)
verdicts.critique:
The economics is right and the implementation is fatal, and the proposal says the fatal part out loud: 'choose h to be exactly orthogonal, in each monthly cross-section, to {1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom} and to the six FF factor weight vectors, by projecting the candidate h onto those columns and subtracting. Then the FM-attainable Sharpe from the alpha channel is exactly zero.'

That is not a model. That is constructing a signal in the null space of the competitor and then reporting that the competitor cannot find it. The author calls it 'a theorem rather than an approximation argument' — it is a theorem, and that is precisely the objection. THIS IS THE SENTENCE THAT KILLS THE PAPER: 'The authors orthogonalise the mispricing against the benchmark's span by construction and then report that the benchmark cannot price it.' No revision recovers from it.

Compounding it: the orthogonalisation is against the LINEAR char span while h is left inside the nonlinear span of the same characteristics. The wedge is engineered to be invisible to FM and visible to DKKM using the very basis distinction the paper purports to test. Not a subtle specification-search problem — the answer is written into the data generating process.

Three further problems each requiring major revision. (i) It changes what 'true' means: rp, cond_var, max_sr and sdf_ret become the marginal investor's objects rather than the representative agent's, so the HJ bound and every HJD number change meaning and must be re-derived. (ii) At the calibrated S* ~ 1.1/month the HJD metric degenerates (E[sdf_ret] -> Rf, sd(sdf_ret) -> 0), so half the paper's evidence base becomes uninformative exactly when the result appears. (iii) The wedge target must use only date-t information for ER to stay analytic, ruling out the natural specification (a wedge on the contemporaneous valuation ratio) and forcing an arbitrary one-month lag.

To be fair on one point: the underlying diagnosis is correct and important. No frictionless representative-agent model with a rank-1 price-of-risk vector can produce a 3-5x complexity advantage; my own numbers agree (the best any covariance-side change achieves is a 1.29x ceiling that collapses to 1.02x under an obvious check). If the paper wants a real-data-sized result, something like this is the only route. The idea is right; the execution assumes the conclusion.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes — trivially, tautologically, and that is exactly why it is worthless as evidence. Define h orthogonal to the FF/FM span and inside the RFF span, and FM's attainable alpha Sharpe is zero by construction while DKKM's is whatever THETA_W is set to. The gap is a free parameter. The interesting counterfactual is the one not run: an ECONOMICALLY specified h with no orthogonalisation. A plausible demand wedge (a small-value-high-volatility tilt, say) loads heavily on the linear characteristic span, because that is what the anomaly literature's characteristics ARE. My P1 experiment is the relevant evidence: even a genuinely nonlinear target (the 1/d ratio tilt) was 98% recovered by a linear method given two constructed columns. I would expect a non-orthogonalised demand wedge to deliver 1.2-1.6x, not 2.5-4x. That number would be a real finding; the orthogonalised number is not.
verdicts.salvage: Replace the orthogonalisation with a specified demand system. Write the wedge as arising from a Koijen-Yogo style clientele whose portfolio weights are a parametric function of characteristics with parameters taken from the estimated demand-system literature — not chosen, and explicitly NOT orthogonalised against anything. Report the resulting DKKM/FM gap, whatever it is, and report separately how much of the wedge lies inside the linear char span (a number the paper should want to disclose: it is the fraction of real-world 'alpha' a linear factor model can reach). Keep the calibration discipline already present (anomaly half-life 1-3 years -> RHO_U = 0.97; anomaly spread -> sd(alpha) ~ 36bp/month) and state up front that the paper is now about a segmented-clientele economy, with rp and the HJ bound reinterpreted accordingly. Switch HJD to the scale-free sqrt(1 - rho_uncentered^2) BEFORE running this or the metric will hide the result. Done that way it is a legitimate and interesting paper; done as written it is unpublishable.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Heterogeneous project durability (discrete survival types), optionally with larger |BETA_ZR|
verdicts.critique:
Worst payoff-to-risk ratio of the six, and the author essentially concedes it ('I rank it last on impact per unit of work').

Credit where due: durability types DO perturb the affine identity, since A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values (line 153) no longer uses a single bond value — it is the only covariance-side proposal that touches the premium at all. But the perturbation is tiny, because the interest-rate factor is nearly unpriced: lambda_xi/lambda_mu = -0.178, from BETA_ZR = -0.00014 and SIGMA_R = 0.002 (config.py:200-204). Duration heterogeneity moves expected returns almost not at all unless BETA_ZR is also raised.

And raising BETA_ZR is not a free rider. BETA_ZR enters vasicek.py's sigma12 recursion (lines 35-42) and therefore B(k,r), D(r), prob_in_money, and the beta_star/scale calibration (lines 68-77). Change it and you must re-fit the beta distribution and regenerate Jstar.csv, and every calibrated moment (E[num], mean bm, mean mve) moves. That is a full recalibration presented as a parameter tweak.

The decisive objection is operational. This is the only proposal requiring a shipped solution file to be regenerated, once per durability type, via the commented-out triple-nested-sum code at vasicek.py:123-174, with no correctness test beyond an internal refinement tolerance. This project already has a documented catastrophe of exactly that form: KP14's G_func.csv was solved under pre-Jun-18 parameters and is wrong by ~49x under current config.py; kp14_fd.py cannot even be re-run because 'from parameters_kp14 import *' refers to a module absent from the repo; and integ_results.npz returns exact zeros over the entire region where 98% of firm-months live, corrupting every downstream KP14 'truth'. Adding three more hand-solved solution files to a codebase with that track record, for a claimed 1.05-1.18x, is not a trade I would sanction. The O(N^2) kron cost also multiplies by M^2 = 9 on terms 3, 5 and 7, in a moments step already pinned to n_jobs = 1 (config.py:40).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No. The author's own estimate is 1.05-1.18x, inside the Monte Carlo noise of a single-seed run and unable to survive a standard-error column (the prior 30-replication experiment here found FM 0.2114 sd 0.0149 vs DKKM3600 0.2091 sd 0.0155). Two specific reasons it lands at the bottom of even that range. First, the author flags it: A_xi already correlates -0.975 with 1/mve, so if durability mix correlates with firm size in equilibrium — and it will, since older larger firms hold older longer-lived project stocks — the new dimension collapses back into size and delivers nothing. Second, the classification story ('recover the simplex point from payout yield, agr volatility, and rate-beta') is exactly the sort of target my P1 experiment shows a linear method recovers once handed the right constructed columns; FM given payout*nproj and the rate-beta interaction would close most of it. The author honestly notes the FF size-by-payout double sort may already recover the mix, and proposes engineering the type parameters so no single characteristic orders the types — a milder version of P5's fatal orthogonalisation, attracting the same criticism.
verdicts.salvage: If anything survives, it is the BETA_ZR change ALONE, without durability types: raising corr_zr from -0.175 toward -0.5 makes the interest-rate factor genuinely priced and gives BGN a second priced dimension — the condition the theory actually requires, and which no other proposal except P2 and P5 supplies. That is one config constant plus one Jstar re-solve, not three. Do it as a standalone experiment with a regression test that the old BETA_ZR reproduces the current moments exactly, and report what it does to the affine identity and to the population ceiling. Drop the M-type durability machinery entirely: days of compute, a 9x runtime multiplier, three hand-solved files with no verification, for a gain inside the noise.

missed_ideas: FAIRNESS FIRST — the comparison is currently rigged toward DKKM and no model change can be interpreted until it is fixed. config.py:187 sets ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0]: FF and FM get plain OLS with zero tuning decisions. Meanwhile bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py:83-97 (find_best_alpha_for_model) selects DKKM's alpha by argmax/argmin of the reported evaluation metric itself, across all iterations, for each of 4 feature counts — post-hoc oracle selection over 24 cells using the statistic being reported. Before any economics changes, give FF/FM the identical ridge grid and the identical selection rule, or replace the argmax with a single pre-specified alpha for everyone. The current 1.04x BGN gap may not survive that alone. No proposal mentions this, and it is the first thing a referee will strike.

THE ECONOMETRICIAN IS DENIED 1/mve, AND rp IS EXACTLY AFFINE IN IT. From panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186, 1+eret_i = pi*e_t/bond_t + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + Chat*pi*bm_i. The true premium is an exact linear function of (1/mve, bm). But MODEL_CHARS gives 'size' = log(mve). FM is therefore being asked to span an exactly-linear truth through a nonlinear transform of the right variable, while DKKM's sin/cos basis can approximate the reciprocal. Any DKKM-over-FM gap in the CURRENT baseline may be nothing but that.
