Add 1/mve (or the earnings-to-price style ratio the model naturally generates) to the characteristic set and re-run the baseline before doing anything else — this single check could reclassify the existing result as an artifact.

NO STANDARD ERRORS ANYWHERE. Every reported gap (BGN DKKM/FF = 1.04x, GS21 = 1.15x) is a single-run point estimate, and several proposals predict effects of 1.05-1.2x. A referee will demand the Monte Carlo distribution across seeds. The prior 30-replication experiment in this project found FM 0.2114 (sd 0.0149) versus DKKM3600 0.2091 (sd 0.0155) — the gap is a small fraction of one standard deviation. Any proposal whose predicted effect is under ~1.3x is not measurable with one seed and should not be attempted without a multi-seed design specified in advance.

THE SPAN PROJECTOR USED THROUGHOUT THE DIAGNOSIS PHASE IS WRONG, AND ALL HEADROOM NUMBERS NEED RECOMPUTING. A linear characteristic method delivers w = X a, so the attainable Sharpe is sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp). The reported figures correspond to w = Sigma^{-1} X a. On the same cross-section (N=1000, band 0.1, X=[1,log mve,bm]) these give 69.4% and 83.4% of max_sr respectively. The BGN diagnosis's '{1,size,bm} attains 91.7%', Proposal 1's '95.03%' and its '69.06%' are all computed against the wrong weight space. Recompute before any decision rests on them.

MEASUREMENT ERROR IN CHARACTERISTICS — cheaper, more general, and more defensible than any of the six. DKKM obtain a 2.6-3.4x complexity gain in real data using the SAME five characteristics. So the count is not the issue; the informational structure is. Here the chars are noiseless, redundant, smoothly invertible functions of 2-3 latent states — exactly the regime where a small correctly-specified model is optimal. Adding classical measurement error, reporting lags, and several redundant-but-imperfect proxies for the same state makes recovering w*(x) genuinely require a rich function class, applies identically to all three models, is one line per characteristic, and is impossible to characterise as tuning. It should have been Proposal 1.

ONE MECHANISM FOR ALL THREE MODELS, NOT THREE TAILORED FIXES. The brief invites per-model alterations and the proposals oblige. But a paper that changes BGN one way, KP14 another and GS21 a third, each until the desired result appears, is three specification searches presented as robustness. The strongest paper picks ONE economically general ingredient (measurement error; a demand wedge; a high-dimensional priced-shock space) and shows it produces the virtue of complexity in all three otherwise-unmodified models. A referee will trust that and will not trust six model-specific dials.

REPORT Sharpe/max_sr, AND PROPAGATE max_sr INTO THE RESULTS FILES. Sharpe_t(w) = max_sr_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*) is an exact identity, so the interpretable quantity is the cosine, not the level. max_sr is already computed in every sdf_loop (sdf_compute_bgn.py:326-328) and saved into *_moments.pkl, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it, so no table shows whether FF at 0.2423 is 30% or 90% of the ceiling. Without it the reader cannot distinguish 'the estimator is failing' from 'the model has nothing to estimate' — the entire question the paper is about. Two-line fix; it should precede everything.

REPORT THE COMPLEXITY CURVE, NOT JUST THE BEST CELL. The diagnostic distinguishing a real virtue-of-complexity result from a shrinkage result is whether Sharpe RISES with P at fixed tuning. It is currently flat (BGN 0.2466 -> 0.2528 from P=6 to P=3600, +2.5%). Several proposals predict a level gap without predicting a rising curve; a level gap with a flat curve is a shrinkage effect and a referee will say so. Every proposal should state its predicted curve shape, and the paper should show it.

MICROCAPS AND THE SIZE DISTRIBUTION. DKKM's real-data Sharpe falls from ~3.7 to ~1.6 in mega/large caps, so much of the empirical virtue of complexity lives in small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility names. BGN's cross-section has sd(log mve) far below CRSP's ~2.0, N is fixed at 1000 with no entry or exit, and there is no fat left tail. A heavier-tailed size distribution with strong size-dependence of both alpha and idiosyncratic variance is a targeted, empirically-anchored change no proposal makes.

TEST ASSETS WITH POWER. generate_25_portfolios.py:107-119 sorts only on mve and bm — two characteristics every method already spans linearly — and compute_pricing_errors.py then runs each method's MVE return as a single factor against them. This test cannot detect nonlinear-in-characteristics mispricing by construction. Add portfolios sorted on interactions (size x bm, roe x agr), on non-monotone transforms, or directly on deciles of the model's TRUE conditional SDF weight. Otherwise the pricing-error evidence is vacuous whichever proposal is adopted.

PRE-REGISTER THE CALIBRATION, AND SHOW THE FAILURES. Several proposals amount to changing one constant (P1's 0.1 -> 1.75) or adding one parameter (P2's SIGMA_KAPPA, P5's THETA_W). The only way these read as science rather than search is if the target moments are stated first, the full scan is shown including settings that do NOT produce the result, and the parameter is pinned by an external moment rather than by the DKKM/FM gap. P1's four-moment scan is closest to this and should be the template; P2 and P5 currently pin their parameters partly by the desired outcome.

CONSIDER PUBLISHING THE NEGATIVE RESULT. The strongest thing in this project is not any of the six proposals — it is the demonstration, with oracle span calculations, that a frictionless representative-agent production model with a rank-1 price-of-risk vector and an exactly-affine cross-section of expected returns CANNOT generate a real-data-sized virtue of complexity, plus the precise identification of which DKKM condition it violates (effective rank of E[FF'] ~ 16 against the several hundred their AIPT calibration requires). A paper that states the necessary conditions, proves the standard models violate them, and then shows the minimal ingredient that restores them is more publishable, and far more robust to a hostile referee, than a paper reporting a tuned 1.4x. Frame the model changes as the CONSTRUCTIVE half of a negative result, not as the result.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1. Limits-to-arbitrage price wedge (moderate_restructuring)
verdicts.critique:
Right diagnosis, wrong instrument, and as written it is rigging on three counts.

(1) CALIBRATED-TO-TARGET FREE PARAMETER. The proposal's own text says kappa_med is 'pinned by the TARGET maximum Sharpe rather than by the misvaluation literature', and then solves kappa_med = SR_alpha_target*sigma_idio/(sqrt(N)(1-rho)M) = 0.033 so that SR* reproduces DKKM's 2.6-3.4x ratio 'exactly'. That is a free parameter inverted from the answer. A referee reads one sentence of the calibration appendix and the paper is dead. Whatever else is true, the wedge amplitude must be an INPUT from an independent source (RKRV misvaluation decomposition, Koijen-Yogo demand elasticities, documented anomaly half-lives) and SR* must be a reported OUTPUT.

(2) THE STATED SDF NO LONGER PRICES THE ASSETS. In BGN log M = -r - 0.5*sigma_z^2 - sigma_z*nu with sigma_z = 0.4, so the model's own HJ bound is sqrt(exp(0.16)-1) = 0.4165/month. The proposal targets total SR* = sqrt(0.21^2+0.6^2) = 0.636/month. After the wedge, E[m R_i^obs] != 1 for every i and the maximum Sharpe exceeds the volatility of the only stochastic discount factor in the economy by 53%. The object evaluate_sdfs.py then scores as 'truth' (Sigma^{-1}rp) is attainable by no agent in the model and corresponds to no marginal rate of substitution. Calling it 'the true SDF' becomes false. The fix is not cosmetic: you must write down the arbitrageur, give her an explicit position/wealth constraint, and show the residual Sharpe she leaves on the table is consistent with that constraint. Otherwise the paper's central object is an econometrician's Sigma^{-1}mu on hand-added alpha.

(3) THE 'NOTHING IN THE FIRM'S PROBLEM CHANGES' CLAIM IS FALSE FOR GS21. I read utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py: default is triggered at line ~74 by `default[t] = (P[t] <= 0)` where P is the SOLVED equity value function P_up/P_down evaluated at (z, x, b); the investment cutoff (`i_cut_down/i_cut_up`), the refinancing debt choice (`b_refin_0/b_refin_I`) and the issuance proceeds Q_I/Q_0 entering prof_I_up/prof_0_up are all read off the same solution. If the marginal holder of equity prices it with a wedge, then the default boundary, the equity-issuance decision and the refinancing choice are all made at the wedged price. Applying exp(-kappa v) only to the reported price assumes managers optimize against a price no one will pay. Internal consistency requires v as a fourth state and a full MATLAB re-solve — which the proposal explicitly claims is unnecessary. KP14 and BGN survive this test (BGN's investment rule at panel_functions_bgn.py:81 is exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r)>1 and the valuation A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values at line 153 depend only on beta and r; KP14's exercise policy comes from G), so the wedge is defensible in two of three models and not the third.

(4) KP14 cannot host this at all until integ_results.npz and the stale G_func.csv are fixed. Layering a wedge on a truth that is currently minus the PVGO share is meaningless.

And there is a strictly better instrument available (see missed idea 1) that produces a multi-dimensional priced-risk space with ZERO change to prices, policies, or calibration and no arbitrage assumption at all. Given that alternative exists, choosing the mispricing route is a choice to take the referee risk unnecessarily.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Adversarially: it probably WOULD produce a gap, and that is exactly the problem — it produces the gap by construction. But two channels let FF/FM capture more than claimed. First, kappa_i = kappa_med*(mve/med)^{-phi}*(sigma/med)^{psi} is a MONOTONE function of two variables, and alpha_i = (1-rho)*kappa_i*v_it is therefore a product of a monotone size/vol function and an independent AR(1). FF's 2x3 design is literally a size x char double sort — it gets a two-bin approximation of exactly the kappa(size) modulation, and FM gets the linear-in-size and linear-in-v parts. Since v_it is revealed through bm^obs and mom (the proposal's own point), FM's monthly refit of a coefficient on bm picks up (1-rho)*E[kappa]*v directly. The residual DKKM-only content is the 1/(d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2) division and the size x vol x signal triple interaction. That is real but it is second-order relative to the first-order linear piece, and span2.py's own 'linear alpha + het d' cell gives RFF/lin = 1.91, not 6.4. Second, the hump requires s_k = 1.9, which the proposal admits blows up SR* through the right tail of E[kappa^2/d] — so the non-monotonicity that FF structurally cannot represent is precisely the part that cannot be calibrated without an implausible Sharpe. My honest estimate of the DEFENSIBLY-calibrated gap is 1.5-2x, not 3-5x.
verdicts.salvage: Reframe as a two-agent segmented-market economy and apply to BGN FIRST and alone. (a) Write an explicit arbitrageur with a quadratic holding cost or a position limit, so the residual Sharpe is an equilibrium object rather than an assumed one, and verify the resulting max_sr respects a stated risk-aversion. (b) Calibrate the wedge amplitude from RKRV firm-specific misvaluation (sd ~0.4 in logs) or from a demand-elasticity estimate, report SR* as an output, and show the result over a grid of amplitudes rather than at one target-inverted value. (c) Make the arbitrage-cost loading kappa depend on staleness/age/turnover rather than on size, since FF's design already contains the size interaction. (d) Do NOT apply to GS21 without re-solving the value function with v as a state; the default boundary and issuance decision are functions of the market price. (e) Add a diagnostic that reports max_i |E[m R_i^obs] - 1| so the reader can see exactly how far the wedge pushes the economy from the stated SDF.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (reparametrization_only)
verdicts.critique:
No economic content, so nothing in the models breaks and the 'simple economic models' claim survives untouched. Three of the five items (NMAT=1, scale-free ridge parameterization, an alpha grid that visits df in (63,360)) are unambiguous repairs and should ship regardless of the outcome. The fairness item — same ridge grid and same post-hoc alpha selection for FF/FM, plus turning on the commented-out FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156 — is not optional; it is the single largest credibility item in the whole bundle, because today an oracle-tuned DKKM is being compared to an untuned FF/FM and the paper's headline is that they tie.

Two structural objections. (i) GAMMA_GRID *= sqrt(130/L) is presented as 'derived', but the derivation holds the Gaussian-kernel exponent fixed at DKKM's real-data value while the audit ALSO measured that widening strictly HURTS when the truth is near-linear (GS21: 0.879 -> 0.799 at 4.65x, -> 0.376 at 10x). A knob whose optimal setting depends on the answer is a tuning knob no matter how it is derived. If it ships, it must ship as a 2x2 of {old, rescaled} gamma x {old, new} DGP, with the old-gamma column reported in the main table. (ii) The proposal quietly concedes the decisive point: on the current models this bundle is worth approximately zero. It should be labelled a precondition, not a lever, and the paper should not open with it.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal says so. FF/FM would be entirely unaffected by items (a)-(e); the only thing that moves is DKKM's basis richness, and the audit measured BGN's total population nonlinearity headroom at 0.7pp of Sharpe and GS21's at 3%. Worse, giving FF/FM the same ridge grid and the same post-hoc alpha selection (which fairness demands) will RAISE FF/FM Sharpes, so the net effect of the honest version of P2 on the DKKM/FF ratio is plausibly negative. Its value is defensive.
verdicts.salvage: Ship items (b) z-scoring instead of double rank-standardization, (c) NMAT=1 reported as five replications, (d) the scale-free penalty and the 11-point log grid, and the FF/FM fairness repairs, all in one commit, as bug fixes with a before/after table showing the c=1 double-descent explosions (BGN HJD 18.52, GS21 23.57) disappearing. Hold the gamma rescale (a) and P=36000 (e) as a robustness appendix conditional on the DGP change, and always report the unmodified gamma grid in the main table.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
This is P2's bandwidth change wearing a realism costume, and the proposal admits it: 'P3 delivers most of P2(a) as a by-product, with no hyperparameter touched.' Dressing a hyperparameter change as an economic one is epistemically worse than doing P2 openly, because it hides the knob.

Structurally the 35 columns carry no new information. Every one is a deterministic transform of quantities the model already produces from a 2-3 dimensional latent state — BGN's date-t cross-section is a bijection of (num_i, sum_j exp(-beta_j)); GS21's is (k, b, z). Thirty-five smooth functions of three numbers span a three-dimensional manifold. What rises is the NOMINAL input dimension L, which raises sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) and hence RFF effective rank. That is a bandwidth effect, full stop.

Specific degeneracies the proposal's own risk section understates: (i) GS21's investment probability is 1.21%/month, so all four multi-horizon asset-growth columns are near-constant and agr is already 98.8% ties; (ii) BGN's book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95, so 1m/12m/36m/60m log book changes take a handful of discrete values with >80% ties, and rank_standardize's argsort tie-breaking turns each into a persistent pseudo-random column entering all 3600 features multiplicatively; (iii) KP14's roe/agr inherit the same project-count lumpiness. A large fraction of the 35 will be manufactured noise, not signals.

The 'peer-relative' block is the worst item: it demeans within an industry partition that is 'a fixed random partition into 10 groups correlated with the model's own permanent firm type (beta_j in BGN, lambda_f in KP14, initial k in GS21)'. Those are LATENT parameters the econometrician cannot see. Handing DKKM a noisy read on beta_j — the single object that drives BGN's entire risk premium (A_mu = 0.0602*bm*betabar) — is planting the answer in the char set. It will be caught.

Finally, K=37 on T=360 costs FM ~20% of squared Sharpe. Widening the gap by degrading the benchmark is not a demonstration of the virtue of complexity.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It would produce a NUMBER, and the number would be attributable to the wrong thing. FM with 35 rank-standardized regressors still spans every linear function of the chars, and since the truth in all three models is 83-99% linear in the chars, the population span ceiling barely moves. What moves is FM's estimation variance (20% squared-Sharpe loss) and FF's conditioning (35 collinear sorted factors). So the measured DKKM/FM ratio of ~1.2-1.3x that the proposal itself predicts is pure benchmark degradation. Diagnostic that settles it: report mean_t SR_rff/SR_lin on the TRUE rp and cond_var with the expanded char set — if it is still ~1.0, the entire realized gap is estimation noise in the competitor.
verdicts.salvage: Keep only characteristics that are genuine observables with independent economic content and low tie fractions: firm age, number of live projects proxied by book, realized return volatility at two horizons, realized market beta, past returns at 2-3 non-overlapping horizons, and multi-year averages of profitability. That is L ~ 12-15, keeps FM at K=17 (2K/T = 9%), and roughly doubles sd(Wx) honestly. Delete the random-industry block entirely — it leaks a latent parameter. Screen every column for tie fraction and drop anything above 20%, and fix the FF tercile degeneracy at fama_functions.py:86-88 in the same commit so agr's q30 = q70 = 0 stops producing an empty medium bucket.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block in all three models (reparametrization_only)
verdicts.critique:
This is the only proposal that makes the models MORE faithful to their published selves rather than less, and I verified its central claim in the code.

BGN is genuinely free, and more cleanly than the proposal argues. sigmaj enters nowhere in the valuation: A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values (panel_functions_bgn.py:153) and G = I*Chat*Jstar(r) (line 157) depend only on beta and r, because cov(log M, log C_j) = -sigma_z*corr_zj*sigmaj = -beta_j identically by the definition at line 61. The investment rule at line 81 is exp(Cbar - beta)*D(r) > 1 — also sigmaj-free. And E[C] = exp(Cbar - 0.5*sigmaj^2 + eps*sigmaj) = exp(Cbar) is invariant. So deleting the '0.1*' at line 54 changes NO price, NO policy, NO expected cash flow, and does not disturb the beta_star/scale calibration (which was fitted to prob_in_money targets that depend on beta alone). It restores idiosyncratic cash-flow risk and nothing else. There is no defensible reason for that 0.1 to be there; the inline comment '# added a factor of 0.1' is an undocumented deviation from the model.

GS21 is the strongest case of all and the proposal undersells it. As shipped, GS21 has ZERO defaults in 2.16M firm-months, maximum market leverage of 1.04%, and z_cut_down pinned at the grid floor everywhere. A Gomes-Schmid model with no default and all-equity firms is not the Gomes-Schmid model — the credit-market channel that the paper exists to study has been calibrated out of existence. Restoring sigma_z is therefore required for the paper's honesty independent of anything to do with DKKM, and reopening default is a feature, not a risk.

KP14 restoring SIGMA_U = 1.5 with THETA_U = 0.5 violates the Feller condition (2*theta*mu = 1.0 < sigma^2 = 2.25, i.e. the CIR df = 4*kappa*theta/sigma^2 = 0.889 < 2), so u hits zero and its stationary Gamma has shape 0.444 — extremely right-skewed. I checked this does not break anything: A = A_0 + (eps-1)A_1 + (u-1)A_2 + (eps-1)(u-1)A_3 has minimum ~2.6 > 0 at u=0, and Kj = (alpha*z*A(eps,1))^{1/(1-alpha)} depends on eps only. So it is feasible, but it should be reported, and the exact noncentral-chi-square scheme in sim_cir is what makes it safe.

The one thing missing from the proposal: a calibration table. Any change of this size must be accompanied by before/after values for the aggregate equity premium, market volatility, market Sharpe, investment rate, book and market leverage, default rate, and the size and value premia, with the published papers' targets in a third column.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: On its own, no — and the proposal is admirably honest that max_sr FALLS and all three Sharpes fall roughly proportionally. Adversarially, the D^{-1} tilt argument is weak in exactly the way the diagnosis measured: under exact factor pricing the inverse-variance tilt is worth 0.19% of SR* at N=1000, and it stays worth ~0.2% even with a 20x spread in d, because idiosyncratic risk is diversifiable. Worse, if the restored idiosyncratic variance is a MONOTONE function of a single characteristic (which is what happens in KP14 today, where idio var ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/size with corr -0.97), FF's tercile sorts on that characteristic recover a crude version of the tilt and DKKM's edge over FF stays small. The multiplier story requires an unspanned premium to multiply, which P4 does not supply. Endorse it as a correctness fix, not as a lever.
verdicts.salvage: Ship BGN's one-character edit immediately — it is free, it is a bug fix, and it changes no price. Ship the GS21 re-solve as the model-fidelity repair it is, extending bgrid and zgrid, removing or guarding the arbitrary P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131, adding an eigenvalue guard on cond_var, and capping the unbounded `while (P[t] <= 0)` loop at lines 74-89 (which can spin forever once defaults become live, and which also fails to write the redrawn xt back into x[t]). Gate KP14 behind the integ_kp14.py quadrature fix and the G_func.csv re-solve; do not touch its sigmas before then. Publish the full calibration table.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (small_code_addition)
verdicts.critique:
Nothing here touches economics, and every item is a correctness fix. Two are decisive: propagating max_sr (already computed in every sdf_loop and stored by calculate_moments.py, never read by evaluate_sdfs.py) so that Sharpe can be read as a fraction of the ceiling, and replacing the leverage-contaminated HJD with a scale-free statistic. The first is the single most informative number in the project and its absence is why the diagnosis phase needed five agents. GS21's reported FF HJD of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is a naked artifact and will be caught.

Three caveats from the structure side. (i) Sharpe/max_sr is only interpretable if max_sr is a real economic object; in KP14 it is currently 34.7 annualized against the model's own bound of sqrt(gamma_x^2+gamma_z^2) = 0.774, so that column would divide by a numerical artifact and must be suppressed until the quadrature is fixed. Conversely, adding this column is precisely the diagnostic that WOULD have caught the KP14 corruption years ago — add an automatic assertion that max_sr does not exceed the model's theoretical HJ bound (BGN: sqrt(exp(sigma_z^2)-1); KP14: sqrt(gamma_x^2+gamma_z^2)*sqrt(dt); GS21: from the EZ SDF). (ii) Test assets sorted on deciles of the true conditional MVE weight are the right power fix but must be labelled an ORACLE diagnostic, not a horse race — they use information no method has. (iii) The universe mismatch at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 (rp/cond_var subset to prepare_panel survivors, sdf_ret computed over the book>0 universe) should be fixed in the same commit; it is currently masked by an implicit coupling.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and it should not. It will probably SHRINK the apparent DKKM advantage, because the scale-free pricing-error statistic removes the six-chances-at-the-right-leverage advantage that the argmin-over-alpha HJD currently hands DKKM while FF/FM sit at alpha=0. That is the correct direction and the paper should say so out loud.
verdicts.salvage: Ship as-is, plus: an assertion that mean_t max_sr_t is below the model's own theoretical HJ bound, a suppression rule for the Sigma-cosine column when that assertion fails, an explicit 'oracle diagnostic' label on the true-MVE-weight-sorted test assets, and the universe fix at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171. Report both the old and new pricing-error columns for one draft and justify the new one from the algebra, not the results.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with heterogeneous fiscal year-ends plus heteroskedastic measurement error
verdicts.critique:
Two halves with very different standing, and the proposal's case for each is partly wrong.

The STALENESS half is defensible and nearly free of parameters — staggered fiscal year-ends plus the conventional six-month lag is the Fama-French convention with zero degrees of freedom, and it is a genuine feature of real data that all three panels lack. But its claimed payoffs do not survive checking. The proposal says it 'breaks the GS21 identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly, which is currently the single most indefensible feature of that panel.' It does not. bm = book/mve = k/(k*P_ex) = 1/P_ex, and lagging book to k_{t-h} changes bm only when investment occurred inside the window — GS21's investment probability is 1.21%/month, so bm_stale = 1/P_ex for ~87% of firm-months at h=12. Only the added noise breaks the identity. Likewise in BGN, book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95 that changes only on project birth or death, so a 12-month-stale book is nearly as good as a fresh one. The mechanism is inert in two of three models; it bites only in GS21's roe (rho_z^12 = 0.657) and even there roe is not a state the SDF weight depends on much.

The HETEROSKEDASTIC-NOISE half is where the objection is. sigma_e,i = sigma_e0*(mve/median)^{-xi} introduces two free parameters whose ONLY purpose is to create a reliability-times-signal product, and the proposal openly selects the reliability proxy to be one FF's 2x3 design cannot sort on: 'that is why the reliability proxy should be STALENESS... which is NOT one of FF's sort variables — and why one would have to add a third sort dimension.' Choosing the DGP feature specifically because the benchmark's estimator cannot represent it is designing the experiment against the competitor. It is more subtle than P1's target-inverted kappa but it is the same species.

The proposal deserves real credit for one thing: its Fourier argument that CLASSICAL homoskedastic EIV attenuates nonlinear components by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) while attenuating the linear component only by the classical factor is correct, sharp, and a genuine theoretical contribution. It should be in the paper regardless of whether the DGP change ships, because it explains why realistic measurement error works AGAINST the virtue of complexity — which is an interesting result on its own and the opposite of what most readers would guess.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Largely by lowering the benchmark, which the proposal concedes. And FM has a partial answer the proposal dismisses too quickly: with staleness h_i observable, FM can add the interaction column h_i*bm_i directly to its regressor set — FM's span is 'linear in whatever columns you give it', and lambda(h)*bm is well approximated by a linear combination of bm, h*bm and h^2*bm. So the honest statement is that FM needs 2-3 extra hand-specified interaction columns to match what the Fourier basis gets automatically, which is a convenience argument, not a span argument. FF is genuinely stuck, but FF is already the weak benchmark. Expected gap contribution: small, and confounded with benchmark degradation.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the staleness layer alone: staggered fiscal months, six-month reporting lag, accounting chars stale between updates, market chars contemporaneous, and stale_i,t as an observable given to ALL THREE methods. Zero free parameters, standard convention, honest realism. Check sd(bm_stale - bm_fresh)/sd(bm) first and drop it in any model where it is under ~0.1. Drop the size-dependent noise variance, or if it is kept, calibrate xi from an external accounting-quality measure, show the result survives with homoskedastic noise of the same average magnitude, and give FM the h*char interaction columns so the comparison is about function-class flexibility rather than about who was allowed to specify interactions. Publish the EIV Fourier result as a standalone theoretical point either way.

missed_ideas: THE BIG ONE — a multi-factor SDF in BGN that leaves every price, policy and calibration target EXACTLY unchanged. BGN's valuation depends on the cash-flow shock only through beta_j, because cov(log M, log C_j) = -sigma_z*corr_zj*sigmaj = -beta_j identically (panel_functions_bgn.py:61), and the asset value is book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values with beta_avg = mean(exp(-beta)) (line 148-153). So replace the scalar shock nu with a K-vector nu, set log M = -r - 0.5|lambda|^2 - lambda'nu, and let project j load b_j'nu with the SINGLE restriction lambda'b_j = beta_j. Every b_j in the (K-1)-dimensional affine set {b : lambda'b = beta_j} gives IDENTICAL prices, identical investment decisions, identical expected returns, identical Jstar and D(r), and an identical beta_star/scale calibration — but a K-factor conditional covariance matrix with heterogeneous, characteristic-linkable loadings. Draw the null-space component of b_j from a distribution indexed by the firm's observable type (e.g. its size decile at project birth, or a persistent 'sector' assigned at entry). This gives exactly what the diagnosis says is missing (raise the priced-risk dimension from 1-2 to tens) with NO wedge, NO arbitrage, NO free parameter that touches any calibration target, and no re-solve of anything. It is a strictly better instrument than P1 and no proposal contains it.

KP14: sector- or vintage-specific investment-specific technology shocks. KP14's economics is that growth options load on the IST shock z; the model as coded has one z and therefore beta_z = alph*share with a p10-p90 value-premium spread of 0.48%/yr. Give each firm a sector s(i) and a sector-specific z_s with a common component plus a sector-specific priced component. This is squarely inside KP14's own story (vintage capital, embodied technical change) and requires only solving the same Feynman-Kac ODE once per sector's parameters — kp14_fd.py already solves a 1000-point upwind FD system in seconds. Result: a K-dimensional priced space whose loadings are (growth-option share) x (sector dummy), i.e. a genuine interaction that FM's single coefficient per char cannot form and FF's 2x3 cannot sort on. No mispricing, no free parameter beyond the sector loading dispersion.

KP14: break beta_x = 1. The deepest defect in KP14 is that price = VAP + PVGO is homogeneous of degree one in x (panel_functions_kp14.py:165,173), so EVERY firm has unit exposure to the dominant priced shock and the cross-sectional loading CV is 3.7%. No proposal addresses this. The standard production-AP fix is a NON-SCALE-INVARIANT component: a fixed operating cost or per-firm overhead subtracted from cash flow, which is Carlson-Fisher-Giammarino / Zhang (2005) operating leverage and is independently calibrated in the literature (fixed costs ~20-30% of revenue). It makes beta_x a decreasing convex function of profitability and size — genuinely nonlinear, textbook, and it breaks the homogeneity that currently makes the cross-section one-dimensional.

GS21: make leverage and default LIVE, as the primary lever rather than a side effect. Equity is a call option on the levered firm, so its beta is a convex, kinked, non-monotone function of (leverage, z, x) — the only genuine nonlinearity available in any of the three models without adding anything foreign. P4 mentions reopening default only as a RISK of raising sigma_z. It should be the headline: recalibrate GS21_TAU, GS21_KAPPA_B, GS21_ZETA and the bgrid so that market leverage is 25-40% and the annual default rate hits the historical ~1%, then re-solve. That simultaneously (a) restores GS21's identity as a credit-channel model, (b) supplies the nonlinearity, (c) fixes the non-stationary size distribution (defaults are the only reset mechanism in the code, and with zero defaults sd(log k) grows as sqrt(t) forever), and (d) requires no economic invention whatsoever — it is just calibrating the published model to its published targets.

Firm-level PARAMETER heterogeneity, which breaks the char-to-state invertibility without any measurement fiction. Right now GS21's four chars invert (k, b, z) exactly and BGN's cross-section is a bijection of two numbers. Give firms persistent heterogeneous structural parameters — pi_i (project arrival) and I_i (project scale) in BGN, tau_i or adjustment-cost curvature in GS21, delta_i in KP14 — drawn at entry and never observed. The observable chars then become a many-to-one projection of a higher-dimensional state, the true SDF weight stops being a smooth invertible function of the chars, and the efficient use of the chars becomes a nonlinear inference problem. This is standard in the structural estimation literature, costs nothing but a per-firm draw, and does not touch the SDF or the valuation logic (though it does require the value function to be solved on a parameter grid in GS21).

Firm entry, exit, and a fat-tailed size distribution. All three panels hold N=1000 fixed with no birth or death, and GS21's size distribution is a non-stationary random walk. DKKM report that their real-data Sharpe of 3.7 falls to ~1.6 in mega/large caps, i.e. most of the empirical virtue of complexity lives in the microcap tail. Adding entry/exit with a Pareto-tailed size distribution — and the associated strong size-dependence of both idiosyncratic volatility and expected returns — is defensible, standard, and targets the part of the real cross-section that actually produces the phenomenon. No proposal mentions it.

Time-varying, state-dependent prices of risk with cross-sectionally visible interactions. BGN's SDF has constant sigma_z; making the price of risk a function of the aggregate state (habit or long-run-risk style) is a one-line change to log M that costs nothing in BGN because the valuation only needs cov(log M, log C_j) — though it does change D(r) and Jstar. The key point the diagnosis raises and no proposal implements: a date-level state is invisible to any cross-sectional portfolio weight, so the conditioning must appear as loading_i x macro_state, i.e. through heterogeneous betas interacting with a time-varying lambda_t. That is the second of the two channels through which complexity pays in DKKM/KMZ, and it is entirely absent from KP14's and GS21's feature maps today.

An automatic internal-consistency audit: report max_i |E_t[m_{t+1} R_{i,t+1}] - 1| across the panel, and assert mean_t max_sr_t is below the model's own theoretical Hansen-Jagannathan bound. This would have caught KP14's corrupt integ_results.npz immediately (34.7 annualized against a bound of 0.774), and it is the test that would flag P1's wedge as breaking the SDF. Every proposal that touches prices should be required to pass it, and the number should appear in the paper.

Consider publishing the honest negative result as the contribution. DKKM's own Theorem 3 and their APT calibration PROVE that in an exact low-K-factor economy with no unspanned premium, complexity does not help and at light shrinkage strictly hurts. Three canonical frictionless production models reproduce that prediction line for line, including the c=1 double-descent collapse. That is a real finding: the empirical virtue of complexity is evidence that the true cross-section is NOT an exact low-factor risk economy — it requires near-arbitrage in the DKKM/AIPT sense. Framed that way the paper needs no rigging at all, and the modelling exercise becomes 'what is the minimal departure from APT that reproduces the empirical fact', which is exactly P1 but with the sign of the argument reversed so that the wedge is the OBJECT OF STUDY rather than an embarrassment to be hidden.

Nobody proposes the cheapest structural realism fix of all: correlated, characteristic-linked idiosyncratic shocks (block/sector correlation in the residuals). Real residual covariance is not diagonal — industry and style clusters mean D is block-structured with cluster membership partly readable from characteristics. Sigma^{-1}mu with a block D is a genuinely nonlinear function of the chars even when mu and the blocks are each linear, and unlike a diagonal D the benefit does NOT vanish at rate 1/N because within-block residual risk is not diversifiable. This is the one way to make the H2 ratio channel matter at N=1000, and it is implementable in every model by giving the idiosyncratic cash-flow shocks a sector factor.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1. Limits-to-arbitrage price wedge (exp(-kappa_i v_it))
verdicts.critique: This is the only proposal that attacks the actual binding constraint, and the framing defense is genuinely strong: DKKM PROVE complexity is worthless under exact factor pricing, so an APT economy is not a valid test bed, and saying so pre-empts the obvious 'you added mispricing' attack. But as written the paper dies on one sentence in the calibration section. The proposal sets kappa_med = SR_alpha_target * sigma_idio / (sqrt(N)*(1-rho)*M) = 0.6*0.10/(31.62*0.0378*1.5) = 0.033 -- i.e. the single economic parameter governing the new mechanism is solved backwards from a TARGET SHARPE, and that target is itself chosen to reproduce DKKM's published 2.6-3.4x ratio. The proposal even discloses the tension ('the binding constraint here is the reported SR*, not realism' -- 3.3% versus Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan's 0.40 log sd). A JF referee reading that reverse-engineers the entire paper: you chose the wedge amplitude to hit the answer you wanted to report. Worse, kappa_med depends explicitly on N. That means max_sr is a function of the simulation's cross-sectional size, not of any equilibrium object -- the 'truth' the Sharpe metric scores against becomes a near-arbitrage whose Sharpe grows like sqrt(N) and that no agent inside the model exploits. Second problem, internal-consistency: sdf_compute currently computes ER from the model's own SDF and port = ER^{-1}1 is the mimicking portfolio for that SDF (verified, utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py:305-330; max_sr is the HJ bound). After the wedge, port is no longer any agent's SDF -- it is the statistical tangency portfolio of observed returns. The paper must say out loud that 'true SDF' has been redefined to 'unconstrained arbitrageur's frontier', and must explain why the arbitrageur who is being scored does not trade the wedge away. Third, technical: the wedge contaminates log bm ADDITIVELY (+q) and log size SUBTRACTIVELY (-q) by construction, so span{log bm_obs, log size_obs} = span{fundamentals} + 2q -- a LINEAR rule in two existing characteristics extracts most of the alpha. This puts the design in span2.py's 'linear alpha + heteroskedastic d' cell (RFF/lin = 1.91), not the 'nonlinear alpha' cell (6.37) the predicted-effect section leans on.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, and smaller than claimed. FM CAN reach the level of q linearly, for the reason above -- the observed chars are contaminated in opposite directions so a linear combination isolates the wedge. What FM cannot form is the modulation kappa(size,vol) x q / (d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2), which is the interaction. FF gets a two-bin approximation of the size half of that modulation through its 2x3 design (verified: fama_functions.py:83-104 builds one size x char double sort per characteristic), so FF is not shut out either. And note the FF factor as coded uses only the extreme buckets -- factor = 0.5*(high_big+high_small-low_big-low_small), the med portfolios are computed and discarded -- so it is a 2x2 monotone long-short and the hump argument does hold against FF. Net: I would expect a genuine but modest DKKM/FM span gap of roughly 1.5-2x, not 3-5x, unless s_k is pushed to ~1.9 to activate the hump -- at which point SR* is driven by the right tail of a lognormal arbitrage-cost distribution and the referee's N-scaling objection bites hardest. The gap is real but it is bought with the parameter that was reverse-engineered.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge, kill the calibration. Three changes make this publishable. (1) GIVE THE DEMAND SHOCK AN AGGREGATE COMPONENT: v_it = w_t + e_it with w_t a common noise-trader factor carrying a price of risk. Then the wedge premium is DeLong-Shleifer-Summers-Waldmann compensation for noise-trader risk -- an equilibrium object, not a free lunch -- max_sr stops growing like sqrt(N), and the arbitrageur's failure to trade it away is modelled rather than assumed. This converts the referee's strongest attack into a citation. (2) CALIBRATE kappa TO AN EXTERNAL MOMENT AND FREEZE IT before running any estimator -- e.g. match the Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan firm-specific misvaluation sd, or the observed magnitude of a standard anomaly long-short -- and report whatever SR* falls out, even if it is unflattering. State in the paper that the parameter was fixed ex ante. (3) REPORT THE N-SCALING TABLE: N in {250, 500, 1000, 2000} with kappa held FIXED. If DKKM/FF is stable in N the result is economics; if it scales with sqrt(N) it is diversification of a planted alpha and should be reported as such. Also, break the mechanical bm/size cancellation -- contaminate the price only, or add independent measurement noise -- so that recovering q genuinely requires the nonlinear basis rather than a two-char linear contrast.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (bandwidth, second rank-standardization, NMAT, alpha grid, c=P/T)
verdicts.critique: Items (b)-(f) are correctness fixes I would insist on and they are cheap. I verified the diagnosis: dkkm_functions.py:110 does return rank_standardize(features) on the sin/cos block, and ridge_regr applies 1/(eigenvalues + 360*z) with no truncation at z=0 (lines 158-160 and 172-174), and mve_data always emits an unpenalized alpha=0 column first (line 301) with the market column exempted from the augmentation via np.eye(X.shape[1])[:-1] (line 311). ALPHA_LST = [0,0.001,0.01,0.05,0.1,1] with ALPHA_LST_GS = ALPHA_LST/100 is a hand-tuned per-model grid (config.py:190-193) and that alone is a referee finding: you gave one model a 100x-different regularization grid and did not say why. But item (a), the bandwidth rescale by sqrt(130/L), is where the paper gets killed. The derivation is elegant -- hold the Gaussian-kernel exponent gamma^2 L/12 fixed at DKKM's real-data value -- but the GS21 agent MEASURED that widening gamma HURTS when the truth is near-linear (36 features: 0.879 -> 0.799 at x4.65, 0.879 -> 0.376 at x10) and the theory agent measured it hurt in the estimation experiment too (0.157 vs 0.254 under linear alpha, homogeneous d). So the rescale is a knob whose sign depends on the DGP, and it will be adopted precisely because it helps under the new DGP. That is the definition of tuning, however good the derivation reads. The proposal's own risk section concedes 'do not apply it before P1/P3', which is an admission that the choice is conditioned on the answer. Bigger problem, item (f): the fairness fix is 'apply find_best_alpha_for_model to FF/FM as well'. I read that function (create_slides_tables.py:81-97): it takes the argmax over alphas of the MEAN Sharpe ACROSS iterations and then reports that alpha's per-iteration values -- post-hoc selection on the evaluation metric itself, with a SEPARATE argmin run for HJD, so two independent oracle choices per table cell. Letting FF/FM cheat symmetrically does not make the number out-of-sample; it institutionalizes the cheat and guarantees a referee comment. The correct fix is a validation split.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal says so honestly -- on the current models the bundle is worth roughly zero because BGN's entire population nonlinearity headroom is 0.7pp of Sharpe and GS21's is 3%. That honesty is to its credit but it also means every point of gap this bundle eventually produces is attributable to estimator plumbing, and a referee will discount it to zero. There is a specific danger: the alpha-grid recentring plus c=36000 will make the DKKM column move visibly (the c=1 double-descent spike at P=T=360 disappears, alpha=0 stops realizing 1.4-13% of max Sharpe), and an incautious draft will read that movement as a result. It is a bug fix. Also NMAT: config.py:178 is NMAT=5 while the comment on the preceding line records that the root codebase used nmat=1 -- so the current setting is an undisclosed local deviation that provably flattens the complexity curve. Fixing it is mandatory, but fixing it will RAISE the Monte-Carlo variance of every DKKM cell and a single lucky draw must not become the headline.
verdicts.salvage: Split into two commits with different rhetorical status. COMMIT A (mandatory, pre-registered as bug fixes, report before/after on the CURRENT models so the reader sees they buy nothing): NMAT=5 -> 1 with the five draws reported as a distribution; the scale-free penalty reparameterization z*trace(X'X)/P, which also eliminates the indefensible GS21 /100; the 11-point log alpha grid; the same grid and the same tuning budget for FF/FM (fama_functions.mve_data:268 currently hardcodes Ridge(alpha=360*alpha) with ALPHA_LST_FAMA=[0]); turning on the commented-out FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156; and deleting the BGN-only rf_stand input at dkkm_functions.py:95-96, which is an unearned conditioning variable for DKKM that FF/FM never see and that the audit measured to be worth 89.9% vs 90.1% of max Sharpe, i.e. nothing. Drop it and lose nothing but a referee attack. COMMIT B (report as a robustness dimension, never as the baseline): the gamma rescale and the z-scoring of features, shown as a full 2x2 of {coded, rescaled} gamma x {old, new} DGP, so the reader can see the sign flip and judge it. AND replace symmetric oracle alpha selection with genuine out-of-sample hyperparameter selection: split the 360 eval months into a 120-month validation block used to pick (alpha, nfeatures) for every method and a 240-month test block used to report. That is the only version of this table I would let through.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 model-generated signals
verdicts.critique: The proposal contains its own refutation and I would quote it back: DKKM's five-characteristic real-data experiment uses exactly this project's five characteristics and still delivers 0.74 -> 1.93-2.50. So the count is demonstrably not the cause, and adding thirty derived transforms of the same two or three latent states is dimension counting dressed as realism. The audit already measured the relevant placebo: at N=200 a basis of 150 RANDOM Gaussian directions carrying zero characteristic information attains 0.74-0.82 of max SR^2. If a random basis of the right size gets most of the way there, the referee's conclusion is that the gain is a property of the feature count, not of the information. Second, and more damaging: the proposal predicts on the current DGPs that 'FM Sharpe DOWN by roughly 10% from the 37-parameter estimation cost, FF Sharpe down more from 35 collinear sorted factors -- so this alone would produce a spurious-looking DKKM/FM ratio of maybe 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency'. A gap produced by handicapping the benchmark is not a result; it is the thing referees are trained to look for. And the FF handicap is worse than stated, because FF's tercile logic degenerates whenever a characteristic has more than 30% ties -- I verified the code at fama_functions.py:86-88 uses data[char].quantile(0.3) and quantile(0.7) with no tie handling, which already breaks agr (91% zeros in BGN, 98.8% in GS21, giving q30 = q70 = 0 and an empty medium bucket). Several of the thirty new multi-horizon transforms in these near-static models will be similarly degenerate, and thirty degenerate sorts fed into an unpenalized OLS tangency at T=360 is not a benchmark, it is a straw man. Third, the fairness section is right that FF/FM must get the same 35 chars, but the proposal does not give FF ridge -- only P2(f) does, and if these ship separately the paper is indefensible.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It would produce A gap, of the wrong kind. Effective rank rising 16.5 -> ~250 is real and the bandwidth by-product (sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(35/12) = 1.708*gamma with the ORIGINAL grid) is genuinely the referee-proof route to nonlinearity -- that part I like a lot, because it achieves P2(a) with no hyperparameter touched. But the mechanism producing the DKKM/FM ratio would be the 2K/T = 20.6% squared-Sharpe estimation penalty on a 37-parameter FM plus badly conditioned FF, and both of those are curable by the benchmark simply using ridge. The moment a referee asks 'what happens if FM is ridge-regularized on the same grid', the 1.2-1.3x collapses toward 1.0, because the truth is still low-dimensional and the extra chars are still redundant transforms of 2-3 states. FF is the only method that stays broken, and FF being bad at 35 collinear sorts is a known, uninteresting fact.
verdicts.salvage: Demote from a source of the result to an enabling change, and make three commitments. (1) Adopt it ONLY for the bandwidth by-product: state explicitly that raising L to ~35 is how the RFF index reaches genuine nonlinearity WITHOUT touching GAMMA_GRID, which removes P2(a)'s tuning exposure entirely. That is a real and defensible contribution. (2) Report ridge-regularized FM and ridge-regularized FF at the identical scale-free z-grid as the primary benchmarks, so that no part of the gap is estimation-cost handicapping. If DKKM still wins against a properly shrunk 37-characteristic linear model, the result is about nonlinearity and you can say so. (3) Screen every derived characteristic for tie fraction and drop anything above ~20% -- and fix the FF tercile degeneracy at fama_functions.py:86-88 in the same commit, because leaving it broken while adding thirty tie-heavy columns is the kind of thing that looks deliberate in hindsight. Also report the random-direction placebo (150 Gaussian directions) alongside the RFF column at every feature count; if RFF does not clearly beat the placebo, the dimension-counting objection is conceded.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block in all three models
verdicts.critique: This is the only proposal that a referee cannot characterize as changing the model to get the answer, because it is undoing changes that were made to the models without disclosure. I verified BGN: panel_functions_bgn.py:54 reads high = np.abs(beta[:-1,:])/sigma_z + 0.1*0.3*np.abs(Cbar) with the inline comment '# added a factor of 0.1'. That is a 10x cut to the idiosyncratic cash-flow band, made in the repo, not in Berk-Green-Naik. KP14 has the same 10x cut on SIGMA_EPS and SIGMA_U, GS21 has 0.1*0.16 on SIGMA_Z. Here is the part the proposal understates and that the authors need to internalize: THE EXISTENCE OF THESE CUTS IS ITSELF A PAPER-KILLER IF A REFEREE FINDS THEM AND THE PAPER HAS NOT DISCLOSED THEM. A paper whose headline is 'these three canonical models cannot generate the virtue of complexity' while silently running all three at one tenth the source papers' idiosyncratic volatility -- producing average pairwise return correlations of 0.57, 0.39 and 0.95 against a real-data 0.15-0.20 -- is not recoverable at revision. So this must be done regardless of whether it helps, and the paper must contain a table of every parameter that differs from the source calibration with a reason for each. The proposal is also admirably honest that standalone this LOWERS max_sr everywhere and moves the DKKM/FF ratio by a few percent. My only real reservation is sequencing risk: GS21 needs a MATLAB re-solve on an external toolchain (the current solfiles' zgrid spans exactly +/-2.72 stationary sd of the 0.1x sigma_z, so at 0.5x everything extrapolates), and KP14 literally cannot be recalibrated until integ_results.npz and G_func.csv are fixed and kp14_fd.py's missing parameters_kp14 import is restored.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: On its own, no -- and the proposal says so, correctly. Under exact factor pricing the D^{-1} tilt is worth 0.186% of SR* at N=1000 even with a 20x spread in d, because idiosyncratic risk is diversifiable. FF could also get a crude version of the tilt if d is monotone in a single characteristic, which is exactly the KP14 case (corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971). So as a standalone this changes nothing and would be correctly read as a null. Its value is as a multiplier: span2.py measures RFF/linear rising 1.00 -> 1.91 when heteroskedastic d is added to a linear alpha and 2.88 -> 6.37 when added to a nonlinear one. It also fixes two numbers that would otherwise draw fire on their own -- KP14's max_sr of 34.7 annualized against the model's own bound of 0.774, and GS21's 0.44/month of which 89-97% is diversifying 3.5-4.3 basis points of per-firm alpha across 500 near-identical firms. Neither of those is a Sharpe ratio anyone will believe.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt as written, with three additions. (1) A disclosure table in the paper listing every parameter that departs from the source paper's calibration, the departure, and the reason -- including the ones you revert, so the reader sees the history. (2) Fix KP14's numerics BEFORE any recalibration and before any KP14 number appears in any table: integ_kp14.py:43 calls quad(integrand, 0, 10, ...) against a CIR transition density with sd ~0.006 and silently returns exact zeros over the eps interval where 98% of firm-months live, which makes the KP14 'true' risk premium equal to minus the PVGO share -- wrong sign, dispersion 173x too large. Every KP14 row currently in the results is uninterpretable and must not be published in any form. (3) When you restore GS21's sigma_z, remove or guard the arbitrary floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 (P_ex = max(0.05/k, P_ex)) and add an eigenvalue check on cond_var before np.linalg.solve -- that clamp is the most plausible source of the 1e9 true SDF weights recorded in the original-vol run, and a silent near-singular solve is exactly the failure mode already documented in KP14.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (scale-free pricing error, Sharpe/max_sr, unconditional Sharpe, better test assets)
verdicts.critique: Items (a)-(c) are mandatory and item (b) is the single most valuable line of code in this entire set. I confirmed it: calculate_moments.py:81-86 stores 'max_sr' in every moments dict, and evaluate_sdfs.py:170-179 reads m['rp'], m['cond_var'] and m['sdf_ret'] and never touches max_sr, so the ceiling never reaches a table. Since the reported Sharpe is exactly SR*_t x cos_Sigma(w, w*_t), a table of Sharpes without max_sr is uninterpretable -- neither the authors nor the referee can tell whether FF at 0.2423 is 20% or 81% of the ceiling, which is the entire difference between 'the estimator fails' and 'the model has nothing in it'. Publish that column and much of the paper writes itself. The HJD replacement is also correct algebra and GS21's reported FF HJD of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is transparently a leverage artifact. BUT: changing the pricing-error metric between drafts, after the old one produced an inconvenient answer, is the second-most-likely thing a referee flags. Report both columns permanently and justify the new one from the derivation, never from the results. Now the item I would reject outright. P5(d) proposes adding test assets formed on 'ten deciles of the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp)'. That is circular: you would build the test assets out of the answer key and then report that the method which best approximates the answer key prices them. Every method's alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha against those portfolios is a monotone transform of cos_Sigma(w, w*) -- the Sharpe you already report -- dressed up as an independent pricing test. A referee will see it immediately and it will contaminate the credibility of the honest parts of the same table.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, by construction -- this changes no economics and the proposal says so. What it will do is make the existing null SHARPER and more publishable as a null: the Sigma-cosine column will show FF at roughly 0.81 and DKKM at 0.85 of the BGN ceiling, which demonstrates in one line that the estimators are near the ceiling and the DGP is the problem. That is a genuine contribution and arguably the paper's most persuasive exhibit whatever else happens. There is also a direction a referee should be told about: the scale-free pricing error REMOVES an asymmetry currently favoring DKKM, which gets six alphas selected post hoc on the evaluation metric (two separate oracle selections, one argmax for Sharpe and one argmin for HJD, at create_slides_tables.py:81-97) while FF/FM have alpha=0 only and no way to rescale. So the fix should make DKKM look slightly worse on pricing error. Disclose that, and disclose that it is the correct direction.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt (a), (b), (c) unchanged and make (b) a headline column in every table. Drop (d)'s w*-sorted decile portfolios entirely. Replace them with test assets that are informative but not circular: 5x5 on (mve, diag(cond_var)) is fine because idiosyncratic variance is a legitimate observable sort; add sorts on characteristic INTERACTIONS (size x bm, roe x agr) and on non-monotone transforms (|bm - median|, extreme deciles) -- these have power against nonlinear-in-characteristics mispricing without being built from the answer. Note the current 25 portfolios are mve x bm only (generate_25_portfolios.py:110-112, pd.qcut on the ranks of mve and bm), i.e. two of the five characteristics that all three methods already span linearly, so the existing test genuinely has no power and this is worth fixing. Also fix the universe mismatch in the same pass: evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 subsets rp and cond_var to firm_ids from the estimator's panel while sdf_ret comes from moments computed over the book>0 universe, so the HJ benchmark and the method returns are not defined over the same assets.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with staggered fiscal year-ends plus heteroskedastic measurement error
verdicts.critique: The Fourier analysis is the best piece of theory in the whole set and I would want it in the paper regardless: classical homoskedastic errors-in-variables attenuates the linear component by lambda = tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2) but attenuates frequency-omega components by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2), so it compresses the DKKM advantage exponentially while compressing FM's only classically. Deriving that, and then declining to add classical EIV because of it, is exactly the kind of reasoning that earns a referee's trust. The staleness half is also defensible -- staggered fiscal year-ends with a six-month lag is the Fama-French convention, not an invention, and it breaks GS21's genuinely indefensible identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly. But the heteroskedastic half is where I object. Setting sigma_e,i = sigma_e0*(mve_i/median)^{-xi} so that the optimal predictor becomes lambda_i x g(x_i) is writing a multiplicative interaction directly into the DGP and then reporting that the method with multiplicative features wins. That is the opposite of P1's virtue, where the ratio and the hump EMERGE from Sigma^{-1}mu rather than being written down. The sentence 'the authors introduced a variable whose only function is to multiply the other signals, and then found that a flexible estimator outperforms linear ones' is a rejection in one line. The proposal half-sees this -- it steers the reliability proxy toward staleness precisely because staleness is not one of FF's sort variables -- but that reasoning is itself incriminating: the proxy was chosen for being invisible to the benchmark rather than for being economically primary.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Probably not against a competent benchmark, and this is the fatal technical objection. The truth is lambda(h_i) x bm_i, a product of an observable reliability variable with a signal. FM as coded regresses on chars linearly (fama_functions.fama_macbeth:159-165, X = [1, raw chars], P = X pinvh(X'X)), so naive FM cannot form it -- true. But nothing stops a referee from asking for FM run on {chars, h, chars x h}, which at L=5 is 16 regressors on 360 months, entirely feasible, and which spans the target to first order. If DKKM beats naive FM but not FM-with-interactions, there is no result, only a claim that the benchmark was specified badly. And FF is not shut out either: its 2x3 design already contains a size x char interaction, so if reliability had been left as a function of size FF would get a two-bin approximation -- which is why the proposal moved to staleness. The proposal also predicts honestly that the effect may be inert in BGN, where book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95 that barely moves month to month, so twelve-month-stale bm is nearly as informative as fresh. Finally, and this is a real self-inflicted wound: at P2's rescaled gamma the multiplicative noise costs a factor exp(-gamma^2 sigma_e^2/2) = 0.70 on exactly the nonlinear components the proposal exists to create.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the staleness mechanism, drop the heteroskedastic noise, and elevate the Fourier result to a standalone theoretical contribution. Specifically: (1) implement staggered fiscal year-ends and the six-month accounting lag as a pure realism layer with zero free parameters -- it is the standard convention, it breaks GS21's bm = 1/P_ex identity, and no referee can call it tuning; report the resulting DKKM/FM change honestly even if it is negative in BGN. (2) Do NOT add size-dependent measurement noise; the interaction is planted and the reliability proxy was visibly selected for being invisible to FF. (3) Publish the errors-in-variables asymmetry as a proposition with the exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) versus lambda contrast -- 'classical measurement error is a headwind for high-dimensional nonlinear SDF estimators and a tailwind for the case against them' is a genuinely novel and quotable point, and it makes the paper better even if the empirical exercise fails. (4) If any interaction-based mechanism survives, pre-commit to reporting FM with a full set of chars x reliability interactions and FF with the corresponding three-way sorts as primary benchmarks, not as robustness. The result must beat the benchmark a smart referee would build, not the one that happens to be in the repo.

missed_ideas: REPRODUCE THE REAL-DATA GAP WITH THIS EXACT PIPELINE FIRST. This is the check I would demand before reading any of the rest, and no proposal mentions it. Run generate_dkkm_factors / estimate_sdf_dkkm / estimate_sdf_fama unchanged on CRSP with the same five characteristics, T=360 rolling, and see whether the code reproduces DKKM's 0.74 -> 1.93-2.50. If it does not, every claim about what the MODELS lack is unfounded, because the estimator implementation is the confound -- and the audit gives specific reasons to worry (NMAT=5 is an undisclosed deviation from the root's nmat=1 at config.py:177-178; the second rank-standardization at dkkm_functions.py:110 makes GAMMA_GRID a near-no-op; the alpha grid has no point with effective df between 63 and 360). If it DOES reproduce the gap, that single exhibit converts the paper from 'we changed models until complexity paid' into 'our estimator is correct, and here is precisely what a structural model must contain for it to pay'. That reframing is worth more than any of the six proposals.

PUBLISH THE NEGATIVE CONTROL AS A HEADLINE EXHIBIT, NOT A FOOTNOTE. The single strongest defense against 'you tuned the DGP until it worked' is to show a DGP where you tuned nothing and it demonstrably does NOT work -- and you already have it in span2.py's exact-factor-pricing cell (SR* 0.0999, equal-weight 0.0998, linear span 0.0999, RFF 0.0994). Run the FULL pipeline, including the modified estimator, on the unmodified models and on a synthetic exact-APT panel, and report the flat complexity curve. A paper that shows the estimator failing where theory says it must fail, and succeeding only where theory says it can, is a paper about a mechanism. A paper that only shows the success is a paper about a search.

REPORT THE COMPLEXITY CURVE'S SHAPE, NOT ITS ARGMAX. DKKM's actual claim is about monotone ascent in c = P/T over three orders of magnitude, not about a single best cell. Yet create_slides_tables.py fixes nfeatures=3600 and then takes an argmax over alpha (line 100-101, two separate oracle selections for Sharpe and HJD). A monotone rising curve across c in {0.017, 0.1, 1, 10, 100} at a FIXED, pre-committed shrinkage is far harder to manufacture than a maximum over a grid, and it is the object the theory predicts. Make the curve the headline figure and relegate the argmax cell to an appendix.

MAKE THE PRICED-RISK SPACE HIGH-DIMENSIONAL INSTEAD OF ADDING A PRICING WEDGE. The diagnosis ranks 'raise the number of independently priced aggregate shocks from 1-2 to tens, with heterogeneous characteristic-dependent loadings' as the second binding blocker, and NO proposal implements it. This is the route a JF referee will fight least: it is fully rational, fully within the frictionless paradigm, requires no redefinition of 'the true SDF', keeps max_sr bounded independently of N, and is the direct lever on EffRank(E[FF']) -- DKKM's own Theorem 3 criterion, which needs hundreds and currently measures 16.5. Concretely: replace GS21's scalar x with a J-dimensional factor (sectoral, vintage, intangible-capital, financial-constraint shocks), give firms loading vectors that are nonlinear functions of their state, and price all J. It is more work than a three-line wedge, but P1's wedge buys a result the referee will discount by 80% while this buys one they cannot attack on identification grounds. At minimum it belongs in the paper as the alternative that was considered.

SELECT HYPERPARAMETERS OUT OF SAMPLE, DO NOT MAKE THE CHEATING SYMMETRIC. P2(f)'s proposal to let FF/FM also use find_best_alpha_for_model is the wrong repair. Split the 360 evaluation months into a validation block (say 120) used to pick (alpha, nfeatures) for every method and a disjoint test block (240) used to report. Every method then gets exactly one specification and one number, chosen without seeing the test data. This costs a third of the evaluation sample and removes the most predictable referee objection in the paper.

REPORT TURNOVER, GROSS LEVERAGE AND NET-OF-COST SHARPE. The audit already found the true HJ portfolio carrying 9x to 44x gross leverage in KP14, and GS21's max_sr is 89-97% driven by diversifying 3.5-4.3 basis points of alpha across 500 near-identical firms. If the manufactured DKKM advantage lives in extreme leverage on small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility names -- which is exactly where DKKM's real-data Sharpe of 3.7 lives, falling to ~1.6 in mega/large caps -- the paper should say so and report the advantage net of a plausible cost model. A referee who suspects the result is a microcap leverage artifact and finds no turnover table will assume the worst.

PRE-REGISTER THE PARAMETER CHOICES AND SHOW THE FULL SENSITIVITY SURFACE. P1's s_k is proposed as a search over {0.8, 1.3, 1.9} with the instruction 'pick the largest s_k for which SR* stays below ~2.5 annualized' -- i.e. pick the parameter that maximizes the mechanism subject to the answer staying plausible. Instead, fix every new parameter from an external moment before running anything, and then report the DKKM/FF ratio over the whole grid of that parameter so the reader sees the sensitivity rather than the selected point. A monotone, smooth, and disclosed sensitivity is credible; a chosen point is not.

CHECK WHETHER THE MODIFIED PANELS STILL MATCH THE MOMENTS THE SOURCE PAPERS WERE CALIBRATED TO. After P1's wedge and P4's volatility restoration, BGN's value and size premia, KP14's growth-option premium and GS21's leverage cross-section will all move. A referee's standard demand is a table of untargeted moments -- average pairwise correlation, sd(log market cap), sd(log book-to-market), the value premium, the size premium, default frequency -- for each model before and after, next to their real-data counterparts. Right now those numbers are badly off in the untouched models (GS21 sd(log mve) = 0.285 and sd(log bm) = 0.101 against real-data ~2.0 and ~0.8; zero defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months with maximum market leverage of 1.04%), and a paper that changes a model without showing its untargeted moments improved will be asked to.

verdicts.proposal_name: P1. Limits-to-arbitrage price wedge (kappa_i * v_it)
verdicts.critique: P1 is the only proposal that clears the gating condition (an expected-return component not proportional to the covariance loadings), and I cannot refute that necessity. But the mechanism as specified hands most of the new premium to FM, not DKKM, and the proposal's own evidence says so. The wedge is discoverable ONLY because it contaminates the characteristics: log bm_obs = log bm_fund + q, size_obs = size_fund - q. So the numerator of the new alpha, alpha_i = (1-rho)*q_it, is by construction an ADDITIVE component of two raw characteristics. FM's weight is w_i,t = a_t'x_it + b (fama_functions.py:158-165, P = X pinvh(X'X) refit every month), so a linear read of bm_obs and size_obs recovers q up to the fundamental-bm confound. That is exactly the proposer's own span2.py cell 'linear alpha, homogeneous d', where RFF/lin = 1.00 -- ZERO DKKM advantage. P1 alone therefore raises SR* a lot and moves the DKKM/FM ratio by nothing. The DKKM-specific content is only (i) the 1/(d_f + kappa^2 sigma_v^2) denominator and (ii) the kappa-hump. On (i), the proposer's own est3.py numbers for 'linear alpha + het d' are lin 0.265, QUAD(21) 0.601, RFF(3600) 0.564 -- a 21-term quadratic OLS BEATS the 3600-feature ridge. That is a virtue of one interaction layer, not a virtue of complexity, and it is available to FM at the cost of appending 15 cross-product columns. On (ii), the hump requires s_k ~ 1.9, which the proposer concedes makes E[kappa^2] = kappa_med^2 * exp(2*1.9^2) = 1370x kappa_med^2: with N=1000 and a lognormal that heavy, SR*^2 = sum_i alpha_i^2/d_i is dominated by the top handful of firms. That is precisely the corruption failure mode -- max_sr becomes a 5-firm artifact, the true w* concentrates on those firms, and cos_Sigma(w_hat, w*) falls for EVERY method including DKKM. Separately, the fork between 'log kappa ~ N permanent firm attribute' and 'kappa = g(mve, sigma_idio)' is decisive and unresolved: the permanent-random version is not a function of the characteristics at all, so it is unlearnable noise for all three estimators and only inflates the denominator of Sharpe/SR*. Only the char-deterministic version can help, and that version makes kappa an exponential of a linear function of two chars -- a smooth two-dimensional surface, i.e. the low-order regime where the audit already measured the RFF basis to be 88% cubic.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM CAN capture it: alpha_i = (1-rho)*kappa_i*v_it = (1-rho)*q_it, and q_it enters log bm_obs and size_obs ADDITIVELY, so the premium is linear in two contaminated characteristics and FM's monthly X(X'X)^{-1} span contains it exactly. FF CAN capture much of it: hml is a tercile long-short in bm_obs, which is monotone in q, and because FF value-weights within buckets (fama_functions.py:88-99, weights proportional to mve within (high & big) etc.), the FF factor set is literally {size x step-function-of-char}, so the leading size-modulation of kappa is a two-bin FF interaction. THE GAP IS SECOND-ORDER: taking the proposal's own calibration, SR_alpha = 0.6/month of which the linear-in-chars part is fully FM-spanned; the residual DKKM-only part is the ratio curvature, which span2.py prices at RFF/lin = 1.91 in POPULATION and est3.py prices at RFF(3600) 0.564 vs QUAD(21) 0.601 with estimation noise -- i.e. DKKM LOSES to a 21-term quadratic. Converting: on BGN's current scale that is FM ~0.30, quadratic-FM ~0.35, DKKM ~0.33 per month. A ratio of 1.1x, not 3-5x. NOISE-FASTER-THAN-SIGNAL: the wedge adds kappa_i^2*sigma_v^2 to every diagonal, i.e. it adds pure idiosyncratic variance to all 1000 firms while adding exploitable alpha to only the tail of the kappa distribution; at s_k = 1.9 the median firm gets almost all noise and almost no signal, which is the regime where ridge-on-3600 features loses to a 6-parameter fit. METRIC: the population conditional Sharpe CAN detect this (it is SR* x cos_Sigma), but HJD as currently coded cannot, because raising SR* from 0.30 to 0.64/month drives sd(sdf_ret) down and E[sdf_ret] up, compressing the whole HJD range (the audit's table: at SR*=2 the entire span from rho=0 to rho=1 is 13% of the level).
verdicts.salvage: Keep the wedge, but change three things so the premium is NOT linear in any characteristic. (1) Make kappa depend on a THREE-WAY interaction that FF's 2x3 design cannot form and that is not size-monotone: e.g. kappa_i = f(idio-vol percentile) x g(turnover/age) x h(|bm - cross-sectional median|), with h non-monotone. (2) Make the demand shock v_it enter the observables only through a NON-MONOTONE or ratio channel, so that no single contaminated char is an affine read of q -- e.g. let v drive a temporary component of BOTH price and reported book so that q is identified only by the DIFFERENCE of two chars divided by a third. (3) Before running any estimator, compute the population gate: mean_t sqrt(rp' S (S'Sigma S)^{-1} S' rp) / sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp) with X = [1, chars, all 15 quadratic cross-products] in the denominator, not just linear chars. If that ratio is below ~2 against the QUADRATIC benchmark, the wedge has not created complexity, only nonlinearity, and the paper's claim must be re-scoped. Also cap s_k at the value where the top 10 firms contribute less than 25% of SR*^2, and report that share in every table.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2. Estimator geometry repair (bandwidth, second rank-standardization, NMAT, alpha grid, c=P/T)
verdicts.critique: The diagnosis is largely right and the proposal admits its own standalone value is approximately zero. Beyond that, three items are wrong or counterproductive. (a) THE EXACT CHANGE FOR THE ALPHA GRID TARGETS DEAD CODE. P2(d) says to reparameterize 'utils_factors/dkkm_functions.py lines 162 and 176 from 360*z to 360*z*trace(X'X)/P'. But mve_data calls ridge_regr with shrinkage_list = np.array([0]) at BOTH line 301 (the alpha=0 column) and line 314 (every alpha>0 column). The penalty for alpha>0 is delivered entirely by the augmentation matrix np.sqrt(360*alph)*np.eye(X.shape[1])[:-1] at line 309. So the proposed edit changes nothing for any nonzero alpha and only touches the already-degenerate alpha=0 path. The correct site is line 309. This matters because the whole proposal is sold as 'derived, not tuned' and the derivation would be applied at a location where it has no effect. (b) NMAT=1 MAKES DKKM WORSE IN LEVEL. Averaging 5 independent W draws is a variance reduction on the estimated stock weight (estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169 accumulates sw_i = fw_i @ pof_i and divides by NMAT). The theoretical argument that this converges to kernel ridge and flattens the complexity CURVE is correct, but the goal here is a large DKKM Sharpe ADVANTAGE, and removing a 5x variance reduction will lower DKKM's realized Sharpe. P2 is trading level for curve shape and does not say so. (c) THE FAIRNESS FIX IS SELF-DEFEATING FOR THE STATED GOAL. P2(f) gives FF/FM the same ridge grid and the same post-hoc alpha selection. Ridge on a 7-factor plug-in tangency at T=360 is worth roughly the 2K/T = 3.9% squared-Sharpe loss, so FF/FM go UP and the gap goes DOWN. Correct science, but it should be labelled as shrinking the target, not enabling it. (d) The gamma rescale is measured to HURT on the current DGPs (GS21: 0.879 -> 0.799 of max SR^2 at gamma x4.65 with 36 features; 0.879 -> 0.376 at x10), and P3, which P2 leans on to justify it, does not actually deliver sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(35/12) once the chars are collinear (see my P3 critique).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: By the proposal's own admission the gap produced is zero on the current models, and the audit bounds it at 0.7pp of Sharpe in BGN and +3% in GS21. Conditional on P1/P4, FM captures the same thing because none of P2 changes what is in the DGP -- it only changes how well DKKM can reach a nonlinearity that must be created elsewhere, and if that nonlinearity turns out to be quadratic (the est3.py evidence), then P2's contribution is negative: it spends the feature budget on high-frequency directions that a 21-term quadratic already covers, which is exactly the measured GS21 result. NOISE FASTER THAN SIGNAL is the central risk here and it is measured, not speculative: widening gamma raises effective rank from 16.5 to 78 but the added directions carry no signal under any low-order truth, so ridge must shrink harder and the realized Sharpe falls (est3.py: linear alpha + hom d gives RFF3600 0.254 vs RFFx8 0.157, a 38% loss). METRIC: P=36000 at c=100 will also re-create alpha=0 pathologies unless the alpha=0 column is removed; note line 301 unconditionally emits it regardless of the grid.
verdicts.salvage: Do three of the five, at the right code sites, and drop the other two. KEEP: (i) the alpha grid, implemented at dkkm_functions.py:309 as sqrt(360*alph*trace(X'X)/P) so z is a scale-free shrinkage fraction, and delete the unconditional alpha=0 column at line 301 (or truncate small eigenvalues in the P>=T branch at line 176); (ii) the second-rank-standardization -> per-column z-score at line 110, which is the one change that both restores gamma-dependence and preserves the amplitude equalization the audit measured to be load-bearing; (iii) the fairness repairs (same grid for FF/FM, drop the BGN-only rf_stand at lines 95-96, turn on the FM standardization at fama_functions.py:152-156) -- do these unconditionally, as correctness. DROP: NMAT=1 (keep 5 and report the cross-draw spread separately as a robustness panel), and the gamma rescale (make it a reported 2x2 robustness cell, never the headline). Add one thing P2 omits: a QUADRATIC-OLS benchmark column (FM plus all 15 cross-products, ridge-tuned on the same grid). If DKKM cannot beat that, there is no virtue of complexity to report regardless of what the bandwidth does.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3. Expand the characteristic set from 5-6 to ~35 model-generated signals
verdicts.critique: The load-bearing quantitative claim is wrong. P3 asserts EffRank ~ 16.5*(L/5)^1.42 -> ~250 at L=35, citing the measured grid L=5 -> 16.5, L=20 -> 98, L=130 -> 773. That grid was measured with characteristics that are (near-)independent draws.
