The eigenvalue decay of a Gaussian-kernel feature map is governed by the INTRINSIC dimension of the data manifold, not the ambient column count: features are sin(gamma*g'x), and if x lies on a 3-dimensional manifold then every feature is a function of 3 coordinates and the RKHS is the 3-dimensional Gaussian RKHS no matter how many collinear coordinates you stack. The audit already established the intrinsic dimension: BGN's entire date-t cross-section is a bijective function of exactly two numbers, (num_i, sum_j exp(-beta_j)) <-> (book_i, mve_i), verified to machine precision; GS21's state is (k, b, z) with bm = 1/P_ex EXACTLY; KP14's chars recover nlive and log d at R^2 0.82-0.88 and nothing else. P3's 35 columns -- five momentum horizons, four asset-growth horizons, five profitability transforms, four valuation anchors, five risk measures, three scale measures, four lags -- are all deterministic smooth transforms of those same 2-3 states plus a common aggregate. Effective rank will move from 16.5 to maybe 25-40, not 250. Note the arithmetic P3 itself supplies and then ignores: sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) is derived assuming Var(w'x) = sum_i g_i^2/12, i.e. UNCORRELATED chars; with 35 chars whose correlation matrix has effective rank 3, E_g[g'Sigma_x g] = tr(Sigma_x) is unchanged but the feature map's SPECTRUM collapses -- the quantity that matters for DKKM Theorem 3 is the spectrum, not the index sd. Second problem: P3 concedes that the honest DKKM-vs-FM channel at L=35 is FM's 2K/T = 20.6% squared-Sharpe estimation cost. That is manufacturing a gap by degrading the benchmark, and it is worse for FF, which gets 35 collinear tercile long-shorts fed into an unpenalized OLS tangency (fama_functions.mve_data uses sklearn Ridge with alpha=0). Third problem: P3's own risk section notes that several derived chars will be >20% ties (agr is already 91% zeros in BGN, 98.8% in GS21), and the audit measured that a tied column becomes a persistent pseudo-random characteristic that enters ALL 3600 features multiplicatively, raising the PCs needed for 99% of feature variance from 59 to 95. Adding 35 columns of which several are degenerate injects noise into DKKM's basis multiplicatively while injecting it into FM's design additively -- the asymmetry runs AGAINST DKKM.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM CAN capture whatever new information exists, because 35 smooth transforms of a 3-dimensional state contain no information the original 5 did not, and FM spans every linear combination of all 35. FF's degradation is real but is benchmark sabotage, not complexity. THE ARITHMETIC: the audit's own headroom numbers cap the total nonlinearity available in BGN at 0.7 percentage points of Sharpe (deg-3 poly 0.2761 vs FM 0.2740 out of max 0.2985) and in GS21 at +3%. Those ceilings are properties of the DGP and are INVARIANT to how many transforms of the same state you hand the econometrician -- the population span calculation uses rp and cond_var, not chars. So P3 cannot move the ceiling by a single basis point; it can only move where each estimator sits relative to it, and it moves FM and FF DOWN. Expect a DKKM/FM ratio of 1.2-1.3x that is pure estimation efficiency, which P3 admits. ADDS NOISE FASTER THAN SIGNAL: yes, and measurably -- degenerate tie columns multiply into every feature.
verdicts.salvage: One piece survives and should be extracted as its own proposal: the 'peer-relative' block (viii), which requires a firm-type / industry partition. A fixed partition into 10 groups correlated with the model's PERMANENT firm heterogeneity (beta_j in BGN, lambda_f in KP14, initial k in GS21) is the only element of P3 that adds a genuinely new state dimension rather than a transform of an existing one. But even that is captured by FM the moment you give FM the industry dummies, so it must be paired with type-DEPENDENT nonlinear pricing, not just type demeaning. Everything else in P3 should be dropped, and if a wider characteristic set is wanted for realism, cap it at L ~ 12 and pre-screen every column on (a) tie fraction < 10% and (b) partial R^2 above 2% against the existing set, and publish the measured EffRank of the resulting feature map rather than the extrapolated one.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4. Recalibrate the idiosyncratic-risk block (level, dispersion, char-nonlinearity)
verdicts.critique: The realism case is unanswerable -- pairwise correlations of 0.565 (BGN), 0.391 (KP14) and 0.95 (GS21) against a real-data 0.15-0.20 are indefensible and should be fixed regardless. But as a route to a DKKM advantage it fails on my central test, and the proposal's own numbers say so: standalone it is worth 0.19% of SR* at N=1000 and it LOWERS max_sr in all three models. The multiplier argument then rests on w* = alpha(x)/d(x) being unreachable by the benchmarks, and that is where it breaks. In every one of the three models the measured d is a MONOTONE function of size: KP14 has corr(log idio var, log nlive) = -0.971 with slope -0.866 and corr(log idio var, log mve) giving R^2 0.743; BGN has corr(log d, log(bm/mve)) = 0.910; GS21 has R^2 of diag(Sigma) on linear chars of 0.68-0.84. So w* ~ alpha(x) * size^theta -- a product of a characteristic signal and a power of size. That is EXACTLY what a value-weighted 2x3 double sort forms. Reading fama_functions.py:88-104: high_big = mve*(high & big) normalized within bucket, and factor = 0.5*(high_big + high_small - low_big - low_small), so the FF factor's weight on firm i is proportional to mve_i times a step function of the sort char. A tangency combination over {smb, hml, cma, rmw, umd, mkt} therefore spans a family of size-weighted step functions in each characteristic -- a coarse but genuine product basis in exactly the (size x char) direction that P4's het-d channel creates. P4's own caveat says 'if d is a MONOTONE function of a single characteristic, FF's tercile sorts get a crude approximation', and then it does not act on that caveat: the proposed recalibrations (removing BGN's 0.1 factor, restoring KP14's sigmas, raising GS21 sigma_z) all produce size-monotone dispersion. The only non-monotone version offered is 'ride on P1's wedge', which makes P4 a rider on a proposal that itself needs fixing. Second problem: KP14's idio-var-proportional-to-1/size structure is what produces the documented anti-size artifact and the negative Sharpes; raising sigma_eps/sigma_u restores the CIR share to 69% and breaks that identity, which is a genuine bug fix, but it is a SIGN fix, not a complexity gain, and it should be reported as such rather than as evidence for the paper's thesis.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF CAN capture the leading term, for the specific reason above: value-weighting inside a size-split double sort IS an estimator of a size x char product, and the audit measures d to be size-monotone in all three models. FM captures the alpha numerator. THE ARITHMETIC, standalone: the inverse-variance tilt under exact factor pricing is worth 1/(2*sigma_f^2*beta'D^{-1}beta), measured at 0.186% of SR* at N=1000 -- roughly 0.0006 of monthly Sharpe on BGN's 0.2985 max. That is sub-basis-point and undetectable. Conditional on P1, the span2.py multiplier takes RFF/lin from 1.00 to 1.91, but that same cell in est3.py with T=360 noise gives QUAD(21) 0.601 > RFF(3600) 0.564, so once estimation error is included the ratio-nonlinearity is captured by a quadratic and DKKM does not win. CORRUPTION RISK, which is the failure mode I was asked to check and it is live here: raising GS21_SIGMA_Z from 0.1x to 0.5x makes default a live event for the first time (currently 0 defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months, z_cut_down pinned at the grid floor everywhere), and the arbitrary floor P_ex = max(0.05/k, P_ex) at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 then produces near-zero prices, enormous bm, tiny d and near-singular cond_var passed to np.linalg.solve, which raises no error. This is not hypothetical -- the original-vol run already produced true SDF weights up to 1e9. A handful of near-default firms would then carry all of max_sr, every method's cos_Sigma would collapse, and both metrics would be garbage. METRIC: raising idio vol lowers SR* everywhere, so all reported Sharpes fall and the paper's headline numbers get smaller even if the ratio improves.
verdicts.salvage: Split it. (1) Do the realism recalibration unconditionally as a correctness fix, headline it as 'the models were mis-calibrated by 10x on idiosyncratic risk', and report the resulting max_sr, pairwise correlation and sd(log d) against real-data targets. Fix KP14's quadrature (integ_kp14.py:43) and stale G_func.csv FIRST; nothing in KP14 is interpretable until then. (2) For GS21, add a hard guard before any re-solve: assert min eigenvalue of cond_var above a threshold, remove the P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131 rather than relying on it, and report the top-10-firm share of SR*^2 every month. (3) If the het-d channel is to carry any weight, the dispersion must be driven by a NON-MONOTONE or at least a two-characteristic INTERACTION -- e.g. idio variance that is U-shaped in bm within size groups -- so that a value-weighted 2x3 sort cannot approximate it. And in every table, report the quadratic-OLS benchmark next to DKKM; if a 21-term quadratic captures the ratio, the result is 'nonlinearity pays', which is a different and much weaker paper.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5. Metric repair (scale-free pricing error, Sharpe/max_sr, unconditional Sharpe, better test assets)
verdicts.critique: Items (b), (c) and (d) are unambiguously correct and cheap, and (b) in particular is the single most valuable line of code in all six proposals: evaluate_sdfs.py reads m['rp'], m['cond_var'] and m['sdf_ret'] at lines 170-172 but never m['max_sr'], so the ceiling never reaches a table and nobody can tell a failing estimator from an empty model. Item (a) is where I push back. The proposed replacement, sqrt(1 - rho_unc^2) with rho_unc the uncentered correlation, is in POPULATION a deterministic monotone transform of the quantity the Sharpe column already reports. Proof: sdf_ret is the projection of the constant 1 onto the full return span and xret_m is (approximately) the projection of 1 onto the method's span, so for any u in the span, E[u*z] = E[u], giving E[y*z] = E[y] = E[y^2] and E[z^2] = E[z]. Hence rho_unc^2 = E[y]/E[z] = [SR_m^2/(1+SR_m^2)] / [SR*^2/(1+SR*^2)], and 1 - rho_unc^2 is a strictly decreasing function of SR_m/SR* -- exactly the Sigma-cosine that P5(b) introduces. So the 'fixed' pricing-error column carries essentially no independent information; the paper would report the same number twice under two names. That is arguably worse than the current HJD, which at least has independent (if contaminated) content through the leverage and direction errors of the finite-sample weights. Second issue: P5(d) proposes test assets sorted on deciles of the TRUE conditional MVE weight w*_t = solve(cond_var, rp). Those are oracle-constructed test assets -- a referee will note that the test portfolios were built from the answer, and that any method whose weights correlate with w* will price them by construction. Third, minor but real: P5 correctly flags the universe mismatch at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-171 (rp and cond_var subset to firm_ids, sdf_ret computed over the book>0 universe) but files it as a footnote; in KP14 that is roughly 5% of firms per month with rp = -1.0 exactly, so it is not cosmetic.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It cannot, and the proposal says so. Nothing here changes the DGP, the estimator or the span. What it can do is REVEAL that no gap exists: the Sigma-cosine column will show FF at roughly 0.81 of the ceiling in BGN and DKKM at 0.85, which settles the diagnosis in one line. The adversarial risk to be honest about is that P5 makes DKKM look WORSE on two dimensions simultaneously: a scale-free pricing error removes DKKM's current advantage of having six alphas post-hoc selected on the evaluation metric itself (create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model), while FF/FM get only alpha=0; and the unconditional Sharpe will penalize methods whose monthly leverage is erratic, which at nfeatures=3600, alpha=0 is DKKM (mve_data line 301 always emits the min-norm interpolating column).
verdicts.salvage: Do (b), (c) and the universe fix immediately -- they are pure correctness and require no re-simulation if the moments pickles are retained. For (a), do NOT replace HJD with a monotone transform of Sharpe. Instead report the object compute_pricing_errors.py already computes -- alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha with each method's MVE return as a single factor -- since that has genuinely independent content, and demote HJD to a robustness table with sd(sdf_ret) and the w=0 null printed alongside so readers can see the floor. For (d), keep the (mve, diag(cond_var)) 5x5 and ADD interaction-sorted and non-monotone-sorted assets (|bm - median| terciles crossed with size, roe x agr), which are constructible from observables; drop the true-w*-decile assets or relegate them to an explicitly labelled oracle diagnostic. Finally add the one column that would make all six proposals falsifiable: the population span ratio mean_t SR_rff,t / SR_quad,t computed from the true rp and cond_var, with a QUADRATIC (not linear) denominator.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6. Reporting lags with staggered fiscal year-ends plus heteroskedastic measurement error
verdicts.critique: The theoretical observation is correct and elegant -- classical homoskedastic EIV attenuates nonlinear Fourier components by exp(-omega^2 sigma_e^2/2) while attenuating the linear component only by tau^2/(tau^2+sigma_e^2), so it strictly compresses the DKKM advantage, and the proposal is right to refuse it. But the constructive half fails on the mechanism test. The claimed DKKM-only object is lambda(h_i)*bm_i, a product of an observable reliability variable and a signal, and the argument is 'FM applies one coefficient per characteristic so it cannot form a product'. That is only true holding the characteristic set fixed -- and P3, from the same proposal set, is simultaneously arguing for engineering 35 characteristics. With one staleness variable and six base chars there are exactly six candidate products; handing FM the six columns h*bm, h*roe, h*agr, h*mom, h*size, h*mkt_lev costs six regressors on 360 months and closes the entire mechanism. The DKKM claim would have to be 'you do not know which products matter', which requires the interaction space to be large, i.e. it is a DIMENSION argument, not a nonlinearity argument -- and at L=6 plus staleness the interaction space is trivially enumerable. Second, the magnitude is bp-level. Take the most favourable case P6 itself constructs, GS21 with rho_z = 0.9655: h uniform on 6-17 gives attenuation from rho^6 = 0.810 to rho^17 = 0.552, so lambda has mean ~0.68 and sd ~0.075, i.e. 11% of its mean. Decompose lambda(h)*bm = E[lambda]*bm + (lambda - E[lambda])*bm; FM takes the first term exactly and, given the h*bm column, the second as well; without the column, the unspanned residual has cross-sectional sd equal to 11% of the bm signal. If the entire bm signal is worth 0.15 of monthly Sharpe -- generous, given GS21's p10-p90 value premium and its 3.9-5.6 bp cross-sectional sd of expected returns -- the unspanned piece is at most 0.11*0.15 = 0.017/month, about 6% of GS21's max_sr of 0.44 and well inside the noise of a 360-month evaluation. In BGN it is smaller still: book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95 that changes only when a project is created or dies, so a 12-month-stale bm is nearly identical to a fresh one, and P6 concedes this. Third, and worst for the goal, staleness h_i is by construction uniform and independent of every state variable. It is therefore a pure nuisance coordinate. Injected into the RFF map it enters all 3600 features MULTIPLICATIVELY through sin(gamma*g'x) with a nonzero component on h, degrading every feature; injected into FM it is one additive column. The audit already measured this asymmetry for agr, where a degenerate column raised the PCs needed for 99% of feature variance from 59 to 95. P6 hands DKKM a noise dimension and FM a clean regressor.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM CAN capture it with six interaction columns, which is a smaller code change than P6 itself. FF partially can: P6 concedes the 2x3 design already contains a size interaction, and its escape -- use staleness rather than size as the reliability proxy -- immediately kills the heteroskedastic-noise half of the proposal, which is calibrated on SIZE (sigma_e,i = sigma_e0*(mve_i/median)^{-xi}). The two halves of P6 are therefore in direct tension: the half FF cannot reach (staleness) is worth ~1.7 bp of monthly Sharpe, and the half with real dispersion (size-linked reliability, a 3x noise spread) is exactly the direction FF's double sort already spans. THE ARITHMETIC: at most 0.017 monthly Sharpe in the best model, less than 0.005 in BGN, and zero once FM is given the interactions -- against a target gap of 3-5x. ADDS NOISE FASTER THAN SIGNAL: yes, unambiguously, via the multiplicative nuisance coordinate. METRIC: the population conditional Sharpe would in principle detect a real interaction, but at 1.7 bp/month it is far below the cross-month sampling variation already documented in the correlations table.
verdicts.salvage: Two fragments are worth keeping, neither as a source of a DKKM gap. (1) Breaking the GS21 identity bm = 1/P_ex exactly is worth doing on its own terms -- that identity is the single most indefensible feature of that panel and any referee will find it -- so apply the fiscal-year lag to GS21's accounting chars purely as a realism fix and do not claim a complexity gain. (2) Write up the Fourier argument (classical EIV attenuates the nonlinear span exponentially while attenuating the linear span only by the classical factor) as a short theoretical note in the paper. It is a genuine, non-obvious contribution and it explains why real-data DKKM works DESPITE measurement error rather than because of it -- which is a useful piece of intellectual honesty given that P6's own logic implies real-world EIV should be shrinking the published 3-5x gap, not creating it. Do not implement heteroskedastic noise: it is calibrated on size, which is the one interaction FF already has.

missed_ideas: THE BIGGEST OMISSION: nobody proposed raising the NUMBER OF PRICED AGGREGATE SHOCKS, even though the diagnosis ranked it as lever #2 and DKKM's Theorem 3 makes the effective rank of E[FF'] the literal criterion. All six proposals leave K at 1 (GS21) or 2 (BGN, KP14). With K=1-2 and N=1000, the audit measured that ANY well-diversified portfolio attains SR* to within 0.19%, so every span argument is vacuous before it starts. The defensible implementation is Ross-style APT: replace the single TFP shock with J = 20-40 sectoral/vintage/intangible-capital shocks, each priced, with firm loadings that are NONLINEAR and INTERACTIVE functions of characteristics (e.g. loading on shock j is a bump function of a firm's position in a two-dimensional (size, age) space). Crucially the loadings must be nonlinear in the chars: if B(x) is linear, FM spans D^{-1}B lambda's leading term and we are back to square one. This is the only change that raises EffRank(E[FF']) from single digits into the hundreds through ECONOMICS rather than through feature engineering, and it does not require any 'mispricing' framing.

NOBODY PROPOSED A FALSIFICATION HARNESS BEFORE SPENDING WEEKS ON MODEL CHANGES. The cheapest decisive experiment: bypass the structural models entirely and inject a known nonlinear alpha directly into rp and the corresponding diagonal into cond_var in a synthetic *_moments.pkl, with chars drawn to match a target intrinsic dimension, then run the ACTUAL pipeline (generate_dkkm_factors -> estimate_sdf_dkkm -> evaluate_sdfs -> create_slides_tables) end to end. If the pipeline cannot recover a gap you planted by hand, no economics will help and the estimator is the problem. This costs a day and would have made P2 either mandatory or irrelevant before any of P1/P3/P4/P6 were designed.

NOBODY PROPOSED RUNNING THIS EXACT PIPELINE ON REAL CRSP/COMPUSTAT DATA to verify it reproduces DKKM's published 3-5x. The pipeline has several non-standard elements relative to the published method (a second rank-standardization of the features at dkkm_functions.py:110, NMAT=5 weight averaging, an unpenalized market column, population-conditional-Sharpe evaluation rather than realized OOS tangency Sharpe). If the pipeline does not reproduce the published result on the data where the result is known to hold, every conclusion about the models is confounded. This is the single most informative experiment available and it is absent from all six proposals.

N = 1000 IS A FREE LEVER NOBODY PULLED. The AIPT near-arbitrage term is alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N * E[alpha^2/d], so it scales LINEARLY in N; real CRSP has 4000-6000 names. Raising N from 1000 to 5000 multiplies any unspanned premium's contribution to SR*^2 by 5 with zero new economics and zero new parameters, and it also moves the estimator into the P/N regime where the RFF Monte-Carlo error over the kernel is the binding constraint rather than the DGP. It costs O(N^2) in sdf_compute, which is the real reason it was not proposed -- but that trade-off should be stated and priced, not ignored.

NOBODY PROPOSED FIRM ENTRY, EXIT AND AN UNBALANCED PANEL. All three models run a fixed set of 1000 firms with full histories. Real cross-sections have turnover, short histories, and characteristics that are missing or stale for young firms -- which is a major reason real-data DKKM benefits from shrinkage across many weak signals (many firms contribute little information individually). A balanced 1000 x 720 panel with no missingness is the regime in which a correctly specified small model is efficient.

NOBODY PROPOSED MAKING THE TRUE WEIGHT DEPEND ON A THRESHOLD OR REGIME rather than a smooth function. Every nonlinearity in P1/P4/P6 is smooth (a ratio, a power law, a product), and smooth low-order functions of 2-3 chars are exactly what a 21-term quadratic captures -- which is why the proposers' own est3.py has QUAD(21) beating RFF(3600) in the linear-alpha-plus-het-d cell. Genuine kinks are what a Fourier basis reaches and a polynomial does not: financial-constraint regimes, a live default boundary (GS21's is empty), collateral constraints that bind for a state-dependent subset, or option-like payoffs that switch on at a characteristic threshold. P4 makes GS21's default region live as a side effect of raising sigma_z; nobody proposed making a live default/constraint boundary the OBJECTIVE, with the boundary depending on two or three characteristics jointly so that it is a curved surface in char space.

NOBODY ADDRESSED THAT THE EVALUATION METRIC DELETES THE ENTIRE CONDITIONAL-TIMING CHANNEL, and then nobody proposed adding a conditioning mechanism anyway. P5 correctly notes that mean_t(w'rp / sqrt(w'Sigma w)) is homogeneous of degree zero in w, so correct levering-up in high-Sharpe months earns nothing; but no proposal adds time-varying prices of risk interacted with characteristics, which is one of the two channels through which complexity pays in DKKM/KMZ. These have to be fixed TOGETHER: adding char x macro-state interactions to the DGP is pointless while the metric cannot see timing, and fixing the metric is pointless while the DGP has no timing content. Note also that a date-level macro variable is invisible to every cross-sectional weighting scheme (which is why BGN's rf_stand is measurably worthless), so the conditioning must enter as a cross-sectionally varying char x state product.

NOBODY PROPOSED THE QUADRATIC-OLS BENCHMARK AS A STANDING COLUMN. Given that FM plus 15 cross-products beat RFF(3600) in the proposers' own Monte Carlo under the most favourable DGP they tested, a paper claiming 'the virtue of complexity' must report FM-with-interactions in every table. Without it, any measured DKKM-over-FM gap is uninterpretable: it could be complexity, or it could be one interaction layer. This single column would have reframed P1 and P4 before they were written.

NOBODY PROPOSED HETEROGENEITY IN THE LATENT FIRM STATE ITSELF. All the char-engineering proposals expand the MEASUREMENT of a 2-3 dimensional state. The cheaper and more defensible move is to raise the dimension of the state: in BGN, give each firm a firm-specific project-beta distribution (a scale and a shape, not just a common beta_star/scale of 0.772/0.137), so the third sufficient statistic betabar is no longer 99% recoverable from (num, S/num) and the cross-section has 4-5 genuine degrees of freedom instead of 2. In KP14, let lambda_f and the H/L regime be firm-specific and persistent. This changes the DGP's intrinsic dimension, which is the quantity that actually drives the feature spectrum, and unlike P3 it cannot be dismissed as relabelling.

NOBODY CHECKED THE FF/FM MARKET-COLUMN ASYMMETRY. fama_functions.fama_french sets the last column to the VALUE-weighted market (mve/mve.sum()) while fama_macbeth sets it to the EQUAL-weighted market (1/len(d)), and dkkm's mve_data always appends the value-weighted market UNPENALIZED (dkkm_functions.py:289-290, 309 excludes the last column from the augmentation). Since the audit shows the alpha->infinity limit of DKKM is exactly the CAPM, and since in GS21 89-97% of max SR^2 comes from the alpha leg rather than the market leg, this asymmetry is doing real work in the reported comparisons and is never disclosed.

result.root_cause:
**The dominant cause is genuine missing economics, and it is one specific, provable thing: all three models are frictionless exact K-factor economies in which mu_t = -cov_t(R, m) by construction, with K = 1 (GS21) or 2 (BGN, KP14). Under exact K-factor pricing with N = 1000, the maximum conditional Sharpe is attained to within ~0.2% by ANY well-diversified portfolio carrying the right factor exposure.** The measured population ceilings say this directly: in BGN, {1, size, bm} in raw levels attains 91.7% of max Sharpe, the actual FM span 91.8%, and a PERFECTLY estimated 56-term degree-3 polynomial 92.5% — total nonlinearity headroom for DKKM over FM is 0.7 percentage points. In GS21, FM attains 96.5% of max Sharpe and RFF-360 attains 99.4% — a ceiling of +3.0%, with the realistic RFF-180 figure at +1.0%. The theory experiment (span2.py) makes the mechanism explicit: with beta = 1 + 2x1 and N = 1000, SR* = 0.0999, equal-weight = 0.0998, linear-char span = 0.0999, RFF = 0.0994; adding a 20x spread in idiosyncratic variance changes nothing (RFF/linear = 0.999). DKKM's own Theorem 3 states the criterion as the effective rank of E[F F']: their AIPT calibration (eta_p ~ p^-0.5, EffRank ~500) produces the virtue of complexity; their APT calibration (p^-2, EffRank ~2.5) produces none and makes complexity *harmful* at light shrinkage. BOP reproduces the APT calibration line for line, including the c = 1 double-descent collapse (BGN Sharpe 0.006 / HJD 18.52; GS21 0.034 / HJD 23.57 at P = T = 360, alpha = 0) and the flat complexity curve (+2.5% BGN, +2.7% GS21 from P = 6 to P = 3600). No estimator change, bandwidth rescale, feature count or shrinkage grid can exceed a population ceiling of 1.01–1.03x. The disciplining counterexample that rules out "too few characteristics" as the cause: DKKM obtain 0.74 -> 1.93–2.50 (2.6–3.4x) in REAL data using exactly these same five characteristics, the same gamma grid, the same rank-standardization, the same T = 360.

**Plumbing is not the dominant cause of the null, but it IS the dominant cause of the current numbers being untrustworthy, and it is a strict precondition for anything else.** Three findings are severe enough to void or invert published cells. (i) KP14's entire "truth" is a numerical artifact: `integ_results.npz` returns exact zeros for E_t[G] over the whole eps interval where ~98% of firm-months live (scipy.quad on [0,10] against a CIR transition density with sd ~0.006, integ_kp14.py:43), so rp = -PVGO/P — wrong sign, mean -38.5%/yr, cross-sectional sd 173x the correct value, and max_sr = 34.7 annualized against the model's own bound of 0.774. G_func.csv was additionally solved under pre-Jun-18 parameters and is ~42-49x off, and it cannot be regenerated because `parameters_kp14` is absent from the repo. Every KP14 row currently in all_results.pdf must be withdrawn. (ii) GS21's shipped value function solves a different stochastic process than the simulation: zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159 matches 4 stationary sd of the (2/3)-exponent sigma_z to fifteen digits while config.py:289 uses the (3/2) exponent (1.468x wider), xgrid likewise (1.484x), r is 0.1/12 in GS21.m versus 0.074830/12 in config, zeta is 0.03 versus 0.01, and the tax base differs. With `fill_value=None` on every interpolator (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74) the pipeline silently extrapolates. So GS21's rp and cond_var are not the true moments of any internally consistent model. (iii) The estimator as configured cannot express complexity even if the DGP supplied it: participation-ratio effective rank of the 3600-feature map is 16.5 (effective c = 0.046 against a nominal 10 and DKKM's headline 1000), 48.9% of its variance sits in the 6-dim linear span and 88.4% in the 56-dim cubic span, the second rank-standardization at dkkm_functions.py:110 makes GAMMA_GRID a near-exact no-op (corr(rank_std(sin(gamma g'x)), rank_std(g'x)) = 0.9997-0.9999 because rank-standardization is monotone-invariant and sin is monotone over the realized range for 76% of features), NMAT = 5 converges the ensemble to kernel ridge and mechanically flattens the Sharpe-vs-P curve, and the alpha grid has NO point with effective df in (63, 360) — precisely the mildly-overparameterized region where the virtue of complexity peaks. Finally, the comparison is mildly rigged in DKKM's favour: DKKM gets 4 x 6 = 24 cells whose winner is chosen post hoc on the evaluation metric itself (create_slides_tables.py:81-97, separate argmax for Sharpe and argmin for HJD), GS21 gets a hand-tuned /100 grid for DKKM only, ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], and BGN's RFF is fed `rf_stand` which FF/FM never see. Net: fixing all of this moves BGN's DKKM/FM ratio by <= 1% and GS21's by <= 3% — but without it, no economics change can be either seen or believed.

**Calibration ranks third for the ratio and first for credibility.** Three undisclosed 10x idiosyncratic-volatility cuts are in the repo — BGN's inline `# added a factor of 0.1` at panel_functions_bgn.py:54, KP14's `KP14_SIGMA_EPS = 0.1*0.2` and `KP14_SIGMA_U = 0.1*1.5`, GS21's `0.1*0.16*...`. They produce average pairwise return correlations of 0.565 / 0.391 / 0.950 against a real-data 0.15–0.20, and in GS21 they eliminate the default region entirely (zero defaults in 2,163,000 firm-months; z_cut_down pinned at the grid floor everywhere). A paper claiming three canonical models cannot generate the virtue of complexity, while silently running all three at one tenth their source papers' idiosyncratic volatility, is not recoverable at revision. But note the arithmetic: the D^{-1} inverse-variance tilt is worth 1.81% of SR* at N = 100, 0.186% at N = 1000, 0.019% at N = 10000, and stays worth ~0.2% even with a 20x spread in d. **Heteroskedastic idiosyncratic variance is a MULTIPLIER on an unspanned premium (RFF/linear ceiling 1.00 -> 1.91 with a linear alpha, 2.88 -> 6.37 with a nonlinear one), never a standalone source.** Restore the cuts for honesty, not for the result.

**What is actually missing, ranked.** (1) An expected-return component NOT proportional to the dominant covariance loadings, contributing alpha' D^{-1} alpha ~ N * E[alpha^2/d] to SR*^2 — the AIPT near-arbitrage. Without it the RFF-over-linear span ceiling is 1.00 and the exercise is over. (2) A priced-risk space of dimension far exceeding L. With K priced factors and only L linear characteristic portfolios, the reachable factor-exposure set is col(B'X), of dimension min(L, K), so SR_lin/SR* ~ sqrt(L/K) — this holds even when the loadings B(x) are linear in x, and it is the one large lever available entirely inside a frictionless rational-expectations model. Going from K = 1-2 to K = 30-50 takes SR_lin/SR* from ~1.00 to ~0.35-0.45 while a basis of effective rank >= K reaches ~1.00. (3) Characteristics that are noisy, lagged, partial proxies rather than exact inverses of a 2-3 dimensional state: GS21 has bm = 1/P_ex to machine precision and an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight; BGN's entire date-t cross-section is a verified bijection of two numbers (num_i, sum_j exp(-beta_j)) <-> (book_i, mve_i). Note the ordering matters: (2) and (3) are defensible inside the paper's "simple economic models" framing; (1) is not, unless the wedge is given an aggregate, priced component so that it is compensation for noise-trader risk rather than an assumed free lunch.

recommended_program.step: 0. GATE: run the population-span and ceiling diagnostics on the pickles you already have, before any rerun
recommended_program.change: Write one script over the existing *_moments.pkl and *_results.pkl. (a) Report mean_t max_sr_t and assert it is below each model's own HJ bound: BGN sqrt(exp(SIGMA_Z^2)-1) = 0.4166/mo, KP14 sqrt(GAMMA_X^2+GAMMA_Z^2)*sqrt(1/12) = 0.2234/mo, GS21 sqrt(exp(gamma_x^2)-1) = 0.5329/mo with gamma_x = 0.5 from GS21.m:28,138. (b) For each eval month compute the attainable Sharpe restricted to w = Xa: SR_X = sqrt(rp' X (X' Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp) using rp = m['rp'][firm_ids] and Sigma = m['cond_var'][firm_ids][:,firm_ids], for X = [1, raw chars], [1, rank chars], [1, rank chars + all 15 quadratic cross-products], [1, deg-3 poly], and the ACTUAL rff() output at D = 36/180/360. Report each as a fraction of max_sr. THE DECISION NUMBER IS mean_t SR_rff / mean_t SR_quad, not SR_rff/SR_linear. (c) Report the same for D random Gaussian directions (placebo). (d) Report SR_alpha^2/SR*^2 = (alpha' D^{-1} alpha)/(rp' Sigma^{-1} rp) after splitting Sigma into common + diagonal.
recommended_program.rationale: Sharpe_t(w) = SR*_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*_t) is an exact identity, so the reported Sharpe is uninterpretable without max_sr. And the population span ratio IS the upper bound on the attainable DKKM advantage for a perfect estimator; the whole diagnosis phase produced conflicting numbers (0.7pp vs 7pp in BGN) partly because two different projectors were used. CRITICAL: the correct projector is onto col(L'X) with z = L^{-1}rp and Sigma = LL' — equivalently the closed form sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp). Some diagnosis-phase numbers used col(L^{-1}X), which on a random 40x5 test gave 0.0174 against a brute-force optimum of 0.00580. Recompute everything.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: None — this is the gate. Predicted outcome: SR_rff/SR_quad in [1.00, 1.10] for BGN and GS21, confirming the diagnosis. If it clears 2.0 anywhere, the estimator is the binding constraint and the priority order inverts.
recommended_program.survived_critique: All three lenses independently demanded it. The mechanism critic supplied the projector correction; the referee critic supplied the FM-with-quadratics denominator; the structure critic supplied the placebo requirement.
recommended_program.residual_objection: At P >= N the RFF column space is R^N and the population ceiling is trivially 1.0, so the diagnostic looks vacuous at D = 3600, N = 1000. Answer: run it at D = 36/180/360 (< N) where the span is genuine, and at D = 3600 use the ridge-implied span at a fixed penalty rather than the exact column space. Empirically the measured effective rank of 16.5 means the numerical span is far below N even at D = 3600, which is itself the finding.

recommended_program.change: utils/evaluate_sdfs.py:170-179 reads m['rp'], m['cond_var'], m['sdf_ret'] and never m['max_sr'] (verified) — add it and carry it into results.pkl. In create_slides_tables.py report Sharpe/mean(max_sr) (the Sigma-cosine) as the HEADLINE column. Add the unconditional Sharpe mean_t(w'rp)/sqrt(mean_t(w'Sigma w) + var_t(w'rp)) and the MEDIAN monthly ratio alongside the mean-of-ratios. Promote alpha' Sigma^{-1} alpha from compute_pricing_errors.py to the headline pricing-error statistic; demote HJD to a robustness table printed alongside sd(sdf_ret) and the w = 0 null. Fix the universe mismatch at evaluate_sdfs.py:170-172 (rp/cond_var subset to firm_ids, sdf_ret computed over the book>0 universe). Add test assets to generate_25_portfolios.py sorted on (mve, diag(cond_var)) and on characteristic interactions and non-monotone transforms.
recommended_program.rationale: Without max_sr nobody can tell 'the estimator is failing' from 'the model has nothing to estimate' — which is the entire question. HJD as coded is the RMSE between an UNNORMALIZED regression return and a unit-cost HJ portfolio return; GS21's FF HJD of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is a naked leverage artifact, and find_best_alpha_for_model's argmin over alpha can select shrinkage-to-zero (HJD -> sqrt(E[sdf_ret^2]) = 0.286 BGN, 0.269 KP14, 0.329 GS21). The 25 test assets are sorted on mve and bm only, two of the five characteristics every method already spans linearly, so the pricing-error evidence currently has no power.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: Slightly NEGATIVE for DKKM: a scale-free pricing error removes DKKM's six-chances-at-the-right-leverage advantage while FF/FM sit at alpha = 0. Report that this is the correct direction.
recommended_program.survived_critique: Endorsed by all three lenses. Two amendments were forced and are incorporated: do NOT use sqrt(1 - rho_unc^2) as the headline, and do NOT build test assets from the true w*.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'You changed the pricing-error metric after the old one gave an inconvenient answer.' Answer: report both columns permanently, justify the new one from the algebra (HJD^2 = S*^2/(1+S*^2) - S_f^2/(1+S_f^2) exactly, so at S* = 2 the entire range between zero skill and perfect correlation is 13.1% of the level and 72% of HJD^2 is the irreducible mean gap), and note that alpha'Sigma^{-1}alpha was already in the codebase.

recommended_program.step: 2. Fairness repair — do this before any economics change or the whole comparison is contested
recommended_program.change: (a) config.py:187 ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] -> the same shrinkage grid DKKM gets, and fama_functions.mve_data:268 Ridge(alpha=360*alpha) -> the same scale-free penalty. (b) Replace create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model's post-hoc argmax/argmin on the evaluation metric with a validation split: use the first 120 of the 360 eval months to pick (alpha, nfeatures) for EVERY method, report on the disjoint last 240. (c) DELETE the BGN-only rf_stand input at dkkm_functions.py:95-96 — it is an unearned conditioning variable (FF/FM never see rf; fama_functions._compute_monthly_fama passes only data[chars]) and it is measurably worthless (span 89.9% of max with it, 90.1% without; 65.6% of sin features are literally unchanged when rf_stand flips from -0.5 to +0.5). (d) Rank-standardize FM's regressors to match DKKM (fama_functions.py:152-156, the standardization block is commented out and FM currently mixes log-size of order 5 with bm of order 1 through pinvh). (e) ADD 'FM + all pairwise char interactions, ridge-tuned on the same grid' as a STANDING benchmark column in every table. (f) Fix the FF tercile degeneracy at fama_functions.py:86-88 (agr is 91% zeros in BGN and 98.8% in GS21, giving q30 = q70 = 0 and an EMPTY medium bucket).
recommended_program.rationale: As it stands, an oracle-tuned DKKM over 24 cells is being compared to an untuned FF/FM with one cell, and the headline finding is that they tie. Item (e) is the decisive one: in the theory agent's own Monte Carlo under the most DKKM-favourable DGP tested (linear alpha + heteroskedastic d), a 21-term quadratic OLS scored 0.601 against RFF-3600's 0.564. Any DKKM-over-FM gap must be reported against FM-with-interactions or it is uninterpretable — it could be complexity, or it could be one interaction layer.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: Shrinks the measured DKKM/FF and DKKM/FM ratios, possibly below 1.0 in some cells. This is the honest baseline against which every subsequent change must be scored.
recommended_program.survived_critique: Unanimous across lenses. One correction incorporated: the crosscut proposal's 'let FF/FM cheat symmetrically' was rejected as institutionalizing the cheat; the validation split replaces it.
recommended_program.residual_objection: The validation split costs a third of the evaluation sample and raises the noise on every cell. Answer: 240 months at these Sharpes still resolves differences of the size the paper needs (3-5x), and a single pre-specified number per method is worth far more than a tighter oracle-selected one.

recommended_program.step: 3. Estimator geometry — the mandatory subset only
recommended_program.change: (a) config.py:178 NMAT = 5 -> 1 (the adjacent comment already records that the root codebase used nmat = 1); report the five W draws as replications with a spread, not an average. (b) Reparameterize the ridge penalty to be scale-free: in dkkm_functions.mve_data the penalty for alpha > 0 is delivered by the augmentation `np.sqrt(360*alph)*np.eye(X.shape[1])[:-1]` at line ~309, NOT by the `360*z` at lines 162/176 (which is always called with shrinkage_list = [0]). Change line ~309 to sqrt(360*alph*trace(X'X)/P). This also eliminates the indefensible ALPHA_LST_GS = ALPHA_LST/100 hand-tuning at config.py:193. (c) ALPHA_LST -> [0, 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, 1e-1, 1], which hits effective df ~ [360, 283, 180, 100, 63, 30, 22, 10, 6, 1] and fills the empty (63, 360) band. (d) Truncate small eigenvalues in the P >= T branch (dkkm_functions.py:172-174 computes 1/(eig + 0) with no truncation) or drop the unconditional alpha = 0 column emitted at line ~301. (e) Report the COMPLEXITY CURVE at fixed pre-committed shrinkage across c = P/T in {0.017, 0.1, 1, 10, 100} as the headline figure, not the argmax cell.
recommended_program.rationale: The applied penalty is P-invariant in relative terms, so the current grid gives effective df [360, 63, 22, 9.5, 6.2, 1.15] — four of six points sit at df <= 22, where DKKM is no richer than a 22-factor model, and the alpha -> infinity limit is EXACTLY the CAPM because the market column is exempted from the augmentation. NMAT = 5 averaging converges to kernel ridge with the same explicit penalty and cancels precisely the draw-specific high-frequency directions complexity is supposed to exploit, which mechanically flattens the curve the paper needs to be rising. DKKM's actual claim is monotone ascent in c, not a maximum over a grid.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: On the CURRENT models, approximately zero (BGN headroom 0.7pp, GS21 3%). What visibly changes: the c = 1 double-descent explosions disappear and the alpha = 0 column stops realizing 1.4-13% of max Sharpe. Label these as bug fixes, not results.
recommended_program.survived_critique: Endorsed by all three lenses. The mechanism critic located the correct code site for (b), which the original proposal targeted incorrectly.
recommended_program.residual_objection: NMAT = 1 will LOWER DKKM's realized Sharpe by removing a 5x variance reduction — the proposal trades level for curve shape. Answer: the curve shape is the object of the DKKM theory and the level is confounded by the oracle selection being removed in step 2; report the five-draw distribution so a lucky draw cannot become the headline.

recommended_program.step: 4. HOLD as robustness only: GAMMA_GRID rescale and the second-rank-standardization replacement
recommended_program.change: Do NOT put these in the baseline. Report a 2x2 of {coded gamma, gamma * sqrt(130/L)} x {old DGP, new DGP}, and separately {rank_standardize(features), per-column z-score} at dkkm_functions.py:110. The z-score is the right form if either ships: simply DELETING the second standardization makes things WORSE (linear-span share rises 48.9% -> 86.4%, effective rank falls 14.4 -> 5.1) because it is silently equalizing the 3.1x sin/cos amplitude asymmetry (sd(sin u) = 0.415 vs sd(cos u) = 0.135 at s = 0.46).
recommended_program.rationale: The derivation (hold the Gaussian-kernel exponent gamma^2 L/12 fixed at DKKM's real-data value, giving gamma * 5.099 at L = 5) is sound, but the sign of the effect depends on the DGP: the GS21 agent measured 36-feature span falling 0.879 -> 0.799 at gamma x4.65 and -> 0.376 at gamma x10, and the theory agent's estimation experiment gave 0.157 vs 0.254 under a linear truth. A knob whose optimal setting depends on the answer is a tuning knob however good the derivation reads.

recommended_program.survived_critique: All three lenses independently demanded demotion to robustness. Step 6's modest characteristic expansion is the referee-proof route to the same place: at L = 12-15, sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) ~ 1.0-1.1*gamma with the ORIGINAL grid.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'You left the bandwidth mis-specified relative to the published method.' Answer: DKKM use the identical grid; what differs is L, and raising L is the honest fix. Report the rescale as robustness so the reader can see the sign flip.

recommended_program.step: 5. KP14 numerics — blocking for KP14, and withdraw all existing KP14 results
recommended_program.change: (a) integ_kp14.py:43 — replace `quad(f, 0, 10, epsabs=1e-10, epsrel=1e-10)` with quantile-anchored quadrature over the noncentral chi-square CIR transition law: eps_nodes = c * ncx2.ppf(linspace(1e-9, 1-1e-9, 20001), d, lam), E[f] = mean(f(nodes)), plus an assertion that the density integrates to 1 to 1e-8 and a node-doubling convergence check on the five SQUARED integrands that set cond_var. Add a regression test asserting E_t[G_up](eps=1.0) is within a few percent of G_up(1.0) (the CIR transition sd is ~0.006, so they must be close; the shipped file is off by ~50 orders of magnitude). (b) Restore utils_kp14/parameters_kp14.py as a shim re-exporting the config names, re-run kp14_fd.py and integ_kp14.py, and COMMIT the regenerated solfiles with the config hash they were solved under. (d) Mask the ~5% of firms with zero live projects (rp = -1.0 exactly) to NaN in the returned rp/cond_var rather than relying on the implicit coupling with prepare_panel. (e) Recalibrate (alpha, mu_z, gamma_z) so KP14_RHO is 0.05-0.08 rather than 0.0158, since PVGO ~ 1/rho currently sits 1.6 percentage points from the transversality boundary (rho = 0 at gamma_z = -0.4294).
recommended_program.rationale: The shipped rp is minus the PVGO share: corr(rp, -PVGOshare) = 0.9505, R^2 = 0.9034, mean -38.5%/yr with the wrong sign and cross-sectional sd 173x the theory value; max_sr averages 34.66 annualized against the model's own bound of 0.774. Every KP14 cell in all_results.pdf is a quadrature artifact.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: KP14 Sharpes go from -2.64 (FF) / -5.35 (FM) / -0.60 (DKKM) to roughly +0.15-0.22/month for all three, i.e. a CLEAN, HONEST NULL with DKKM/FF ~ 1.0. That is the right thing to publish.
recommended_program.survived_critique: Unanimous. The structure lens corrected the regime-fix scope from 2 sites to 6 and flagged the transversality knife-edge; the referee lens established that the diagnosis text and the proposal disagreed about which convention kp14_fd.py uses, so the resolution must come from the published paper.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'The corrected KP14 shows an even cleaner null than the broken one.' Answer: yes, and the paper must be ready to say so. A correct null is the constructive half of the argument, not a failure.

recommended_program.step: 6. Measurement realism and a MODEST characteristic expansion, given identically to all three methods
recommended_program.change: (a) Staggered fiscal year-ends: assign each firm a fixed fiscal month, update accounting characteristics (book, op_cash_flow, and everything derived: bm, roe, agr, book_lev) annually with the conventional 6-month lag, leave market characteristics (mve, size, mom) contemporaneous, and add `stale` = months since last accounting update as an observable to ALL methods. Zero free parameters — this is the Fama-French convention. (b) Repair GS21's mkt_lev: panel_functions_gs21.py:278 currently computes book_lev * bm = coupon/equity (mean 0.0013); the correct object is Q_0/(Q_0 + mve) using the Q_0 interpolator already in scope via the star-import at line 15, and it equals 0.33 at the calibration center. The 'GS21 firms are effectively all-equity' finding is an artifact of this bug. (c) Expand chars to L ~ 12-15 with a hard screen: keep only columns with tie fraction < 10% and incremental partial R^2 > 2% against the existing set. Candidates: multi-horizon returns (2-6, 7-12, 13-36), 12m and 60m realized volatility, 12m realized beta, multi-year mean profitability, 12m book growth (replacing the 1-month agr), 6m and 12m lags of size and bm, firm age where it is not constant. (d) Give FF and FM the identical char set and fix the FF tie handling in the same commit.
recommended_program.rationale: The characteristics currently invert the state exactly (GS21: bm = 1/P_ex verified by np.allclose; BGN: the cross-section is a bijection of two numbers to machine precision), which is why an MLP recovers 98.3% of GS21's true SDF weight and why a small model is the CORRECTLY SPECIFIED model. Staleness is the cheapest way to break exact invertibility with zero free parameters. L ~ 12-15 also delivers sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) ~ 1.0-1.1*gamma with the UNCHANGED gamma grid, achieving most of step 4's bandwidth effect without touching a hyperparameter.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: Small and possibly negative in BGN (book = I*num is a small integer averaging 5.95, so a 12-month-stale book is nearly as informative as a fresh one). Largest in GS21, where rho_z^12 = 0.657 makes staleness bite. Realistically +5-15% on the DKKM/FM ratio, mostly as an enabler.
recommended_program.survived_critique: Survived after being cut down hard. Three items were REMOVED in critique and must stay removed: 'age' in BGN (all firms are born at t=0, so cumcount is cross-sectionally CONSTANT and rank_standardize's argsort would inject a second pseudo-random column), 'nproj' (= bm*exp(size)/I exactly — it hands FM a nonlinear function of two chars for free), and the peer-relative block keyed to latent parameters (beta_j, lambda_f, initial k) which leaks the answer.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'Adding characteristics helps FM at least as much and the gap you report is FM's estimation penalty.' Answer: capping at L ~ 15 keeps FM at K = 17, i.e. 2K/T = 9% squared-Sharpe loss, and step 2(a)+(e) gives FM ridge and interactions, so the residual gap cannot be estimation-cost handicapping.

recommended_program.change: (a) BGN: panel_functions_bgn.py:54, replace the hand-inserted `0.1*0.3*np.abs(Cbar)` band with a multiplier m in [1.0, 1.25], NOT 1.75. Verified free: sigma_j enters only the draw (51-55), corr_zj := beta/(sigma_z*sigmaj) (61) and C = exp(Cbar - 0.5 sigmaj^2 + eps*sigmaj) (121), so cov(log M, log C_j) = -beta_j identically and E[C] = Chat — no price, no policy, no investment rule, no Jstar, no beta_star/scale calibration moves. (b) KP14 (gated on step 5): remove the two `0.1*` factors on SIGMA_EPS and SIGMA_U; this restores the CIR share of idiosyncratic variance from 2.2% to 69.2% and BREAKS the idio-var ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/size identity (corr -0.971) that mechanically produces the negative Sharpes. Check A(eps,u) > 0 over the realized support and report the implied sd(log K). (c) GS21: reconcile ALL FIVE solve/simulation mismatches (sigma_x and sigma_z exponents 3/2 -> 2/3, r 0.074830/12 vs 0.1/12, zeta 0.01 vs 0.03, the tax base at GS21.m:124 vs panel_functions_gs21.py:113-118), verify GS21.m reproduces the shipped solfiles bit-for-bit (tauchen.m and gaussHermite.m are MISSING from the repo — supply them or port GS21.m to Python), add an explicit off-grid counter to replace the silent fill_value=None extrapolation, THEN restore sigma_z toward the paper value. (d) Publish a table of every parameter that departs from the source calibration, with the reason, plus a table of UNTARGETED moments (pairwise correlation, sd(log mve), sd(log bm), value premium, size premium, default frequency, idiosyncratic share) before and after, against real-data counterparts.
recommended_program.rationale: Three undisclosed 10x cuts give pairwise correlations of 0.565/0.391/0.950 against a real-data 0.15-0.20 and eliminate GS21's default region. Independent of any DKKM result, a referee who diffs the repo and finds these unremarked ends the paper. The disclosure table is not optional.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: max_sr FALLS in all three models and all Sharpes fall roughly proportionally; the ratio moves by only a few percent. Report as a correctness fix. Its real value is as a multiplier on step 8-9 (RFF/linear ceiling 1.00 -> 1.91 with a linear alpha, 2.88 -> 6.37 with a nonlinear one, once heteroskedastic d is present).
recommended_program.survived_critique: Endorsed. The BGN multiplier was cut from 1.75 to <= 1.25 by two independent lenses: at m = 1.75, sigma_j reaches 3.87, per-project cash-flow CV averages 121, realized excess kurtosis is 149, and mean diag(cond_var) is 7.7x the average realized cross-sectional variance — the metric would grade every method against tail variance the 360-month training sample never displays. Measured corr(60m realized vol, true conditional sd) = 0.11-0.15.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'You reverted your own parameter cut because it improved the estimator comparison.' Answer: revert it BEFORE running any estimator, disclose the history in the parameter table, and show that standalone it lowers max_sr and moves the ratio by <3%. Also add the guard the critics demanded: check that mean(diag(cond_var)) matches the average realized cross-sectional variance to within ~25%, and that realized excess kurtosis is single-digit.

recommended_program.step: 8. PRIMARY MODEL-STRUCTURE CHANGE: raise the dimension of the priced-risk space, starting with BGN where it is algebraically free
recommended_program.change: BGN: replace the scalar SDF shock nu with a K-vector, log M = -r - 0.5|lambda|^2 - lambda'nu, and give project j a loading vector b_j subject to the SINGLE restriction lambda'b_j = beta_j. Because BGN's valuation depends on the cash-flow shock ONLY through cov(log M, log C_j) = -sigma_z*corr_zj*sigmaj = -beta_j (panel_functions_bgn.py:61) and A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values (line 153) with beta_avg = mean(exp(-beta)), EVERY b_j in the (K-1)-dimensional affine set {b : lambda'b = beta_j} gives identical prices, identical investment decisions (line 81: exp(Cbar-beta)*D(r) > 1 is sigma_j- and b-free), identical expected returns, identical Jstar and D(r), and an identical beta_star/scale calibration. Draw the null-space component from a distribution indexed by a persistent firm-level 'sector' assigned at entry, so the loadings are recoverable from observables (a sector-mean characteristic) rather than from latent parameters. The moment algebra stays bilinear: sdf_compute_bgn.py:184 becomes exp(kron(col2a,col2a).data + kron(col2b,col2b).data + ...), ~5 lines per factor. Target K = 20-40. KP14: sector-specific IST shocks — solve the same 1000-point Feynman-Kac ODE once per sector (seconds each), giving beta_z = alph * share_i * (sector loading), a product of an observable share and a sector identity. GS21: activate the DECLARED but unused Epstein-Zin parameters at GS21.m:14-16 (beta = 0.994, varphi = 2, gamma = 10 appear nowhere else in the file; the SDF at line 138 is an exogenous lognormal with a free gamma_x = 0.5 implying a monthly Sharpe bound of 0.533 = 1.85 annualized, 3-4x the empirical market Sharpe) and add stochastic volatility to x, which delivers a second priced factor whose price is PINNED by gamma and varphi rather than chosen.
recommended_program.rationale: With K priced factors and only L linear characteristic portfolios, the reachable factor-exposure set is col(B'X) of dimension min(L, K), so SR_lin/SR* ~ sqrt(L/K) — this holds even when B(x) is linear in x, so it is dimension counting in the EXPOSURE space, not a nonlinearity assumption. Going from K = 1-2 to K = 30 takes SR_FM/SR* from ~1.00 to ~sqrt(6/30) = 0.45 and SR_FMquad/SR* to ~sqrt(21/30) = 0.84, while a basis of effective rank >= 30 reaches ~1.00. It is also the direct lever on DKKM's own Theorem 3 criterion, EffRank(E[FF']), currently measured at 16.5 against the several hundred their AIPT calibration requires. And it requires no wedge, no arbitrage assumption, no redefinition of 'the true SDF', and in BGN no re-solve and no recalibration whatsoever.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: At K = 30 and L = 12: DKKM/FF ~ 2.5-3x, DKKM/FM ~ 2-2.5x, DKKM/FM-with-interactions ~ 1.3-1.5x. This is the honest arithmetic and the paper must report all three ratios. The complexity curve should rise monotonically in c for the first time.
recommended_program.survived_critique: This is the structure lens's and the mechanism lens's top 'missed idea' for BGN, and it survives every objection raised against the proposals it replaces. It defeats the KP14 technology-torus critique (no non-stationary firm-specific z), the GS21 credit-state critique (no 64 GB Mmat, no free price of risk), and the P1 critique (no mispricing, no SDF violation).
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'FM given K sector dummies spans the exposure space exactly, so this is a statement about the char encoding, not about complexity.' Answer, and it must be built in from the start: do NOT make sector membership an observable categorical. Let the null-space loadings be smooth functions of continuous characteristics (e.g. bump functions over a two-dimensional observable coordinate that is itself a noisy function of firm history), give FM the same continuous coordinates plus all quadratics, and report DKKM/FM-quad as the primary ratio. Second objection: with K > 21, FM-with-interactions still gets sqrt(21/K); answer: K = 40-50 gives DKKM/FM-quad of 1.4-1.5x, and DKKM/FF6 of ~3x, which IS the comparison DKKM themselves make.

recommended_program.step: 9. SECONDARY MODEL-STRUCTURE CHANGE (high risk, high reward): an AIPT premium introduced as compensation for NOISE-TRADER RISK, not as an assumed free lunch
recommended_program.change: Observed price = fundamental price x exp(-kappa_i * v_it) with v_it = w_t + e_it, where w_t is an AGGREGATE noise-trader factor carrying its own price of risk and e_it is idiosyncratic, both AR(1). kappa_i is an arbitrage-cost loading depending on staleness/age/turnover — NOT on size, because FF's 2x3 design already contains the size interaction. Analytic ER transform: with kappa predetermined at t, a_i = exp(q_it - kappa_{i,t+1} rho v_it + 0.5 kappa^2 sigma_v^2), ER_obs = outer(a,a) * ER, with the diagonal multiplied by exp(kappa^2 sigma_v^2). Three non-negotiable conditions: (i) calibrate kappa from an EXTERNAL moment (Rhodes-Kropf-Robinson-Viswanathan firm-specific misvaluation sd ~0.40 in logs, or a documented anomaly long-short magnitude), freeze it before running anything, and report SR* as an OUTPUT; (ii) report an N-scaling table at N in {250, 500, 1000, 2000} with kappa FIXED, since alpha'D^{-1}alpha ~ N — if the DKKM/FM ratio moves with N you have measured diversification; (iii) do NOT apply to GS21 without adding v as a state and re-solving, because GS21's default trigger, investment cutoff and refinancing choice are all read off the SOLVED price (panel_functions_gs21.py:74 and the i_cut/b_refin interpolators), so a wedge on the reported price alone means managers optimize against a price nobody will pay. BGN and KP14 pass this internal-consistency test.
recommended_program.rationale: This is the only ingredient that clears condition (C2), an expected-return component not proportional to the covariance loadings. Under exact factor pricing every basis is within 0.6% of SR*; with a nonlinear alpha plus heteroskedastic d the population RFF/linear ceiling is 21x and the T=360 Monte Carlo gives RFF-3600 at 1.249 versus linear at 0.071. The aggregate component w_t is what converts an assumed free lunch into DeLong-Shleifer-Summers-Waldmann noise-trader-risk compensation, which is an equilibrium object, bounds max_sr independently of N, and explains why the arbitrageur does not trade it away.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: The only change that can plausibly reach the real-data 3-5x. Realistic defensible range against FM-with-interactions: 1.5-2.5x; against FF6: 2.5-4x.
recommended_program.survived_critique: Survived only in this heavily amended form. Three amendments are load-bearing and were forced by critique: the aggregate noise-trader component (otherwise the model contains an unexploited near-arbitrage that grows with N and E[m R_i] != 1 for every i), the ex-ante external calibration (the original solved kappa_med = 0.033 backwards from a target Sharpe reproducing DKKM's published ratio — one sentence a referee would quote), and the GS21 exclusion.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'The wedge contaminates log bm additively (+q) and log size subtractively (-q), so a linear contrast of two existing characteristics extracts the alpha and FM spans it.' This is the strongest surviving technical objection and it is correct as stated. Answer: apply the wedge to the price only and add independent measurement noise to reported book, or route the demand shock so that q is identified only by a RATIO of characteristics — then verify with the step-0 diagnostic that R^2(q | linear chars) < 0.5 BEFORE running any estimator. If it does not clear that bar, the wedge has created a linear premium, not complexity.

recommended_program.step: 10. FRAMING: publish the negative result as the paper's spine and the model changes as its constructive half
recommended_program.change: Restructure the paper as: (1) the necessary and sufficient conditions for the virtue of complexity, stated formally — unspanned premium (C2), flat spectrum / EffRank in the hundreds (C3), span gap (C1), c >> 1 with tuned shrinkage (C4), limits to learning (C5); (2) a proof-by-measurement that three canonical frictionless production models violate C2 and C3, with the oracle span calculations, the measured EffRank of 16.5, and the reproduced APT-calibration signature including the c=1 collapse; (3) the minimal departures (steps 8 and 9) that restore them, with the honest magnitudes. Include the negative control: run the full pipeline on a synthetic exact-APT panel and show the flat curve.
recommended_program.rationale: This is the strongest and most robust thing the project has, and it inverts the referee's attack surface: instead of 'you changed models until complexity paid', the claim becomes 'the empirical virtue of complexity is evidence that the true cross-section is NOT an exact low-factor risk economy — here is exactly which condition it must violate.' It also converts steps 5, 6 and 7 from suspicious interventions into ordinary model corrections.
recommended_program.expected_gap_effect: None directly; it determines whether a 1.5-2.5x result is publishable (it is, in this framing) or dismissed as a search (it would be, in the original framing).
recommended_program.survived_critique: Independently proposed by all three critique lenses as the missed high-value option.
recommended_program.residual_objection: 'A negative result is a weaker paper.' Answer: DKKM PROVE that under correct specification complexity strictly reduces the Sharpe ratio, so a model that reproduces that prediction is validating the theory, not failing. The constructive half then has a target and a stopping rule instead of a search.

per_model.binding_constraint: The cross-section of expected returns is EXACTLY two-dimensional and exactly affine. From panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186: term1 and term3 are date-level scalars, term2 = pi*A*e_t with A = P - G, term4 = Chat*pi*book, so 1+eret_i = [pi*e_t/bond_t] + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + (Chat*pi)*bm_i, with the bm coefficient identically Chat*pi = 0.0244763 at EVERY date. Combined with one priced shock (log M = -r - 0.5 sigma_z^2 - sigma_z nu, a rank-1 price-of-risk vector, |lambda_xi|/lambda_mu = 0.178) and a date-t cross-section that is a verified bijection of two numbers, the population headroom for any nonlinearity over FM is 0.7 percentage points of max Sharpe.
per_model.primary_recommendation: Multi-dimensional priced-risk space via the null-space construction: log M = -r - 0.5|lambda|^2 - lambda'nu with project loadings b_j restricted only by lambda'b_j = beta_j. Every price, policy, investment rule, Jstar, D(r) and the beta_star/scale calibration are LITERALLY unchanged (verified: valuation depends on the cash-flow shock only through cov(log M, log C_j) = -beta_j), while the systematic covariance goes from rank 2 to rank K+1 with heterogeneous, char-measurable loadings. Target K = 20-40. Cost: ~5 lines per factor in sdf_compute_bgn.py:184 because the exponent stays bilinear. No re-solve, no recalibration, no wedge.

per_model.do_not_do: Do NOT set the band multiplier to 1.75. At m = 1.75 sigma_j reaches 3.87, per-project cash-flow CV averages 121, realized excess kurtosis is 149, mean diag(cond_var) is 0.03733 against an average realized cross-sectional variance of 0.00482 (a factor of 7.7), and corr(60-month realized vol, true conditional sd) is 0.11-0.15 — the metric would grade every method against unlearnable tail variance, and the resulting d ~ 1/(size-ish) tilt imports KP14's anti-size artifact wholesale. Withdraw every existing KP14 number.

Pair it with heterogeneous returns to scale alpha_i over the empirically standard [0.60, 0.90], which makes beta_z,i = alph_i * share_i a genuine PRODUCT of two observables with alph_i varying 1.5x to 9x, requires only a ~10-node grid solve of G, and keeps the SDF two-dimensional and exogenous exactly as KP14 specify. Then apply the step-8 sector-IST construction on top.

And do NOT adopt the 100-domain technology torus: making z firm-specific turns log z_i - log z_j into a random walk with sd growing without bound, which raised to the project-scale exponent 1/(1-alpha) = 4 gives sd(log K) = 1.7 and rising, importing exactly the non-stationary size distribution the GS21 diagnosis flagged as a pathology; and 1/rho_i near the transversality boundary produces a 12x convex spread in PVGO driven purely by a drawn discount-rate parameter.
